Generic untyped pointer used in APIs that want an explicit opaque block pointer type.

Enumeration of FIPS usage counters for specific EVP AES modes. Used to index per‑algorithm counters in FIPS mode via FIPS_read_counter. Values map named counters to small integers; fips_counter_max marks the largest defined value. No storage is defined here; the enum serves as the identifier type.
Tag type used to disambiguate between container-based Span constructors via SFINAE/overload resolution. Has no data or behavior.
Sentinel constant used as the dynamic extent marker for Span and related APIs. Indicates the span size is determined at runtime.

CRYPTO ByteString: a non-owning view over a contiguous byte sequence, with length, used for safe parsing of TLS/ASN.1 structures. It does not manage memory; caller retains ownership of underlying data.
Internal buffer backing a CBB. Tracks data pointer, current length, capacity, ownership (resizable), and sticky error flag. Managed by CBB; not exposed for standalone construction.

Internal state for a child CBB which is writing a pending length-prefixed region into a shared base buffer. Tracks base buffer, offset to pending length, encoded length field size, and whether the pending element is ASN.1.

CRYPTO ByteBuilder: a growable or fixed-size buffer writer for constructing length-prefixed messages (TLS/ASN.1). Top-level instances own or reference the output buffer; child instances encode nested, pending length-prefixed contents. After failure, only cleanup is valid.
Opaque state storage used inside evp_aead_ctx_st for AEAD implementation-specific context and alignment. Contents are not public; treat as an internal buffer.
Context object for an AEAD algorithm configured with a specific key and any message-independent parameters. Holds the selected EVP_AEAD, opaque implementation state, and (optionally) a tag length.
Input vector element used to pass a pointer and length for additional authenticated data or input-only segments. Typically provided as an array up to CRYPTO_IOVEC_MAX elements.
I/O vector element combining input and corresponding output buffers with a common length for vectored AEAD operations. Used in sealv/openv APIs.
Enumeration indicating operation direction for certain TLS/SSL3 AEADs (open/decrypt vs seal/encrypt). Used with EVP_AEAD_CTX_init_with_direction.

Opaque-ish AES key schedule object used by low-level AES routines. Holds expanded round keys (rd_key) for up to AES_MAXNR rounds and the number of rounds (rounds). Constructed by AES_set_encrypt_key or AES_set_decrypt_key before use with the various AES encrypt/decrypt and mode functions.

objects.description: Function type for legacy d2i-style parsers that operate on void*. Used as a generic callback type for parsing functions.

objects.definition: typedef int i2d_of_void(const void *, unsigned char **);
objects.description: Function type for legacy i2d-style serializers that operate on void*. Used as a generic callback type for marshalling functions.
Alias type used to reference ASN1_ITEMs from constant-initialized structures. It is the same as const ASN1_ITEM.
Opaque placeholder type used as the generic C representation for values handled via ASN1_ITEM-based generic functions.

Core string-like container used for many ASN.1 universal types (strings, INTEGER/ENUMERATED, BIT STRING, times, and raw SEQUENCE/SET/OTHER). The type field selects the semantic; data/length hold a type-specific in-memory representation; flags carry BIT STRING padding info, etc.
Typedef alias of ASN1_STRING representing the BIT STRING universal type. See ASN1_STRING for representation details; flags may include ASN1_STRING_FLAG_BITS_LEFT indicating explicit padding count.
Typedef alias of ASN1_STRING representing INTEGER values. Data holds big-endian absolute value; sign encoded via type (V_ASN1_INTEGER or V_ASN1_NEG_INTEGER).
Typedef alias of ASN1_STRING representing ENUMERATED values. As with INTEGER, absolute value in data; sign via type (V_ASN1_ENUMERATED or V_ASN1_NEG_ENUMERATED).
Typedef alias of ASN1_STRING for UTCTime values; data contains DER text like "YYMMDDHHMMSSZ".
Typedef alias of ASN1_STRING for GeneralizedTime values; data contains DER text like "YYYYMMDDHHMMSSZ".
Typedef alias of ASN1_STRING used as a CHOICE of UTCTime or GeneralizedTime for X.509 Time. Type field indicates which is used.
Typedef alias of ASN1_STRING representing BMPString.
Typedef alias of ASN1_STRING representing GeneralString.
Typedef alias of ASN1_STRING representing IA5String.
Typedef alias of ASN1_STRING representing OCTET STRING values.
Typedef alias of ASN1_STRING representing PrintableString.
Typedef alias of ASN1_STRING representing T61String (treated as Latin-1 here).
Typedef alias of ASN1_STRING representing UniversalString.
Typedef alias of ASN1_STRING representing UTF8String.
Typedef alias of ASN1_STRING representing VisibleString (ISO64/IA5 subset).
Opaque marker type representing the ASN.1 NULL value. Non-NULL pointer denotes presence; it is safe but unnecessary to free.
Opaque type representing an ASN.1 OBJECT IDENTIFIER. Encapsulates the DER OID body and optional registry metadata.

Discriminated union capable of holding any single ASN.1 value. The 'type' field is a V_ASN1_* tag selector; 'value' holds the corresponding representation (typically pointers to ASN1_STRING-derived aliases, OBJECTs, or primitive BOOLEAN). Do not build manually; use ASN1_TYPE_set/ASN1_TYPE_set1.
Type alias for a stack of ASN1_TYPE used to represent SEQUENCE OF/SET OF ANY aggregates. The owning variant must be freed with sk_ASN1_TYPE_pop_free + ASN1_TYPE_free.

Template descriptor for a single ASN.1 field within a SEQUENCE/CHOICE or a top-level primitive wrapper. Encodes flags, tag, byte offset in the containing struct, and a reference to the child item (ASN1_ITEM or ASN1_ADB). Used by OpenSSL’s legacy ASN.1 templating system.

ANY DEFINED BY dispatch table descriptor. Describes how to choose a concrete type based on a selector field in a struct. References a table of value→template mappings plus optional default/null templates.
Entry in an ASN1_ADB table mapping a selector integer/NID to the template used to decode/encode that alternative.

Top-level ASN.1 type descriptor used by OpenSSL’s template engine. Describes the item kind (primitive/SEQUENCE/CHOICE/EXTERN/MSTRING), underlying type/mask, member templates and counts, auxiliary function table, and size/selector information.
Deprecated tag and length cache structure. Only a forward declaration is provided here; the actual definition is elsewhere. Purpose is to cache decoded tag/length to speed up parsing.

Auxiliary metadata for an ASN.1 item, including optional reference counting and an informational callback invoked at key encode/decode lifecycle points. Also stores offsets for refcount and cached encoding fields inside user structs.

Opaque I/O abstraction used throughout BoringSSL to represent sources/sinks and filters (memory, file, fd, socket, connect, pairs, etc.). The complete definition is not present in this header; it is intentionally opaque.
Opaque descriptor of a BIO’s method table (function pointers and metadata). Used to implement built-in and custom BIO types. The struct layout is hidden; configure via BIO_meth_* functions.

Resizable memory buffer object used by memory BIOs. The type is referenced here; full definition is in <openssl/buffer.h>. Included here only where APIs accept/return it for memory BIO contents management.
Function type for informational callbacks invoked by some BIO control paths (e.g., via BIO_callback_ctrl). Receives the BIO, a state code, and a return/status value; returns int.
Type-safe OpenSSL stack of BIO pointers generated by the DEFINE_STACK_OF macro. Provides the usual STACK_OF operations for BIO elements.

State structure for the BLAKE2b-256 hash implementation. Holds the chaining value (h), counters (t_low/t_high), the number of bytes used in the current block (block_used), and the working block buffer. In this header, API functions take BLAKE2B_CTX*, which is an alias defined elsewhere for this struct; the struct itself is fully defined here with no internal heap allocations. Lifecycle is caller-managed (stack or embedded); no destroy function is required.

objects.definition:
#if defined(OPENSSL_64_BIT)
typedef uint64_t BN_ULONG;
#define BN_BITS2 64
#define BN_DEC_FMT1 "%" PRIu64
#define BN_HEX_FMT1 "%" PRIx64
#define BN_HEX_FMT2 "%016" PRIx64
#elif defined(OPENSSL_32_BIT)
typedef uint32_t BN_ULONG;
#define BN_BITS2 32
#define BN_DEC_FMT1 "%" PRIu32
#define BN_HEX_FMT1 "%" PRIx32
#define BN_HEX_FMT2 "%08" PRIx32
#else
#error "Must define either OPENSSL_32_BIT or OPENSSL_64_BIT"
#endif
objects.description: Alias for the native machine word used internally by big-number arithmetic. It is 64-bit on OPENSSL_64_BIT builds and 32-bit on OPENSSL_32_BIT builds.
Callback holder used by long-running BN generation/primality routines. Stores a user pointer and a function invoked with progress events.
Enumeration of outcomes from enhanced Miller–Rabin primality testing.

Internal representation of an arbitrary-precision integer (BIGNUM). Holds a little-endian array of BN_ULONG limbs, current width, allocation size, sign flag, and internal flags. Construction/destruction is via BN_new/BN_free and most operations in this header. Width may be non-minimal; callers should treat struct as opaque unless implementing BN internals.
C++ RAII helper that calls BN_CTX_start in the constructor and BN_CTX_end in the destructor for a given BN_CTX, ensuring proper scoped management of temporary BIGNUMs.

Generic growable byte buffer used in BoringSSL/OpenSSL. Holds a pointer to a heap-allocated char array (data), its current logical length, and the allocated capacity (max). Data may be reallocated by reserve/grow operations; callers should not assume data remains stable across such calls. Length can be less than or equal to max.
Typedefs or classes are not defined here for built-in char; this entry is not applicable and should be ignored. No custom typedef introducing a new name for char exists in this header.
No typedef introducing size_t is defined in this header; it is included from standard headers. This is not a custom type and should be ignored.

Opaque-ish structure representing the state of an in-progress EVP cipher operation (encryption or decryption). Holds selected cipher, key/IV, mode buffers, flags, and working state. Construct via allocation/init helpers; do not stack-copy raw memory without initializing. Fields are public in this header for BoringSSL but should be treated as internal unless explicitly documented.

Simple aggregate pairing a cipher implementation with an IV buffer sized to EVP_MAX_IV_LENGTH. Useful for carrying cipher selection and IV together (e.g., in formats that store per-entry cipher parameters).

Opaque context type representing the state for computing a CMAC (Cipher-based Message Authentication Code). This header only references CMAC_CTX and provides functions to allocate, free, copy, initialize, update, and finalize it, but does not define its structure here. Treat it as an opaque handle managed via the provided API.

Represents a single key/value entry from an OpenSSL-style configuration file, including the section name, the key (name), and the associated value. A stack container for this type is also declared via DEFINE_STACK_OF(CONF_VALUE).

Opaque handle representing a parsed configuration database for OpenSSL-style config files. It owns parsed sections and their associated CONF_VALUE entries. The underlying structure is intentionally hidden in this header.

Stack container specialization that holds pointers to CONF_VALUE entries. Defined via DEFINE_STACK_OF(CONF_VALUE) macro; the concrete struct definition is generated elsewhere. Used to represent a section’s list of key/value pairs.

Opaque state object for BoringSSL’s FIPS AES-CTR-based deterministic random bit generator (CTR-DRBG). The struct is forward-declared elsewhere and intentionally opaque in this header; it is allocated and initialized via the provided constructor functions and must be freed with CTR_DRBG_free or cleared with CTR_DRBG_clear. Internal layout and fields are not exposed here.

Enumeration of SPAKE2 participant roles. One party must be Alice and the other Bob to break protocol symmetry. Values are used when creating a SPAKE2_CTX. Note: This is an enum type; only its values are used, not pointers to it.

Opaque SPAKE2 protocol context object used for a single SPAKE2 execution. The concrete struct definition is not provided in this header (it is intentionally opaque). Allocate with SPAKE2_CTX_new and free with SPAKE2_CTX_free. After a successful SPAKE2_process_msg call, the context is complete and must only be freed.

8-byte DES block container. It holds the raw 64-bit block used for DES input/output and for keys (including parity bits). Parity for key material is expected to be odd; use DES_set_odd_parity to set it. Used as plaintext/ciphertext block type and as IV type for CBC/CFB modes.

DES key schedule structure containing the 16 round subkeys (each round represented as two 32-bit words). Must be initialized via DES_set_key (or the deprecated DES_set_key_unchecked) before encryption/decryption routines. Used with both single DES and 3DES APIs.

Opaque Diffie-Hellman key/group handle used by BoringSSL. This header only declares functions operating on DH; the struct definition is not present here, implying DH is an opaque type defined elsewhere. Manage via DH_new/DH_free and reference counting via DH_up_ref. Thread-safe for non-mutating operations.
Arbitrary-precision integer type used for primes, generators, and keys (p, q, g, public/private keys) within DH operations. Not defined in this header.
Callback descriptor used by BN/DH parameter generation routines to report progress. Not defined in this header.
ByteString reader for parsing DER and other encodings; used by DH_parse_parameters. Not defined in this header.
ByteString builder for constructing DER and other encodings; used by DH_marshal_parameters. Not defined in this header.
Message-digest method descriptor used to select hash in DH_compute_key_hashed. Not defined in this header.
Opaque digest algorithm descriptor type returned by EVP_md* and related lookup functions. Definition is not present in this header; it is an external/opaque type in BoringSSL.

Digest operation context holding the in-progress state for a specific hashing operation. The struct is defined here under the name env_md_ctx_st with a typedef-style trailing alias comment to EVP_MD_CTX. It embeds an internal buffer large enough to store any supported digest state, a pointer to the selected EVP_MD, and optional PKEY-related context pointers.
Forward-declared vtable type for operations on the auxiliary pctx stored in EVP_MD_CTX. Only an incomplete declaration is provided here; methods and layout are hidden.

Opaque handle to a DSA key or parameter object. Represents DSA parameters (p, q, g) and optionally a public/private key pair. The concrete struct is not defined in this header (opaque type). Lifetime managed by reference counting via DSA_new/DSA_free/DSA_up_ref. Thread-safe for concurrent reads; avoid concurrent mutation.

Represents a DSA signature as two BIGNUM components r and s. Construct with DSA_SIG_new or by parsing/ASN.1 decode; free with DSA_SIG_free. Components can be accessed via DSA_SIG_get0 and set via DSA_SIG_set0 (takes ownership).

Arbitrary-precision integer used for DSA components (p, q, g, public key, private key, r, s). Not defined in this header; referenced only. Excluded per instructions if strictly requiring explicit definition here, but included here only because it appears as a field of DSA_SIG_st. Concrete definition is elsewhere.
Enumeration of X9.62 point encoding formats used when serializing EC points. Values indicate compressed, uncompressed, or hybrid encodings.
Opaque/incomplete type representing an EC method descriptor. Only forward-declared here; actual structure layout is hidden. Used with query helpers such as EC_METHOD_get_field_type.
Simple POD describing a supported named elliptic curve: its NID and a human-readable comment/name string. Typically populated by EC_get_builtin_curves.

Dispatch table for an ECDSA implementation. Contains function pointers for init/finish and signing, an application data pointer, shared method metadata in "common", and a flags field (e.g., ECDSA_FLAG_OPAQUE). Instances are typically provided by ENGINEs or internal method providers. Note: struct openssl_method_common_st and EC_KEY are referenced types defined elsewhere. Construction is usually via provider/engine code; there is no constructor in this header.
Opaque elliptic-curve point type referenced from this header. It is declared/defined in <openssl/ec_key.h>, not in this header. Included here only as a parameter type for ECDH APIs.
Opaque elliptic-curve key pair/parameters type referenced from this header. It is declared/defined in <openssl/ec_key.h>, not in this header. Included here only as a parameter type for ECDH APIs.
ECDSA signature container holding the two BIGNUM components r and s. Represents an ECDSA-Sig-Value at the low level and is used by APIs that operate on signatures without ASN.1/byte formatting.

Opaque engine object representing a collection of algorithm method tables. Not defined in this header; only referenced for API functions and deleter. Lifetime is managed manually; not reference-counted as a whole (methods it references are).
Opaque method table type for RSA operations. Only referenced here for getting/setting on an ENGINE. Actual structure is defined elsewhere.
Opaque method table type for ECDSA operations. Only referenced here for getting/setting on an ENGINE. Actual structure is defined elsewhere.

Common header that must be the first member of all method structures. Contains a placeholder reference counter and a flag indicating whether the method is static. The reference count fields are currently not used; METHOD_ref/unref are no-ops.

objects.definition:
typedef int (*ERR_print_errors_callback_t)(const char *str, size_t len,
                                           void *ctx);
objects.description: Function pointer type for callbacks used by ERR_print_errors_cb. The callback receives a human-readable string describing an error queue entry and an opaque context pointer, and returns 1 to continue iteration or 0 to stop.
Opaque handle type representing a public/private key object used across EVP APIs. Fully defined elsewhere; only referenced here.
Opaque context object for configuring and executing EVP_PKEY operations (sign/verify/encrypt/decrypt/derive/keygen/paramgen). Fully defined elsewhere; only referenced here.
Opaque descriptor type for specifying supported key algorithms to parsing/creation functions. Only returned as const pointers by factory functions in this header. Fully defined elsewhere.
Opaque digest operation context used by high-level DigestSign/DigestVerify and legacy Sign/Verify flows. Fully defined elsewhere; only referenced here.
Opaque message-digest algorithm descriptor used to select hash functions in various APIs. Fully defined elsewhere; only referenced here.
Opaque OpenSSL ENGINE handle used for legacy engine selection; passed through in several APIs. Fully defined elsewhere.
Opaque RSA key object type referenced for getting/setting concrete RSA keys from EVP_PKEY. Fully defined elsewhere.
Opaque DSA key object type referenced for getting/setting concrete DSA keys from EVP_PKEY. Fully defined elsewhere.
Opaque EC key object type referenced for getting/setting concrete EC keys from EVP_PKEY. Fully defined elsewhere.
Opaque Diffie-Hellman key object type referenced for getting/setting concrete DH keys from EVP_PKEY. Fully defined elsewhere.
Opaque I/O abstraction used for printing functions. Fully defined elsewhere.
Opaque ASN.1 print context used when printing keys/params. Fully defined elsewhere.
Opaque/utility input buffer parser (CBB/CBS pair) used by parsing functions. Fully defined elsewhere.
Opaque/utility output buffer builder used by marshaling functions. Fully defined elsewhere.
Arbitrary-precision integer type used here for RSA public exponent during keygen. Fully defined elsewhere.

Opaque-ish HMAC context structure holding the selected hash (EVP_MD) and three digest contexts (main, inner, outer) used to compute HMAC incrementally. Defined here with its concrete layout for C; commonly referenced via the alias name HMAC_CTX. Lifetime is stack-allocable via HMAC_CTX_init/cleanup or heap-allocable via HMAC_CTX_new/free.

Opaque handle to an HPKE Key Encapsulation Mechanism (KEM) algorithm. Instances are obtained via factory functions in this header and queried for identifiers and key/enc sizes. The concrete structure is not defined here.
Opaque handle to an HPKE Key Derivation Function (KDF) algorithm. Instances are obtained via factory functions and queried for identifiers and (if HKDF-based) the underlying EVP_MD.
Opaque handle to an HPKE AEAD algorithm. Instances are obtained via factory functions and queried for identifiers and mapped to EVP_AEAD.

HPKE recipient key container holding the chosen KEM and the encoded private/public key material. Fields are private-to-library; callers must not access or modify them directly. Manage with the provided init/generate/copy/move/cleanup APIs.

HPKE encryption context storing algorithm choices, AEAD state, exporter secret, sequence number, and role flag. Fields are private-to-library; callers must not access or modify them directly. Initialize via setup_sender/recipient/auth_* and use for seal/open/export until cleanup.
Opaque container for an HRSS private key. The internal bytes are not public API; treat as an opaque fixed-size struct holding implementation-specific state/secret material.
Opaque container for an HRSS public key. The layout is intentionally hidden and should only be created via the provided API functions or by parsing/marshalling.

MD4 context/state structure holding the 128-bit chaining value (h), bit count split into low/high 32-bit words (Nl, Nh), the partial input block buffer (data), and the number of buffered bytes (num). Used with the MD4_Init/Update/Final/Transform routines to compute MD4 digests.

MD5 context/state structure holding the running hash state (h), bit count split into low/high 32-bit words (Nl, Nh), the partial input block buffer (data), and the number of bytes currently buffered (num). This structure is used by the MD5_Init/Update/Final/Transform APIs to compute MD5 digests. MD5_CTX is an alias declared in included headers (not defined here) and typically typedefs to this struct.
Opaque container for an ML-DSA-65 private key. The internal layout is unstable and must not be serialized or exposed outside the process. Use the provided API to create, derive, or use keys.
Opaque container for an ML-DSA-65 public key. The internal format is unstable; use marshal/parse helpers for serialization.
Opaque pre-hash state for ML-DSA-65 incremental hashing used to produce a message representative for signing/verification.
Opaque container for an ML-DSA-87 private key. Not stable for serialization; keep in-process only.
Opaque container for an ML-DSA-87 public key. Use marshal/parse helpers for external representation.
Opaque pre-hash state for ML-DSA-87 incremental hashing to compute message representatives.
Opaque container for an ML-DSA-44 private key. Internal layout is unstable; do not serialize directly.
Opaque container for an ML-DSA-44 public key. Use provided marshal/parse functions for wire format.
Opaque pre-hash state for ML-DSA-44 incremental hashing to derive message representatives.

Opaque container for an ML-KEM-768 public key material. The internal layout is intentionally unstable and should not be serialized or exposed outside the process. Use provided API to derive, serialize, parse, and consume this key.

Opaque container for an ML-KEM-768 private key material. Contents are process-internal and unstable; do not serialize directly. Use API functions to generate or derive from seed and to perform decapsulation or derive the public key.
Opaque container for an ML-KEM-1024 public key material. The internal format is unstable and must remain in-process. Use the provided API to construct, serialize, parse, and use this key.

Opaque container for an ML-KEM-1024 private key material. Contents are unstable and not for external serialization. Construct via the API; use for decapsulation or to derive the corresponding public key.

Deprecated OpenSSL structure representing a registered primitive name entry in the global object name table. Each entry records a type (e.g., digest method or cipher method), whether the entry is an alias, the textual name, and an associated data pointer/string. Used only by deprecated OBJ_NAME_do_all/_sorted traversal APIs; table contents and semantics are ill-specified.

objects.definition: typedef int pem_password_cb(char *buf, int size, int rwflag, void *userdata);
objects.description: Callback function type used to obtain a password for encrypting/decrypting PEM data. Implementations should write the password (as a C string or raw bytes expected by the caller) into buf, not exceeding size, and return the length written or -1 on error. The userdata pointer is passed through by callers.

Deprecated compatibility struct representing the SignedData payload of a PKCS#7 object. It holds unordered stacks of certificates and CRLs. Construction/destruction is managed indirectly via PKCS7 parsing/serialization helpers in this header; no dedicated constructor/destructor is provided here.

Deprecated compatibility struct intended to represent a signed-and-enveloped PKCS#7 payload, mirroring OpenSSL's API. It contains stacks of certificates and CRLs. No direct constructors or manipulators are defined here.
Opaque/deprecated placeholder type for an enveloped-data PKCS#7 content. It is intentionally incomplete here and only referenced via PKCS7's union. No operations are defined in this header.
Opaque/deprecated placeholder type for a digest-data PKCS#7 content. Only referenced via PKCS7's union. No operations are defined in this header.
Opaque/deprecated placeholder type for an encrypted-data PKCS#7 content. Only referenced via PKCS7's union. No operations are defined in this header.
Opaque/deprecated placeholder for signer-info structures (compatibility with OpenSSL). Not constructed or manipulated by APIs in this header.

Compatibility PKCS#7 ContentInfo wrapper. Holds raw BER bytes and decoded, immutable content selector fields. Only SignedData is meaningfully supported by the functions in this header; other content types are stubs. Memory must be released with PKCS7_free. Constructed by d2i_PKCS7, d2i_PKCS7_bio, or PKCS7_sign (restricted modes).

Opaque PKCS#12 container type used by this API. It is referenced and managed via PKCS12_free, constructed by PKCS12_create and the various d2i_... functions. The actual struct definition is not present in this header and is treated as an opaque type.

Opaque type representing a PKCS#8 PrivateKeyInfo. The concrete layout is not defined in this header. Instances are produced by PKCS8_decrypt and consumed by PKCS8_encrypt. Lifetime can be managed with PKCS8_PRIV_KEY_INFO_free (deleter macro provided in C++ section).
Opaque type representing the ASN.1 structure for a signature container (used here as the container for EncryptedPrivateKeyInfo output from PKCS8_encrypt). The definition is not in this header.

Opaque key container for public/private keys. Not defined here. Returned by PKCS8_parse_encrypted_private_key and PKCS12_get_key_and_certs, and accepted by PKCS8_marshal_encrypted_private_key and PKCS12_create.

OpenSSL/BoringSSL stack type holding X509 pointers. Used as output collection for certificates in PKCS12_get_key_and_certs and PKCS12_parse. The underlying macro/type is defined elsewhere; no definition here.
BoringSSL CBB (C Byte Builder) opaque output buffer type. Used as an output serializer in PKCS8_marshal_encrypted_private_key. Not defined in this header.
BoringSSL CBS (C Byte String) parsing cursor type. Used as input to PKCS8_parse_encrypted_private_key and PKCS12_get_key_and_certs. Not defined in this header.
Opaque cipher implementation descriptor. Used to select PBES2 encryption in PKCS8_encrypt and PKCS8_marshal_encrypted_private_key. Not defined here.
I/O abstraction type used by d2i_PKCS12_bio and i2d_PKCS12_bio. Not defined here.
C stdio FILE handle used by d2i_PKCS12_fp and i2d_PKCS12_fp.

Opaque Poly1305 MAC computation state stored as a 512-byte array. It is initialized with a one-time 32-byte key and then fed data via update before finalizing to produce a 16-byte tag. Although the underlying type is a fixed-size byte array, callers should treat it as an opaque state blob for the CRYPTO_poly1305_* API.

Opaque reference-counted binary blob used to hold immutable data. The concrete struct definition is not present in this header (it is intentionally opaque). Lifetime is managed via CRYPTO_BUFFER_free and CRYPTO_BUFFER_up_ref. Instances can be pooled/interned via CRYPTO_BUFFER_POOL to deduplicate identical blobs.

Opaque intern table (pool) for CRYPTO_BUFFERs. Ensures only one instance of a given blob is kept and shared by reference. The struct definition is not present in this header (it is intentionally opaque). Must be empty when freed.

Structure of function pointers describing a RAND_METHOD (legacy OpenSSL-style RNG vtable). In BoringSSL it is a dummy/compatibility type used only as the return type of RAND_SSLeay/RAND_OpenSSL and for RAND_METHOD pointers. The callbacks, if populated, would define seeding, byte generation, cleanup, additional seeding, pseudo-random generation, and status checks. In BoringSSL these methods are not used for actual RNG selection; treat as a compatibility placeholder.

State structure for the RC4 stream cipher, holding the permutation (data) and indices (x, y). The trailing comment indicates this struct is typedef-aliased to RC4_KEY by included headers (e.g., via base headers); in this file the full struct definition is present. Used with RC4_set_key to initialize and RC4 to encrypt/decrypt.

RIPEMD-160 message-digest running context/state. Holds the 160-bit hash state (h[5]), bit counters (Nl, Nh), the partial data block buffer, and the number of buffered bytes. Commonly typedef’d as RIPEMD160_CTX in OpenSSL headers; this header references RIPEMD160_CTX but defines the struct here.

Typedef alias for the RIPEMD-160 context structure defined in this header as struct RIPEMD160state_st. The actual typedef declaration is not present in this header, but the alias name is referenced by the function prototypes. Treat as an alias of the context struct for API usage.

Opaque RSA key object representing public and/or private RSA key material. The full struct is not defined in this header; use the provided constructor/destructor and accessors to manage it. Thread-safe for concurrent non-mutating operations; mutating functions require exclusive access.

Opaque type name referenced for RSA PSS parameter retrieval. Only forward-declared via return type of RSA_get0_pss_params; the actual structure is not defined here. In BoringSSL, RSA_get0_pss_params always returns NULL unless special PSS encodings are enabled.

Method table (vtable) for RSA implementations, typically used by ENGINEs or alternative backends to override RSA operations such as init/finish, signing, raw signing, decryption, and the core private exponentiation (private_transform). Contains a common header, app-specific data pointer, function pointers, and flags.
No custom data types are defined in this header. The file is intentionally empty and retained for compatibility with older code that expected this header to exist.

Opaque-ish SHA-1 context structure holding the internal hash state (five 32-bit words), bit count split into low/high 32-bit words (Nl, Nh), a 64-byte message block buffer, and the number of bytes used in the buffer. Named as SHA_CTX via the trailing comment alias style used by BoringSSL/OpenSSL. Used with SHA1_Init/Update/Final and SHA1_Transform.
State object for SHA-224 and SHA-256 hash computations. Holds the internal chaining values, bit counters, data buffer, and bookkeeping fields. Used with SHA224_* and SHA256_* APIs.
State object for SHA-384, SHA-512, and SHA-512/256 hash computations. Maintains the internal state words, processed byte counters (split high/low), partial block buffer, and bookkeeping fields.

Alias for an unsigned 8-bit integer type, used throughout the API for keys, signatures, and message buffers. Note: This type is typically defined in <stdint.h> and is only referenced here, not defined by this header.

Unsigned integral type for object sizes and lengths. It is referenced as parameter types for lengths. Note: This type is defined by the C standard and is only referenced here, not defined by this header.
Enumeration of outcomes for custom private-key operations used by SSL_PRIVATE_KEY_METHOD hooks.
Vtable of callbacks to offload private key operations (sign, raw RSA decrypt, and async completion) for an SSL connection.
Enumeration of results from decrypting a session ticket via an SSL_TICKET_AEAD_METHOD.
Vtable defining custom AEAD for encrypting/decrypting TLS session tickets.
TLS 1.3/QUIC encryption levels used with QUIC integration.
Vtable for QUIC transport hooks enabling a QUIC stack to drive TLS handshake keys and IO.

objects.definition:
enum ssl_early_data_reason_t BORINGSSL_ENUM_INT {
  ssl_early_data_unknown = 0,
  ssl_early_data_disabled = 1,
  ssl_early_data_accepted = 2,
  ssl_early_data_protocol_version = 3,
  ssl_early_data_peer_declined = 4,
  ssl_early_data_no_session_offered = 5,
  ssl_early_data_session_not_resumed = 6,
  ssl_early_data_unsupported_for_session = 7,
  ssl_early_data_hello_retry_request = 8,
  ssl_early_data_alpn_mismatch = 9,
  ssl_early_data_channel_id = 10,
  ssl_early_data_ticket_age_skew = 12,
  ssl_early_data_quic_parameter_mismatch = 13,
  ssl_early_data_alps_mismatch = 14,
  ssl_early_data_reason_max_value = ssl_early_data_alps_mismatch,
};
objects.description: Enumeration describing why 0-RTT (early data) was accepted or rejected.
DTLS-SRTP protection profile descriptor containing name and numeric ID.
Immutable parsed view of a ClientHello used in early server callbacks for certificate selection and DoS protection.
Return codes for the select-certificate callback indicating success, retry, error, or disabling ECH after decrypting ClientHelloInner.
Result codes for custom certificate verification callbacks.
Client behavior modes for handling peer-initiated renegotiation.
High-level policy selector to constrain TLS config to FIPS/WPA3/CNSA profiles.
Deprecated compression method descriptor for OpenSSL compatibility.
Opaque configuration context type referenced for compatibility. Only forward-declared here; no definition provided.
Deprecated alias for an OpenSSL compression method type. Here it is an incomplete void typedef for compatibility.

objects.definition:
typedef struct stack_st OPENSSL_STACK;

typedef OPENSSL_STACK _STACK;
objects.description: Opaque stack type for BoringSSL. Represents a resizable array of pointers. Intended to be used via typed wrappers generated by DEFINE_STACK_OF/DEFINE_CONST_STACK_OF macros. The concrete struct definition is not exposed in this header.
Type-erased element-freeing callback used by raw OPENSSL_sk_* functions. Actual concrete type at call sites is void (*)(T *) for some T.
Type-erased element-copying callback used by raw OPENSSL_sk_* functions. Actual concrete type is T *(*)(const T *).
Type-erased comparison function for elements in stacks. Semantics: returns <0, 0, >0 like qsort/bsearch, but receives pointers to element pointers.
Type-erased predicate used by OPENSSL_sk_delete_if. Returns 1 to delete the element, 0 to keep.
Helper function type that adapts a type-erased free function to the concrete element type; used internally by raw stack routines.
Helper function type that adapts a type-erased copy function to the concrete element type; used internally by raw stack routines.

objects.definition: typedef int (*OPENSSL_sk_call_cmp_func)(OPENSSL_sk_cmp_func, const void *, const void *);
objects.description: Helper function type that adapts a type-erased comparison function to the concrete element type; used internally by raw stack routines.
Helper function type that adapts a type-erased delete-if predicate to the concrete element type; used internally by raw stack routines.
Alias type for a NUL-terminated C string pointer used in stacks. When used with DEFINE_NAMED_STACK_OF(OPENSSL_STRING, char), forms typed stack APIs sk_OPENSSL_STRING_*.

No structs, enums, typedefs, or classes are defined in this header. It contains only preprocessor macros (#define) for TLS alert codes, extension types, cipher suite IDs, and related constants. Therefore, there are no custom data types to extract.

Opaque method table describing a specific Trust Token protocol variant (e.g., PMB tokens or VOPRF on P-384). Only referenced here; the concrete struct definition is not present in this header and is expected to be defined internally in the library.
Represents a single-use Trust Token value. For clients, this includes the token and its signature; for issuers, this is the token itself. The structure owns a byte buffer (data,len).
OpenSSL STACK_OF specialization for TRUST_TOKEN objects, representing a variable-length list of TRUST_TOKEN pointers with stack.h semantics.
Opaque handle for the client half of the Trust Token protocol. A TRUST_TOKEN_CLIENT instance performs a single protocol operation and is configured with public keys and optional SRR verification key.
Opaque handle for the issuer half of the Trust Token protocol. It can be reused across operations and configured with private keys, SRR signing key, and metadata key.
Alias for a stack (SEQUENCE OF) of GENERAL_NAME entries used in various X.509 extensions.
Alias for a stack of X509_EXTENSION used when handling SEQUENCE OF Extension values.
Represents the BasicConstraints extension indicating CA capability and optional path length constraint.
ExtKeyUsageSyntax: a stack of ASN1_OBJECT OIDs representing allowed extended key usages.
Represents an OtherName choice inside GENERAL_NAME with arbitrary OID and ASN.1 value.
Represents the EDI Party Name choice in GENERAL_NAME.
CHOICE wrapper for various name forms used in SAN and related extensions. Keep type and union consistent.
Represents the AuthorityKeyIdentifier extension fields (keyid, optional issuer and serial).
Represents a GeneralSubtree used within name constraints (base with optional min/max).
Represents the NameConstraints extension with permitted and excluded subtree lists.
Represents an AccessDescription (method OID and location GeneralName) used in AIA/SIA.
SEQUENCE OF AccessDescription for AuthorityInfoAccessSyntax.
Represents DistributionPointName choice (fullName or relativeName) within CRL distribution points.
Represents a CRL DistributionPoint with optional reasons and CRL issuer.
SEQUENCE OF DistributionPoint for the CRLDistributionPoints extension.
Represents the IssuingDistributionPoint CRL extension controlling scope of a CRL.
Part of policy qualifier UserNotice; names an organization and notice numbers.
UserNotice policy qualifier containing optional reference and explicit text.
Represents a PolicyQualifierInfo with qualifier determined by pqualid (CPS URI, UserNotice, or other).
Represents PolicyInformation element (policy OID with optional qualifiers).
SEQUENCE OF PolicyInformation representing the CertificatePolicies extension.
Represents one mapping pair in the PolicyMappings extension.
SEQUENCE OF POLICY_MAPPING for PolicyMappings extension.
Represents PolicyConstraints extension fields.
Represents a SignedPublicKeyAndChallenge (legacy SPKAC) container with signed spkac and signature info.
Represents the PublicKeyAndChallenge part of SPKAC (misnamed historically).
Represents RSASSA-PSS-params structure per RFC 4055 (hash, MGF, salt length, trailer, cached mask hash).
Internal container used in X509_INFO to carry a decrypted private key handle.
Aggregate holder used by PEM loader to bundle a cert, CRL, or private key with optional encryption metadata.
Deprecated descriptor of a custom X.509 extension, tying an OID to ASN.1 item and helper callbacks.
Context object supplying surrounding certificate/CRL/request and config to deprecated config-based extension builders.
AlgorithmIdentifier pair (OID plus optional parameter) used across X.509 structures.

Exported POD-like result container for OCSP verification, with an equality operator. Holds a ResponseStatus indicating response availability/quality and, when status is PROVIDED, the OCSPRevocationStatus for the certificate.

functions.name: CRYPTO_is_confidential_build
functions.description: Returns 1 if the linked BoringSSL was built with BORINGSSL_CONFIDENTIAL, otherwise 0. Use to detect internal/confidential builds at runtime.

functions.name: CRYPTO_has_asm
functions.description: Returns 1 unless BoringSSL was built with OPENSSL_NO_ASM, in which case returns 0. Allows callers to detect whether assembly optimizations are available.

functions.name: BORINGSSL_self_test
functions.description: Triggers most FIPS KAT-based self tests (skips long-running SLH-DSA tests). Returns 1 on success, 0 on error. Intended for validating key cryptographic functionality.

functions.name: BORINGSSL_self_test_all
functions.description: Triggers all FIPS KAT-based self tests (including long-running ones). Returns 1 on success, 0 on error. This is the FIPS 140 'self-test' entry point and is very time-consuming.

functions.name: BORINGSSL_integrity_test
functions.description: Runs the module integrity test by comparing code/data against a build-time injected hash. Returns 1 on success, 0 on mismatch. Only available when built in FIPS mode without ASAN.
requirements: Only available in FIPS builds without ASAN; calling or linking may fail if not built accordingly.

functions.name: CRYPTO_pre_sandbox_init
functions.description: Initializes the crypto library and pre-acquires resources needed for sandboxed environments. Safe to call multiple times and concurrently across threads.
requirements: May be called multiple times and concurrently; no additional ordering requirements stated.

functions.name: CRYPTO_set_fuzzer_mode
functions.description: In non-production fuzzing builds, toggles 'fuzzer mode', which disables various signature checks and disables some encryption in TLS to aid fuzzing BoringSSL itself. No effect or availability in production builds.
requirements: Only available when compiled with FUZZING_BUILD_MODE_UNSAFE_FOR_PRODUCTION; do not use in production.
Passing a nonzero enabled turns fuzzer mode on; zero turns it off (behavior inferred from parameter name and description).

functions.name: FIPS_mode
functions.description: Returns 1 if BoringSSL was built with BORINGSSL_FIPS, otherwise 0. Allows runtime detection of a FIPS build.

functions.name: FIPS_read_counter
functions.description: Returns the usage counter for the specified FIPS-designated API/algorithm. Always returns 0 unless built with BORINGSSL_FIPS_COUNTERS.
requirements: counter must be a valid value of enum fips_counter_t.

functions.name: OpenSSL_version
functions.description: Compatibility function. Returns "BoringSSL" if which == OPENSSL_VERSION and placeholder strings otherwise.
requirements: which should be one of OPENSSL_VERSION, OPENSSL_CFLAGS, OPENSSL_BUILT_ON, OPENSSL_PLATFORM, or OPENSSL_DIR.

functions.name: SSLeay_version
functions.description: Compatibility function that calls OpenSSL_version(which).
requirements: which should be one of OPENSSL_VERSION, OPENSSL_CFLAGS, OPENSSL_BUILT_ON, OPENSSL_PLATFORM, or OPENSSL_DIR.

functions.name: SSLeay
functions.description: Compatibility function that returns OPENSSL_VERSION_NUMBER from base.h.

functions.name: OpenSSL_version_num
functions.description: Compatibility function that returns OPENSSL_VERSION_NUMBER from base.h.

functions.name: CRYPTO_malloc_init
functions.description: Deprecated/compatibility initializer that returns 1 and performs no action.

functions.name: OPENSSL_malloc_init
functions.description: Deprecated/compatibility initializer that returns 1 and performs no action.

functions.name: ENGINE_load_builtin_engines
functions.description: Compatibility stub that does nothing.

functions.name: ENGINE_register_all_complete
functions.description: Compatibility stub that returns 1 and does nothing.

functions.name: ENGINE_cleanup
functions.description: Compatibility stub that does nothing.

functions.name: OPENSSL_load_builtin_modules
functions.description: Compatibility stub that does nothing.

functions.name: OPENSSL_init_crypto
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int OPENSSL_init_crypto(uint64_t opts, const OPENSSL_INIT_SETTINGS *settings);
functions.description: Compatibility initializer. In BoringSSL the OPENSSL_INIT_* options do nothing; this function returns 1.
requirements: opts may include OPENSSL_INIT_* flags, which are defined as 0 in BoringSSL (inputs are effectively ignored).
settings is accepted but not used; no specific requirements stated (treat as optional/ignored).

functions.name: OPENSSL_cleanup
functions.description: Compatibility stub that does nothing.

functions.name: FIPS_mode_set
functions.description: Returns 1 if 'on' matches whether BoringSSL was built with BORINGSSL_FIPS, otherwise 0. Used to check/configure FIPS mode compatibility.
requirements: Pass on=1 to match FIPS builds and on=0 to match non-FIPS builds; otherwise the function returns 0.

functions.name: FIPS_module_name
functions.description: Returns the name of the FIPS module.

functions.name: FIPS_module_hash
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the 32-byte hash of the FIPS module.
requirements: Treat the returned pointer as read-only; do not modify the data.

functions.name: FIPS_version
functions.description: Returns the FIPS module version as a decimal yyyymmdd integer, or 0 if not exactly at a verified version.

functions.name: FIPS_query_algorithm_status
functions.description: Returns 1 if the named algorithm is FIPS validated in the current BoringSSL, otherwise 0.
requirements: algorithm must be a valid null-terminated C string pointer.

functions.name: CRYPTO_library_init
functions.description: Compatibility stub that does nothing. Historically required to initialize the library; no longer necessary.

functions.name: OPENSSL_malloc
functions.description: Allocates size bytes using BoringSSL’s allocator, which tracks allocation lengths and zeroes memory on free. Returned memory must be freed with OPENSSL_free.
requirements: size may be zero; behavior follows malloc(3)-like semantics (returned pointer may be NULL on allocation failure).
Returned pointer must be freed with OPENSSL_free, not free().
On failure, pushes ERR_R_MALLOC_FAILURE on the OpenSSL error stack.

functions.name: OPENSSL_zalloc
functions.description: Allocates size bytes like OPENSSL_malloc, but initializes the returned memory to zero. Must be freed with OPENSSL_free.
requirements: Returned pointer must be freed with OPENSSL_free.
On allocation failure, returns NULL (error handling per OPENSSL_malloc semantics).

functions.name: OPENSSL_calloc
functions.description: Allocates an array of num elements of size bytes using the BoringSSL allocator (like calloc), zero-initialized. Must be freed with OPENSSL_free. On overflow, records ERR_R_OVERFLOW.
requirements: num * size must not overflow size_t; on overflow, pushes ERR_R_OVERFLOW and returns NULL.
Returned pointer must be freed with OPENSSL_free.
Returns NULL on allocation failure.

functions.name: OPENSSL_realloc
functions.description: Allocates a new buffer of new_size bytes, copies the contents of ptr, then wipes and frees the original buffer. Unlike realloc, a new buffer is always allocated. New memory must be freed with OPENSSL_free.
requirements: ptr must be a pointer previously obtained from a BoringSSL allocation function compatible with OPENSSL_free (e.g., OPENSSL_malloc/OPENSSL_zalloc/OPENSSL_calloc/OPENSSL_memdup/OPENSSL_strdup/OPENSSL_strndup).
After successful return, the old ptr is freed and must not be used.
Returned pointer must be freed with OPENSSL_free.
Returns NULL on allocation failure (original ptr is still wiped and freed per description).

functions.name: OPENSSL_free
functions.description: Securely frees memory allocated by BoringSSL allocation functions. It zeroes the memory and frees internal bookkeeping. Does nothing if ptr is NULL.
requirements: ptr must have been obtained from a BoringSSL allocation function that requires OPENSSL_free (e.g., OPENSSL_malloc/OPENSSL_zalloc/OPENSSL_calloc/OPENSSL_memdup/OPENSSL_strndup/OPENSSL_strdup, etc.).
Safe to pass NULL (no-op).

functions.name: OPENSSL_cleanse
functions.description: Overwrites len bytes at ptr with zeroes (similar in intent to C11 memset_s).
requirements: ptr must point to a buffer of at least len bytes.
Behavior is undefined if ptr is NULL and len > 0.

functions.name: CRYPTO_memcmp
functions.signature: int CRYPTO_memcmp(const void *a, const void *b, size_t len);
functions.description: Constant-time memory comparison that returns 0 iff the first len bytes of a and b are equal. Takes time dependent on len but independent of contents. Return value for inequality is unspecified except that it is non-zero (cannot be used for ordering).
requirements: a and b must each point to at least len bytes (non-overlapping or overlapping is acceptable for reading).
len may be zero.

functions.name: OPENSSL_hash32
functions.description: Computes a 32-bit FNV-1a hash over len bytes at ptr.
requirements: ptr must point to at least len bytes if len > 0.
Safe for any binary data; no alignment requirements stated.

functions.name: OPENSSL_strhash
functions.description: Computes a 32-bit hash of the NUL-terminated string s by applying OPENSSL_hash32 to it.
requirements: s must be a valid NUL-terminated C string.

functions.name: OPENSSL_strdup
functions.description: Duplicates the NUL-terminated string s (like strdup(3)). Returned memory must be freed with OPENSSL_free.
requirements: s must be a valid NUL-terminated C string.
Returned pointer must be freed with OPENSSL_free.
Returns NULL on allocation failure.

functions.name: OPENSSL_strnlen
functions.description: Returns the length of s, up to a maximum of len, like strnlen(3).
requirements: s must be a valid pointer to a character array of at least min(actual length, len) bytes.
Does not read beyond len bytes.

functions.name: OPENSSL_isalpha
functions.description: ASCII-only, locale-independent isalpha(3). Recognizes only 'A'-'Z' and 'a'-'z'.
requirements: c is an int value; only ASCII classification is performed. Values outside ASCII are returned as non-alphabetic.

functions.name: OPENSSL_isdigit
functions.description: ASCII-only, locale-independent isdigit(3). Recognizes only '0'-'9'.
requirements: c is an int value; only ASCII classification is performed.

functions.name: OPENSSL_isxdigit
functions.description: ASCII-only, locale-independent isxdigit(3). Recognizes '0'-'9', 'a'-'f', 'A'-'F'.
requirements: c is an int value; only ASCII classification is performed.

functions.name: OPENSSL_fromxdigit
functions.description: If c is an ASCII hexadecimal digit (per OPENSSL_isxdigit), writes its numeric value to *out and returns 1; otherwise returns 0 without writing.
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to at least one byte of writable memory.
c is an int value; only ASCII hex digits are recognized.

functions.name: OPENSSL_isalnum
functions.description: ASCII-only, locale-independent isalnum(3). Recognizes what OPENSSL_isalpha and OPENSSL_isdigit recognize.
requirements: c is an int value; only ASCII classification is performed.

functions.name: OPENSSL_tolower
functions.description: ASCII-only, locale-independent tolower(3). Lowercases ASCII letters; returns other values unchanged.
requirements: c is an int value; only ASCII mapping is performed.

functions.name: OPENSSL_isspace
functions.description: ASCII-only, locale-independent isspace(3). Recognizes '\t', '\n', '\v', '\f', '\r', and ' '.
requirements: c is an int value; only ASCII classification is performed.

functions.name: OPENSSL_strcasecmp
functions.description: ASCII-only, locale-independent strcasecmp(3); compares two NUL-terminated strings case-insensitively in ASCII.
requirements: a and b must be valid NUL-terminated strings.

functions.name: OPENSSL_strncasecmp
functions.signature: int OPENSSL_strncasecmp(const char *a, const char *b, size_t n);
functions.description: ASCII-only, locale-independent strncasecmp(3); compares up to n bytes of two strings case-insensitively in ASCII.
requirements: a and b must point to valid character arrays of at least min(actual length, n) bytes.
Comparison stops at NUL or after n bytes.

functions.name: BIO_snprintf
functions.signature: int BIO_snprintf(char *buf, size_t n, const char *format, ...);
functions.description: Like snprintf(3): formats output into buf with size n, always NUL-terminating if n > 0. Returns the number of characters that would have been written, excluding the NUL terminator.
requirements: buf must point to a buffer of at least n bytes unless n==0.
format must be a valid printf-style format string; variadic arguments must match the format.
Return value should be checked for truncation (>= n indicates truncation).

functions.name: BIO_vsnprintf
functions.signature: int BIO_vsnprintf(char *buf, size_t n, const char *format, va_list args);
functions.description: Like vsnprintf(3): formats output into buf with size n using a va_list. Returns the number of characters that would have been written, excluding the NUL terminator.
requirements: buf must point to a buffer of at least n bytes unless n==0.
format must be a valid printf-style format string.
args must be a valid, initialized va_list matching format.

functions.name: OPENSSL_vasprintf
functions.signature: int OPENSSL_vasprintf(char **str, const char *format, va_list args);
functions.description: Like vasprintf(3): allocates a new string holding the formatted output and stores it in *str. Memory must be freed with OPENSSL_free. Returns the number of characters printed (excluding NUL) on success, or -1 on failure.
requirements: str must be non-NULL and point to a char* variable to receive the allocation.
On success, *str must be freed with OPENSSL_free.
format must be a valid printf-style format string; args must be a valid va_list.

functions.name: OPENSSL_asprintf
functions.description: Like asprintf(3): allocates a new string for the formatted output and stores it in *str. Memory must be freed with OPENSSL_free. Returns the number of characters printed (excluding NUL) on success, or -1 on failure.
requirements: str must be non-NULL and point to a char* variable to receive the allocation.
On success, *str must be freed with OPENSSL_free.
format must be a valid printf-style format string; variadic arguments must match the format.

functions.name: OPENSSL_strndup
functions.description: Duplicates up to size bytes from str, always NUL-terminates the result. Returned memory must be freed with OPENSSL_free.
requirements: str must point to a character array of at least min(actual length, size) bytes; stops early at the first NUL.
Returned pointer must be freed with OPENSSL_free.
Returns NULL on allocation failure.

functions.name: OPENSSL_memdup
functions.description: Allocates and returns a duplicate of size bytes from data. Must be freed with OPENSSL_free. Returns NULL on allocation failure.
requirements: data must point to at least size bytes of readable memory if size > 0.
Returned pointer must be freed with OPENSSL_free.

functions.name: OPENSSL_strlcpy
functions.signature: size_t OPENSSL_strlcpy(char *dst, const char *src, size_t dst_size);
functions.description: Acts like strlcpy(3): copies up to dst_size-1 bytes from the NUL-terminated src into dst, NUL-terminating if dst_size > 0. Returns the length of src.
requirements: dst must point to a buffer of at least dst_size bytes (dst_size may be 0).
src must be a valid NUL-terminated string.
Caller should check return value to detect truncation (return >= dst_size implies truncation).

functions.name: OPENSSL_strlcat
functions.signature: size_t OPENSSL_strlcat(char *dst, const char *src, size_t dst_size);
functions.description: Acts like strlcat(3): appends src to dst of total size dst_size, NUL-terminating if space permits. Returns the sum of the initial length of dst and the length of src.
requirements: dst must point to a buffer of at least dst_size bytes and be NUL-terminated initially if dst_size > 0.
src must be a valid NUL-terminated string.
Caller should check return value to detect truncation (return >= dst_size implies truncation).

functions.name: CRYPTO_malloc
functions.signature: void *CRYPTO_malloc(size_t size, const char *file, int line);
functions.description: Deprecated wrapper that calls OPENSSL_malloc. file and line are ignored.
requirements: Returned pointer must be freed with OPENSSL_free.
file and line parameters are ignored and may be NULL/any value.
Returns NULL on allocation failure.

functions.name: CRYPTO_realloc
functions.signature: void *CRYPTO_realloc(void *ptr, size_t new_size, const char *file, int line);
functions.description: Deprecated wrapper that calls OPENSSL_realloc. file and line are ignored.
requirements: ptr must be a pointer compatible with OPENSSL_free (previously allocated by BoringSSL allocators).
Returned pointer must be freed with OPENSSL_free.
After success, original ptr is freed and must not be used.
file and line are ignored.

functions.name: CRYPTO_free
functions.signature: void CRYPTO_free(void *ptr, const char *file, int line);
functions.description: Deprecated wrapper that calls OPENSSL_free. file and line are ignored.
requirements: ptr must be from a BoringSSL allocation requiring OPENSSL_free.
Safe to pass NULL (no-op).
file and line are ignored.

functions.name: OPENSSL_clear_free
functions.description: Compatibility function that calls OPENSSL_free. BoringSSL already clears memory on free; len is accepted for API compatibility.
requirements: ptr must be from a BoringSSL allocation requiring OPENSSL_free.
Safe to pass NULL (no-op).
len parameter is ignored by BoringSSL’s implementation.

functions.name: CRYPTO_secure_malloc_init
functions.description: Stub for compatibility; returns 0 (secure heap not supported).
requirements: None; function always returns 0 and performs no initialization.

functions.name: CRYPTO_secure_malloc_initialized
functions.description: Stub for compatibility; returns 0 (secure heap not supported).
requirements: None.

functions.name: CRYPTO_secure_used
functions.description: Stub for compatibility; returns 0 (secure heap not supported).
requirements: None.

functions.name: OPENSSL_secure_malloc
functions.description: Compatibility alias that calls OPENSSL_malloc.
requirements: Returned pointer must be freed with OPENSSL_free.
Returns NULL on allocation failure.

functions.name: OPENSSL_secure_clear_free
functions.description: Compatibility alias that calls OPENSSL_clear_free (and thus OPENSSL_free).
requirements: ptr must be from a BoringSSL allocation requiring OPENSSL_free.
Safe to pass NULL (no-op).
len parameter is accepted for compatibility and may be ignored.

functions.name: operator==
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
bool operator==(bssl::Span<T> lhs, bssl::Span<T> rhs);
functions.description: Element-wise comparison for equality of two spans. Returns true if both spans have the same length and all corresponding elements compare equal. Defined as a friend in an internal base so it participates in ADL; effectively applies to spans of const element type (mutable spans convert to const for comparison).
requirements: No special preconditions beyond that both spans reference valid ranges. Lengths may differ; the function handles that by returning false.

functions.name: operator!=
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
bool operator!=(bssl::Span<T> lhs, bssl::Span<T> rhs);
functions.description: Negation of operator==. Returns true iff the spans are not equal in length or in any element.
requirements: No special preconditions beyond that both spans reference valid ranges.

functions.name: bssl::Span::Span
functions.signature:
template <typename T, size_t N>
constexpr bssl::Span<T, N>::Span();
functions.description: Default constructor. Constructs an empty span with null data and size 0. Only available when N == 0 or N == dynamic_extent.
requirements: Enabled only when N == 0 or N == bssl::dynamic_extent.
Resulting span is empty; data() may be nullptr.

functions.name: bssl::Span::data
functions.signature:
template <typename T, size_t N>
constexpr T *bssl::Span<T, N>::data() const;
functions.description: Returns the underlying pointer to the first element of the span (or nullptr if empty).
requirements: The span must have been constructed from a valid source; if size() > 0, the returned pointer must remain valid for the lifetime of the span.

functions.name: bssl::Span::size
functions.signature:
template <typename T, size_t N>
constexpr size_t bssl::Span<T, N>::size() const;
functions.description: Returns the number of elements in the span.

functions.name: bssl::Span::empty
functions.signature:
template <typename T, size_t N>
constexpr bool bssl::Span<T, N>::empty() const;
functions.description: Returns true if size() == 0.

functions.name: bssl::Span::begin
functions.signature:
template <typename T, size_t N>
constexpr T *bssl::Span<T, N>::begin() const;
functions.description: Returns an iterator (pointer) to the first element of the span.
requirements: If size() > 0, the returned pointer must be valid and dereferenceable; otherwise it may equal data() which can be nullptr.

functions.name: bssl::Span::cbegin
functions.signature:
template <typename T, size_t N>
constexpr const T *bssl::Span<T, N>::cbegin() const;
functions.description: Returns a const iterator (pointer) to the first element of the span.
requirements: If size() > 0, the returned pointer must be valid and dereferenceable; otherwise it may be nullptr.

functions.name: bssl::Span::end
functions.signature:
template <typename T, size_t N>
constexpr T *bssl::Span<T, N>::end() const;
functions.description: Returns an iterator (pointer) one past the last element of the span.
requirements: If size() > 0, end() == data() + size() must be a valid past-the-end pointer for the underlying array.

functions.name: bssl::Span::cend
functions.signature:
template <typename T, size_t N>
constexpr const T *bssl::Span<T, N>::cend() const;
functions.description: Returns a const iterator (pointer) one past the last element of the span.
requirements: If size() > 0, cend() == data() + size() must be a valid past-the-end pointer for the underlying array.

functions.name: bssl::Span::front
functions.signature:
template <typename T, size_t N>
constexpr T &bssl::Span<T, N>::front() const;
functions.description: Returns a reference to the first element. Aborts if the span is empty.
requirements: size() must be > 0; otherwise the function aborts (BSSL_CHECK).

functions.name: bssl::Span::back
functions.signature:
template <typename T, size_t N>
constexpr T &bssl::Span<T, N>::back() const;
functions.description: Returns a reference to the last element. Aborts if the span is empty.
requirements: size() must be > 0; otherwise the function aborts (BSSL_CHECK).

functions.name: bssl::Span::operator[]
functions.signature:
template <typename T, size_t N>
constexpr T &bssl::Span<T, N>::operator[](size_t i) const;
functions.description: Returns a reference to the i-th element without bounds checking beyond an internal assert. Aborts if i >= size().
requirements: i must be < size(); otherwise the function aborts (BSSL_CHECK).

functions.name: bssl::Span::at
functions.signature:
template <typename T, size_t N>
T &bssl::Span<T, N>::at(size_t i) const;
functions.description: Returns a reference to the i-th element. Delegates to operator[]; aborts if i >= size().
requirements: i must be < size(); otherwise the function aborts (BSSL_CHECK).

functions.name: bssl::Span::subspan
functions.signature:
template <typename T, size_t N>
constexpr bssl::Span<T> bssl::Span<T, N>::subspan(size_t pos, size_t len) const;
functions.description: Returns a view of a subrange [pos, pos+len). Aborts if pos or len are out of range. Unlike std::span, dynamic_extent for len is not treated specially here.
requirements: pos must be <= size(); len must be <= size() - pos; otherwise the function aborts (BSSL_CHECK).

functions.name: bssl::Span::first
functions.signature:
template <typename T, size_t N>
constexpr bssl::Span<T> bssl::Span<T, N>::first(size_t len) const;
functions.description: Returns a view of the first len elements. Aborts if len > size().
requirements: len must be <= size(); otherwise the function aborts (BSSL_CHECK).

functions.name: bssl::Span::last
functions.signature:
template <typename T, size_t N>
constexpr bssl::Span<T> bssl::Span<T, N>::last(size_t len) const;
functions.description: Returns a view of the last len elements. Aborts if len > size().
requirements: len must be <= size(); otherwise the function aborts (BSSL_CHECK).

functions.name: bssl::MakeSpan
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
constexpr bssl::Span<T> bssl::MakeSpan(T *ptr, size_t size);
functions.description: Helper to create a span from a pointer and size. Equivalent to bssl::Span<T>(ptr, size).
requirements: If size > 0, ptr must point to at least size contiguous objects of type T and be valid for the required access.
For fixed-extent instantiations of Span<T, N>, size must equal N at runtime (constructor enforces with BSSL_CHECK).

functions.name: bssl::MakeConstSpan
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
constexpr bssl::Span<const T> bssl::MakeConstSpan(T *ptr, size_t size);
functions.description: Helper to create a read-only span from a pointer and size. Equivalent to bssl::Span<const T>(ptr, size).
requirements: If size > 0, ptr must point to at least size contiguous objects of type T and be valid for reading.
For fixed-extent instantiations of Span<const T, N>, size must equal N at runtime (constructor enforces with BSSL_CHECK).

functions.name: bssl::StringAsBytes
functions.description: Returns a read-only byte view over the characters in the given string_view without copying, by reinterpreting the data as uint8_t. Useful for treating text or arbitrary strings as a byte span.
requirements: s.data() must be valid for s.size() bytes during the lifetime of the returned span (string_view’s source must outlive the span).

functions.name: bssl::BytesAsStringView
functions.description: Returns a string_view over the given byte span without copying, by reinterpreting the bytes as char. Useful for passing byte buffers to APIs expecting string_view.
requirements: b.data() must be valid for b.size() bytes during the lifetime of the returned string_view.

functions.name: CBS_init
functions.signature: OPENSSL_INLINE void CBS_init(CBS *cbs, const uint8_t *data, size_t len)
functions.description: Initializes a CBS to point to an external byte range. Does not take ownership of the memory. Use to set up parsing over an existing buffer.
requirements: cbs must be a valid pointer to a CBS struct.
data may be NULL only if len is zero (implied typical constraint; behavior of NULL+nonzero unspecified).
The underlying memory pointed to by data must remain valid and unmodified for the lifetime of the CBS use.

functions.name: CBS_skip
functions.description: Advances the CBS by len bytes, discarding them from the front.
requirements: cbs must be initialized.
len must be less than or equal to the number of remaining bytes (CBS_len(cbs)).
Returns 1 on success, 0 if attempting to skip past end.

functions.name: CBS_data
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the current contents of the CBS without advancing.
requirements: cbs must be initialized.
Returned pointer remains valid only as long as the underlying buffer remains valid and the CBS is not modified.

functions.name: CBS_len
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes remaining in the CBS.
requirements: cbs must be initialized.

functions.name: CBS_stow
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int CBS_stow(const CBS *cbs, uint8_t **out_ptr, size_t *out_len)
functions.description: Copies the remaining contents of the CBS into a newly-allocated buffer and returns it via out_ptr/out_len. Frees any previous *out_ptr with OPENSSL_free.
requirements: cbs must be initialized.
out_ptr and out_len must be non-NULL.
On success, *out_ptr must be freed with OPENSSL_free when no longer needed.
If cbs is empty, *out_ptr will be set to NULL and *out_len to 0.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on allocation failure.

functions.name: CBS_strdup
functions.description: Copies the CBS contents to a newly-allocated, NUL-terminated C string. Previous *out_ptr is freed with OPENSSL_free.
requirements: cbs must be initialized.
out_ptr must be non-NULL.
On success, *out_ptr must be freed with OPENSSL_free.
If cbs contains any NUL byte, the string is truncated at the first NUL; use CBS_contains_zero_byte to check.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on allocation failure.

functions.name: CBS_contains_zero_byte
functions.description: Checks whether the current CBS contents contains a NUL (0x00) byte.
requirements: cbs must be initialized.
Returns 1 if a NUL byte is present, 0 otherwise.

functions.name: CBS_mem_equal
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int CBS_mem_equal(const CBS *cbs, const uint8_t *data, size_t len)
functions.description: Compares the CBS contents to an external byte array of length len. Uses constant-time comparison when lengths match.
requirements: cbs must be initialized.
data must point to at least len bytes when len > 0.
Returns 1 if equal, 0 otherwise.

functions.name: CBS_get_u8
functions.description: Reads the next big-endian uint8 from the CBS and advances it.
requirements: cbs must be initialized and have at least 1 byte remaining.
out must be non-NULL.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on underflow.

functions.name: CBS_get_u16
functions.description: Reads the next big-endian uint16 from the CBS and advances it.
requirements: cbs must have at least 2 bytes remaining.
out must be non-NULL.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on underflow.

functions.name: CBS_get_u16le
functions.description: Reads the next little-endian uint16 from the CBS and advances it.
requirements: cbs must have at least 2 bytes remaining.
out must be non-NULL.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on underflow.

functions.name: CBS_get_u24
functions.description: Reads the next big-endian 24-bit unsigned value from the CBS and advances it.
requirements: cbs must have at least 3 bytes remaining.
out must be non-NULL.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on underflow.

functions.name: CBS_get_u32
functions.description: Reads the next big-endian uint32 from the CBS and advances it.
requirements: cbs must have at least 4 bytes remaining.
out must be non-NULL.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on underflow.

functions.name: CBS_get_u32le
functions.description: Reads the next little-endian uint32 from the CBS and advances it.
requirements: cbs must have at least 4 bytes remaining.
out must be non-NULL.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on underflow.

functions.name: CBS_get_u64
functions.description: Reads the next big-endian uint64 from the CBS and advances it.
requirements: cbs must have at least 8 bytes remaining.
out must be non-NULL.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on underflow.

functions.name: CBS_get_u64le
functions.description: Reads the next little-endian uint64 from the CBS and advances it.
requirements: cbs must have at least 8 bytes remaining.
out must be non-NULL.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on underflow.

functions.name: CBS_get_last_u8
functions.description: Reads the last byte of the CBS into out and shortens the CBS by one.
requirements: cbs must have at least 1 byte remaining.
out must be non-NULL.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on underflow.

functions.name: CBS_get_bytes
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int CBS_get_bytes(CBS *cbs, CBS *out, size_t len)
functions.description: Slices the next len bytes as a sub-CBS in out and advances the input CBS.
requirements: cbs must have at least len bytes remaining.
out must be non-NULL.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on underflow.

functions.name: CBS_copy_bytes
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int CBS_copy_bytes(CBS *cbs, uint8_t *out, size_t len)
functions.description: Copies the next len bytes into out and advances the CBS.
requirements: cbs must have at least len bytes remaining.
out must point to a buffer with capacity >= len.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on underflow.

functions.name: CBS_get_u8_length_prefixed
functions.description: Parses an 8-bit length-prefixed value into out and advances the CBS past it.
requirements: cbs must contain a one-byte length followed by that many bytes.
out must be non-NULL.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on malformed or truncated input.

functions.name: CBS_get_u16_length_prefixed
functions.description: Parses a big-endian 16-bit length-prefixed value into out and advances the CBS past it.
requirements: cbs must contain a two-byte big-endian length followed by that many bytes.
out must be non-NULL.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on malformed or truncated input.

functions.name: CBS_get_u24_length_prefixed
functions.description: Parses a big-endian 24-bit length-prefixed value into out and advances the CBS past it.
requirements: cbs must contain a three-byte big-endian length followed by that many bytes.
out must be non-NULL.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on malformed or truncated input.

functions.name: CBS_get_until_first
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int CBS_get_until_first(CBS *cbs, CBS *out, uint8_t c)
functions.description: Finds the first occurrence of byte c, sets out to the bytes before it, and advances the CBS over them.
requirements: cbs must be initialized.
out must be non-NULL.
Returns 1 if c is found; 0 if not found (CBS left unmodified).

functions.name: CBS_get_u64_decimal
functions.description: Parses a decimal unsigned integer from ASCII digits at the front of the CBS, writing to out and consuming the digits.
requirements: cbs must start with at least one decimal digit; empty input is invalid.
No leading zeros are allowed.
Only non-negative values are accepted; optional signs are not allowed.
out must be non-NULL.
Returns 1 on success; 0 on parse error or overflow.

functions.name: CBS_get_asn1
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int CBS_get_asn1(CBS *cbs, CBS *out, CBS_ASN1_TAG tag_value)
functions.description: Parses a DER-encoded ASN.1 element with the given tag and sets out to its contents (value only), advancing the CBS.
requirements: cbs must contain a complete ASN.1 element with tag matching tag_value.
out must be non-NULL.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on malformed input, mismatch, or truncation.

functions.name: CBS_get_asn1_element
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int CBS_get_asn1_element(CBS *cbs, CBS *out, CBS_ASN1_TAG tag_value)
functions.description: Like CBS_get_asn1, but out includes the tag and length header bytes as well as contents.
requirements: Same as CBS_get_asn1.
out must be non-NULL.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.

functions.name: CBS_peek_asn1_tag
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int CBS_peek_asn1_tag(const CBS *cbs, CBS_ASN1_TAG tag_value)
functions.description: Looks ahead at the next ASN.1 element’s tag without consuming input and reports whether it matches tag_value.
requirements: cbs must be initialized.
Returns 1 if non-empty and the next tag matches; 0 otherwise. Note: a later CBS_get_asn1 may still fail if the element is malformed.

functions.name: CBS_get_any_asn1
functions.description: Parses the next ASN.1 element, returning its contents (value only) in out and its tag in out_tag, and advances the CBS.
requirements: cbs must contain a complete ASN.1 element.
out and/or out_tag may be NULL to ignore respective outputs.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on malformed or truncated input.

functions.name: CBS_get_any_asn1_element
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int CBS_get_any_asn1_element(CBS *cbs, CBS *out, CBS_ASN1_TAG *out_tag, size_t *out_header_len)
functions.description: Parses the next ASN.1 element, returning out including header, out_tag with the tag, and out_header_len with header length; advances the CBS.
requirements: cbs must contain a complete ASN.1 element.
out, out_tag, and out_header_len may be NULL to ignore.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on malformed or truncated input.

functions.name: CBS_get_any_ber_asn1_element
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int CBS_get_any_ber_asn1_element(CBS *cbs, CBS *out, CBS_ASN1_TAG *out_tag, size_t *out_header_len, int *out_ber_found, int *out_indefinite)
functions.description: Like CBS_get_any_asn1_element, but accepts BER: indefinite-length elements and non-minimal lengths. out_indefinite is set if the length was indefinite. If out_ber_found is not NULL, it is set when the element is valid BER but invalid DER. EOC elements are not parsed as standalone elements.
requirements: cbs must contain a BER-decodable element; EOC must be handled by the caller when parsing indefinite-length content.
out/out_tag/out_header_len may be NULL to ignore.

out_indefinite must be non-NULL if caller needs to know indefinite state; otherwise may be NULL only if caller ignores it? (The function signature requires a pointer; provide a valid pointer if you need the value.)
Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.

functions.name: CBS_get_asn1_uint64
functions.description: Parses an ASN.1 INTEGER using DER rules via CBS_get_asn1 and returns it as a uint64, rejecting negative or too-large values.
requirements: cbs must contain a valid INTEGER element.
out must be non-NULL.
Fails (returns 0) if INTEGER is negative or does not fit in 64 bits or input malformed.

functions.name: CBS_get_asn1_uint64_with_tag
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int CBS_get_asn1_uint64_with_tag(CBS *cbs, uint64_t *out, CBS_ASN1_TAG tag)
functions.description: Parses an implicitly-tagged ASN.1 INTEGER with the specified tag and returns it as a uint64, rejecting negative or too-large values.
requirements: cbs must contain an element with tag equal to tag and with INTEGER encoding semantics.
out must be non-NULL.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on malformed input or invalid/negative/overflowing value.

functions.name: CBS_get_asn1_int64
functions.description: Parses an ASN.1 INTEGER into a signed 64-bit integer.
requirements: cbs must contain a valid INTEGER element.
out must be non-NULL.
Returns 1 on success; 0 on malformed input or if the value does not fit in 64 bits.

functions.name: CBS_get_asn1_int64_with_tag
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int CBS_get_asn1_int64_with_tag(CBS *cbs, int64_t *out, CBS_ASN1_TAG tag)
functions.description: Parses an implicitly-tagged ASN.1 INTEGER with the specified tag into a signed 64-bit integer.
requirements: cbs must contain an element with tag equal to tag and with INTEGER encoding semantics.
out must be non-NULL.
Returns 1 on success; 0 on malformed input or overflow.

functions.name: CBS_get_asn1_bool
functions.description: Parses an ASN.1 BOOLEAN and writes 0 or 1 to out.
requirements: cbs must contain a valid BOOLEAN element.
out must be non-NULL.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.

functions.name: CBS_get_optional_asn1
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int CBS_get_optional_asn1(CBS *cbs, CBS *out, int *out_present, CBS_ASN1_TAG tag)
