On success, returns a pointer to a GeneralizedTime: if out is NULL, a newly-allocated ASN1_GENERALIZEDTIME is returned; if out is non-NULL and *out is NULL, *out is set to a newly-allocated result and returned; if out and *out are both non-NULL, the existing object at *out is updated and returned. Returns NULL on error.
requirements: t must point to a valid ASN1_TIME object; the function may fail if t cannot be decoded.
If out is NULL, the caller takes ownership of the returned ASN1_GENERALIZEDTIME and must free it with ASN1_GENERALIZEDTIME_free.
If out is non-NULL and *out is NULL, the function allocates a new ASN1_GENERALIZEDTIME, assigns it to *out, and the caller must free it with ASN1_GENERALIZEDTIME_free.
If out and *out are both non-NULL, *out must point to a valid ASN1_GENERALIZEDTIME that can be updated in-place.
The function returns NULL on error; callers must check for NULL before using the result.

functions.name: ASN1_TIME_set_string
functions.description: Sets s from a valid UTCTime or GeneralizedTime string (acts like the specific setters depending on input). Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise.
requirements: str must be valid UTCTime or GeneralizedTime format.

functions.name: ASN1_TIME_set_string_X509
functions.description: Like ASN1_TIME_set_string, but converts GeneralizedTime to UTCTime if within the UTCTime range (RFC 5280).
requirements: str must be valid UTCTime or GeneralizedTime.

functions.name: ASN1_TIME_to_time_t
functions.description: Converts t to time_t, writing to out. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure (e.g., not representable in time_t).
requirements: out must be non-NULL.
t must be valid.

functions.name: ASN1_TIME_to_posix
functions.description: Converts t to POSIX time (seconds since epoch) in out. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: out must be non-NULL.
t must be valid.

functions.name: ASN1_TIME_to_posix_nonstandard
functions.description: Like ASN1_TIME_to_posix but allows non-standard four-digit timezone offsets on UTC times. Prefer ASN1_TIME_to_posix.
requirements: out must be non-NULL.

functions.name: ASN1_NULL_new
functions.description: Returns an opaque, non-NULL pointer representing ASN.1 NULL. Safe to free but not necessary.

functions.name: ASN1_NULL_free
functions.description: No-op free for ASN1_NULL.

functions.name: d2i_ASN1_NULL
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT ASN1_NULL *d2i_ASN1_NULL(ASN1_NULL **out, const uint8_t **inp, long len);
functions.description: Parses a DER-encoded ASN.1 NULL, advancing *inp, returning a non-NULL opaque pointer. See d2i_SAMPLE.
requirements: Out semantics per d2i_SAMPLE.

functions.name: i2d_ASN1_NULL
functions.description: Serializes an ASN.1 NULL to DER. See i2d_SAMPLE.

functions.name: ASN1_OBJECT_create
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT ASN1_OBJECT *ASN1_OBJECT_create(int nid, const uint8_t *data, size_t len, const char *sn, const char *ln);
functions.description: Creates a new ASN1_OBJECT from the given DER-encoded OID (contents only). nid should be NID_undef; sn and ln are optional names but have no effect beyond storage.
requirements: data must point to DER contents of the OID (no tag/length), of length len.
nid should be NID_undef; passing mismatched nid can cause misbehavior in other functions.
Returned object must be freed with ASN1_OBJECT_free unless static.

functions.name: ASN1_OBJECT_free
functions.description: Frees an ASN1_OBJECT unless it is a static one returned by OBJ_nid2obj, in which case it does nothing.
requirements: Safe to call with NULL.

functions.name: d2i_ASN1_OBJECT
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT ASN1_OBJECT *d2i_ASN1_OBJECT(ASN1_OBJECT **out, const uint8_t **inp, long len);
functions.description: Parses a DER-encoded OBJECT IDENTIFIER (full element). See d2i_SAMPLE.

functions.name: i2d_ASN1_OBJECT
functions.description: Serializes an OBJECT IDENTIFIER to DER. See i2d_SAMPLE.

functions.name: c2i_ASN1_OBJECT
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT ASN1_OBJECT *c2i_ASN1_OBJECT(ASN1_OBJECT **out, const uint8_t **inp, long len);
functions.description: Decodes OBJECT IDENTIFIER contents (no tag/length) from exactly len bytes, consuming all len. See d2i_SAMPLE.
requirements: len must be exact content length.

functions.name: ASN1_TYPE *ASN1_TYPE_new
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new, empty ASN1_TYPE object, or NULL on allocation failure. The resulting object has type -1 and is not a valid ANY value until initialized (e.g., via ASN1_TYPE_set or ASN1_TYPE_set1). Release with ASN1_TYPE_free when done.
requirements: The returned pointer must be freed with ASN1_TYPE_free to avoid memory leaks.
The newly-created ASN1_TYPE has type -1 and must be initialized before use as a valid ASN.1 value.
Callers must check for a NULL return to detect allocation failure.

functions.name: ASN1_TYPE_free
functions.description: Frees an ASN1_TYPE and its contents.
requirements: Safe to call with NULL.

functions.name: d2i_ASN1_TYPE
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT ASN1_TYPE *d2i_ASN1_TYPE(ASN1_TYPE **out, const uint8_t **inp, long len);
functions.description: Parses an ASN.1 value of any supported primitive universal type (and some structured types) into ASN1_TYPE. May accept BER currently for some cases. Caller must validate values of type SEQUENCE/SET/OTHER/unsupported primitive types when interpreting.
requirements: Out semantics per d2i_SAMPLE.
Caller must perform additional validation for non-primitive or unsupported types.
BER acceptance will be removed in future.

functions.name: i2d_ASN1_TYPE
functions.description: Serializes an ASN1_TYPE to DER. See i2d_SAMPLE.

functions.name: ASN1_TYPE_get
functions.description: Returns the V_ASN1_* tag of a, or 0 if not fully initialized.
requirements: a must be non-NULL.

functions.name: ASN1_TYPE_set
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT void ASN1_TYPE_set(ASN1_TYPE *a, int type, void *value);
functions.description: Sets a to the given type and value, taking ownership (for non-BOOLEAN/NULL types). Frees previous contents. For BOOLEAN, value NULL->FALSE, non-NULL->TRUE; for NULL, value must be NULL.
requirements: type must be a valid V_ASN1_* type according to ASN1_TYPE rules.
For BOOLEAN, value pointer may be invalid (e.g., (void*)1) when setting TRUE.
For NULL, value must be NULL.
For other types, value must point to an object of the corresponding type; ownership transfers to a.

functions.name: ASN1_TYPE_set1
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int ASN1_TYPE_set1(ASN1_TYPE *a, int type, const void *value);
functions.description: Like ASN1_TYPE_set but does not take ownership; copies the value. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: type/value must be consistent as in ASN1_TYPE_set.
Returns 0 on allocation/copy failure.

functions.name: ASN1_TYPE_cmp
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int ASN1_TYPE_cmp(const ASN1_TYPE *a, const ASN1_TYPE *b);
functions.description: Returns 0 if a and b are equal, non-zero otherwise (equality test only; not an ordering).
requirements: a and b must be non-NULL.

functions.name: d2i_ASN1_SEQUENCE_ANY
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT ASN1_SEQUENCE_ANY *d2i_ASN1_SEQUENCE_ANY(ASN1_SEQUENCE_ANY **out, const uint8_t **inp, long len);
functions.description: Parses a DER-encoded SEQUENCE OF ANY into a STACK_OF(ASN1_TYPE). The resulting stack owns its elements and must be freed with sk_ASN1_TYPE_pop_free + ASN1_TYPE_free.
requirements: Out semantics per d2i_SAMPLE.
Caller must free with sk_ASN1_TYPE_pop_free and ASN1_TYPE_free, not sk_ASN1_TYPE_free.
May currently accept BER.

functions.name: i2d_ASN1_SEQUENCE_ANY
functions.description: Serializes a SEQUENCE OF ANY (STACK_OF(ASN1_TYPE)) to DER.
requirements: Freeing and ownership as standard i2d conventions.

functions.name: d2i_ASN1_SET_ANY
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT ASN1_SEQUENCE_ANY *d2i_ASN1_SET_ANY(ASN1_SEQUENCE_ANY **out, const uint8_t **inp, long len);
functions.description: Parses a DER-encoded SET OF ANY into STACK_OF(ASN1_TYPE). Ownership as in SEQUENCE ANY.
requirements: Out semantics per d2i_SAMPLE.
Free with sk_ASN1_TYPE_pop_free + ASN1_TYPE_free.
May currently accept BER.

functions.name: i2d_ASN1_SET_ANY
functions.description: Serializes a SET OF ANY (STACK_OF(ASN1_TYPE)) to DER.

functions.name: ASN1_UTCTIME_print
functions.description: Writes a human-readable representation of a to out. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: out must be a valid BIO.
a must be valid UTCTime.

functions.name: ASN1_GENERALIZEDTIME_print
functions.description: Writes human-readable GeneralizedTime to out.
requirements: out must be a valid BIO.

functions.name: ASN1_TIME_print
functions.description: Writes a human-readable representation of a (Time) to out.
requirements: out must be a valid BIO.

functions.name: ASN1_STRING_print
functions.description: Writes a human-readable representation of str to out, replacing unprintable characters with '.'. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: out must be a valid BIO.

functions.name: ASN1_STRING_print_ex
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int ASN1_STRING_print_ex(BIO *out, const ASN1_STRING *str, unsigned long flags);
functions.description: Writes a human-readable/escaped representation of str to out using flags (ASN1_STRFLGS_*). Returns bytes written, or -1 on error. If out is NULL, returns would-be length.
requirements: flags controls escaping/format; if unsure, use ASN1_STRFLGS_RFC2253.

functions.name: ASN1_STRING_print_ex_fp
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int ASN1_STRING_print_ex_fp(FILE *fp, const ASN1_STRING *str, unsigned long flags);
functions.description: Like ASN1_STRING_print_ex but writes to FILE*.
requirements: fp must be a valid FILE*.

functions.name: i2a_ASN1_INTEGER
functions.description: Writes a human-readable representation of integer a to bp. Returns number of bytes written or negative on error (partial output may occur on error).
requirements: bp must be a valid BIO.

functions.name: i2a_ASN1_ENUMERATED
functions.description: Writes a human-readable representation of enumerated a to bp. Returns bytes written or negative on error (partial possible).
requirements: bp must be a valid BIO.

functions.name: i2a_ASN1_OBJECT
functions.description: Writes a human-readable representation of object identifier a to bp. Returns bytes written or negative on error (partial possible).
requirements: bp must be a valid BIO.

functions.name: i2a_ASN1_STRING
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int i2a_ASN1_STRING(BIO *bp, const ASN1_STRING *a, int type);
functions.description: Writes a hex/text representation of the internal contents of a to bp (does not decode to Unicode). type is ignored. Good for OCTET STRINGs.
requirements: bp must be a valid BIO.

functions.name: i2t_ASN1_OBJECT
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int i2t_ASN1_OBJECT(char *buf, int buf_len, const ASN1_OBJECT *a);
functions.description: Writes a textual representation of a to buf using OBJ_obj2txt with always_return_oid=0. Returns number of bytes written.
requirements: buf must have size buf_len.
If output truncated, behavior follows OBJ_obj2txt semantics.

functions.name: ASN1_get_object
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int ASN1_get_object(const unsigned char **inp, long *out_length, int *out_tag, int *out_class, long max_len);
functions.description: Parses a DER element header from up to max_len bytes at *inp. On success advances *inp to the body and sets out_length, out_tag, out_class. Returns V_ASN1_CONSTRUCTED for constructed, 0 for primitive, 0x80 on error. Only supports DER (no indefinite or non-minimal lengths).
requirements: inp, out_length, out_tag, out_class must be non-NULL.
max_len must be >= 0 and reflect available bytes.
Caller must ensure the body is available and handle errors.

functions.name: ASN1_put_object
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT void ASN1_put_object(unsigned char **outp, int constructed, int length, int tag, int xclass);
functions.description: Writes a DER/BER header to *outp describing an element with given length, tag, and class. constructed: 0=primitive, 1=constructed definite-length, 2=constructed indefinite-length. Advances *outp by bytes written.
requirements: outp and *outp must be non-NULL and have sufficient space; no bounds checks.
xclass must be one of V_ASN1_UNIVERSAL/APPLICATION/CONTEXT_SPECIFIC/PRIVATE.
Use definite-length DER whenever possible (recommend CBB APIs instead).

functions.name: ASN1_put_eoc
functions.description: Writes the end-of-contents marker (two zero bytes) at *outp, advances pointer, and returns 2. For BER indefinite-length encodings.
requirements: outp and *outp must be non-NULL and have space for two bytes.

functions.name: ASN1_object_size
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int ASN1_object_size(int constructed, int length, int tag);
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes needed to encode a DER/BER header for the given parameters, or -1 on error. constructed: 0/1 definite-length DER; 2 for BER indefinite-length.
requirements: length must be >= 0 for definite-length encodings.
tag must not include class/constructed bits.

functions.name: ASN1_STRING_set_default_mask
functions.description: Deprecated no-op. Does nothing.

functions.name: ASN1_STRING_set_default_mask_asc
functions.description: Deprecated. Always returns 1.

functions.name: ASN1_STRING_get_default_mask
functions.description: Deprecated. Always returns B_ASN1_UTF8STRING.

functions.name: ASN1_STRING_TABLE_cleanup
functions.description: Deprecated no-op. Does nothing.

functions.name: ASN1_INTEGER_set
functions.description: Deprecated setter using long. Prefer ASN1_INTEGER_set_uint64/int64.
requirements: a must be non-NULL.
Return 1 on success, 0 on error.

functions.name: ASN1_ENUMERATED_set
functions.description: Deprecated setter using long. Prefer ASN1_ENUMERATED_set_uint64/int64.
requirements: a must be non-NULL.

functions.name: ASN1_INTEGER_get
functions.description: Deprecated getter returning long, or -1 on error/out-of-range. Cannot distinguish -1 value from error; prefer get_uint64/get_int64.
requirements: a must be non-NULL.
Caller must not rely on -1 to indicate a valid value.

functions.name: ASN1_ENUMERATED_get
functions.description: Deprecated getter returning long, or -1 on error/out-of-range. Prefer get_uint64/get_int64.
requirements: a must be non-NULL.

functions.name: BIO_new
functions.description: Allocates a new BIO using the given BIO_METHOD with an initial refcount of 1. Returns a fresh BIO or NULL on error.
requirements: method must be a valid, initialized BIO_METHOD pointer appropriate for the intended BIO type.
Caller owns the returned BIO reference and must release it with BIO_free (or BIO_free_all for chains).

functions.name: BIO_free
functions.description: Decrements the reference count of bio; on reaching zero, destroys method state (if any) and frees bio. Repeats for the rest of the chain if present. Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise.
requirements: bio may be NULL (behavior unspecified in header; typical OpenSSL returns 0).
If bio is part of a chain, this will free the entire remainder of the chain.
After successful call, the caller must not use bio.

functions.name: BIO_vfree
functions.description: Compatibility variant of BIO_free with void return. Performs the same actions as BIO_free.
requirements: bio should be a valid BIO or NULL.
Do not use bio after calling.

functions.name: BIO_up_ref
functions.description: Increments the reference count of bio. Returns 1 on success.
requirements: bio must be a valid, initialized BIO.

functions.name: BIO_read
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BIO_read(BIO *bio, void *data, int len);
functions.description: Attempts to read up to len bytes from bio into data. Returns number of bytes read, 0 on EOF, or a negative value on error.
requirements: bio must be initialized (BIO_get_init true).
data must point to a buffer of at least len bytes.
len must be non-negative.

functions.name: BIO_gets
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BIO_gets(BIO *bio, char *buf, int size);
functions.description: Reads a line from bio into buf, writing at most size bytes including a trailing NUL. Returns number of bytes read or negative on error. Includes newline if a full line was read.
requirements: bio must support line reads (memory BIOs support it; others may not).
buf must have capacity of at least size bytes.
size must be > 0 to receive any data.

functions.name: BIO_write
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BIO_write(BIO *bio, const void *data, int len);
functions.description: Writes len bytes from data to bio. Returns number of bytes written or a negative value on error.
requirements: bio must be initialized (BIO_get_init true).
data must point to at least len bytes of readable memory.
len must be non-negative.

functions.name: BIO_write_all
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BIO_write_all(BIO *bio, const void *data, size_t len);
functions.description: Writes all len bytes to bio, looping as needed. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: bio must be initialized.
data must point to at least len bytes.
bio must be in a state where repeated writes and retries are allowed (may use BIO_should_retry to handle non-blocking cases).

functions.name: BIO_puts
functions.description: Writes a NUL-terminated string to bio. Returns number of bytes written or negative on error.
requirements: buf must be a valid NUL-terminated string.
bio must support write operations.

functions.name: BIO_flush
functions.description: Flushes any buffered output for bio. Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise.
requirements: bio must support BIO_CTRL_FLUSH via its method.

functions.name: BIO_ctrl
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT long BIO_ctrl(BIO *bio, int cmd, long larg, void *parg);
functions.description: Sends control request cmd to bio. cmd should be one of BIO_C_* or BIO_CTRL_* values. Return value is command-specific.
requirements: bio must be a valid BIO.
cmd must be a control code supported by bio’s method; arguments must match the expected types for that code.
parg and larg usage depend on cmd.

functions.name: BIO_ptr_ctrl
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT char *BIO_ptr_ctrl(BIO *bp, int cmd, long larg);
functions.description: Like BIO_ctrl but passes address of a void* internally; returns the value written to it, or NULL if the control request returns <= 0.
requirements: bp must be valid.
cmd must be a control accepting a pointer-return semantics from BIO_ptr_ctrl.

functions.name: BIO_int_ctrl
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT long BIO_int_ctrl(BIO *bp, int cmd, long larg, int iarg);
functions.description: Like BIO_ctrl but passes the address of a copy of iarg as parg.
requirements: bp must be valid.
cmd must expect an integer pointer parameter.

functions.name: BIO_reset
functions.description: Resets bio to its initial state (type-specific semantics). Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise.
requirements: bio must support BIO_CTRL_RESET via its method.

functions.name: BIO_eof
functions.description: Returns non-zero if bio has reached end-of-file (type-specific semantics; always non-zero for BIO_pair).
requirements: bio must support BIO_CTRL_EOF via its method.

functions.name: BIO_set_flags
functions.description: ORs flags into bio->flags.
requirements: bio must be valid.
flags should be BIO_FLAGS_* bits relevant to the BIO implementation.

functions.name: BIO_clear_flags
functions.description: Clears bits in bio->flags corresponding to flags.
requirements: bio must be valid.
flags should correspond to BIO_FLAGS_* bits.

functions.name: BIO_test_flags
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BIO_test_flags(const BIO *bio, int flags);
functions.description: Returns bio->flags AND flags.
requirements: bio must be a valid pointer.

functions.name: BIO_should_read
functions.description: Returns non-zero if a read operation temporarily failed and should be retried (e.g., EAGAIN).
requirements: bio must be valid.

functions.name: BIO_should_write
functions.description: Returns non-zero if a write operation temporarily failed and should be retried.
requirements: bio must be valid.

functions.name: BIO_should_retry
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the last I/O failure was temporary and should be retried; zero if permanent error.
requirements: bio must be valid.

functions.name: BIO_should_io_special
functions.description: Returns non-zero if a special I/O operation temporarily failed and should be retried. The specific operation is obtained via BIO_get_retry_reason.
requirements: bio must be valid.

functions.name: BIO_get_retry_reason
functions.description: Returns the special I/O operation that should be retried, one of BIO_RR_* values.
requirements: bio must be valid.
Should be called after BIO_should_io_special indicates a special retry.

functions.name: BIO_set_retry_reason
functions.description: Sets the special I/O retry reason on bio to reason (BIO_RR_*).
requirements: bio must be valid.
reason should be one of BIO_RR_* constants.

functions.name: BIO_set_retry_read
functions.description: Sets BIO_FLAGS_READ and BIO_FLAGS_SHOULD_RETRY on bio indicating read should be retried.
requirements: bio must be valid.

functions.name: BIO_set_retry_write
functions.description: Sets BIO_FLAGS_WRITE and BIO_FLAGS_SHOULD_RETRY on bio indicating write should be retried.
requirements: bio must be valid.

functions.name: BIO_get_retry_flags
functions.description: Gets the BIO_FLAGS_READ, BIO_FLAGS_WRITE, BIO_FLAGS_IO_SPECIAL, and BIO_FLAGS_SHOULD_RETRY flags from bio.
requirements: bio must be valid.

functions.name: BIO_clear_retry_flags
functions.description: Clears BIO_FLAGS_READ, BIO_FLAGS_WRITE, BIO_FLAGS_IO_SPECIAL, and BIO_FLAGS_SHOULD_RETRY on bio.
requirements: bio must be valid.

functions.name: BIO_method_type
functions.description: Returns the BIO type (one of BIO_TYPE_* values).
requirements: bio must be valid.

functions.name: BIO_callback_ctrl
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT long BIO_callback_ctrl(BIO *bio, int cmd, BIO_info_cb *fp);
functions.description: Manipulates an informational callback for bio; cmd is generally BIO_CTRL_SET_CALLBACK but may be method-specific. Returns a method-defined value.
requirements: bio must be valid.
cmd must be supported by bio’s method.
fp may be NULL depending on cmd semantics.

functions.name: BIO_pending
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes pending to be read from bio.
requirements: bio must be valid and support BIO_CTRL_PENDING.

functions.name: BIO_ctrl_pending
functions.description: Compatibility alias that calls BIO_pending.
requirements: bio must be valid.

functions.name: BIO_wpending
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes pending to be written by bio.
requirements: bio must be valid and support BIO_CTRL_WPENDING.

functions.name: BIO_set_close
functions.description: Sets the close flag for bio (semantics depend on BIO type; e.g., memory BIO ownership of buffer). Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise.
requirements: bio must be valid.
close_flag should be BIO_NOCLOSE or BIO_CLOSE, or type-appropriate value.

functions.name: BIO_number_read
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes read from bio.
requirements: bio must be valid.

functions.name: BIO_number_written
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes written to bio.
requirements: bio must be valid.

functions.name: BIO_push
functions.description: Appends appended_bio (which may itself be a chain) to the end of the chain with bio at the head. Returns bio. Takes ownership of caller’s reference to appended_bio.
requirements: bio must be the head of a chain or a single BIO.
appended_bio must be a valid BIO (or chain).
After call, caller must not free appended_bio separately; it’s owned by the chain.

functions.name: BIO_pop
functions.description: Removes bio from the head of a chain and returns the next BIO, or NULL if none. Caller takes ownership of the removed bio’s reference.
requirements: bio must be a chain head or single BIO.
Caller becomes responsible for freeing the returned next BIO chain appropriately.

functions.name: BIO_next
functions.description: Returns the next BIO in the chain after bio, or NULL if none.
requirements: bio must be valid.

functions.name: BIO_free_all
functions.description: Calls BIO_free on bio (compatibility wrapper). Frees entire chain starting at bio.
requirements: bio may be NULL or a valid BIO/chain.
Do not use any BIOs in the chain after call.

functions.name: BIO_find_type
functions.description: Walks the chain and returns the first BIO whose type matches type (one of BIO_TYPE_*).
requirements: bio must be valid or NULL.
type must be a BIO_TYPE_* value.

functions.name: BIO_copy_next_retry
functions.description: Copies retry flags and retry_reason from the next BIO in the chain to bio.
requirements: bio must be valid.
bio must have a next BIO to copy from for effect.

functions.name: BIO_printf
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BIO_printf(BIO *bio, const char *format, ...) OPENSSL_PRINTF_FORMAT_FUNC(2, 3);
functions.description: printf-style formatted output to bio. Returns number of bytes written or negative on error.
requirements: bio must be valid and writable.
format must be a valid printf-style format string. Variadic arguments must match format.

functions.name: BIO_indent
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BIO_indent(BIO *bio, unsigned indent, unsigned max_indent);
functions.description: Writes min(indent, max_indent) spaces to bio. Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise.
requirements: bio must be valid and writable.

functions.name: BIO_hexdump
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BIO_hexdump(BIO *bio, const uint8_t *data, size_t len, unsigned indent);
functions.description: Writes a hex dump of data to bio with each line indented by indent spaces. Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise.
requirements: bio must be valid and writable.
data must point to at least len bytes.

functions.name: ERR_print_errors
functions.description: Prints the current OpenSSL/BoringSSL error stack to bio using human-readable strings where possible.
requirements: bio must be valid and writable.

functions.name: BIO_read_asn1
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BIO_read_asn1(BIO *bio, uint8_t **out, size_t *out_len, size_t max_len);
functions.description: Reads a single ASN.1 object from bio. On success sets *out to an allocated buffer (free with OPENSSL_free) and *out_len to its length, and returns 1. Otherwise returns 0. Enforces max_len and 2^32 limits; no long-form tags; indefinite-length reads entire stream up to max_len.
requirements: bio must be readable.
out and out_len must be non-NULL.
max_len limits total object size; function fails if object length exceeds max_len or 2^32.
On failure, an unspecified amount of data may have been consumed from bio.
Caller must free *out with OPENSSL_free on success.

functions.name: BIO_s_mem
functions.description: Returns a BIO_METHOD implementing in-memory buffer BIOs.

functions.name: BIO_new_mem_buf
functions.description: Creates a read-only memory BIO over buf of length len. Does not copy or take ownership of buf. If len < 0, treats buf as NUL-terminated (deprecated behavior).
requirements: buf must remain valid and unchanged for the lifetime of the BIO.
len must be >= 0 to specify exact size; negative length triggers legacy NUL-terminated mode (avoid in new code).

functions.name: BIO_mem_contents
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BIO_mem_contents(const BIO *bio, const uint8_t **out_contents, size_t *out_len);
functions.description: For a writable memory BIO, sets *out_contents to point to the internal buffer and *out_len to its length. Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise.
requirements: bio must be a memory BIO.
out_contents and out_len must be non-NULL.
The returned pointer is owned by the BIO; do not free or modify it; it becomes invalid if the BIO is modified or freed.

functions.name: BIO_get_mem_data
functions.description: Sets *contents to the memory BIO’s current contents and returns the length. Warning: return value 0 may mean either empty buffer or failure; prefer BIO_mem_contents.
requirements: bio must be a memory BIO.
contents must be non-NULL if provided.
Caller must not free or modify the returned buffer pointer.

functions.name: BIO_get_mem_ptr
functions.description: Sets *out to a BUF_MEM describing the memory BIO’s current contents. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: bio must be a memory BIO.
out must be non-NULL.
Caller must not free BUF_MEM unless it has taken ownership via other APIs.

functions.name: BIO_set_mem_buf
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BIO_set_mem_buf(BIO *bio, BUF_MEM *b, int take_ownership);
functions.description: Replaces memory BIO contents with b. If take_ownership is non-zero, b will be freed when the BIO is closed. Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise.
requirements: bio must be a memory BIO.
b must be a valid BUF_MEM or NULL per implementation.
Ownership depends on take_ownership; avoid freeing b if ownership transferred.

functions.name: BIO_set_mem_eof_return
functions.description: Sets read-return value for empty memory BIO. If eof_value == 0, empty reads return EOF (0). If non-zero, reads return eof_value and set retry flag; typically set to -1 for unambiguous signaling. Default: read-only BIOs 0; writable BIOs -1.
requirements: bio must be a memory BIO.
Choose a negative eof_value (typically -1) to avoid ambiguity with normal positive returns.

functions.name: BIO_s_fd
functions.description: Returns a BIO_METHOD for file-descriptor BIOs (POSIX I/O).
requirements: Only available when !OPENSSL_NO_POSIX_IO.

functions.name: BIO_new_fd
functions.description: Creates a new file-descriptor BIO wrapping fd. If close_flag is non-zero, fd will be closed when the BIO is freed.
requirements: Only available when !OPENSSL_NO_POSIX_IO.
fd must be a valid open file descriptor for the process.
close_flag typically BIO_CLOSE (non-zero) or BIO_NOCLOSE (0).

functions.name: BIO_set_fd
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BIO_set_fd(BIO *bio, int fd, int close_flag);
functions.description: Sets bio’s underlying file descriptor to fd. If close_flag is non-zero, fd will be closed when bio is freed. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error. Also usable with socket BIOs.
requirements: bio must be a fd or socket BIO (or compatible).
fd must be a valid descriptor for the platform.
close_flag controls ownership (BIO_CLOSE vs BIO_NOCLOSE).

functions.name: BIO_get_fd
functions.description: Returns the file descriptor currently used by bio or -1 if none. If out_fd is not NULL and a descriptor exists, also stores it at *out_fd. Usable with socket BIOs.
requirements: bio must be a fd/socket/connect BIO (descriptor-capable).
out_fd may be NULL.

functions.name: BIO_s_file
functions.description: Returns a BIO_METHOD for FILE* stream BIOs.

functions.name: BIO_new_file
functions.description: Opens filename with fopen-style mode and wraps it in a file BIO. On Windows, caller must specify text vs binary in mode. Returns new BIO or NULL on error.
requirements: filename and mode must be valid C strings.
The process must have permissions to open filename in the given mode.

functions.name: BIO_new_fp
functions.description: Creates a file BIO wrapping file. If flags includes BIO_CLOSE, fclose will be called when the BIO is closed. On Windows, if flags includes BIO_FP_TEXT, switches the FILE to text mode (not recommended).
requirements: file must be a valid, open FILE*.
flags may include BIO_CLOSE and optionally BIO_FP_TEXT (Windows).
Beware platform mode changes side effects per comments.

functions.name: BIO_get_fp
functions.description: Sets *out_file to the FILE* wrapped by bio. Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise.
requirements: bio must be a file BIO.
out_file must be non-NULL.

functions.name: BIO_set_fp
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BIO_set_fp(BIO *bio, FILE *file, int flags);
functions.description: Sets the FILE* for bio. If flags includes BIO_CLOSE, fclose will be called when bio is closed. Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise. On Windows, BIO_FP_TEXT causes FILE to be switched to text mode.
requirements: bio must be a file BIO.
file must be a valid, open FILE*.
flags may include BIO_CLOSE and, on Windows, BIO_FP_TEXT.

functions.name: BIO_read_filename
functions.description: Opens filename for reading and sets it as bio’s FILE. Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise. The FILE will be closed when bio is freed. On Windows, opens in binary mode.
requirements: bio must be a file BIO.
filename must be a valid path string.
Existing wrapped FILE (if any) may be replaced; ownership per close flag semantics.

functions.name: BIO_write_filename
functions.description: Opens filename for writing and sets it as bio’s FILE. Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise. The FILE will be closed when bio is freed. On Windows, opens in binary mode.
requirements: bio must be a file BIO.
filename must be a valid path and writable.

functions.name: BIO_append_filename
functions.description: Opens filename for appending and sets it as bio’s FILE. Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise. The FILE will be closed when bio is freed. On Windows, opens in binary mode.
requirements: bio must be a file BIO.
filename must be a valid path with append permissions.

functions.name: BIO_rw_filename
functions.description: Opens filename for reading and writing and sets it as bio’s FILE. Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise. The FILE will be closed when bio is freed. On Windows, opens in binary mode.
requirements: bio must be a file BIO.
filename must be a valid path with read/write permissions.

functions.name: BIO_tell
functions.description: Returns current file offset for bio, or negative on error or if unsupported. Note: on 32-bit long platforms, cannot report 64-bit offsets.
requirements: bio must be a file or fd/socket BIO supporting tell semantics.

functions.name: BIO_seek
functions.description: Sets file offset to offset. Returns non-negative on success, negative on error. For fd BIOs returns resulting file offset on success; for file BIOs returns 0 on success. Warning: return conventions differ from most functions; 32-bit long may limit offsets.
requirements: bio must be a file or fd BIO supporting seek.
offset must be within supported range of underlying platform.

functions.name: BIO_s_socket
functions.description: Returns a BIO_METHOD for socket BIOs (wraps recv/send on Windows; read/write elsewhere).
requirements: Only available when !OPENSSL_NO_SOCK.

functions.name: BIO_new_socket
functions.description: Creates a socket BIO wrapping socket fd. If close_flag is BIO_CLOSE (non-zero), closing the BIO closes the socket. Returns BIO or NULL on error.
requirements: Only available when !OPENSSL_NO_SOCK.
fd must be a valid socket handle (int).
close_flag controls ownership.

functions.name: BIO_s_connect
functions.description: Returns a BIO_METHOD for connect BIOs (create and manage outbound socket connections).
requirements: Only available when !OPENSSL_NO_SOCK.

functions.name: BIO_new_connect
functions.description: Creates a connect BIO targeting host_and_optional_port in form "host" or "host:port". If port omitted, must be supplied separately via BIO_set_conn_port. Returns new BIO or NULL.
requirements: Only available when !OPENSSL_NO_SOCK.
host_and_optional_port must be a valid hostname with optional ":port".

functions.name: BIO_set_conn_hostname
functions.description: Sets hostname (and optional port) for a connect BIO. Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise. If port omitted, provide with BIO_set_conn_port.
requirements: bio must be a connect BIO.
host_and_optional_port must be a valid string.

functions.name: BIO_set_conn_port
functions.description: Sets port or service name for a connect BIO. Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise.
requirements: bio must be a connect BIO.
port_str must be a valid service/port string.

functions.name: BIO_set_conn_int_port
functions.description: Sets integer port for a connect BIO. Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise.
requirements: bio must be a connect BIO.
port must point to a valid integer port number in host byte order.

functions.name: BIO_set_nbio
functions.description: Enables/disables non-blocking mode for connect BIOs. Must be called before connecting. Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise. For socket/fd BIOs, configure non-blocking via platform APIs.
requirements: bio must be a connect BIO for effect.
Call before BIO_do_connect to take effect.
on non-zero enables non-blocking; zero disables.

functions.name: BIO_do_connect
functions.description: Initiates the connection for a connect BIO if not already connected. Returns 1 on success, <= 0 otherwise.
requirements: bio must be a connect BIO with hostname and port configured.
May need to handle retry if non-blocking (check BIO_should_retry).

functions.name: BIO_new_bio_pair
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BIO_new_bio_pair(BIO **out1, size_t writebuf1, BIO **out2, size_t writebuf2);
functions.description: Creates two connected BIOs; bytes written to one can be read from the other. writebuf1 and writebuf2 specify each side’s write buffer size. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: out1 and out2 must be non-NULL.
writebuf1 and writebuf2 specify buffer sizes; must be reasonable non-zero sizes per implementation.
Caller must free both BIOs when done (e.g., BIO_free or BIO_free_all).

functions.name: BIO_ctrl_get_read_request
functions.description: For a BIO pair endpoint, returns number of bytes the other side attempted to read unsuccessfully.
requirements: bio must be one end of a BIO pair.

functions.name: BIO_ctrl_get_write_guarantee
functions.description: For a BIO pair endpoint, returns number of bytes bio will accept on the next BIO_write.
requirements: bio must be one end of a BIO pair.

functions.name: BIO_shutdown_wr
functions.description: Marks bio as closed for writing from the peer’s perspective; subsequent BIO_write calls on bio will fail. Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise.
requirements: bio must be one end of a BIO pair.

functions.name: BIO_get_new_index
functions.description: Returns a new type value for user-defined custom BIOs.

functions.name: BIO_meth_new
functions.description: Allocates a new, uninitialized BIO_METHOD with specified type (or 0) and optional name. Initialize with BIO_meth_set_* and mark BIOs initialized with BIO_set_init. Returns BIO_METHOD* or NULL on allocation failure.
requirements: Caller must later free with BIO_meth_free.
Caller must configure required method callbacks before use.

functions.name: BIO_meth_free
functions.description: Frees a BIO_METHOD allocated by BIO_meth_new.
requirements: method may be NULL or a valid BIO_METHOD pointer not used by active BIOs.

functions.name: BIO_meth_set_create
functions.description: Sets the create callback called on BIO_new for this method. Return 1 on success. The callback should return 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: method must be from BIO_meth_new.
create_func must be a valid function pointer.

functions.name: BIO_meth_set_destroy
functions.description: Sets the destroy callback to release method-specific BIO data. Returns 1. Return value of destroy_func is ignored.
requirements: method must be from BIO_meth_new.
destroy_func may be NULL (semantics method-dependent).

functions.name: BIO_meth_set_write
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BIO_meth_set_write(BIO_METHOD *method, int (*write_func)(BIO *, const char *, int));
functions.description: Sets the implementation of BIO_write for method. Returns 1. Methods implementing BIO_write should also implement BIO_CTRL_FLUSH via ctrl.
requirements: method must be from BIO_meth_new.
write_func must match signature (BIO*, const char*, int).

functions.name: BIO_meth_set_read
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BIO_meth_set_read(BIO_METHOD *method, int (*read_func)(BIO *, char *, int));
functions.description: Sets the implementation of BIO_read for method. Returns 1.
requirements: method must be from BIO_meth_new.
read_func must match signature (BIO*, char*, int).

functions.name: BIO_meth_set_gets
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BIO_meth_set_gets(BIO_METHOD *method, int (*gets_func)(BIO *, char *, int));
functions.description: Sets the implementation of BIO_gets for method. Returns 1.
requirements: method must be from BIO_meth_new.
gets_func must match signature (BIO*, char*, int).

functions.name: BIO_meth_set_ctrl
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BIO_meth_set_ctrl(BIO_METHOD *method, long (*ctrl_func)(BIO *, int, long, void *));
functions.description: Sets the implementation of BIO_ctrl for method. Returns 1.
requirements: method must be from BIO_meth_new.
ctrl_func must match signature (BIO*, int, long, void*).

functions.name: BIO_meth_set_callback_ctrl
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BIO_meth_set_callback_ctrl(BIO_METHOD *method, long (*callback_ctrl_func)(BIO *, int, BIO_info_cb *));
functions.description: Sets the implementation of BIO_callback_ctrl for method. Returns 1.
requirements: method must be from BIO_meth_new.
callback_ctrl_func must match signature (BIO*, int, BIO_info_cb*).

functions.name: BIO_set_data
functions.description: Associates custom method-specific data with bio for use by custom BIO implementations.
requirements: Should only be called by custom BIO method implementations; built-in BIOs’ data is private to the library.
ptr may be NULL to clear.

functions.name: BIO_get_data
functions.description: Returns the custom data previously set on bio via BIO_set_data (for custom BIOs).
requirements: Only for use by custom BIO implementations; for general use prefer ex_data/app_data APIs.

functions.name: BIO_set_init
functions.description: Marks whether bio has been fully initialized. Until set, BIO_read/BIO_write will fail.
requirements: Should be called by custom BIO create/init code after setting up internal state.
init non-zero indicates initialized.

functions.name: BIO_get_init
functions.description: Returns whether bio is fully initialized.
requirements: bio must be valid.

functions.name: BIO_get_ex_new_index
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BIO_get_ex_new_index(long argl, void *argp, CRYPTO_EX_unused *unused, CRYPTO_EX_dup *dup_unused, CRYPTO_EX_free *free_func);
functions.description: Allocates a new ex_data index for BIO objects. See ex_data.h for details.
requirements: free_func may be provided for cleanup; other callbacks are unused here as indicated by names.
Arguments usage is per ex_data API; specifics not documented here.

functions.name: BIO_set_ex_data
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BIO_set_ex_data(BIO *bio, int idx, void *arg);
functions.description: Associates application-specific ex_data value arg with index idx on bio. Returns 1 on success.
requirements: bio must be valid.
idx must be an index obtained via BIO_get_ex_new_index or agreed-upon application index.

functions.name: BIO_get_ex_data
functions.description: Retrieves ex_data value for index idx from bio.
requirements: bio must be valid.
idx must be a valid ex_data index.

functions.name: BIO_f_base64
functions.description: Returns a filter BIO_METHOD that base64-encodes writes and decodes reads. BIO_gets is not supported. Call BIO_flush after writing to finalize encoding. The flag BIO_FLAGS_BASE64_NO_NL may put all data on one line. Deprecated: prefer EVP_EncodeBlock / EVP_DecodeBase64.

functions.name: BIO_set_retry_special
functions.description: Marks bio with a special I/O retry condition (sets appropriate flags).
requirements: bio must be valid.

functions.name: BIO_set_write_buffer_size
functions.description: Deprecated compatibility function; returns zero.

functions.name: BIO_set_shutdown
functions.description: Sets a method-specific shutdown bit on bio.
requirements: bio must be valid.
shutdown is an integer flag; semantics are method-specific.

functions.name: BIO_get_shutdown
functions.description: Returns the method-specific shutdown bit.
requirements: bio must be valid.

functions.name: BIO_meth_set_puts
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BIO_meth_set_puts(BIO_METHOD *method, int (*puts)(BIO *, const char *));
functions.description: Sets the puts implementation for a custom BIO method. Returns 1. In BoringSSL, BIO_puts is generally implemented via BIO_write.
requirements: method must be from BIO_meth_new.
puts must match signature (BIO*, const char*).

functions.name: BIO_meth_get_write
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int (*BIO_meth_get_write(const BIO_METHOD *method))(BIO *, const char *, int);
functions.description: Returns a function pointer compatible with BIO_meth_set_write for BIO_s_socket methods. Provided solely for compatibility; inherently unsafe for general use and may diverge from true implementation.
requirements: Only valid/supported when method is BIO_s_socket; otherwise program may abort.
Caller should avoid using this in new code.

functions.name: BIO_meth_get_read
functions.description: Returns a function pointer compatible with BIO_meth_set_read for BIO_s_socket. Compatibility-only; unsafe in general.
requirements: method must be BIO_s_socket; otherwise program may abort.
Avoid in new code.

functions.name: BIO_meth_get_gets
functions.description: Returns a function pointer compatible with BIO_meth_set_gets for BIO_s_socket. Compatibility-only; unsafe in general.
requirements: method must be BIO_s_socket; otherwise program may abort.

functions.name: BIO_meth_get_puts
functions.description: Returns a function pointer compatible with BIO_meth_set_puts for BIO_s_socket. Compatibility-only; unsafe in general.
requirements: method must be BIO_s_socket; otherwise program may abort.

functions.name: BIO_meth_get_ctrl
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT long (*BIO_meth_get_ctrl(const BIO_METHOD *method))(BIO *, int, long, void *);
functions.description: Returns a function pointer compatible with BIO_meth_set_ctrl for BIO_s_socket. Compatibility-only; unsafe in general.
requirements: method must be BIO_s_socket; otherwise program may abort.

functions.name: BIO_meth_get_create
functions.description: Returns a function pointer compatible with BIO_meth_set_create for BIO_s_socket. Compatibility-only; unsafe in general.
requirements: method must be BIO_s_socket; otherwise program may abort.

functions.name: BIO_meth_get_destroy
functions.description: Returns a function pointer compatible with BIO_meth_set_destroy for BIO_s_socket. Compatibility-only; unsafe in general.
requirements: method must be BIO_s_socket; otherwise program may abort.

functions.name: BIO_meth_get_callback_ctrl
functions.description: Returns a function pointer compatible with BIO_meth_set_callback_ctrl for BIO_s_socket. Compatibility-only; unsafe in general.
requirements: method must be BIO_s_socket; otherwise program may abort.

functions.name: BLAKE2B256_Init
functions.description: Initializes a BLAKE2b-256 hashing context. Use this before any Update/Final calls on the same context. The context contains no internal pointers, so its storage and lifetime are fully managed by the caller; no special destructor is needed.
requirements: b2b must be a non-NULL pointer to writable BLAKE2B_CTX storage.
Must be called before BLAKE2B256_Update and BLAKE2B256_Final on the same context.
The caller allocates and manages the context memory; no special free function is required.

functions.name: BLAKE2B256_Update
functions.signature: void BLAKE2B256_Update(BLAKE2B_CTX *b2b, const void *data, size_t len)
functions.description: Appends len bytes from data to the ongoing BLAKE2b-256 hash state in b2b. May be called multiple times between Init and Final to process streaming input.
requirements: b2b must be a non-NULL pointer to a BLAKE2B_CTX that has been initialized with BLAKE2B256_Init.
If len > 0, data must be a non-NULL pointer to at least len readable bytes.
May be called zero or more times after initialization and before BLAKE2B256_Final.

functions.name: BLAKE2B256_Final
functions.description: Finalizes the BLAKE2b-256 computation and writes a 32-byte digest to out. Completes the current hash calculation for the given context.
requirements: out must point to a writable buffer of at least BLAKE2B256_DIGEST_LENGTH (32) bytes.
b2b must be a non-NULL pointer to a BLAKE2B_CTX that has been initialized (and optionally updated).
After finalization, the context should be reinitialized with BLAKE2B256_Init before reuse (inferred from typical hash API patterns).

functions.name: BLAKE2B256
functions.signature: void BLAKE2B256(const uint8_t *data, size_t len, uint8_t out[BLAKE2B256_DIGEST_LENGTH])
functions.description: One-shot convenience function that computes the BLAKE2b-256 digest of len bytes from data and writes the 32-byte result to out.
requirements: If len > 0, data must be a non-NULL pointer to at least len readable bytes.
out must point to a writable buffer of at least BLAKE2B256_DIGEST_LENGTH (32) bytes.

functions.name: BN_new
functions.description: Allocates and initializes a new BIGNUM on the heap. Use BN_free to release it.
requirements: Caller must free the returned BIGNUM with BN_free.
Returns NULL on allocation failure; caller must handle NULL.

functions.name: BN_init
functions.description: Initializes a stack-allocated BIGNUM structure for later use.
requirements: bn must be a valid, writable pointer to uninitialized BIGNUM storage.
Must not be used on heap-allocated BIGNUMs created by BN_new (those are already initialized).

functions.name: BN_free
functions.description: Frees the data referenced by bn and, if bn was heap-allocated, frees bn itself.
requirements: bn may be NULL (no effect).
After calling, bn must not be used again.

functions.name: BN_clear_free
functions.description: Securely clears sensitive data and frees the BIGNUM and its internal buffer.
requirements: bn may be NULL (no effect).
After calling, bn must not be used again.

functions.name: BN_dup
functions.description: Allocates and returns a duplicate of src.
requirements: src must be a valid BIGNUM.
Returns NULL on allocation failure; caller must handle NULL.
Caller must free the returned BIGNUM with BN_free.

functions.name: BN_copy
functions.description: Copies src into dest; returns dest on success or NULL on allocation failure.
requirements: dest and src must be valid BIGNUM pointers.
dest may alias src.
Caller must handle NULL return on allocation failure.

functions.name: BN_clear
functions.description: Sets bn to zero and erases old data.
requirements: bn must be a valid, initialized BIGNUM.

functions.name: BN_value_one
functions.description: Returns a pointer to a static BIGNUM with value 1.
requirements: Returned pointer must not be freed or modified by the caller.

functions.name: BN_num_bits
functions.description: Returns the minimum number of bits needed to represent |bn|’s absolute value.
requirements: bn must be a valid BIGNUM.

functions.name: BN_num_bytes
functions.description: Returns the minimum number of bytes needed to represent |bn|’s absolute value.
requirements: bn must be a valid BIGNUM.
Value fits in int; BIGNUMs are bounded accordingly by library design.

functions.name: BN_zero
functions.description: Sets bn to zero.
requirements: bn must be a valid, initialized BIGNUM.

functions.name: BN_one
functions.description: Sets bn to one. Returns 1 on success, 0 on allocation failure.
requirements: bn must be a valid BIGNUM.
Caller must check return value for allocation failure.

functions.name: BN_set_word
functions.description: Sets bn to the given machine-word value. Returns 1 on success, 0 on allocation failure.
requirements: bn must be a valid BIGNUM.
Caller must check return value for allocation failure.

functions.name: BN_set_u64
functions.description: Sets bn to the given 64-bit unsigned value. Returns 1 on success, 0 on allocation failure.
requirements: bn must be a valid BIGNUM.
Caller must check return value for allocation failure.

functions.name: BN_set_negative
functions.description: Sets the sign flag of bn; sign non-zero makes bn negative, zero makes it non-negative.
requirements: bn must be a valid BIGNUM.
Only the sign flag changes; magnitude unchanged.

functions.name: BN_is_negative
functions.description: Returns 1 if bn is negative, 0 otherwise.
requirements: bn must be a valid BIGNUM.

functions.name: BN_bin2bn
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT BIGNUM *BN_bin2bn(const uint8_t *in, size_t len, BIGNUM *ret);
functions.description: Parses a big-endian byte array into a BIGNUM. If ret is NULL a new BIGNUM is allocated; otherwise ret is reused. Returns the result or NULL on allocation failure.
requirements: in may be NULL only if len==0 (implicit from typical usage; not explicitly stated).
If ret is non-NULL, it must be an initialized BIGNUM suitable for reuse.
Caller must free the returned BIGNUM if a new one is allocated.

functions.name: BN_bn2bin
functions.description: Serializes the absolute value of in to big-endian bytes into out. Writes exactly BN_num_bytes(in) bytes and returns that count.
requirements: out must have at least BN_num_bytes(in) bytes available.
Leaks the magnitude of in; use BN_bn2bin_padded for secret values.

functions.name: BN_lebin2bn
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT BIGNUM *BN_lebin2bn(const uint8_t *in, size_t len, BIGNUM *ret);
functions.description: Parses a little-endian byte array into a BIGNUM. If ret is NULL, allocates a new BIGNUM. Returns the result or NULL on allocation failure.
requirements: If ret is non-NULL, it must be an initialized BIGNUM suitable for reuse.
Caller must free the returned BIGNUM if allocated.

functions.name: BN_bn2le_padded
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_bn2le_padded(uint8_t *out, size_t len, const BIGNUM *in);
functions.description: Serializes |in|’s absolute value to little-endian in exactly len bytes, zero-padding as needed. Returns 1 on success, 0 if len is too small.
requirements: out must have at least len bytes available.
Fails if len < BN_num_bytes(in).

functions.name: BN_bn2bin_padded
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_bn2bin_padded(uint8_t *out, size_t len, const BIGNUM *in);
functions.description: Serializes |in|’s absolute value to big-endian in exactly len bytes, left-padded with zeros. Returns 1 on success, 0 if len is too small.
requirements: out must have at least len bytes available.
Fails if len < BN_num_bytes(in).

functions.name: BN_bn2cbb_padded
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_bn2cbb_padded(CBB *out, size_t len, const BIGNUM *in);
functions.description: Appends |in| serialized as big-endian, zero-left-padded to len bytes, to a CBB. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: out must be a valid, initialized CBB with sufficient space (growth may allocate).
Fails if len < BN_num_bytes(in).

functions.name: BN_bn2hex
functions.description: Returns a newly-allocated NUL-terminated hex string of bn (with leading '-' if negative).
requirements: Caller must free the returned string with OPENSSL_free (per OpenSSL/BoringSSL conventions).
Returns NULL on allocation failure; caller must handle NULL.

functions.name: BN_hex2bn
functions.description: Parses a leading hexadecimal integer from in (optional leading '-'; trailing non-hex allowed). If *outp is NULL, allocates a new BIGNUM and stores it; otherwise reuses *outp. Returns number of input bytes consumed, or 0 on error.
requirements: outp may be NULL to only parse/validate? (Header states: If |outp| is not NULL, construct and store; behavior when outp==NULL is not explicitly defined; recommended to pass non-NULL).
If *outp is NULL, allocation may occur; caller must free the allocated BIGNUM.
Input may include '-' to indicate negative.

functions.name: BN_bn2dec
functions.description: Returns a newly-allocated NUL-terminated decimal string representation of a (with leading '-' if negative).
requirements: Converting very large integers is quadratic in bit length; callers should cap input sizes for performance.
Caller must free the returned string; returns NULL on allocation failure.

functions.name: BN_dec2bn
functions.description: Parses a leading decimal integer from in (optional leading '-'; trailing non-decimal allowed). If *outp is NULL, allocates a new BIGNUM and stores it; otherwise reuses *outp. Returns the number of input bytes consumed, or 0 on error.
requirements: outp should be non-NULL to receive result.
If *outp is NULL, allocation may occur; caller must free the allocated BIGNUM.
Performance is quadratic in bit length; callers should cap input sizes.

functions.name: BN_asc2bn
functions.description: Parses a leading integer from in in hex if prefixed by 0x/0X (after optional '-'), otherwise decimal. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: outp must be non-NULL to receive the constructed BIGNUM.
If *outp is NULL, a new BIGNUM is allocated; caller must free it.
Input may include leading '-' followed by optional 0x/0X.

functions.name: BN_print
functions.description: Writes a hex encoding of a to the BIO. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: bio must be a valid, writable BIO.

functions.name: BN_print_fp
functions.description: Writes a hex encoding of a to the FILE*, via a temporary BIO. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: fp must be a valid FILE* opened for writing.

functions.name: BN_get_word
functions.description: Returns the absolute value of bn as a single machine word; if too large, returns the maximum BN_ULONG.
requirements: bn must be a valid BIGNUM.
Caller must note saturation behavior for large bn.

functions.name: BN_get_u64
functions.description: Writes the absolute value of bn into *out as uint64_t and returns 1; returns 0 if bn does not fit.
requirements: bn must be a valid BIGNUM.
out must be a non-NULL pointer to uint64_t.
Caller must check return value to distinguish success vs overflow.

functions.name: BN_parse_asn1_unsigned
functions.description: Parses a non-negative DER INTEGER from cbs into ret. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: cbs must point to a CBS containing a DER INTEGER at the current position.
ret must be a valid BIGNUM.
Parsed integer must be non-negative; negatives are rejected.

functions.name: BN_marshal_asn1
functions.description: Appends bn encoded as a non-negative DER INTEGER to cbb. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: cbb must be a valid, initialized CBB.
bn must be non-negative (function marshals non-negative form).

functions.name: BN_CTX_new
functions.description: Allocates a new BN_CTX (temporary BIGNUM pool). Returns NULL on allocation failure.
requirements: Caller must free the returned BN_CTX with BN_CTX_free.
BN_CTX is used to allocate temporaries via BN_CTX_start/BN_CTX_get/BN_CTX_end.

functions.name: BN_CTX_free
functions.description: Frees all BIGNUMs contained in ctx and then frees ctx.
requirements: ctx may be NULL (no effect).
After calling, ctx must not be used again.

functions.name: BN_CTX_start
functions.description: Begins a new BN_CTX frame; subsequent BN_CTX_get calls allocate temporaries within this frame.
requirements: ctx must be a valid BN_CTX.
Must be paired with BN_CTX_end before returning from the function that started it.
All BN_CTX_get calls must be made before calling other functions that use the same ctx.

functions.name: BN_CTX_get
functions.description: Obtains a temporary BIGNUM from ctx for the current frame. Returns NULL on allocation failure; subsequent calls will return NULL until BN_CTX_end.
requirements: ctx must be a valid BN_CTX and BN_CTX_start must have been called.
Caller must not use returned BIGNUMs after BN_CTX_end.
If this returns NULL, all further BN_CTX_get calls will return NULL until BN_CTX_end.

functions.name: BN_CTX_end
functions.description: Ends the current BN_CTX frame; invalidates all BIGNUMs returned since the matching BN_CTX_start.
requirements: ctx must be a valid BN_CTX.
Must be called after a matching BN_CTX_start before returning from that scope.

functions.name: BN_add
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_add(BIGNUM *r, const BIGNUM *a, const BIGNUM *b);
functions.description: Computes r = a + b. Returns 1 on success, 0 on allocation failure. r may alias a or b.
requirements: r, a, b must be valid BIGNUMs.
Caller must check return value.

functions.name: BN_uadd
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_uadd(BIGNUM *r, const BIGNUM *a, const BIGNUM *b);
functions.description: Computes r = |a| + |b| (ignores signs). Returns 1 on success, 0 on allocation failure. r may alias a or b.
requirements: r, a, b must be valid BIGNUMs.
Caller must check return value.

functions.name: BN_add_word
functions.description: Adds word w to a in place. Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise.
requirements: a must be a valid BIGNUM.
Caller must check return value.

functions.name: BN_sub
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_sub(BIGNUM *r, const BIGNUM *a, const BIGNUM *b);
functions.description: Computes r = a - b. Returns 1 on success, 0 on allocation failure. r may alias a or b.
requirements: r, a, b must be valid BIGNUMs.
Caller must check return value.

functions.name: BN_usub
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_usub(BIGNUM *r, const BIGNUM *a, const BIGNUM *b);
functions.description: Computes r = |a| - |b| (ignores signs). Requires |b| <= |a|. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error. r may alias a or b.
requirements: r, a, b must be valid BIGNUMs.
Requires |b| <= |a| (non-negative result).
Caller must check return value.

functions.name: BN_sub_word
functions.description: Subtracts word w from a in place. Returns 1 on success, 0 on allocation failure.
requirements: a must be a valid BIGNUM.
Caller must check return value.

functions.name: BN_mul
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_mul(BIGNUM *r, const BIGNUM *a, const BIGNUM *b, BN_CTX *ctx);
functions.description: Computes r = a * b. r may alias a or b. Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise.
requirements: r, a, b must be valid BIGNUMs.
ctx may be NULL (function will create a local BN_CTX).
Caller must check return value.

functions.name: BN_mul_word
functions.description: Multiplies bn by word w in place. Returns 1 on success, 0 on allocation failure.
requirements: bn must be a valid BIGNUM.
Caller must check return value.

functions.name: BN_sqr
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_sqr(BIGNUM *r, const BIGNUM *a, BN_CTX *ctx);
functions.description: Computes r = a^2 efficiently (may be faster than BN_mul). Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise. r may alias a.
requirements: r and a must be valid BIGNUMs.
ctx may be NULL (a local BN_CTX will be created).
Caller must check return value.

functions.name: BN_div
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_div(BIGNUM *quotient, BIGNUM *rem, const BIGNUM *numerator, const BIGNUM *divisor, BN_CTX *ctx);
functions.description: Divides numerator by divisor. Writes quotient and remainder if non-NULL. Rounds quotient toward zero; remainder has same sign behavior accordingly. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: divisor must be non-zero; zero is an error.
quotient and/or rem may be NULL to skip that output.
r, inputs must be valid BIGNUMs.
ctx may be NULL (local BN_CTX will be used).
Caller must check return value and handle errors.

functions.name: BN_div_word
functions.description: Computes numerator = numerator / divisor in place, returns the remainder, or (BN_ULONG)-1 on error.
requirements: divisor must be non-zero.
numerator must be a valid BIGNUM.
Caller must check for (BN_ULONG)-1 to detect errors.

functions.name: BN_sqrt
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_sqrt(BIGNUM *out_sqrt, const BIGNUM *in, BN_CTX *ctx);
functions.description: Computes integer square root of in and stores in out_sqrt. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error. Negative inputs and non-squares produce errors with appropriate error codes.
requirements: in must be non-negative and a perfect square to succeed.
out_sqrt must be a valid BIGNUM (may alias in).
ctx must be a valid BN_CTX (may be NULL to use a local context).
Caller must check return value and error queue for details.

functions.name: BN_cmp
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_cmp(const BIGNUM *a, const BIGNUM *b);
functions.description: Three-way comparison of a and b. Returns <0, 0, >0 for a<b, a==b, a>b.
requirements: a and b must be valid BIGNUMs.

functions.name: BN_cmp_word
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_cmp_word(const BIGNUM *a, BN_ULONG b);
functions.description: Three-way comparison of a and the word b.
requirements: a must be a valid BIGNUM.

functions.name: BN_ucmp
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_ucmp(const BIGNUM *a, const BIGNUM *b);
functions.description: Three-way comparison of |a| and |b|, comparing absolute values only.
requirements: a and b must be valid BIGNUMs.

functions.name: BN_equal_consttime
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_equal_consttime(const BIGNUM *a, const BIGNUM *b);
functions.description: Constant-time equality test: returns 1 if a==b, 0 otherwise (time depends on sizes, not contents).
requirements: a and b must be valid BIGNUMs.

functions.name: BN_abs_is_word
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_abs_is_word(const BIGNUM *bn, BN_ULONG w);
functions.description: Returns 1 if |bn|’s absolute value equals w, 0 otherwise.
requirements: bn must be a valid BIGNUM.

functions.name: BN_is_zero
functions.description: Returns 1 if bn is zero, 0 otherwise.
requirements: bn must be a valid BIGNUM.

functions.name: BN_is_one
functions.description: Returns 1 if bn equals one, 0 otherwise.
requirements: bn must be a valid BIGNUM.

functions.name: BN_is_word
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_is_word(const BIGNUM *bn, BN_ULONG w);
functions.description: Returns 1 if bn equals exactly w (including sign), 0 otherwise.
requirements: bn must be a valid BIGNUM.

functions.name: BN_is_odd
functions.description: Returns 1 if bn is odd, 0 otherwise.
requirements: bn must be a valid BIGNUM.

functions.name: BN_is_pow2
functions.description: Returns 1 if a is a power of two, 0 otherwise.
requirements: a must be a valid BIGNUM.

functions.name: BN_lshift
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_lshift(BIGNUM *r, const BIGNUM *a, int n);
functions.description: Computes r = a << n. Returns 1 on success, 0 on allocation failure. r may alias a.
requirements: a and r must be valid BIGNUMs.
n must be non-negative (implied; negative generally invalid).
Caller must check return value.

functions.name: BN_lshift1
functions.description: Computes r = a << 1. Returns 1 on success, 0 on allocation failure. r may alias a.
requirements: a and r must be valid BIGNUMs.
Caller must check return value.

functions.name: BN_rshift
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_rshift(BIGNUM *r, const BIGNUM *a, int n);
functions.description: Computes r = a >> n (arithmetic on sign). Returns 1 on success, 0 on allocation failure. r may alias a.
requirements: a and r must be valid BIGNUMs.
n must be non-negative (implied).
Caller must check return value.

functions.name: BN_rshift1
functions.description: Computes r = a >> 1. Returns 1 on success, 0 on allocation failure. r may alias a.
requirements: a and r must be valid BIGNUMs.
Caller must check return value.

functions.name: BN_set_bit
functions.description: Sets the nth least-significant bit of a. Returns 1 on success, 0 on allocation failure.
requirements: a must be a valid BIGNUM.
n must be >= 0.
Caller must check return value.

functions.name: BN_clear_bit
functions.description: Clears the nth least-significant bit of a. Returns 1 on success, 0 on allocation failure.
requirements: a must be a valid BIGNUM.
n must be >= 0.
Caller must check return value.

functions.name: BN_is_bit_set
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_is_bit_set(const BIGNUM *a, int n);
functions.description: Returns 1 if the nth least-significant bit of a exists and is set; 0 otherwise.
requirements: a must be a valid BIGNUM.
n must be >= 0.

functions.name: BN_mask_bits
functions.description: Truncates a to n bits. Returns 1 on success or 0 if n is negative.
requirements: a must be a valid BIGNUM.
n must be >= 0.

functions.name: BN_count_low_zero_bits
functions.description: Returns the number of trailing zero bits in bn (factors of two). Returns 0 if bn is zero.
requirements: bn must be a valid BIGNUM.

functions.name: BN_mod_word
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT BN_ULONG BN_mod_word(const BIGNUM *a, BN_ULONG w);
functions.description: Returns a mod w, or (BN_ULONG)-1 on error.
requirements: w should be non-zero (division by zero would be error).
a must be a valid BIGNUM.
Caller must check for (BN_ULONG)-1 indicating error.

functions.name: BN_mod_pow2
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_mod_pow2(BIGNUM *r, const BIGNUM *a, size_t e);
functions.description: Computes r = a mod 2^e. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: r and a must be valid BIGNUMs.
e is the exponent of two; size_t range.

functions.name: BN_nnmod_pow2
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_nnmod_pow2(BIGNUM *r, const BIGNUM *a, size_t e);
functions.description: Computes r = a mod 2^e with r always non-negative. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: r and a must be valid BIGNUMs.
e is the exponent of two.

functions.name: BN_nnmod
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_nnmod(BIGNUM *rem, const BIGNUM *numerator, const BIGNUM *divisor, BN_CTX *ctx);
functions.description: Computes non-negative remainder: rem = numerator mod divisor with 0 <= rem < divisor. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: divisor must be non-zero.
rem, numerator, divisor must be valid BIGNUMs.
ctx may be NULL (local context used).

functions.name: BN_mod_add
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_mod_add(BIGNUM *r, const BIGNUM *a, const BIGNUM *b, const BIGNUM *m, BN_CTX *ctx);
functions.description: Computes r = (a + b) mod m. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: a, b, m, r must be valid BIGNUMs.
m must be non-zero (implied by modulo).
ctx may be NULL (local context used).

functions.name: BN_mod_add_quick
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_mod_add_quick(BIGNUM *r, const BIGNUM *a, const BIGNUM *b, const BIGNUM *m);
functions.description: Like BN_mod_add but requires 0 <= a,b < m; may be faster. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: a and b must be non-negative and less than m.
r, a, b, m must be valid BIGNUMs.

functions.name: BN_mod_sub
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_mod_sub(BIGNUM *r, const BIGNUM *a, const BIGNUM *b, const BIGNUM *m, BN_CTX *ctx);
functions.description: Computes r = (a - b) mod m. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: r, a, b, m must be valid BIGNUMs.
m must be non-zero (implied).
ctx may be NULL (local context used).

functions.name: BN_mod_sub_quick
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_mod_sub_quick(BIGNUM *r, const BIGNUM *a, const BIGNUM *b, const BIGNUM *m);
functions.description: Like BN_mod_sub but requires 0 <= a,b < m; may be faster. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: a and b must be non-negative and less than m.
r, a, b, m must be valid BIGNUMs.

functions.name: BN_mod_mul
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_mod_mul(BIGNUM *r, const BIGNUM *a, const BIGNUM *b, const BIGNUM *m, BN_CTX *ctx);
functions.description: Computes r = (a * b) mod m. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: r, a, b, m must be valid BIGNUMs.
m must be non-zero (implied).
ctx may be NULL (local context used).

functions.name: BN_mod_sqr
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_mod_sqr(BIGNUM *r, const BIGNUM *a, const BIGNUM *m, BN_CTX *ctx);
functions.description: Computes r = (a^2) mod m. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: r, a, m must be valid BIGNUMs.
m must be non-zero (implied).
ctx may be NULL (local context used).

functions.name: BN_mod_lshift
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_mod_lshift(BIGNUM *r, const BIGNUM *a, int n, const BIGNUM *m, BN_CTX *ctx);
functions.description: Computes r = (a << n) mod m. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error. r may alias a.
requirements: r, a, m must be valid BIGNUMs.
n must be >= 0.
ctx may be NULL (local context used).

functions.name: BN_mod_lshift_quick
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_mod_lshift_quick(BIGNUM *r, const BIGNUM *a, int n, const BIGNUM *m);
functions.description: Like BN_mod_lshift but requires a be non-negative and less than m. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: a must be non-negative and less than m.
r, a, m must be valid BIGNUMs.
n must be >= 0.

functions.name: BN_mod_lshift1
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_mod_lshift1(BIGNUM *r, const BIGNUM *a, const BIGNUM *m, BN_CTX *ctx);
functions.description: Computes r = (a << 1) mod m. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error. r may alias a.
requirements: r, a, m must be valid BIGNUMs.
ctx may be NULL (local context used).

functions.name: BN_mod_lshift1_quick
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_mod_lshift1_quick(BIGNUM *r, const BIGNUM *a, const BIGNUM *m);
functions.description: Like BN_mod_lshift1 but requires a be non-negative and less than m. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: a must be non-negative and less than m.
r, a, m must be valid BIGNUMs.

functions.name: BN_mod_sqrt
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT BIGNUM *BN_mod_sqrt(BIGNUM *in, const BIGNUM *a, const BIGNUM *p, BN_CTX *ctx);
functions.description: Computes a square root r of a modulo prime p (r^2 ≡ a mod p). Returns newly-allocated BIGNUM or in if provided, or NULL on error or if a is not a square mod p (error BN_R_NOT_A_SQUARE). May return either square root non-deterministically.
requirements: p must be a prime and > 2 for two roots (function may fail or return arbitrary value if p is composite).
If in is non-NULL, it must be a valid BIGNUM to receive the result.
ctx must be a valid BN_CTX (may be NULL to use a local context).
Caller must not pass attacker-controlled composite p.
Caller must free the returned BIGNUM if a new one is allocated.

functions.name: BN_rand
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_rand(BIGNUM *rnd, int bits, int top, int bottom);
functions.description: Generates a random integer of the specified bit length. top controls setting of the most significant bit(s); bottom controls LSB parity. Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise.
requirements: rnd must be a valid BIGNUM.
bits >= 0 (implied).
top must be one of BN_RAND_TOP_ANY, BN_RAND_TOP_ONE, BN_RAND_TOP_TWO.
bottom must be BN_RAND_BOTTOM_ANY or BN_RAND_BOTTOM_ODD.
Caller must check return value.

functions.name: BN_pseudo_rand
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_pseudo_rand(BIGNUM *rnd, int bits, int top, int bottom);
functions.description: Alias for BN_rand.
requirements: Same as BN_rand.

functions.name: BN_rand_range
functions.description: Sets rnd to a random value in [0, range). Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise.
requirements: rnd and range must be valid BIGNUMs.
range must be positive (implied by interval semantics).
Caller must check return value.

functions.name: BN_rand_range_ex
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_rand_range_ex(BIGNUM *r, BN_ULONG min_inclusive, const BIGNUM *max_exclusive);
functions.description: Sets r to a random value in [min_inclusive, max_exclusive). Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise.
requirements: r and max_exclusive must be valid (max_exclusive a positive BIGNUM).
Requires min_inclusive < max_exclusive (implied by range).
Caller must check return value.

functions.name: BN_pseudo_rand_range
functions.description: Alias for BN_rand_range.
requirements: Same as BN_rand_range.

functions.name: BN_GENCB_new
functions.description: Allocates a new BN_GENCB callback structure. Returns NULL on allocation failure.
requirements: Caller must free with BN_GENCB_free.
Used to receive progress callbacks in long-running generation functions.

functions.name: BN_GENCB_free
functions.description: Frees a BN_GENCB structure.
requirements: callback may be NULL (no effect).

functions.name: BN_GENCB_set
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT void BN_GENCB_set(BN_GENCB *callback, int (*f)(int event, int n, BN_GENCB *), void *arg);
functions.description: Initializes callback to call f with user data arg for progress notifications.
requirements: callback must be a valid BN_GENCB pointer.
f may be NULL to disable callbacks.
arg is stored as-is in the structure.

functions.name: BN_GENCB_call
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_GENCB_call(BN_GENCB *callback, int event, int n);
functions.description: Invokes the callback if non-NULL, returning its result; returns 1 if callback is NULL.
requirements: callback may be NULL; then returns 1.
Callback function should return 0 to abort or 1 to continue (per convention).

functions.name: BN_GENCB_get_arg
functions.description: Returns the user-supplied arg stored in callback.
requirements: callback must be a valid BN_GENCB pointer.

functions.name: BN_generate_prime_ex
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_generate_prime_ex(BIGNUM *ret, int bits, int safe, const BIGNUM *add, const BIGNUM *rem, BN_GENCB *cb);
functions.description: Generates a prime of given bit length into ret. If safe!=0, generates a safe prime ((p-1)/2 also prime). If add/rem provided, enforces ret % add == rem (or 1 if rem==NULL). Calls cb for progress if non-NULL. Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise.
requirements: ret must be a valid BIGNUM to receive the result.
bits must be positive enough to represent the desired size.
If add is non-NULL, rem may be NULL to imply remainder 1.
cb may be NULL or a valid BN_GENCB.

functions.name: BN_enhanced_miller_rabin_primality_test
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_enhanced_miller_rabin_primality_test(enum bn_primality_result_t *out_result, const BIGNUM *w, int checks, BN_CTX *ctx, BN_GENCB *cb);
functions.description: Performs the Enhanced Miller-Rabin primality test on odd integers >3 with a given number of iterations. Writes the result code to out_result. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure. Calls cb each iteration if non-NULL.
requirements: out_result must be non-NULL to receive the result.
w must be a valid BIGNUM; only odd integers >3 are tested by the algorithm (others result per implementation).
checks controls iterations; see BN_prime_checks_* for guidance.
ctx may be NULL (local context used).
cb may be NULL or a valid BN_GENCB.

functions.name: BN_primality_test
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_primality_test(int *is_probably_prime, const BIGNUM *candidate, int checks, BN_CTX *ctx, int do_trial_division, BN_GENCB *cb);
functions.description: Tests if candidate is probably prime using trial division (optional) and Miller-Rabin. Sets *is_probably_prime to 1 if probably prime, 0 if composite. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: is_probably_prime must be a non-NULL pointer to int.
candidate must be a valid BIGNUM.
checks controls the false-positive rate; see BN_prime_checks_* constants.
ctx may be NULL (local context used).
do_trial_division non-zero enables small-prime trial division.
cb may be NULL or a valid BN_GENCB.

functions.name: BN_is_prime_fasttest_ex
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_is_prime_fasttest_ex(const BIGNUM *candidate, int checks, BN_CTX *ctx, int do_trial_division, BN_GENCB *cb);
functions.description: Deprecated. Returns 1 if candidate is probably prime, 0 if composite, -1 on error, using Miller-Rabin (optional trial division).
requirements: Use BN_primality_test instead for new code.
candidate must be a valid BIGNUM.
checks controls the false-positive rate; see BN_prime_checks_* constants.
ctx may be NULL (local context used).
cb may be NULL or valid BN_GENCB.

functions.name: BN_is_prime_ex
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_is_prime_ex(const BIGNUM *candidate, int checks, BN_CTX *ctx, BN_GENCB *cb);
functions.description: Deprecated. Equivalent to BN_is_prime_fasttest_ex with do_trial_division=0.
requirements: Use BN_primality_test instead for new code.
candidate must be a valid BIGNUM.
ctx may be NULL (local context used).
cb may be NULL or valid BN_GENCB.

functions.name: BN_gcd
