functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_gcd(BIGNUM *r, const BIGNUM *a, const BIGNUM *b, BN_CTX *ctx);
functions.description: Computes r = gcd(|a|, |b|). Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise.
requirements: r, a, b must be valid BIGNUMs.
ctx may be NULL (local context used).

functions.name: BN_mod_inverse
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT BIGNUM *BN_mod_inverse(BIGNUM *out, const BIGNUM *a, const BIGNUM *n, BN_CTX *ctx);
functions.description: Computes modular inverse of a modulo n and returns out (or a newly-allocated BIGNUM if out==NULL), or NULL on error. Not constant-time for even n; avoid with secrets.
requirements: a, n must be valid BIGNUMs; n must be non-zero; a and n should be co-prime to have an inverse.
If out is NULL, caller must free the returned BIGNUM.
If n is even, algorithm may have side-channel leaks; do not use with secret values.
For constant-time with secret exponents/moduli, prefer BN_mod_inverse_blinded or exponentiation trick when n is prime.
ctx may be NULL (local context used).

functions.name: BN_mod_inverse_blinded
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_mod_inverse_blinded(BIGNUM *out, int *out_no_inverse, const BIGNUM *a, const BN_MONT_CTX *mont, BN_CTX *ctx);
functions.description: Computes out = a^{-1} mod n using blinding, where n is the modulus in mont. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure and sets *out_no_inverse=1 if a has no inverse mod n.
requirements: a must be non-negative and less than n (the mont modulus).
n must be > 1 (as stored in mont).
mont must be a valid BN_MONT_CTX with modulus n.
out must be a valid BIGNUM.
out_no_inverse must be non-NULL to receive whether no inverse exists.
May falsely report no inverse if the random blinding value is non-invertible; suitable when n has few non-invertible elements (e.g., RSA modulus).
ctx may be NULL (local context used).

functions.name: BN_mod_inverse_odd
functions.signature: int BN_mod_inverse_odd(BIGNUM *out, int *out_no_inverse, const BIGNUM *a, const BIGNUM *n, BN_CTX *ctx);
functions.description: Computes out = a^{-1} mod n for odd n. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure and sets *out_no_inverse=1 if a has no inverse. Not constant-time; use BN_mod_inverse_blinded for secrets.
requirements: a must be non-negative and less than n.
n must be odd and > 1.
out must be a valid BIGNUM; out_no_inverse must be non-NULL.
ctx may be NULL (local context used).

functions.name: BN_MONT_CTX_new_for_modulus
functions.description: Allocates and initializes a Montgomery context for modulus mod (treated as public). Returns NULL on error.
requirements: mod must be a valid modulus BIGNUM (typically odd and >1; specific constraints not restated here).
ctx may be NULL (local context used).
Caller must free the returned BN_MONT_CTX with BN_MONT_CTX_free.

functions.name: BN_MONT_CTX_new_consttime
functions.description: Allocates and initializes a Montgomery context for modulus mod, treating mod as secret (constant-time where applicable). Returns NULL on error.
requirements: mod must be a valid modulus BIGNUM.
ctx may be NULL (local context used).
Caller must free the returned BN_MONT_CTX with BN_MONT_CTX_free.

functions.name: BN_MONT_CTX_free
functions.description: Frees a BN_MONT_CTX and associated memory.
requirements: mont may be NULL (no effect).

functions.name: BN_MONT_CTX_copy
functions.description: Copies the Montgomery context from to to. Returns to on success, NULL on error.
requirements: to and from must be valid BN_MONT_CTX pointers.
Caller must handle NULL return on error.

functions.name: BN_to_montgomery
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_to_montgomery(BIGNUM *ret, const BIGNUM *a, const BN_MONT_CTX *mont, BN_CTX *ctx);
functions.description: Transforms a into Montgomery domain: ret = a*R mod n. Assumes 0 <= a < n. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: a must be in [0, n), where n is mont modulus.
ret must be a valid BIGNUM; may alias a.
mont must be a valid BN_MONT_CTX.
ctx may be NULL (local context used).

functions.name: BN_from_montgomery
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_from_montgomery(BIGNUM *ret, const BIGNUM *a, const BN_MONT_CTX *mont, BN_CTX *ctx);
functions.description: Converts from Montgomery domain: ret = a * R^{-1} mod n. Assumes a in [0, n*R); n < R so [0, n*n) valid. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: a must be within [0, n*R).
ret must be a valid BIGNUM; may alias a.
mont must be a valid BN_MONT_CTX.
ctx may be NULL (local context used).

functions.name: BN_mod_mul_montgomery
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_mod_mul_montgomery(BIGNUM *r, const BIGNUM *a, const BIGNUM *b, const BN_MONT_CTX *mont, BN_CTX *ctx);
functions.description: Computes r = a*b mod n in Montgomery domain, where a and b are already in Montgomery form and in [0, n). Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: a and b must be in Montgomery domain and in [0, n).
r must be a valid BIGNUM; may alias inputs.
mont must be a valid BN_MONT_CTX.
ctx may be NULL (local context used).

functions.name: BN_exp
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_exp(BIGNUM *r, const BIGNUM *a, const BIGNUM *p, BN_CTX *ctx);
functions.description: Computes r = a^p using square-and-multiply (not constant-time). Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise.
requirements: r, a, p must be valid BIGNUMs.
Not suitable for secret exponents/bases due to side channels.
ctx may be NULL (local context used).

functions.name: BN_mod_exp
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_mod_exp(BIGNUM *r, const BIGNUM *a, const BIGNUM *p, const BIGNUM *m, BN_CTX *ctx);
functions.description: Computes r = a^p mod m using the best algorithm for provided values. Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise. Use consttime variants when secrets involved.
requirements: r, a, p, m must be valid BIGNUMs; m must be non-zero.
ctx may be NULL (local context used).
For secret exponents, use BN_mod_exp_mont_consttime.

functions.name: BN_mod_exp_mont
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_mod_exp_mont(BIGNUM *r, const BIGNUM *a, const BIGNUM *p, const BIGNUM *m, BN_CTX *ctx, const BN_MONT_CTX *mont);
functions.description: Computes r = a^p mod m using Montgomery arithmetic, treating a as secret, requiring 0 <= a < m. Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise.
requirements: r, a, p, m must be valid BIGNUMs; mont must be a valid BN_MONT_CTX for m.
ctx may be NULL (local context used).

functions.name: BN_mod_exp_mont_consttime
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_mod_exp_mont_consttime(BIGNUM *rr, const BIGNUM *a, const BIGNUM *p, const BIGNUM *m, BN_CTX *ctx, const BN_MONT_CTX *mont);
functions.description: Constant-time modular exponentiation: rr = a^p mod m, treating a, p, m as secret and requiring 0 <= a < m. Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise.
requirements: rr, a, p, m must be valid BIGNUMs; mont must be a valid BN_MONT_CTX for m.
ctx may be NULL (local context used).
Use when operands are secret to avoid side channels.

functions.name: BN_bn2mpi
functions.description: Deprecated serialization: writes length-prefixed big-endian MPI format of in to out. If out==NULL, returns required size. Returns bytes written (or required size).
requirements: out must have sufficient space if non-NULL (query by calling with out==NULL).
Use only for compatibility; prefer modern encodings.

functions.name: BN_mpi2bn
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT BIGNUM *BN_mpi2bn(const uint8_t *in, size_t len, BIGNUM *out);
functions.description: Parses MPI format (from BN_bn2mpi) from in,len. If out==NULL, allocates a new BIGNUM; else reuses out. Returns result or NULL on error.
requirements: in must point to len bytes of MPI data.
If out is NULL, caller must free returned BIGNUM.
Returns NULL and updates error queue on parse error.

functions.name: BN_mod_exp_mont_word
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_mod_exp_mont_word(BIGNUM *r, BN_ULONG a, const BIGNUM *p, const BIGNUM *m, BN_CTX *ctx, const BN_MONT_CTX *mont);
functions.description: Modular exponentiation with word base: r = a^p mod m using Montgomery arithmetic. Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise.
requirements: r, p, m must be valid BIGNUMs; mont must be a valid BN_MONT_CTX for m.
ctx may be NULL (local context used).

functions.name: BN_mod_exp2_mont
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_mod_exp2_mont(BIGNUM *r, const BIGNUM *a1, const BIGNUM *p1, const BIGNUM *a2, const BIGNUM *p2, const BIGNUM *m, BN_CTX *ctx, const BN_MONT_CTX *mont);
functions.description: Computes r = (a1^p1) * (a2^p2) mod m using Montgomery arithmetic. Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise.
requirements: r, a1, p1, a2, p2, m must be valid BIGNUMs; mont must be valid for m.
ctx may be NULL (local context used).

functions.name: BN_MONT_CTX_new
functions.description: Deprecated: allocates an uninitialized BN_MONT_CTX. Use BN_MONT_CTX_new_for_modulus instead.
requirements: Caller must initialize with BN_MONT_CTX_set or use the newer constructor.
Caller must free with BN_MONT_CTX_free.

functions.name: BN_MONT_CTX_set
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_MONT_CTX_set(BN_MONT_CTX *mont, const BIGNUM *mod, BN_CTX *ctx);
functions.description: Deprecated: initializes mont for modulus mod. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error. Prefer BN_MONT_CTX_new_for_modulus.
requirements: mont must be a valid BN_MONT_CTX (typically from BN_MONT_CTX_new).
mod must be a valid modulus BIGNUM.
ctx may be NULL (local context used).

functions.name: BN_bn2binpad
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_bn2binpad(const BIGNUM *in, uint8_t *out, int len);
functions.description: Deprecated: big-endian, left-padded serialization like BN_bn2bin_padded, but returns len on success and -1 on error (int sizes).
requirements: out must have at least len bytes available.
Use BN_bn2bin_padded instead (size_t-clean).

functions.name: BN_bn2lebinpad
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int BN_bn2lebinpad(const BIGNUM *in, uint8_t *out, int len);
functions.description: Deprecated: little-endian, zero-padded serialization like BN_bn2le_padded, but returns len on success and -1 on error.
requirements: out must have at least len bytes available.
Use BN_bn2le_padded instead (size_t-clean).

functions.name: BN_secure_new
functions.description: Compatibility alias that calls BN_new.
requirements: Caller must free with BN_free.
Returns NULL on allocation failure.

functions.name: BN_le2bn
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT BIGNUM *BN_le2bn(const uint8_t *in, size_t len, BIGNUM *ret);
functions.description: Alias that calls BN_lebin2bn (little-endian bytes to BIGNUM).
requirements: Same as BN_lebin2bn.

functions.name: BN_num_bits_word
functions.description: Returns the number of bits required to represent the non-negative word l.
requirements: Input is a machine word; function behavior for arbitrary values is defined (counts bits).

functions.name: BUF_MEM_new
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new BUF_MEM structure with no allocated data buffer. Use to initialize a resizable buffer before reserving or growing storage.
requirements: Caller must check the return value for NULL to detect allocation failure.
The returned BUF_MEM must later be released with BUF_MEM_free.

functions.name: BUF_MEM_free
functions.description: Frees the memory owned by a BUF_MEM: releases buf->data if allocated and then frees the BUF_MEM object itself.
requirements: buf must be a valid BUF_MEM previously obtained from BUF_MEM_new (or compatible creator) and not already freed.
After return, buf must not be used again.

functions.name: BUF_MEM_reserve
functions.description: Ensures that buf has at least cap bytes of capacity, allocating or reallocating the internal buffer if needed. Does not change the logical length.
requirements: buf must be a valid, initialized BUF_MEM (e.g., from BUF_MEM_new).
cap is the required capacity in bytes; it should be large enough for subsequent writes.
Returns 1 on success and 0 on error; callers must check the return value before using the buffer capacity.

functions.name: BUF_MEM_grow
functions.description: Ensures that buf’s logical length is exactly len, allocating memory if needed. If the length increases, newly added bytes are zero-filled. Returns the resulting length on success or 0 on error.
requirements: buf must be a valid, initialized BUF_MEM.
len is the desired length in bytes; growing may reallocate the internal buffer.
Callers must check the return value: 0 indicates an error, otherwise the return equals buf->length.

functions.name: BUF_MEM_grow_clean
functions.description: Convenience wrapper that calls BUF_MEM_grow. In BoringSSL, freed memory is always zeroed; newly grown bytes are zero-filled as per BUF_MEM_grow.
requirements: buf must be a valid, initialized BUF_MEM.
len is the desired length in bytes.
Callers must check the return value: 0 indicates an error.

functions.name: BUF_MEM_append
functions.signature: int BUF_MEM_append(BUF_MEM *buf, const void *in, size_t len);
functions.description: Appends len bytes from in to the end of buf, growing the buffer as needed. Returns 1 on success and 0 on error.
requirements: buf must be a valid, initialized BUF_MEM.
If len > 0, in must point to at least len readable bytes.
On success, buf->length increases by len; callers must check the return value (1 success, 0 error).

functions.name: BUF_strdup
functions.description: Deprecated wrapper that calls OPENSSL_strdup to duplicate a NUL-terminated string. Returns a newly allocated copy.
requirements: str must point to a NUL-terminated string.
Callers must check for NULL return indicating allocation failure.
The returned string must be freed with the appropriate deallocator for OPENSSL allocations (e.g., OPENSSL_free).

functions.name: BUF_strnlen
functions.description: Deprecated wrapper that calls OPENSSL_strnlen to compute the length of a string up to a maximum bound.
requirements: str must be a readable pointer to memory for up to max_len bytes or until a NUL terminator is found, whichever comes first.

functions.name: BUF_strndup
functions.description: Deprecated wrapper that calls OPENSSL_strndup to duplicate up to size bytes from a string, NUL-terminating the result. Returns a newly allocated string.
requirements: str must be a readable pointer to memory for up to size bytes (and may be NUL-terminated earlier).
Callers must check for NULL return indicating allocation failure.
The returned string must be freed with the appropriate OPENSSL deallocator.

functions.name: BUF_memdup
functions.description: Deprecated wrapper that calls OPENSSL_memdup to duplicate an arbitrary memory block of length size. Returns a newly allocated buffer with a byte-for-byte copy.
requirements: If size > 0, data must point to at least size readable bytes.
Callers must check for NULL return indicating allocation failure.
The returned pointer must be freed with the appropriate OPENSSL deallocator.

functions.name: BUF_strlcpy
functions.signature: size_t BUF_strlcpy(char *dst, const char *src, size_t dst_size);
functions.description: Deprecated wrapper that calls OPENSSL_strlcpy to copy a NUL-terminated src into dst with size bounding similar to strlcpy semantics.
requirements: dst must point to a writable buffer of at least dst_size bytes.
src must point to a NUL-terminated string readable by the caller.
Callers should use the return value per OPENSSL_strlcpy semantics to detect truncation; behavior is otherwise per the underlying implementation.

functions.name: BUF_strlcat
functions.signature: size_t BUF_strlcat(char *dst, const char *src, size_t dst_size);
functions.description: Deprecated wrapper that calls OPENSSL_strlcat to append a NUL-terminated src to dst with size bounding similar to strlcat semantics.
requirements: dst must point to a writable buffer of at least dst_size bytes and be a valid C string if concatenation is intended.
src must point to a NUL-terminated string readable by the caller.
Callers should use the return value per OPENSSL_strlcat semantics to detect truncation; behavior is otherwise per the underlying implementation.

functions.name: EVP_rc4
functions.description: Returns an EVP_CIPHER object for the RC4 stream cipher. Use with EVP_CipherInit_ex/EVP_EncryptInit_ex/EVP_DecryptInit_ex to configure an EVP_CIPHER_CTX.
requirements: None specific. Use the returned cipher with an initialized EVP_CIPHER_CTX.

functions.name: EVP_des_cbc
functions.description: Returns an EVP_CIPHER for DES in CBC mode.
requirements: Key and IV sizes must match EVP_CIPHER_key_length() and EVP_CIPHER_iv_length() when initializing a context.

functions.name: EVP_des_ecb
functions.description: Returns an EVP_CIPHER for DES in ECB mode.
requirements: Key size must match EVP_CIPHER_key_length() when initializing a context.
ECB mode has no IV.

functions.name: EVP_des_ede
functions.description: Returns an EVP_CIPHER for two-key 3DES (DES-EDE) in ECB mode (per OpenSSL/BoringSSL naming).
requirements: Key size must match EVP_CIPHER_key_length() when initializing a context.
ECB mode has no IV.

functions.name: EVP_des_ede3
functions.description: Returns an EVP_CIPHER for three-key 3DES (DES-EDE3) in ECB mode.
requirements: Key size must match EVP_CIPHER_key_length() when initializing a context.
ECB mode has no IV.

functions.name: EVP_des_ede_cbc
functions.description: Returns an EVP_CIPHER for two-key 3DES (DES-EDE) in CBC mode.
requirements: Key and IV sizes must match EVP_CIPHER_key_length() and EVP_CIPHER_iv_length() when initializing a context.

functions.name: EVP_des_ede3_cbc
functions.description: Returns an EVP_CIPHER for three-key 3DES (DES-EDE3) in CBC mode.
requirements: Key and IV sizes must match EVP_CIPHER_key_length() and EVP_CIPHER_iv_length() when initializing a context.

functions.name: EVP_aes_128_ecb
functions.description: Returns an EVP_CIPHER for AES-128 in ECB mode.
requirements: Key size must match EVP_CIPHER_key_length() when initializing a context.
ECB mode has no IV.

functions.name: EVP_aes_128_cbc
functions.description: Returns an EVP_CIPHER for AES-128 in CBC mode.
requirements: Key and IV sizes must match EVP_CIPHER_key_length() and EVP_CIPHER_iv_length() when initializing a context.

functions.name: EVP_aes_128_ctr
functions.description: Returns an EVP_CIPHER for AES-128 in CTR mode (stream-like).
requirements: Key and IV/nonce sizes must match the cipher’s expected lengths when initializing a context.

functions.name: EVP_aes_128_ofb
functions.description: Returns an EVP_CIPHER for AES-128 in OFB mode (stream-like).
requirements: Key and IV sizes must match the cipher’s expected lengths when initializing a context.

functions.name: EVP_aes_256_ecb
functions.description: Returns an EVP_CIPHER for AES-256 in ECB mode.
requirements: Key size must match EVP_CIPHER_key_length() when initializing a context.
ECB mode has no IV.

functions.name: EVP_aes_256_cbc
functions.description: Returns an EVP_CIPHER for AES-256 in CBC mode.
requirements: Key and IV sizes must match EVP_CIPHER_key_length() and EVP_CIPHER_iv_length() when initializing a context.

functions.name: EVP_aes_256_ctr
functions.description: Returns an EVP_CIPHER for AES-256 in CTR mode (stream-like).
requirements: Key and IV/nonce sizes must match the cipher’s expected lengths when initializing a context.

functions.name: EVP_aes_256_ofb
functions.description: Returns an EVP_CIPHER for AES-256 in OFB mode (stream-like).
requirements: Key and IV sizes must match the cipher’s expected lengths when initializing a context.

functions.name: EVP_aes_256_xts
functions.description: Returns an EVP_CIPHER for AES-256 in XTS mode (tweakable block cipher for disk encryption).
requirements: Key and IV/tweak sizes must match the cipher’s expected lengths when initializing a context.

functions.name: EVP_enc_null
functions.description: Returns a 'cipher' that passes plaintext through as ciphertext. Useful for testing or plumbing.
requirements: None specific. No encryption occurs.

functions.name: EVP_rc2_cbc
functions.description: Returns an EVP_CIPHER implementing 128-bit RC2 in CBC mode.
requirements: Key and IV sizes must match EVP_CIPHER_key_length() and EVP_CIPHER_iv_length() when initializing a context.

functions.name: EVP_get_cipherbynid
functions.description: Returns the EVP_CIPHER corresponding to the NID, or NULL if unknown. Note: using this may link most ciphers into the binary.
requirements: nid must be a NID for a known cipher or the function returns NULL.

functions.name: EVP_CIPHER_CTX_init
functions.description: Initializes an already-allocated EVP_CIPHER_CTX.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, allocated pointer.
Must be called before using the context with other EVP_CIPHER_CTX APIs unless using EVP_CIPHER_CTX_new.

functions.name: EVP_CIPHER_CTX_new
functions.description: Allocates and initializes a new EVP_CIPHER_CTX. Returns NULL on allocation failure.
requirements: Caller must free the returned context with EVP_CIPHER_CTX_free when done.

functions.name: EVP_CIPHER_CTX_cleanup
functions.description: Frees any memory referenced by ctx. Returns one.
requirements: ctx must have been initialized (by EVP_CIPHER_CTX_init or EVP_CIPHER_CTX_new).
After cleanup, the context should not be used unless reinitialized.

functions.name: EVP_CIPHER_CTX_free
functions.description: Calls EVP_CIPHER_CTX_cleanup on ctx and frees ctx.
requirements: ctx must be a pointer previously allocated by EVP_CIPHER_CTX_new or otherwise valid for cleanup and free.

functions.name: EVP_CIPHER_CTX_copy
functions.description: Duplicates the current state of in into out. out must have been previously initialized.
requirements: out must be initialized with EVP_CIPHER_CTX_init or created with EVP_CIPHER_CTX_new.
in must point to a valid, initialized EVP_CIPHER_CTX.
Returns one on success and zero on error.

functions.name: EVP_CIPHER_CTX_reset
functions.description: Calls EVP_CIPHER_CTX_cleanup followed by EVP_CIPHER_CTX_init and returns one.
requirements: ctx must be a valid pointer.
After reset, any previous configuration is cleared.

functions.name: EVP_CipherInit_ex
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int EVP_CipherInit_ex(EVP_CIPHER_CTX *ctx, const EVP_CIPHER *cipher, ENGINE *engine, const uint8_t *key, const uint8_t *iv, int enc);
functions.description: Configures ctx for a fresh encryption or decryption operation using cipher. If reusing a previous configuration, cipher/key/iv may be NULL and enc may be -1 to reuse prior values.
requirements: ctx must be initialized.
If providing key and/or iv, their lengths must match EVP_CIPHER_key_length(cipher) and EVP_CIPHER_iv_length(cipher) respectively.
If reusing previous values, cipher/key/iv may be NULL and enc may be -1.
enc must be nonzero for encrypt, zero for decrypt, or -1 for reuse.
Returns one on success and zero on error.

functions.name: EVP_EncryptInit_ex
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int EVP_EncryptInit_ex(EVP_CIPHER_CTX *ctx, const EVP_CIPHER *cipher, ENGINE *impl, const uint8_t *key, const uint8_t *iv);
functions.description: Convenience wrapper for EVP_CipherInit_ex with enc=1 (encryption).
requirements: Same as EVP_CipherInit_ex, with enc fixed to encryption.
Returns one on success and zero on error.

functions.name: EVP_DecryptInit_ex
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int EVP_DecryptInit_ex(EVP_CIPHER_CTX *ctx, const EVP_CIPHER *cipher, ENGINE *impl, const uint8_t *key, const uint8_t *iv);
functions.description: Convenience wrapper for EVP_CipherInit_ex with enc=0 (decryption).
requirements: Same as EVP_CipherInit_ex, with enc fixed to decryption.
Returns one on success and zero on error.

functions.name: EVP_EncryptUpdate_ex
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int EVP_EncryptUpdate_ex(EVP_CIPHER_CTX *ctx, uint8_t *out, size_t *out_len, size_t max_out_len, const uint8_t *in, size_t in_len);
functions.description: Encrypts input and writes up to max_out_len bytes to out. Sets *out_len on success. Output size per-call and total depend on cipher mode and padding.
requirements: ctx must be configured for encryption.
out must have at least max_out_len bytes available.
If max_out_len is too small for required output, the function returns zero.
For block ciphers (block size != 1), a single call outputs at most in_len + block_size - 1 bytes.
Total output across updates and final is at most total input + 1, rounded up to a block size.
Returns one on success and zero on error.

functions.name: EVP_EncryptFinal_ex2
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int EVP_EncryptFinal_ex2(EVP_CIPHER_CTX *ctx, uint8_t *out, size_t *out_len, size_t max_out_len);
functions.description: Finishes encryption and writes up to max_out_len bytes to out. Applies or omits padding based on context settings. Sets *out_len on success.
requirements: ctx must be configured for encryption.
out must have at least max_out_len bytes available.
If max_out_len is too small for required output, the function returns zero.
If block size is 1, there is no final output.
If padding is enabled and block size != 1, standard padding is applied.
If padding is disabled and a partial block remains, the function returns zero.
Returns one on success and zero on error.

functions.name: EVP_DecryptUpdate_ex
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int EVP_DecryptUpdate_ex(EVP_CIPHER_CTX *ctx, uint8_t *out, size_t *out_len, size_t max_out_len, const uint8_t *in, size_t in_len);
functions.description: Decrypts input and writes up to max_out_len bytes to out. Sets *out_len on success. Output sizing depends on mode and prior data.
requirements: ctx must be configured for decryption.
out must have at least max_out_len bytes available.
If max_out_len is too small for required output, the function returns zero.
For block ciphers (block size != 1), a single call outputs at most in_len + block_size - 1 bytes.
Total output across updates and final is at most the total input.
For AEAD ciphers, decrypted data must not be processed until EVP_DecryptFinal_ex2 succeeds.
Returns one on success and zero on error.

functions.name: EVP_DecryptFinal_ex2
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int EVP_DecryptFinal_ex2(EVP_CIPHER_CTX *ctx, uint8_t *out, size_t *out_len, size_t max_out_len);
functions.description: Finishes decryption and writes up to max_out_len bytes to out. Removes padding if enabled. Sets *out_len on success.
requirements: ctx must be configured for decryption.
out must have at least max_out_len bytes available.
If max_out_len is too small for required output, the function returns zero.
If block size is 1, there is no final output.
If padding is enabled and block size != 1, standard padding is removed from the final block.
Returns one on success and zero on error.
Security note: calling after decrypting unauthenticated ciphertext with padding enabled and block size != 1 can enable padding oracle attacks.

functions.name: EVP_CipherUpdate_ex
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int EVP_CipherUpdate_ex(EVP_CIPHER_CTX *ctx, uint8_t *out, size_t *out_len, size_t max_out_len, const uint8_t *in, size_t in_len);
functions.description: Calls either EVP_EncryptUpdate_ex or EVP_DecryptUpdate_ex based on ctx configuration.
requirements: ctx must be configured for encryption or decryption.
Same buffer sizing requirements as the corresponding _Update_ex function.

functions.name: EVP_CipherUpdateAAD
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int EVP_CipherUpdateAAD(EVP_CIPHER_CTX *ctx, const uint8_t *in, size_t in_len);
functions.description: Adds in_len bytes of additional authenticated data (AAD) for AEAD ciphers, to be supplied fully before any plaintext/ciphertext.
requirements: ctx must be configured for an AEAD cipher that supports AAD.
All AAD must be provided before any plaintext or ciphertext is processed.
Returns one on success and zero on error.

functions.name: EVP_CipherFinal_ex2
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int EVP_CipherFinal_ex2(EVP_CIPHER_CTX *ctx, uint8_t *out, size_t *out_len, size_t max_out_len);
functions.description: Calls either EVP_EncryptFinal_ex2 or EVP_DecryptFinal_ex2 based on ctx configuration.
requirements: ctx must be configured for encryption or decryption.
Same buffer sizing requirements as the corresponding _Final_ex2 function.

functions.name: EVP_CIPHER_CTX_cipher

functions.name: EVP_CIPHER_CTX_encrypting

functions.name: EVP_CIPHER_CTX_block_size

functions.name: EVP_CIPHER_CTX_iv_length

functions.name: EVP_CIPHER_CTX_mode

functions.name: EVP_CIPHER_CTX_ctrl
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int EVP_CIPHER_CTX_ctrl(EVP_CIPHER_CTX *ctx, int command, int arg, void *ptr);
functions.description: Generic control function for cipher contexts, taking an EVP_CTRL_* command with command-specific arg and ptr semantics.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, initialized context.
command must be one of the defined EVP_CTRL_* values.
The required types/values for arg and ptr depend on the specific command.
Returns implementation-defined success (typically one) or zero on error.

functions.name: EVP_CIPHER_CTX_set_padding
functions.description: Enables (nonzero pad) or disables (zero) padding for block ciphers. Returns one.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, initialized context.
Padding settings affect behavior of finalization (e.g., partial blocks invalid if disabled).

functions.name: EVP_CIPHER_CTX_set_key_length
functions.description: Sets the key length for ctx if the cipher supports variable-length keys. Returns one on success, zero on error.
requirements: ctx must be configured with a cipher that supports variable key length (EVP_CIPH_VARIABLE_LENGTH flag).
key_len must be a supported key size for the cipher.

functions.name: EVP_CIPHER_nid
functions.description: Returns a NID identifying the cipher.
requirements: cipher must be non-NULL.

functions.name: EVP_CIPHER_block_size
functions.description: Returns the block size (bytes) for cipher, or one for stream ciphers.
requirements: cipher must be non-NULL.

functions.name: EVP_CIPHER_key_length
functions.description: Returns the key size (bytes) for cipher. For variable-length ciphers, returns the default key length.
requirements: cipher must be non-NULL.

functions.name: EVP_CIPHER_iv_length
functions.description: Returns the IV size (bytes) for cipher, or zero if cipher does not use an IV.
requirements: cipher must be non-NULL.

functions.name: EVP_CIPHER_flags

functions.name: EVP_CIPHER_mode

requirements: cipher must be non-NULL.

functions.name: EVP_BytesToKey
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int EVP_BytesToKey(const EVP_CIPHER *type, const EVP_MD *md, const uint8_t salt[8], const uint8_t *data, size_t data_len, unsigned count, uint8_t *key, uint8_t *iv);
functions.description: Derives a key and IV for the given cipher by iterating the digest md count times over data and optional salt. Returns key length (without IV) on success or zero on error. Provided for legacy PBKDF1 compatibility.
requirements: type and md must be non-NULL and supported.
If salt is NULL, an empty salt is used. Only salt lengths of 0 or 8 are supported.
If key and/or iv are non-NULL, the buffers must be large enough for EVP_CIPHER_key_length(type) and EVP_CIPHER_iv_length(type) respectively.
Either key or iv may be NULL to skip that output.
count specifies the iteration count; must be a positive integer for meaningful security (legacy API does not enforce).
Returns zero on error.

functions.name: EVP_CipherInit
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int EVP_CipherInit(EVP_CIPHER_CTX *ctx, const EVP_CIPHER *cipher, const uint8_t *key, const uint8_t *iv, int enc);
functions.description: Deprecated. Acts like EVP_CipherInit_ex but calls EVP_CIPHER_CTX_init on ctx first if cipher is not NULL.

functions.description: Deprecated. Like EVP_CipherUpdate_ex but without an explicit output size parameter; no bounds checking is performed. For AEAD ciphers with out==NULL, behaves like EVP_CipherUpdateAAD.
requirements: ctx must be configured for encryption or decryption.

Returns one on success and zero on error.

functions.name: EVP_EncryptUpdate

functions.name: EVP_Cipher
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int EVP_Cipher(EVP_CIPHER_CTX *ctx, uint8_t *out, const uint8_t *in, size_t in_len);
functions.description: Deprecated and historically exposed internals. If the cipher does not have EVP_CIPH_FLAG_CUSTOM_CIPHER, processes in_len bytes and writes in_len bytes to out (in_len must be a multiple of the block size). If the cipher has EVP_CIPH_FLAG_CUSTOM_CIPHER, behaves like EVP_CipherUpdate when in!=NULL and like EVP_CipherFinal_ex when in==NULL. Error signaling differs between modes per the documentation.
requirements: ctx must be configured.
If cipher does not have EVP_CIPH_FLAG_CUSTOM_CIPHER: in_len must be a multiple of the cipher block size; behavior otherwise is undefined. out must have space for in_len bytes.
If cipher has EVP_CIPH_FLAG_CUSTOM_CIPHER: when in!=NULL behaves like EVP_CipherUpdate; when in==NULL behaves like EVP_CipherFinal_ex.
Warning: In the custom-cipher case, return value semantics differ historically; zero may indicate success with zero output.

functions.name: AES_CMAC
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int AES_CMAC(uint8_t out[16], const uint8_t *key, size_t key_len, const uint8_t *in, size_t in_len);
functions.description: Computes the 16-byte CMAC (per RFC 4493) over the input buffer using AES-CBC. key_len selects AES-128 (16) or AES-256 (32). On success writes a 16-byte tag to out and returns 1; returns 0 on error. Use for one-shot CMAC without maintaining a context.
requirements: out must reference writable storage for at least 16 bytes.
key must point to at least key_len bytes.
key_len must be either 16 (AES-128) or 32 (AES-256).
in must point to at least in_len bytes (no guarantee that NULL is allowed when in_len is 0).
Return value must be checked: 1 indicates success, 0 indicates error.

The returned CMAC_CTX must later be released with CMAC_CTX_free.

functions.name: CMAC_CTX_free
functions.description: Frees a CMAC_CTX previously allocated for CMAC operations.
requirements: ctx must be a valid CMAC_CTX previously allocated by CMAC_CTX_new or equivalent.
Do not use ctx after this call.

functions.name: CMAC_CTX_copy
functions.description: Copies the current CMAC computation state from in to out. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error. Useful to branch computation or duplicate progress.
requirements: out must be a valid, allocated CMAC_CTX ready to receive the copy.
in must be a valid, initialized CMAC_CTX whose state can be duplicated.
out and in must both be non-NULL.
Return value must be checked: 1 indicates success, 0 indicates error.

functions.name: CMAC_Init
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int CMAC_Init(CMAC_CTX *ctx, const void *key, size_t key_len, const EVP_CIPHER *cipher, ENGINE *engine);
functions.description: Initializes ctx to compute a CMAC using the specified AES-CBC cipher and key. The CMAC RFC specifies AES-128 (key_len 16, cipher EVP_aes_128_cbc()), but this implementation also supports AES-256 (key_len 32, cipher EVP_aes_256_cbc()). The engine argument is ignored. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: ctx must be a valid CMAC_CTX (e.g., from CMAC_CTX_new).
key must point to at least key_len bytes.
key_len should be 16 for AES-128 or 32 for AES-256; other sizes are not supported.
cipher should correspond to the key size: EVP_aes_128_cbc() for 16-byte keys, EVP_aes_256_cbc() for 32-byte keys.
engine is ignored; callers may pass NULL.
Must be called before CMAC_Update/CMAC_Final.
Return value must be checked: 1 indicates success, 0 indicates error.

functions.name: CMAC_Reset
functions.description: Resets ctx so a fresh message can be authenticated with the same configuration. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: ctx must be a valid CMAC_CTX that has been initialized via CMAC_Init.
Return value must be checked: 1 indicates success, 0 indicates error.

functions.name: CMAC_Update
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int CMAC_Update(CMAC_CTX *ctx, const uint8_t *in, size_t in_len);
functions.description: Processes in_len bytes from in into the ongoing CMAC computation. Can be called multiple times. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: ctx must be a valid CMAC_CTX initialized with CMAC_Init.
in must point to at least in_len bytes (no guarantee that NULL is allowed when in_len is 0).
May be called repeatedly to process a message in chunks.
Return value must be checked: 1 indicates success, 0 indicates error.

functions.name: CMAC_Final
functions.description: Finalizes the CMAC computation. Sets *out_len to 16 and, if out is not NULL, writes the 16-byte authenticator to it. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: ctx must be a valid CMAC_CTX that has been initialized (and optionally updated) prior to finalization.
out, if non-NULL, must reference writable storage for at least 16 bytes.
out_len must be non-NULL and writable; on success it will be set to 16.
Return value must be checked: 1 indicates success, 0 indicates error.

functions.name: NCONF_new
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new, empty CONF object. The method parameter is unused in BoringSSL and must be NULL. Use NCONF_free to release the returned object.
requirements: method must be NULL (per header documentation).
Caller must check the return value for NULL (allocation failure).
The returned CONF* must be freed with NCONF_free.

functions.name: NCONF_free
functions.description: Frees all resources owned by conf and then frees conf itself. Use to release CONF objects allocated by NCONF_new or returned by related factory functions.
requirements: conf must be a valid pointer to a CONF previously allocated (e.g., by NCONF_new); passing invalid pointers is undefined.
Do not use conf after calling NCONF_free (it becomes invalid).
Whether NULL is accepted is not stated; behavior for conf == NULL is unknown.

functions.name: NCONF_load
functions.description: Parses the configuration file at filename and merges the values into conf. Returns 1 on success and 0 on error. If an error occurs and out_error_line is not NULL, *out_error_line is set to the 1-based line number where the error occurred.
requirements: conf must be a valid, initialized CONF pointer (e.g., from NCONF_new).
filename must point to a readable config file path; passing NULL or an unreadable path causes failure (returns 0).
If out_error_line is non-NULL, it must be a valid pointer to long for receiving the error line.
Caller must check the return value (1 = success, 0 = error) and, on error, may consult *out_error_line when provided.

functions.name: NCONF_load_bio
functions.description: Like NCONF_load but reads configuration data from the provided BIO instead of a named file. Returns 1 on success and 0 on error. On error, if out_error_line is not NULL, *out_error_line is set to the offending line number.
requirements: conf must be a valid, initialized CONF pointer.
bio must be a valid, readable BIO positioned at the start of the config content.
If out_error_line is non-NULL, it must be a valid pointer to long for receiving the error line.
Caller must check the return value (1 = success, 0 = error).

functions.name: NCONF_get_section
functions.description: Retrieves all key/value pairs for a given section of the configuration. If section is NULL, returns the default section. On error, returns NULL.
requirements: conf must be a valid, initialized CONF pointer.
section may be NULL to request the default section; otherwise it must name an existing section.
Caller must handle a NULL return (error or section not found).
The returned STACK_OF(CONF_VALUE) is owned by conf; the caller must not free or modify it unless documented elsewhere.

functions.name: NCONF_get_string
functions.signature: const char *NCONF_get_string(const CONF *conf, const char *section, const char *name);
functions.description: Looks up the value for key name in the specified section of conf. If section is NULL, the default section is searched. Returns the value string on success or NULL on error or if not found.
requirements: conf must be a valid, initialized CONF pointer.
section may be NULL to use the default section.
name must be a valid, non-NULL key name.
Caller must handle a NULL return value (error or missing key).
The returned pointer is owned by conf; do not free or modify it.

functions.name: CONF_modules_load_file
functions.signature: int CONF_modules_load_file(const char *filename, const char *appname, unsigned long flags);
functions.description: No-op in BoringSSL; defined to always succeed without loading any options. Returns 1.
requirements: No operational effect; callers should not rely on any configuration being applied.
Return value is always 1 in BoringSSL.

functions.name: CONF_modules_unload
functions.description: No-op in BoringSSL; provided for compatibility with OpenSSL APIs. Does nothing regardless of the all parameter.
requirements: No operational effect; callers should not expect any modules to be unloaded.

functions.name: CONF_modules_free
functions.description: No-op in BoringSSL; provided for compatibility. Does nothing.
requirements: No operational effect.

functions.name: OPENSSL_config
functions.description: No-op in BoringSSL; provided for compatibility with OpenSSL. Does nothing regardless of config_name.
requirements: No operational effect; callers should not expect any configuration to be applied.
Behavior for config_name == NULL is not specified; treated as no-op.

functions.name: OPENSSL_no_config
functions.description: No-op in BoringSSL; provided for compatibility. Does nothing.
requirements: No operational effect.

functions.name: bssl::UniquePtr<CONF>::Deleter::operator()
functions.description: Custom deleter used by bssl::UniquePtr for CONF objects, generated by BORINGSSL_MAKE_DELETER(CONF, NCONF_free). Invoking it frees the CONF by calling NCONF_free(ptr). Typically used implicitly when a bssl::UniquePtr<CONF> goes out of scope or is reset.
requirements: ptr should be a CONF* allocated/owned by the corresponding UniquePtr<CONF>, or NULL.
After invocation, ptr must not be used (the object is freed).
Thread-safety and NULL-acceptance depend on NCONF_free; behavior when ptr is invalid is undefined.

functions.name: CTR_DRBG_new
functions.signature: CTR_DRBG_STATE *CTR_DRBG_new(const uint8_t entropy[CTR_DRBG_ENTROPY_LEN], const uint8_t *personalization, size_t personalization_len);
functions.description: Allocates and initializes a CTR-DRBG state which does not use a derivation function. The DRBG is seeded with exactly CTR_DRBG_ENTROPY_LEN (48) bytes of entropy and optional personalization data. Returns NULL on allocation failure or if personalization_len is invalid. Use the returned state with CTR_DRBG_generate and reseed with CTR_DRBG_reseed/CTR_DRBG_reseed_ex as needed; free with CTR_DRBG_free.
requirements: entropy must point to exactly CTR_DRBG_ENTROPY_LEN (48) bytes of input entropy.
personalization may be NULL only if personalization_len is 0; otherwise it must point to at least personalization_len bytes.
personalization_len must be a valid length; values causing failure are not specified in this header (unknown; validated by the implementation).
The returned CTR_DRBG_STATE must be freed with CTR_DRBG_free.

functions.name: CTR_DRBG_new_df
functions.signature: CTR_DRBG_STATE *CTR_DRBG_new_df(const uint8_t *entropy, size_t entropy_len, const uint8_t nonce[CTR_DRBG_NONCE_LEN], const uint8_t *personalization, size_t personalization_len);
functions.description: Allocates and initializes a CTR-DRBG state which uses a derivation function. The DRBG is instantiated from variable-length entropy, a fixed-size nonce, and optional personalization data. Returns NULL on allocation failure or invalid arguments.
requirements: entropy must point to entropy_len bytes; entropy_len must be between CTR_DRBG_MIN_ENTROPY_LEN (32) and CTR_DRBG_MAX_ENTROPY_LEN (64), inclusive.
nonce must point to exactly CTR_DRBG_NONCE_LEN (16) bytes.
personalization may be NULL only if personalization_len is 0; otherwise it must point to at least personalization_len bytes.
The returned CTR_DRBG_STATE must be freed with CTR_DRBG_free.

functions.name: CTR_DRBG_free
functions.description: Frees a CTR_DRBG_STATE previously returned by a constructor and releases its resources. Safe to call with NULL, in which case it does nothing.
requirements: state may be NULL; no action is taken in that case.
If non-NULL, state must have been allocated by a compatible constructor (e.g., CTR_DRBG_new or CTR_DRBG_new_df) and not already freed.

functions.name: CTR_DRBG_reseed
functions.signature: int CTR_DRBG_reseed(CTR_DRBG_STATE *drbg, const uint8_t entropy[CTR_DRBG_ENTROPY_LEN], const uint8_t *additional_data, size_t additional_data_len);
functions.description: Reseeds an existing CTR-DRBG instance with exactly CTR_DRBG_ENTROPY_LEN (48) bytes of new entropy and optional additional data (up to CTR_DRBG_SEED_LEN bytes). Returns 1 on success and 0 on error.
requirements: drbg must be a valid, initialized CTR_DRBG_STATE.
entropy must point to exactly CTR_DRBG_ENTROPY_LEN (48) bytes of input entropy.
additional_data may be NULL only if additional_data_len is 0; otherwise it must point to at least additional_data_len bytes.
additional_data_len must be at most CTR_DRBG_SEED_LEN (32 + CTR_DRBG_NONCE_LEN).
Callers must check the return value: 1 indicates success; 0 indicates error.

functions.name: CTR_DRBG_reseed_ex
functions.signature: int CTR_DRBG_reseed_ex(CTR_DRBG_STATE *drbg, const uint8_t *entropy, size_t entropy_len, const uint8_t *additional_data, size_t additional_data_len);
functions.description: Like CTR_DRBG_reseed but accepts variable-length entropy input up to CTR_DRBG_MAX_ENTROPY_LEN (64). Returns 1 on success and 0 on error. Other behavior matches CTR_DRBG_reseed.
requirements: drbg must be a valid, initialized CTR_DRBG_STATE.
entropy must point to entropy_len bytes; entropy_len must be > 0 and <= CTR_DRBG_MAX_ENTROPY_LEN (64).
additional_data may be NULL only if additional_data_len is 0; otherwise it must point to at least additional_data_len bytes.
additional_data_len is expected to follow the same limit as CTR_DRBG_reseed (at most CTR_DRBG_SEED_LEN), per “acts like CTR_DRBG_reseed” (inferred from comment).
Callers must check the return value: 1 indicates success; 0 indicates error.

functions.name: CTR_DRBG_generate
functions.signature: int CTR_DRBG_generate(CTR_DRBG_STATE *drbg, uint8_t *out, size_t out_len, const uint8_t *additional_data, size_t additional_data_len);
functions.description: Generates out_len pseudorandom bytes into out, optionally processing up to CTR_DRBG_ENTROPY_LEN (48) bytes of additional data for this request. out_len must be <= CTR_DRBG_MAX_GENERATE_LENGTH (65536). Returns 1 on success and 0 on error.
requirements: drbg must be a valid, initialized CTR_DRBG_STATE.
out must point to a writable buffer of at least out_len bytes.
out_len must be <= CTR_DRBG_MAX_GENERATE_LENGTH (65536).
additional_data may be NULL only if additional_data_len is 0; otherwise it must point to at least additional_data_len bytes.
additional_data_len must be <= CTR_DRBG_ENTROPY_LEN (48).
Callers must check the return value: 1 indicates success; 0 indicates error.

functions.name: CTR_DRBG_clear
functions.description: Zeroizes the internal state of the DRBG instance. Intended to securely clear sensitive material in the state.
requirements: drbg must be a valid (non-NULL) CTR_DRBG_STATE pointer. Behavior for NULL is not specified in this header (unknown).
After clearing, the state should not be used unless reinitialized or reseeded as appropriate (inferred from purpose of clearing).

functions.name: bssl::UniquePtr<CTR_DRBG_STATE>::Deleter::operator()
functions.description: Custom deleter for bssl::UniquePtr<CTR_DRBG_STATE>, generated by BORINGSSL_MAKE_DELETER(CTR_DRBG_STATE, CTR_DRBG_free). Invoking this calls CTR_DRBG_free(ptr). This enables RAII-style automatic cleanup of CTR_DRBG_STATE objects. Note: The exact type is macro-generated; the signature is inferred from BoringSSL’s deleter pattern.
requirements: ptr may be NULL; CTR_DRBG_free is a no-op on NULL.
If non-NULL, ptr must be a valid CTR_DRBG_STATE allocated by a compatible constructor and not already freed.
Intended to be used implicitly by bssl::UniquePtr<CTR_DRBG_STATE>; callers normally should not call it directly.

functions.name: X25519_keypair
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT void X25519_keypair(uint8_t out_public_value[32], uint8_t out_private_key[32]);
functions.description: Generates a fresh X25519 Diffie–Hellman key pair. Writes the 32-byte public value to out_public_value and the 32-byte private key to out_private_key. Use the resulting keys with X25519 or to distribute the public value to peers.
requirements: out_public_value must point to a writable buffer of at least 32 bytes.
out_private_key must point to a writable buffer of at least 32 bytes.
Buffers must be valid for writing and not overlap in undefined ways.
No return value: callers cannot detect failure via return; assume generation succeeds as per API.

functions.name: X25519
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int X25519(uint8_t out_shared_key[32], const uint8_t private_key[32], const uint8_t peer_public_value[32]);
functions.description: Computes a 32-byte X25519 shared key from a local private key and a peer’s public value. On success returns 1 and writes the shared key to out_shared_key; returns 0 on error. The shared key should be fed into a KDF (include both public values) rather than used directly as an application key.
requirements: out_shared_key must point to a writable buffer of at least 32 bytes.
private_key must reference a 32-byte private key buffer.
peer_public_value must reference a 32-byte peer public value buffer.
Callers must check the return value: 1 indicates success, 0 indicates error.
Do not use the raw shared key directly; derive application keys via a KDF and include both public values (usage guidance from comments).

functions.name: X25519_public_from_private
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT void X25519_public_from_private(uint8_t out_public_value[32], const uint8_t private_key[32]);
functions.description: Derives the X25519 public value corresponding to a given 32-byte private key and writes it to out_public_value. Useful for reconstructing or publishing the public value from stored private material.
requirements: out_public_value must point to a writable buffer of at least 32 bytes.
private_key must reference a 32-byte private key buffer.

functions.name: ED25519_keypair
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT void ED25519_keypair(uint8_t out_public_key[32], uint8_t out_private_key[64]);
functions.description: Generates a fresh Ed25519 key pair. Writes the 32-byte public key to out_public_key and the 64-byte private key (which includes the 32-byte seed plus a cached public key suffix) to out_private_key.
requirements: out_public_key must point to a writable buffer of at least 32 bytes.
out_private_key must point to a writable buffer of at least 64 bytes.
Buffers must be valid for writing and not overlap in undefined ways.

functions.name: ED25519_sign
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int ED25519_sign(uint8_t out_sig[64], const uint8_t *message, size_t message_len, const uint8_t private_key[64]);
functions.description: Signs message using the Ed25519 private key and writes a 64-byte signature to out_sig. Returns 1 on success or 0 on allocation failure.
requirements: out_sig must point to a writable buffer of at least 64 bytes.
private_key must reference a 64-byte Ed25519 private key as produced by ED25519_keypair or ED25519_keypair_from_seed.
message must reference message_len bytes of readable data (message_len may be zero).
Callers must check the return value: 1 indicates success, 0 indicates failure.

functions.name: ED25519_verify
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int ED25519_verify(const uint8_t *message, size_t message_len, const uint8_t signature[64], const uint8_t public_key[32]);
functions.description: Verifies that signature is a valid Ed25519 signature by public_key over message. Returns 1 if valid, 0 otherwise.
requirements: message must reference message_len bytes of readable data (message_len may be zero).
signature must reference a 64-byte signature buffer.
public_key must reference a 32-byte Ed25519 public key.
Callers must check the return value: 1 indicates a valid signature, 0 indicates invalid.

functions.name: ED25519_keypair_from_seed
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT void ED25519_keypair_from_seed(uint8_t out_public_key[32], uint8_t out_private_key[64], const uint8_t seed[32]);
functions.description: Deterministically derives an Ed25519 public key and private key from a 32-byte seed (the RFC 8032 private key). Writes the 32-byte public key and 64-byte private key (seed plus cached public suffix). Intended for interoperability with systems that store only the seed.
requirements: out_public_key must point to a writable buffer of at least 32 bytes.
out_private_key must point to a writable buffer of at least 64 bytes.
seed must reference a 32-byte buffer.

functions.name: SPAKE2_CTX_new
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT SPAKE2_CTX *SPAKE2_CTX_new(enum spake2_role_t my_role, const uint8_t *my_name, size_t my_name_len, const uint8_t *their_name, size_t their_name_len);
functions.description: Allocates and initializes a new SPAKE2 context for a single execution of the SPAKE2 protocol. The my_role parameter must differ between the two peers (one alice, one bob). Optional opaque names (my_name/their_name) can be bound into the protocol to avoid context confusion across devices.
requirements: Callers must use a matching, opposite role on the peer (one spake2_role_alice, the other spake2_role_bob).
The returned SPAKE2_CTX is for a single protocol run.
If my_name_len > 0, my_name must point to a readable buffer of at least my_name_len bytes.
If their_name_len > 0, their_name must point to a readable buffer of at least their_name_len bytes.
Caller must eventually free the returned context with SPAKE2_CTX_free.

functions.name: SPAKE2_CTX_free
functions.description: Frees a SPAKE2_CTX and all resources it holds. Safe to call on a completed context after SPAKE2_process_msg or to clean up on error.
requirements: ctx must be either NULL or a pointer previously returned by SPAKE2_CTX_new.
Must not be used on a context after it has been freed.

functions.name: SPAKE2_generate_msg
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int SPAKE2_generate_msg(SPAKE2_CTX *ctx, uint8_t *out, size_t *out_len, size_t max_out_len, const uint8_t *password, size_t password_len);
functions.description: Generates and outputs this party’s SPAKE2 message using the provided password. Writes at most max_out_len bytes to out and sets *out_len to the number of bytes written (up to SPAKE2_MAX_MSG_SIZE). Can only be called once per SPAKE2_CTX. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SPAKE2_CTX returned by SPAKE2_CTX_new and not yet used to generate a message.
This function can only be called once per SPAKE2_CTX.
out must point to a writable buffer of at least max_out_len bytes.
out_len must be a valid pointer for writing the resulting length.
To ensure success, max_out_len should be at least SPAKE2_MAX_MSG_SIZE (32) bytes.
password must reference password_len bytes of readable data.
Callers must check the return value: 1 indicates success, 0 indicates error.

functions.name: SPAKE2_process_msg
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int SPAKE2_process_msg(SPAKE2_CTX *ctx, uint8_t *out_key, size_t *out_key_len, size_t max_out_key_len, const uint8_t *their_msg, size_t their_msg_len);
functions.description: Completes the SPAKE2 exchange given the peer’s message, producing shared keying material. Writes at most max_out_key_len bytes to out_key and sets *out_key_len. If max_out_key_len is smaller than the generated key material, the key is silently truncated. Requires that SPAKE2_generate_msg was previously called on ctx. On success, the context is complete and only SPAKE2_CTX_free may be called thereafter. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SPAKE2_CTX on which SPAKE2_generate_msg has been successfully called and which has not yet been completed.
After a successful return, ctx is complete; the only valid subsequent operation is SPAKE2_CTX_free.
out_key must point to a writable buffer of at least max_out_key_len bytes.
out_key_len must be a valid pointer for writing the resulting length.
their_msg must reference their_msg_len bytes of readable data (format/size not further specified here).
If the caller wants to avoid truncation, max_out_key_len should be at least SPAKE2_MAX_KEY_SIZE (64) bytes.
Callers must check the return value: 1 indicates success, 0 indicates error.

functions.name: DES_set_key
functions.description: Performs the DES key schedule for the provided 8-byte key and initializes the output DES_key_schedule. Intended to be called before any DES encryption/decryption routines that require a prepared schedule.
requirements: key must point to a valid DES_cblock containing 8 bytes.
schedule must be a valid, writable pointer to DES_key_schedule.
Call before using schedule with DES operations.
enc/dec operations using schedule must use the same key as provided here (inferred).

functions.name: DES_set_odd_parity
functions.description: Sets the least-significant bit in each byte of the key to ensure odd parity, modifying the key in place. Used to normalize DES keys to proper parity.
requirements: key must point to a valid, writable DES_cblock (8 bytes).
Modifies key in place; callers should supply a mutable key and re-run key schedule after changing parity (inferred).

functions.name: DES_ecb_encrypt
functions.signature: void DES_ecb_encrypt(const DES_cblock *in, DES_cblock *out, const DES_key_schedule *schedule, int is_encrypt);
functions.description: Encrypts or decrypts a single 8-byte DES block in ECB mode using a prepared key schedule. Set is_encrypt to DES_ENCRYPT or DES_DECRYPT.
requirements: in must point to exactly one DES block (8 bytes).
out must point to writable storage for one DES block (8 bytes).
schedule must be initialized by DES_set_key with the intended key.
is_encrypt must be either DES_ENCRYPT or DES_DECRYPT.

functions.name: DES_ncbc_encrypt
functions.signature: void DES_ncbc_encrypt(const uint8_t *in, uint8_t *out, size_t len, const DES_key_schedule *schedule, DES_cblock *ivec, int enc);
functions.description: Encrypts or decrypts a buffer using DES in CBC mode without padding. Processes len bytes from in to out using the given key schedule and 8-byte IV; enc selects DES_ENCRYPT or DES_DECRYPT.
requirements: in must point to at least len bytes; out must point to writable storage for len bytes.
schedule must be initialized by DES_set_key.
ivec must point to a valid 8-byte DES_cblock; it is used as the IV and may be updated (inferred from API pattern).
enc must be either DES_ENCRYPT or DES_DECRYPT.
len should be a multiple of 8 bytes because DES CBC here does not perform padding (inferred from DES CBC raw API and function naming ‘ncbc’).

functions.name: DES_ecb3_encrypt
functions.signature: void DES_ecb3_encrypt(const DES_cblock *input, DES_cblock *output, const DES_key_schedule *ks1, const DES_key_schedule *ks2, const DES_key_schedule *ks3, int enc);
functions.description: Encrypts or decrypts a single 8-byte block using Triple-DES (EDE) in ECB mode. Uses three prepared key schedules; enc selects DES_ENCRYPT or DES_DECRYPT.
requirements: input must point to exactly one DES block (8 bytes); output must be writable for 8 bytes.
ks1, ks2, ks3 must each be initialized by DES_set_key for their respective keys.
enc must be either DES_ENCRYPT or DES_DECRYPT.

functions.name: DES_ede3_cbc_encrypt
functions.signature: void DES_ede3_cbc_encrypt(const uint8_t *in, uint8_t *out, size_t len, const DES_key_schedule *ks1, const DES_key_schedule *ks2, const DES_key_schedule *ks3, DES_cblock *ivec, int enc);
functions.description: Encrypts or decrypts a buffer using Triple-DES (EDE3) in CBC mode without padding. Processes len bytes using three key schedules and an 8-byte IV; enc selects DES_ENCRYPT or DES_DECRYPT.
requirements: in must point to at least len bytes; out must be writable for len bytes.
ks1, ks2, ks3 must each be initialized by DES_set_key for their respective keys.
ivec must point to a valid 8-byte DES_cblock; it is used as the IV and may be updated (inferred).
enc must be either DES_ENCRYPT or DES_DECRYPT.
len should be a multiple of 8 bytes because this raw CBC routine does not add padding (inferred).

functions.name: DES_ede2_cbc_encrypt
functions.signature: void DES_ede2_cbc_encrypt(const uint8_t *in, uint8_t *out, size_t len, const DES_key_schedule *ks1, const DES_key_schedule *ks2, DES_cblock *ivec, int enc);
functions.description: Encrypts or decrypts a buffer using two-key Triple-DES (EDE2) in CBC mode without padding. Uses two key schedules (first and third keys are identical).
requirements: in must point to at least len bytes; out must be writable for len bytes.
ks1 and ks2 must be initialized by DES_set_key; ks1 is reused as the third key (per EDE2 mode).
ivec must point to a valid 8-byte DES_cblock; it is used as the IV and may be updated (inferred).
enc must be either DES_ENCRYPT or DES_DECRYPT.
len should be a multiple of 8 bytes because this raw CBC routine does not add padding (inferred).

functions.name: DES_set_key_unchecked
functions.description: Deprecated alias that calls DES_set_key. Performs the DES key schedule without additional checks.
requirements: key must point to a valid 8-byte DES_cblock.
schedule must be a valid, writable pointer to DES_key_schedule.

functions.name: DES_ede3_cfb64_encrypt
functions.signature: void DES_ede3_cfb64_encrypt(const uint8_t *in, uint8_t *out, long length, DES_key_schedule *ks1, DES_key_schedule *ks2, DES_key_schedule *ks3, DES_cblock *ivec, int *num, int enc);
functions.description: Encrypts or decrypts data using Triple-DES (EDE3) in CFB-64 mode. Processes length bytes as a stream using three key schedules, an 8-byte IV, and a feedback position counter pointed to by num. enc selects DES_ENCRYPT or DES_DECRYPT.
requirements: in must point to at least length bytes; out must be writable for length bytes.
ks1, ks2, ks3 must be initialized by DES_set_key.
ivec must point to a valid 8-byte DES_cblock; used as the IV and updated in place (inferred).
num must point to an integer that tracks/returns the current position in the 8-byte feedback block; its value should be in the range [0, 7] (inferred from CFB-64 API pattern).
enc must be either DES_ENCRYPT or DES_DECRYPT.

functions.name: DES_ede3_cfb_encrypt
functions.signature: void DES_ede3_cfb_encrypt(const uint8_t *in, uint8_t *out, int numbits, long length, DES_key_schedule *ks1, DES_key_schedule *ks2, DES_key_schedule *ks3, DES_cblock *ivec, int enc);
functions.description: Encrypts or decrypts data using Triple-DES (EDE3) in generic CFB mode with a specified feedback size of numbits. Processes length bytes using three key schedules and an 8-byte IV. enc selects DES_ENCRYPT or DES_DECRYPT.
requirements: in must point to at least length bytes; out must be writable for length bytes.
ks1, ks2, ks3 must be initialized by DES_set_key.
ivec must point to a valid 8-byte DES_cblock; used as the IV and updated in place (inferred).
numbits should be a positive number of feedback bits, typically 1..64 and a multiple that aligns with the intended CFB segment size (inferred from CFB API pattern).
enc must be either DES_ENCRYPT or DES_DECRYPT.

functions.name: DH_new
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new, empty DH object for Diffie-Hellman parameters/keys, or NULL on allocation failure. Use DH_free to release it. The module is deprecated; prefer X25519 or ECDH P-256.
requirements: Caller must free the returned DH* with DH_free when no longer needed.
Thread-safety: a newly returned DH* must not be concurrently modified without external synchronization.

functions.name: DH_free
functions.description: Decrements the reference count of dh and frees it when it reaches zero. Safe to call with NULL (a no-op in OpenSSL-style APIs, though not explicitly stated here).
requirements: dh must be a valid DH* previously allocated or up-ref’d for this API.
Do not use dh after calling DH_free unless you have another reference (via DH_up_ref).

functions.name: DH_up_ref
functions.description: Atomically increments the reference count of dh and returns 1 on success. Does not otherwise mutate dh and may be used concurrently.
requirements: dh must be a valid, initialized DH*.
Check the return value; 1 indicates success, 0 indicates failure.

functions.name: DH_bits
functions.description: Returns the size, in bits, of dh’s group modulus p.
requirements: dh must reference a DH with parameters set (p present) for a meaningful value.

functions.name: DH_get0_pub_key
functions.description: Returns a pointer to dh’s public key BIGNUM, or NULL if unset.
requirements: dh must be a valid DH*.
Returned pointer is owned by dh; do not free or modify it; it remains valid as long as dh is alive and not modified.

functions.name: DH_get0_priv_key
functions.description: Returns a pointer to dh’s private key BIGNUM, or NULL if dh is a public key only or the private key is unset.
requirements: dh must be a valid DH*.
Returned pointer is owned by dh; do not free or modify it; it remains valid as long as dh is alive and not modified.

functions.name: DH_get0_p
functions.description: Returns a pointer to dh’s group modulus p.
requirements: dh must be a valid DH*.
Returned pointer is owned by dh; do not free or modify it.

functions.name: DH_get0_q
functions.description: Returns a pointer to dh’s subgroup order q, or NULL if unset.
requirements: dh must be a valid DH*.
Returned pointer is owned by dh; do not free or modify it.

functions.name: DH_get0_g
functions.description: Returns a pointer to dh’s group generator g.
requirements: dh must be a valid DH*.
Returned pointer is owned by dh; do not free or modify it.

functions.name: DH_get0_key
functions.signature: void DH_get0_key(const DH *dh, const BIGNUM **out_pub_key, const BIGNUM **out_priv_key);
functions.description: Outputs pointers to dh’s public and private key BIGNUMs to out_pub_key and out_priv_key (if non-NULL). Sets the private key to NULL if dh is a public key only.
requirements: dh must be a valid DH*.
If provided, out_pub_key and/or out_priv_key must be valid pointers to receive results.
Returned BIGNUM pointers are owned by dh; do not free or modify them.

functions.name: DH_set0_key
functions.description: Sets dh’s public and/or private key to the provided BIGNUMs. For each non-NULL argument, ownership is transferred to dh on success. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: dh must be a valid DH*.
pub_key and priv_key, if non-NULL, must be dynamically allocated BIGNUMs that the caller relinquishes ownership of on success.
On failure, ownership of arguments is not transferred (behavior implied by usual OpenSSL patterns; check return value).
Do not pass stack-allocated or otherwise unmanaged BIGNUMs as they will be freed by dh on success.

functions.name: DH_get0_pqg
functions.signature: void DH_get0_pqg(const DH *dh, const BIGNUM **out_p, const BIGNUM **out_q, const BIGNUM **out_g);
functions.description: Outputs pointers to dh’s parameters p, q, and g to the respective outputs if non-NULL.
requirements: dh must be a valid DH*.
If provided, out_p, out_q, and/or out_g must be valid pointers to receive results.
Returned BIGNUM pointers are owned by dh; do not free or modify them.

functions.name: DH_set0_pqg
functions.description: Sets dh’s parameters p, q, and g to the provided values. Ownership of each non-NULL argument is transferred to dh on success. q may be NULL. p and g must either be provided here or already set on dh. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: dh must be a valid DH*.
q may be NULL; p and g must either be non-NULL here or already configured on dh.
For each non-NULL argument, caller relinquishes ownership to dh on success.
Do not pass stack-allocated or otherwise unmanaged BIGNUMs as they will be freed by dh on success.
Check the return value; 1 indicates success.

functions.name: DH_set_length
functions.description: Sets the bit length of the secret exponent used by DH_generate_key for dh. Returns 1 on success.
requirements: dh must be a valid DH*.
priv_length is a bit length; no specific range is documented here beyond type limits.

functions.name: DH_get_rfc7919_2048
functions.description: Allocates and returns a DH object initialized with the standardized ffdhe2048 group from RFC 7919 Appendix A.1, or NULL on allocation failure.
requirements: Caller must free the returned DH* with DH_free when no longer needed.

functions.name: BN_get_rfc3526_prime_1536
functions.description: Initializes ret (or allocates a new BIGNUM if ret is NULL) with the 1536-bit MODP prime from RFC 3526. Returns ret (possibly newly allocated) or NULL on allocation failure. The associated generator for this group is 2.
requirements: If ret is NULL, caller must free the returned BIGNUM with BN_free.
If ret is non-NULL, it must be a valid, mutable BIGNUM to be overwritten.

functions.name: BN_get_rfc3526_prime_2048
functions.description: Initializes ret (or allocates a new BIGNUM if ret is NULL) with the 2048-bit MODP prime from RFC 3526. Returns ret or NULL on allocation failure. The group generator is 2.
requirements: If ret is NULL, caller must free the returned BIGNUM with BN_free.
If ret is non-NULL, it must be a valid, mutable BIGNUM to be overwritten.

functions.name: BN_get_rfc3526_prime_3072
functions.description: Initializes ret (or allocates a new BIGNUM if ret is NULL) with the 3072-bit MODP prime from RFC 3526. Returns ret or NULL on allocation failure. The group generator is 2.
requirements: If ret is NULL, caller must free the returned BIGNUM with BN_free.
If ret is non-NULL, it must be a valid, mutable BIGNUM to be overwritten.

functions.name: BN_get_rfc3526_prime_4096
functions.description: Initializes ret (or allocates a new BIGNUM if ret is NULL) with the 4096-bit MODP prime from RFC 3526. Returns ret or NULL on allocation failure. The group generator is 2.
requirements: If ret is NULL, caller must free the returned BIGNUM with BN_free.
If ret is non-NULL, it must be a valid, mutable BIGNUM to be overwritten.

functions.name: BN_get_rfc3526_prime_6144
functions.description: Initializes ret (or allocates a new BIGNUM if ret is NULL) with the 6144-bit MODP prime from RFC 3526. Returns ret or NULL on allocation failure. The group generator is 2.
requirements: If ret is NULL, caller must free the returned BIGNUM with BN_free.
If ret is non-NULL, it must be a valid, mutable BIGNUM to be overwritten.

functions.name: BN_get_rfc3526_prime_8192
functions.description: Initializes ret (or allocates a new BIGNUM if ret is NULL) with the 8192-bit MODP prime from RFC 3526. Returns ret or NULL on allocation failure. The group generator is 2.
requirements: If ret is NULL, caller must free the returned BIGNUM with BN_free.
If ret is non-NULL, it must be a valid, mutable BIGNUM to be overwritten.

functions.name: DH_generate_parameters_ex
functions.signature: int DH_generate_parameters_ex(DH *dh, int prime_bits, int generator, BN_GENCB *cb);
functions.description: Generates DH parameters (a safe prime p of prime_bits and generator g) and stores them in dh. generator should typically be DH_GENERATOR_2. Invokes the BN generation callback cb during progress and once with event==3 when complete. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: dh must be a valid DH* to receive generated parameters.
prime_bits specifies the prime length in bits; must be positive and within implementation limits (OPENSSL_DH_MAX_MODULUS_BITS).
generator should generally be DH_GENERATOR_2 unless a specific alternative is required.
cb may be NULL or a valid BN_GENCB* prepared per bn.h.

functions.name: DH_generate_key
functions.description: Generates a random private key for dh if absent and sets/updates the corresponding public key. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: dh must be a valid DH* with parameters p and g configured (either via set functions or a standard group).
Thread-safety: function mutates dh; do not call concurrently with other mutating operations on the same DH.

functions.name: DH_compute_key_padded
functions.description: Computes the DH shared secret with peer’s public key peers_key using dh and writes it as a big-endian integer padded to DH_size(dh) bytes into out. Returns the number of bytes written (always DH_size(dh)) or a negative value on error. Preferred over DH_compute_key because it preserves leading zeros and matches PKCS #3.
requirements: out must point to a buffer of at least DH_size(dh) bytes.
peers_key must be a valid BIGNUM public key for the same group; callers should validate it (e.g., with DH_check_pub_key) to avoid errors.
dh must contain a valid key pair and parameters; it must have a private key set.
Be aware the return-value convention is nonstandard here: negative on error, otherwise DH_size(dh).
Thread-safety: does not mutate dh and may be used concurrently.

functions.name: DH_compute_key_hashed
functions.signature: int DH_compute_key_hashed(DH *dh, uint8_t *out, size_t *out_len, size_t max_out_len, const BIGNUM *peers_key, const EVP_MD *digest);
functions.description: Computes the DH shared secret with peers_key using dh, hashes it with digest, and writes the hash output to out if the hash output length is <= max_out_len. Sets *out_len to the number of bytes written. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error. Uses standard BoringSSL success/failure convention.
requirements: dh must contain a valid key pair and parameters; it must have a private key set.
peers_key must be a valid BIGNUM public key for the same group; callers should validate it (e.g., with DH_check_pub_key).
digest must be a valid EVP_MD specifying the hash function.
out must point to a buffer with capacity at least max_out_len bytes.
out_len must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the actual number of bytes written.
If the hash output length exceeds max_out_len, the function signals an error (returns 0).
Thread-safety: does not mutate dh and may be used concurrently.

functions.name: DH_size
functions.description: Returns the size, in bytes, of the DH group’s prime (i.e., the size of DH secrets and padded shared keys).
requirements: dh must be a valid DH* with parameters set (p present) for a meaningful value.

functions.name: DH_num_bits
functions.description: Returns the minimum number of bits needed to represent the absolute value of the DH group’s prime.
requirements: dh must be a valid DH* with parameters set (p present) for a meaningful value.

functions.name: DH_check
functions.description: Checks the suitability of dh as a DH group and sets DH_CHECK_* flags in *out_flags to indicate any issues. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error. May be computationally expensive.
requirements: dh must be a valid DH* with parameters set.
out_flags must be a non-NULL pointer to an int to receive bitwise DH_CHECK_* flags.
Caller must inspect *out_flags for DH_CHECK_* issues even when the function returns 1.

functions.name: DH_check_pub_key
functions.signature: int DH_check_pub_key(const DH *dh, const BIGNUM *pub_key, int *out_flags);
functions.description: Validates pub_key for use with dh and sets DH_CHECK_PUBKEY_* flags in *out_flags to describe any problems. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: dh must be a valid DH* with parameters set.
pub_key must be a BIGNUM candidate public key for the same group.
out_flags must be a non-NULL pointer to receive DH_CHECK_PUBKEY_* bit flags.
Caller must inspect *out_flags for issues even when the function returns 1.

functions.name: DHparams_dup
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new DH with parameters copied from dh, or NULL on error.
requirements: dh must be a valid DH* with parameters set to copy.
Caller must free the returned DH* with DH_free.

functions.name: DH_parse_parameters
functions.description: Parses a DER-encoded DHParameter (PKCS #3) from cbs, advances cbs on success, and returns a newly-allocated DH* or NULL on error.
requirements: cbs must point to a buffer containing a DER-encoded DHParameter structure and will be advanced on success.
Caller must free the returned DH* with DH_free.

functions.name: DH_marshal_parameters
functions.description: Encodes dh as a DER-encoded DHParameter (PKCS #3) and appends it to cbb. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: cbb must be an initialized CBB ready to receive appended data.
dh must be a valid DH* with parameters set.
Caller must check the return value for success (1) or failure (0).

functions.name: DH_generate_parameters
functions.signature: DH *DH_generate_parameters(int prime_len, int generator, void (*callback)(int, int, void *), void *cb_arg);
functions.description: Deprecated. Generates DH parameters similarly to DH_generate_parameters_ex and returns a newly-allocated DH* on success or NULL on error. Provided for compatibility only.
requirements: Prefer DH_generate_parameters_ex for new code.
callback and cb_arg are used for progress callbacks per legacy API; may be NULL depending on usage.
Caller must free the returned DH* with DH_free.

functions.name: d2i_DHparams
functions.signature: DH *d2i_DHparams(DH **ret, const unsigned char **inp, long len);
functions.description: Deprecated. Parses a DER-encoded DHParameter (PKCS #3) from *inp of length len into ret as per d2i conventions, advancing *inp. Use DH_parse_parameters instead.
requirements: inp must point to a buffer containing len bytes of DER-encoded DHParameter; *inp is advanced on success.
ret may be NULL to allocate a new DH or may point to an existing DH* to reuse; standard d2i semantics apply.
Caller should free any newly allocated DH* with DH_free.
Prefer DH_parse_parameters in new code.

functions.name: i2d_DHparams
functions.description: Deprecated. Encodes in as a DER-encoded DHParameter (PKCS #3) as per i2d conventions and writes/appends to *outp. Use DH_marshal_parameters instead.
requirements: in must be a valid DH* with parameters set.
outp follows standard i2d semantics (may be NULL to query length in typical APIs; specific behaviors not restated here).
Prefer DH_marshal_parameters for new code.
Caller must check the return value for success (>0) or failure (<=0) per i2d conventions (details not restated here).

functions.name: DH_compute_key
functions.description: Deprecated variant. Computes the DH shared secret and writes a variable-length big-endian value without leading zero padding into out. Returns the number of bytes written or a negative value on error. Susceptible to side-channel issues; prefer DH_compute_key_padded.
requirements: out must point to a buffer of at least DH_size(dh) bytes.
peers_key must be a valid BIGNUM public key for the same group; callers should validate it (e.g., with DH_check_pub_key).
dh must contain a valid key pair and parameters; it must have a private key set.
Be aware the return-value convention is nonstandard here: negative on error, otherwise number of bytes written (<= DH_size(dh)).
Thread-safety: does not mutate dh and may be used concurrently.

functions.name: EVP_md4
functions.description: Returns an EVP_MD object implementing the MD4 hash algorithm. Use to configure an EVP_MD_CTX for MD4-based hashing.

functions.name: EVP_md5
functions.description: Returns an EVP_MD object implementing the MD5 hash algorithm. Use to configure an EVP_MD_CTX for MD5-based hashing.

functions.name: EVP_sha1
functions.description: Returns an EVP_MD object implementing the SHA-1 hash algorithm. Use to configure an EVP_MD_CTX for SHA-1-based hashing.

functions.name: EVP_sha224
functions.description: Returns an EVP_MD object implementing the SHA-224 hash algorithm. Use to configure an EVP_MD_CTX for SHA-224-based hashing.

functions.name: EVP_sha256
