functions.name: HKDF
functions.signature: int HKDF(uint8_t *out_key, size_t out_len, const EVP_MD *digest, const uint8_t *secret, size_t secret_len, const uint8_t *salt, size_t salt_len, const uint8_t *info, size_t info_len);
functions.description: Computes HKDF (RFC 5869) using the given digest. It performs Extract-and-Expand on initial keying material secret with optional salt and info, writing out_len bytes of output keying material to out_key. Returns 1 on success and 0 on error. Intended for deriving cryptographic keys from high-entropy input keying material; not a password-based key derivation function.
requirements: out_key must point to a writable buffer of at least out_len bytes.
out_len must not exceed the HKDF maximum for the selected digest (RFC 5869: out_len <= 255 * HashLen). Exceeding this results in an error (e.g., HKDF_R_OUTPUT_TOO_LARGE).
digest must be a valid, initialized EVP_MD algorithm pointer and must be the intended hash for both extract and expand stages.
secret must point to at least secret_len bytes of initial keying material.
salt must point to at least salt_len bytes if salt_len > 0. If salt_len == 0, salt may be NULL (inferred from common OpenSSL/BoringSSL API patterns).
info must point to at least info_len bytes if info_len > 0. If info_len == 0, info may be NULL (inferred from common OpenSSL/BoringSSL API patterns).
Caller must check the return value and must not use out_key contents on failure (return 0).
No key stretching: do not use this function by itself for password hashing/derivation.

functions.name: HKDF_extract
functions.signature: int HKDF_extract(uint8_t *out_key, size_t *out_len, const EVP_MD *digest, const uint8_t *secret, size_t secret_len, const uint8_t *salt, size_t salt_len);
functions.description: Computes the HKDF pseudorandom key (PRK) from initial keying material secret and salt using the given digest (RFC 5869 Extract). Writes the PRK to out_key and the actual number of bytes written to *out_len. Returns 1 on success and 0 on error. Note: parameter order differs from RFC 5869’s notation; secret is the IKM and salt is the salt.
requirements: out_key must point to a writable buffer large enough for the PRK; the maximum PRK size is EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE.
out_len must be a valid, writable pointer; on success, *out_len is set to the PRK length (typically the digest’s output size, up to EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE).
digest must be a valid, initialized EVP_MD algorithm pointer.
secret must point to at least secret_len bytes of input keying material (IKM).
salt must point to at least salt_len bytes if salt_len > 0. If salt_len == 0, salt may be NULL (inferred from common OpenSSL/BoringSSL API patterns and RFC 5869 allowing an optional salt).
Caller must check the return value and must not use outputs on failure (return 0).
Be careful with parameter order: the function takes (secret, salt) in that order, which differs from some RFC text and pseudocode.

functions.name: HKDF_expand
functions.signature: int HKDF_expand(uint8_t *out_key, size_t out_len, const EVP_MD *digest, const uint8_t *prk, size_t prk_len, const uint8_t *info, size_t info_len);
functions.description: Computes HKDF output keying material (OKM) of length out_len from a PRK and optional info using the given digest (RFC 5869 Expand). Writes the result to out_key. Returns 1 on success and 0 on error.
requirements: out_key must point to a writable buffer of at least out_len bytes.
out_len must not exceed the HKDF maximum for the selected digest (RFC 5869: out_len <= 255 * HashLen). Exceeding this results in an error (e.g., HKDF_R_OUTPUT_TOO_LARGE).
digest must be a valid, initialized EVP_MD algorithm pointer and should match the digest used for HKDF_extract when the PRK was produced.
prk must point to at least prk_len bytes containing a valid HKDF PRK. (Typically this is the output of HKDF_extract for the same digest.)
info must point to at least info_len bytes if info_len > 0. If info_len == 0, info may be NULL (inferred from common OpenSSL/BoringSSL API patterns).
Caller must check the return value and must not use out_key contents on failure (return 0).

functions.name: HMAC
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT uint8_t *HMAC(const EVP_MD *evp_md, const void *key, size_t key_len, const uint8_t *data, size_t data_len, uint8_t *out, unsigned int *out_len);
functions.description: Computes a one-shot HMAC over data using the specified message-digest algorithm and key. Writes the MAC into out and its length to *out_len (if not NULL). Returns out on success or NULL on error. Typical usage: select an EVP_MD (e.g., EVP_sha256()), provide key and data buffers, and supply an output buffer large enough for the digest.
requirements: evp_md must reference a valid hash function (e.g., from EVP_sha256()) and must not be NULL.
out must point to a buffer with at least EVP_MD_size(evp_md) bytes available; EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE is always sufficient.
If out_len is non-NULL, it must point to writable memory to receive the actual MAC length.
data must reference at least data_len bytes; key must reference at least key_len bytes (key_len may be zero for an empty key).
Returns out on success; returns NULL on error and no output is produced.

functions.name: HMAC_CTX_init
functions.description: Initializes an HMAC_CTX for use in incremental HMAC operations. Intended for stack-allocated HMAC_CTX objects; no allocation is performed.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to HMAC_CTX storage (typically stack-allocated).
ctx must not already hold allocated internal state unless it has been previously cleaned up via HMAC_CTX_cleanup or HMAC_CTX_reset before re-initializing.

functions.name: HMAC_CTX_new
functions.description: Allocates and initializes a new HMAC_CTX object. Returns the allocated context or NULL on allocation failure. Caller must free with HMAC_CTX_free.
requirements: Caller must check for NULL return to detect allocation failure.
The returned context must be released with HMAC_CTX_free to avoid memory leaks.

functions.name: HMAC_CTX_cleanup
functions.description: Releases internal resources owned by ctx but does not free the ctx object itself. Use to clean up a context initialized with HMAC_CTX_init.
requirements: ctx must be a valid HMAC_CTX previously initialized (e.g., via HMAC_CTX_init or HMAC_CTX_new).
After cleanup, the ctx object remains allocated; to reuse it, call HMAC_CTX_init again or HMAC_CTX_reset.
Do not use ctx for HMAC operations after cleanup until it has been re-initialized.

functions.name: HMAC_CTX_cleanse
functions.description: Zeroes the digest state in ctx and then performs the actions of HMAC_CTX_cleanup. Intended to scrub sensitive state before cleanup.
requirements: ctx must be a valid HMAC_CTX.
After cleanse, ctx no longer holds an active HMAC state; reinitialize with HMAC_CTX_init or free with HMAC_CTX_free before reuse.

functions.name: HMAC_CTX_free
functions.description: Cleans up the HMAC_CTX (as per HMAC_CTX_cleanup) and then frees the ctx pointer.
requirements: ctx may be NULL (no effect) or a valid HMAC_CTX obtained from HMAC_CTX_new.
Do not use ctx after this call.

functions.name: HMAC_Init_ex
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int HMAC_Init_ex(HMAC_CTX *ctx, const void *key, size_t key_len, const EVP_MD *md, ENGINE *impl);
functions.description: Initializes or reinitializes an HMAC operation on an existing HMAC_CTX. Sets the hash function to md and the key to key/key_len. On subsequent (non-initial) calls, md may be NULL to reuse the previous hash; if the hash is unchanged and key is NULL, the previous key is reused. Returns 1 on success or 0 on allocation failure. WARNING: On non-initial calls, passing key as NULL while keeping the same md reuses the previous key (not the empty key).
requirements: ctx must be initialized via HMAC_CTX_init or created via HMAC_CTX_new before calling.
For initial setup, md must be a valid digest; for reinitialization, md may be NULL to reuse the previous digest.
If the digest has not changed and key is NULL, the previous key is reused; to use an empty key on reinit, explicitly pass key_len = 0 with a non-NULL key pointer to a zero-length buffer.
key must reference at least key_len bytes; key_len may be zero for an empty key on initial setup or when explicitly desired.
Returns 1 on success; returns 0 on allocation failure and the ctx may be left unchanged or partially updated depending on failure (caller should handle error).
impl is reserved for engine selection; may be NULL.

functions.name: HMAC_Update
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int HMAC_Update(HMAC_CTX *ctx, const uint8_t *data, size_t data_len);
functions.description: Feeds data into the ongoing HMAC computation in ctx. Can be called multiple times to process streaming input. Returns 1.
requirements: ctx must be initialized for an HMAC operation via HMAC_Init_ex before calling.
data must point to at least data_len bytes (data may be NULL only if data_len is 0).
Caller should check the return value; non-1 indicates failure.

functions.name: HMAC_Final
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int HMAC_Final(HMAC_CTX *ctx, uint8_t *out, unsigned int *out_len);
functions.description: Finalizes the HMAC computation in ctx, writing the result to out and the length to *out_len if provided. The out buffer must be large enough for HMAC_size(ctx); EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE is always sufficient. Returns 1 on success or 0 on allocation failure.
requirements: ctx must have an active HMAC operation initialized with HMAC_Init_ex and updated as needed.
out must point to a buffer with at least HMAC_size(ctx) bytes available; EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE is sufficient for any supported digest.
If out_len is non-NULL, it must point to writable memory to receive the MAC length.
Caller must check the return value; 0 indicates failure (e.g., allocation failure).
After successful finalization, ctx’s state for that operation is consumed; to compute another HMAC, reinitialize via HMAC_Init_ex.

functions.name: HMAC_size
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of the HMAC that will be produced by the current configuration of ctx.
requirements: ctx must have been set up with HMAC_Init_ex prior to calling.
ctx must not be NULL.

functions.name: HMAC_CTX_get_md
functions.description: Returns the digest algorithm configured in ctx for the HMAC operation.
requirements: ctx must be a valid pointer to an HMAC_CTX (typically set up via HMAC_Init_ex).
The returned EVP_MD pointer is owned by the library; do not free it.

functions.name: HMAC_CTX_copy_ex
functions.description: Copies the HMAC state from src into an already-initialized dest. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: dest must have been initialized by calling HMAC_CTX_init before this call.
src must be a valid, initialized HMAC_CTX whose state can be copied.
Caller must check the return value; 0 indicates failure and dest may be unchanged or partially modified depending on failure.

functions.name: HMAC_CTX_reset
functions.description: Resets ctx by calling HMAC_CTX_cleanup followed by HMAC_CTX_init, making it ready for reuse.
requirements: ctx must be a valid HMAC_CTX pointer.
After reset, any previous HMAC operation state in ctx is discarded.

functions.name: HMAC_Init
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int HMAC_Init(HMAC_CTX *ctx, const void *key, int key_len, const EVP_MD *md);
functions.description: Deprecated. Initializes an HMAC operation on ctx with md and key/key_len. Prefer HMAC_Init_ex. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error as per implementation.
requirements: ctx must be initialized (e.g., via HMAC_CTX_init) before calling.
key must reference at least key_len bytes; key_len may be zero to use an empty key.
md must be a valid digest algorithm pointer.
Callers should migrate to HMAC_Init_ex for new code.

functions.name: HMAC_CTX_copy
functions.description: Deprecated. Initializes dest by calling HMAC_CTX_init and then copies the HMAC state from src into dest. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: dest must not already be initialized for an operation with HMAC_Init_ex (the function calls HMAC_CTX_init on dest itself).
src must be a valid, initialized HMAC_CTX to copy from.
Caller must check the return value; 0 indicates failure.

functions.name: EVP_hpke_x25519_hkdf_sha256
functions.description: Returns the KEM descriptor for DHKEM(X25519, HKDF-SHA256) to be used when configuring an HPKE context or keys. Typical usage: pass the returned pointer to functions that require a const EVP_HPKE_KEM* parameter.
requirements: Return value must be checked for NULL to detect allocation or configuration failures.
The returned pointer is a library-owned singleton; do not free it or modify through it.

functions.name: EVP_hpke_p256_hkdf_sha256
functions.description: Returns the KEM descriptor for DHKEM(P-256, HKDF-SHA256). Use when configuring HPKE operations that require a const EVP_HPKE_KEM*.
requirements: Check for NULL return before use.
The returned descriptor is library-owned; do not free or mutate.

functions.name: EVP_hpke_xwing
functions.description: Returns the KEM descriptor for the XWING KEM (BoringSSL experimental/alternative KEM) usable with HPKE.
requirements: Check for NULL return before use.
The returned descriptor is library-owned; do not free or mutate.
Interoperability and parameter details beyond the identifier are not specified in this header.

functions.name: EVP_hpke_mlkem768
functions.description: Returns the KEM descriptor for ML-KEM-768 usable with HPKE.
requirements: Check for NULL return before use.
The returned descriptor is library-owned; do not free or mutate.

functions.name: EVP_hpke_mlkem1024
functions.description: Returns the KEM descriptor for ML-KEM-1024 usable with HPKE.
requirements: Check for NULL return before use.
The returned descriptor is library-owned; do not free or mutate.

functions.name: EVP_HPKE_KEM_id
functions.description: Returns the HPKE KEM identifier for the given KEM descriptor, matching one of the EVP_HPKE_* KEM constants.
requirements: kem must be a valid pointer previously obtained from a BoringSSL HPKE KEM getter or from an initialized HPKE key/context.
Behavior is undefined for NULL kem.

functions.name: EVP_HPKE_KEM_public_key_len
functions.description: Returns the encoded public key length for the given KEM. At most EVP_HPKE_MAX_PUBLIC_KEY_LENGTH.
requirements: kem must be a valid KEM descriptor pointer.
Do not assume the same size across KEMs; query per KEM.

functions.name: EVP_HPKE_KEM_private_key_len

requirements: kem must be a valid KEM descriptor pointer.

functions.name: EVP_HPKE_KEM_enc_len
functions.description: Returns the length of the encapsulated shared secret (enc) for the given KEM. At most EVP_HPKE_MAX_ENC_LENGTH.
requirements: kem must be a valid KEM descriptor pointer.

functions.name: EVP_hpke_hkdf_sha256
functions.description: Returns the KDF descriptor for HKDF-SHA256 to be used with HPKE.
requirements: Check for NULL return before use.
Descriptor is library-owned; do not free or mutate.

functions.name: EVP_HPKE_KDF_id
functions.description: Returns the HPKE KDF identifier for the given KDF descriptor.
requirements: kdf must be a valid KDF descriptor pointer.

functions.name: EVP_HPKE_KDF_hkdf_md
functions.description: Returns the OpenSSL EVP_MD for the HKDF hash associated with the KDF descriptor, or NULL if the KDF is not HKDF-based (all currently supported are HKDF-based).
requirements: kdf must be a valid KDF descriptor pointer.
Caller must not free the returned EVP_MD; it is library-owned.

functions.name: EVP_hpke_aes_128_gcm
functions.description: Returns the AEAD descriptor for AES-128-GCM usable with HPKE.
requirements: Check for NULL return before use.
Descriptor is library-owned; do not free or mutate.

functions.name: EVP_hpke_aes_256_gcm
functions.description: Returns the AEAD descriptor for AES-256-GCM usable with HPKE.
requirements: Check for NULL return before use.
Descriptor is library-owned; do not free or mutate.

functions.name: EVP_hpke_chacha20_poly1305
functions.description: Returns the AEAD descriptor for ChaCha20-Poly1305 usable with HPKE.
requirements: Check for NULL return before use.
Descriptor is library-owned; do not free or mutate.

functions.name: EVP_HPKE_AEAD_id
functions.description: Returns the HPKE AEAD identifier for the given AEAD descriptor.
requirements: aead must be a valid AEAD descriptor pointer.

functions.name: EVP_HPKE_AEAD_aead
functions.description: Returns the underlying EVP_AEAD implementation corresponding to the HPKE AEAD descriptor.
requirements: aead must be a valid AEAD descriptor pointer.
Caller must not free the returned EVP_AEAD; it is library-owned.

functions.name: EVP_HPKE_KEY_zero
functions.description: Initializes an uninitialized EVP_HPKE_KEY to the zero state so it can be safely initialized later or uniformly cleaned up.
requirements: key must be a valid pointer to storage for EVP_HPKE_KEY.
Callers should follow with EVP_HPKE_KEY_init, EVP_HPKE_KEY_copy, or EVP_HPKE_KEY_generate before use.

functions.name: EVP_HPKE_KEY_cleanup
functions.description: Releases memory referenced by an EVP_HPKE_KEY previously zeroed or initialized. Safe to call on a zero-state key.
requirements: key must have been set to zero state with EVP_HPKE_KEY_zero or initialized by another EVP_HPKE_KEY_* initializer.

functions.name: EVP_HPKE_KEY_new
functions.description: Allocates a new heap-allocated EVP_HPKE_KEY. Caller must free with EVP_HPKE_KEY_free.
requirements: Check for NULL return before use.
After allocation, initialize using EVP_HPKE_KEY_generate, EVP_HPKE_KEY_init, or EVP_HPKE_KEY_copy before operational use.

functions.name: EVP_HPKE_KEY_free
functions.description: Frees a heap-allocated EVP_HPKE_KEY created by EVP_HPKE_KEY_new.
requirements: key must have been allocated by EVP_HPKE_KEY_new (may be NULL for no-op).
Do not use key after freeing.

functions.name: EVP_HPKE_KEY_copy
functions.description: Initializes dst as a copy of src. On success returns 1 and dst must later be cleaned with EVP_HPKE_KEY_cleanup.
requirements: dst must be in zero state or uninitialized storage that the function will initialize.
src must point to a valid, initialized EVP_HPKE_KEY.
Check return value: 1 on success, 0 on error. On failure, calling EVP_HPKE_KEY_cleanup on dst is safe but not required.

functions.name: EVP_HPKE_KEY_move
functions.description: Moves the key material from in to out. After the call, in is left in the zero state and out takes ownership of the key.
requirements: out must be initialized or in zero state prior to call.
in must be a valid EVP_HPKE_KEY (initialized or zero state).
Do not use in for cryptographic operations after the move unless reinitialized.

functions.name: EVP_HPKE_KEY_init
functions.signature: int EVP_HPKE_KEY_init(EVP_HPKE_KEY *key, const EVP_HPKE_KEM *kem, const uint8_t *priv_key, size_t priv_key_len);
functions.description: Decodes an encoded private key for the given KEM into key. Returns 1 on success, 0 if the private key was invalid.
requirements: key must be in zero state or otherwise uninitialized and suitable for initialization.
kem must be a valid KEM descriptor pointer.
priv_key must point to a buffer containing an encoded private key matching kem; length must equal EVP_HPKE_KEM_private_key_len(kem).
On success, caller must later call EVP_HPKE_KEY_cleanup.
Check return value and avoid using key on failure.

functions.name: EVP_HPKE_KEY_generate
functions.description: Generates a new recipient KEM keypair for the specified KEM and initializes key.
requirements: key must be in zero state or otherwise suitable for initialization.
kem must be a valid KEM descriptor pointer.
Check return value: 1 on success, 0 on error. On success, caller must later call EVP_HPKE_KEY_cleanup.

functions.name: EVP_HPKE_KEY_kem
functions.description: Returns the KEM associated with the initialized key.
requirements: key must be a valid, initialized EVP_HPKE_KEY.
Returned pointer is library-owned; do not free or modify.

functions.name: EVP_HPKE_KEY_public_key
functions.signature: int EVP_HPKE_KEY_public_key(const EVP_HPKE_KEY *key, uint8_t *out, size_t *out_len, size_t max_out);
functions.description: Writes the encoded public key for key into out and sets *out_len. Returns 1 on success, 0 if max_out is too small or on error.
requirements: key must be a valid, initialized EVP_HPKE_KEY.
out must point to a writable buffer of at least max_out bytes.
out_len must be non-NULL.
max_out must be >= required size; use EVP_HPKE_KEM_public_key_len(EVP_HPKE_KEY_kem(key)) or EVP_HPKE_MAX_PUBLIC_KEY_LENGTH to size the buffer.
Check return value before using output.

functions.name: EVP_HPKE_KEY_private_key
functions.signature: int EVP_HPKE_KEY_private_key(const EVP_HPKE_KEY *key, uint8_t *out, size_t *out_len, size_t max_out);
functions.description: Writes the encoded private key for key into out and sets *out_len. Returns 1 on success, 0 if max_out is too small or on error.
requirements: key must be a valid, initialized EVP_HPKE_KEY.
out must point to a writable buffer of at least max_out bytes.
out_len must be non-NULL.
Max size may be up to EVP_HPKE_MAX_PRIVATE_KEY_LENGTH; exact size via EVP_HPKE_KEM_private_key_len(EVP_HPKE_KEY_kem(key)).
Check return value before using output.

functions.name: EVP_HPKE_CTX_zero
functions.description: Initializes an uninitialized EVP_HPKE_CTX to the zero state so it can be set up as a sender or recipient later.
requirements: ctx must be a valid pointer to storage for EVP_HPKE_CTX.
After zeroing, set up using one of the EVP_HPKE_CTX_setup_* functions before use.

functions.name: EVP_HPKE_CTX_cleanup
functions.description: Releases memory referenced by an EVP_HPKE_CTX that was previously zeroed or set up. Safe to call on a zero-state context.
requirements: ctx must have been initialized with EVP_HPKE_CTX_zero or one of the setup functions before cleanup.

functions.name: EVP_HPKE_CTX_new
functions.description: Allocates a new heap-allocated EVP_HPKE_CTX. Caller must free with EVP_HPKE_CTX_free.
requirements: Check for NULL return before use.
After allocation, set up using one of the EVP_HPKE_CTX_setup_* functions before use.

functions.name: EVP_HPKE_CTX_free
functions.description: Frees a heap-allocated EVP_HPKE_CTX created by EVP_HPKE_CTX_new.
requirements: ctx must have been allocated by EVP_HPKE_CTX_new (may be NULL for no-op).
Do not use ctx after freeing.

functions.name: EVP_HPKE_CTX_setup_sender
functions.signature: int EVP_HPKE_CTX_setup_sender(EVP_HPKE_CTX *ctx, uint8_t *out_enc, size_t *out_enc_len, size_t max_enc, const EVP_HPKE_KEM *kem, const EVP_HPKE_KDF *kdf, const EVP_HPKE_AEAD *aead, const uint8_t *peer_public_key, size_t peer_public_key_len, const uint8_t *info, size_t info_len);
functions.description: Implements HPKE SetupBaseS: encapsulates a shared secret to peer_public_key and initializes ctx as a sender. Writes the encapsulated value (enc) to out_enc and sets *out_enc_len. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error (including invalid peer_public_key or too-small buffer).
requirements: ctx must be zeroed or uninitialized storage ready for setup; on success caller must later call EVP_HPKE_CTX_cleanup.
out_enc must point to a writable buffer of at least max_enc bytes; set max_enc >= required size (<= EVP_HPKE_MAX_ENC_LENGTH or query via EVP_HPKE_KEM_enc_len(kem)).
out_enc_len must be non-NULL.
kem, kdf, and aead must be valid descriptors.
peer_public_key must be a valid encoded public key for kem with length peer_public_key_len exactly matching EVP_HPKE_KEM_public_key_len(kem).
info may be NULL if info_len is zero; otherwise must reference info_len bytes.
On failure, it is safe but not required to call EVP_HPKE_CTX_cleanup.

functions.name: EVP_HPKE_CTX_setup_sender_with_seed_for_testing
functions.signature: int EVP_HPKE_CTX_setup_sender_with_seed_for_testing(EVP_HPKE_CTX *ctx, uint8_t *out_enc, size_t *out_enc_len, size_t max_enc, const EVP_HPKE_KEM *kem, const EVP_HPKE_KDF *kdf, const EVP_HPKE_AEAD *aead, const uint8_t *peer_public_key, size_t peer_public_key_len, const uint8_t *info, size_t info_len, const uint8_t *seed, size_t seed_len);
functions.description: Testing-only variant of SetupBaseS that behaves deterministically given a seed. Seed format depends on kem (for X25519: sender's ephemeral private key; for P-256: an HKDF input). Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: All requirements of EVP_HPKE_CTX_setup_sender apply.
seed must point to seed_len bytes; format depends on kem as documented (X25519 ephemeral private key; P-256 HKDF input).
Use only for testing; not intended for production randomness.

functions.name: EVP_HPKE_CTX_setup_recipient
functions.signature: int EVP_HPKE_CTX_setup_recipient(EVP_HPKE_CTX *ctx, const EVP_HPKE_KEY *key, const EVP_HPKE_KDF *kdf, const EVP_HPKE_AEAD *aead, const uint8_t *enc, size_t enc_len, const uint8_t *info, size_t info_len);
functions.description: Implements HPKE SetupBaseR: decapsulates the shared secret using key and initializes ctx as a recipient. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error (including invalid enc).
requirements: ctx must be zeroed or suitable for initialization; on success caller must later call EVP_HPKE_CTX_cleanup.
key must be a valid initialized EVP_HPKE_KEY whose KEM matches the encapsulated value enc.
kdf and aead must be valid descriptors compatible with the sender.
enc must point to an encapsulated value with length enc_len exactly matching EVP_HPKE_KEM_enc_len(EVP_HPKE_KEY_kem(key)).
info may be NULL if info_len is zero; otherwise must reference info_len bytes.
On failure, it is safe but not required to call EVP_HPKE_CTX_cleanup.

functions.name: EVP_HPKE_CTX_setup_auth_sender
functions.signature: int EVP_HPKE_CTX_setup_auth_sender(EVP_HPKE_CTX *ctx, uint8_t *out_enc, size_t *out_enc_len, size_t max_enc, const EVP_HPKE_KEY *key, const EVP_HPKE_KDF *kdf, const EVP_HPKE_AEAD *aead, const uint8_t *peer_public_key, size_t peer_public_key_len, const uint8_t *info, size_t info_len);
functions.description: Implements HPKE SetupAuthS: like SetupBaseS but authenticates the context using the sender's long-term key. Produces enc and initializes ctx as a sender.
requirements: All requirements of EVP_HPKE_CTX_setup_sender apply, except kem is derived from key.
key must be a valid initialized EVP_HPKE_KEY for the same KEM as peer_public_key.
peer_public_key must be a valid encoded recipient public key for that KEM with exact length.
Check return value; on success, later call EVP_HPKE_CTX_cleanup.

functions.name: EVP_HPKE_CTX_setup_auth_sender_with_seed_for_testing
functions.signature: int EVP_HPKE_CTX_setup_auth_sender_with_seed_for_testing(EVP_HPKE_CTX *ctx, uint8_t *out_enc, size_t *out_enc_len, size_t max_enc, const EVP_HPKE_KEY *key, const EVP_HPKE_KDF *kdf, const EVP_HPKE_AEAD *aead, const uint8_t *peer_public_key, size_t peer_public_key_len, const uint8_t *info, size_t info_len, const uint8_t *seed, size_t seed_len);
functions.description: Testing-only deterministic variant of SetupAuthS that accepts a seed whose format depends on the KEM (X25519: ephemeral private key; P-256: HKDF input).
requirements: All requirements of EVP_HPKE_CTX_setup_auth_sender apply.
seed must point to seed_len bytes in the KEM-specific format.
Use only for testing; not intended for production randomness.

functions.name: EVP_HPKE_CTX_setup_auth_recipient
functions.signature: int EVP_HPKE_CTX_setup_auth_recipient(EVP_HPKE_CTX *ctx, const EVP_HPKE_KEY *key, const EVP_HPKE_KDF *kdf, const EVP_HPKE_AEAD *aead, const uint8_t *enc, size_t enc_len, const uint8_t *info, size_t info_len, const uint8_t *peer_public_key, size_t peer_public_key_len);
functions.description: Implements HPKE SetupAuthR: like SetupBaseR but verifies the context was authenticated with the sender's public key (peer_public_key). Initializes ctx as a recipient.
requirements: All requirements of EVP_HPKE_CTX_setup_recipient apply.
peer_public_key must be the sender's public key for the same KEM as key; length must match EVP_HPKE_KEM_public_key_len(EVP_HPKE_KEY_kem(key)).
Check return value; on success, later call EVP_HPKE_CTX_cleanup.

functions.name: EVP_HPKE_CTX_open
functions.signature: int EVP_HPKE_CTX_open(EVP_HPKE_CTX *ctx, uint8_t *out, size_t *out_len, size_t max_out_len, const uint8_t *in, size_t in_len, const uint8_t *ad, size_t ad_len);
functions.description: Decrypts and authenticates ciphertext in using the recipient-configured HPKE context, authenticating associated data ad. Writes plaintext to out and sets *out_len. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure (e.g., authentication failure, wrong context role, buffer too small).
requirements: ctx must have been successfully set up as a recipient via an EVP_HPKE_CTX_setup_* function.
out must point to a writable buffer with at least max_out_len bytes; to ensure success, set max_out_len >= in_len.
out_len must be non-NULL.
in must point to in_len bytes of ciphertext produced by EVP_HPKE_CTX_seal with the matching context state/sequence.
ad may be NULL if ad_len is zero; otherwise must reference ad_len bytes.
Calls must be in-order and one-per-sequence number; sender and recipient must maintain matching call counts (stateful, ordered).
Check return value before using output.

functions.name: EVP_HPKE_CTX_seal
functions.signature: int EVP_HPKE_CTX_seal(EVP_HPKE_CTX *ctx, uint8_t *out, size_t *out_len, size_t max_out_len, const uint8_t *in, size_t in_len, const uint8_t *ad, size_t ad_len);
functions.description: Encrypts and authenticates plaintext in with associated data ad using a sender-configured HPKE context. Writes ciphertext to out and sets *out_len. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure (e.g., wrong context role or buffer too small).
requirements: ctx must have been successfully set up as a sender via an EVP_HPKE_CTX_setup_* function.

out must point to a writable buffer with at least max_out_len bytes; to ensure success, set max_out_len >= in_len + EVP_HPKE_CTX_max_overhead(ctx) (or use EVP_HPKE_MAX_OVERHEAD as a safe upper bound).
out_len must be non-NULL.
in must point to in_len bytes of plaintext.
ad may be NULL if ad_len is zero; otherwise must reference ad_len bytes.
Calls must be in-order and one-per-sequence number; sender and recipient must maintain matching call counts (stateful, ordered).
Check return value before using output.

functions.name: EVP_HPKE_CTX_export
functions.signature: int EVP_HPKE_CTX_export(const EVP_HPKE_CTX *ctx, uint8_t *out, size_t secret_len, const uint8_t *context, size_t context_len);
functions.description: Exports a secret of secret_len bytes from the HPKE context using the provided context string to bind application-specific context. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, set-up HPKE context (sender or recipient).
out must point to a writable buffer of at least secret_len bytes.
context may be NULL if context_len is zero; otherwise must reference context_len bytes.
Check return value before using output.

functions.name: EVP_HPKE_CTX_max_overhead
functions.description: Returns the maximum number of additional bytes added by sealing data with the given sender-configured context.
requirements: ctx must be a valid HPKE context set up as a sender.
Use result to size ciphertext buffers for EVP_HPKE_CTX_seal.

functions.name: EVP_HPKE_CTX_kem
functions.description: Returns the KEM configured in the HPKE context, or NULL if the context has not been set up.
requirements: ctx must be non-NULL.
Do not free the returned descriptor.

functions.name: EVP_HPKE_CTX_aead
functions.description: Returns the AEAD configured in the HPKE context, or NULL if the context has not been set up.
requirements: ctx must be non-NULL.
Do not free the returned descriptor.

functions.name: EVP_HPKE_CTX_kdf
functions.description: Returns the KDF configured in the HPKE context, or NULL if the context has not been set up.
requirements: ctx must be non-NULL.
Do not free the returned descriptor.

functions.name: HRSS_generate_key
functions.signature: int HRSS_generate_key(struct HRSS_public_key *out_pub, struct HRSS_private_key *out_priv, const uint8_t input[HRSS_GENERATE_KEY_BYTES]);
functions.description: Deterministically generates an HRSS key pair from the provided entropy. On success, writes the public key to out_pub and the private key to out_priv and returns 1; returns 0 on allocation failure. Intended for callers that can supply HRSS_GENERATE_KEY_BYTES of entropy and need reproducible key pairs for testing or KATs.
requirements: out_pub must be a non-NULL pointer to writable storage for a struct HRSS_public_key.
out_priv must be a non-NULL pointer to writable storage for a struct HRSS_private_key.
input must point to exactly HRSS_GENERATE_KEY_BYTES bytes of caller-provided entropy.
Caller must handle a return value of 0 as an allocation failure and treat outputs as unspecified in that case.
Function is deterministic with respect to input; identical input yields identical key pair.

functions.name: HRSS_encap
functions.signature: int HRSS_encap(uint8_t out_ciphertext[HRSS_CIPHERTEXT_BYTES], uint8_t out_shared_key[HRSS_KEY_BYTES], const struct HRSS_public_key *in_pub, const uint8_t in[HRSS_ENCAP_BYTES]);
functions.description: Deterministically encapsulates a random session key to the given public key using the provided entropy. Writes the ciphertext to out_ciphertext and the shared key to out_shared_key. Returns 1 on success or 0 on allocation failure. Intended for KEM encapsulation when the caller can supply HRSS_ENCAP_BYTES of entropy (e.g., for test vectors).
requirements: out_ciphertext must be a non-NULL pointer to a writable buffer of at least HRSS_CIPHERTEXT_BYTES bytes.
out_shared_key must be a non-NULL pointer to a writable buffer of at least HRSS_KEY_BYTES bytes.
in_pub must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid, initialized HRSS_public_key (produced by HRSS_generate_key or HRSS_parse_public_key).
in must point to exactly HRSS_ENCAP_BYTES bytes of caller-provided entropy.
Caller must check the return value; a return of 0 indicates allocation failure and outputs are unspecified.
Operation is deterministic with respect to in and in_pub; identical inputs produce identical outputs.

functions.name: HRSS_decap
functions.signature: int HRSS_decap(uint8_t out_shared_key[HRSS_KEY_BYTES], const struct HRSS_private_key *in_priv, const uint8_t *ciphertext, size_t ciphertext_len);
functions.description: Decapsulates a session key from the provided ciphertext using the private key. If the ciphertext is valid, writes the decrypted key to out_shared_key; otherwise writes an HMAC of the ciphertext under a secret key stored in in_priv. Returns 1 on success (regardless of ciphertext validity) or 0 on allocation failure. Constant-time behavior is intended except that an incorrect ciphertext length may leak which branch was taken.
requirements: out_shared_key must be a non-NULL pointer to a writable buffer of at least HRSS_KEY_BYTES bytes.
in_priv must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid, initialized HRSS_private_key (from HRSS_generate_key).
ciphertext may be any length; when ciphertext_len != HRSS_CIPHERTEXT_BYTES, the function may leak (via side channels) whether decryption vs. fallback HMAC was performed.
ciphertext, if non-NULL, must point to at least ciphertext_len bytes readable by the function; when ciphertext_len is non-zero, ciphertext must not be NULL.
Caller must check the return value; 0 indicates allocation failure and output is unspecified.
On success (return 1), out_shared_key is always written (either to the decapsulated key or to the fallback HMAC-derived key).

functions.name: HRSS_marshal_public_key
functions.signature: void HRSS_marshal_public_key(uint8_t out[HRSS_PUBLIC_KEY_BYTES], const struct HRSS_public_key *in_pub);
functions.description: Serializes the given HRSS public key into a fixed-size byte array. Intended for transmitting or storing the public key.
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to a writable buffer of at least HRSS_PUBLIC_KEY_BYTES bytes.
in_pub must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid, initialized HRSS_public_key (from HRSS_generate_key or HRSS_parse_public_key).
Caller must ensure the buffer lifetime of out spans the call; no return value is provided to signal errors.

functions.name: HRSS_parse_public_key
functions.signature: int HRSS_parse_public_key(struct HRSS_public_key *out, const uint8_t in[HRSS_PUBLIC_KEY_BYTES]);
functions.description: Parses a serialized HRSS public key from the provided byte array into out. Returns 1 on success or 0 on error (e.g., malformed input).
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to writable storage for a struct HRSS_public_key.
in must be a non-NULL pointer to exactly HRSS_PUBLIC_KEY_BYTES bytes containing a serialized public key.
Caller must check the return value; on 0, out is unspecified and must not be used.

functions.name: EVP_PKEY_CTX_hkdf_mode
functions.description: Configures which HKDF operation the EVP_PKEY context will run. Accepts one of the EVP_PKEY_HKDEF_MODE_* constants and returns 1 on success, 0 on error. Use with EVP_PKEY-based HKDF flow for OpenSSL compatibility; prefer <openssl/hkdf.h> otherwise. Note: although called a “mode”, HKDF-Extract and HKDF-Expand are distinct operations with distinct inputs/keys.
requirements: ctx must be a valid EVP_PKEY_CTX created with EVP_PKEY_CTX_new_id(EVP_PKEY_HKDF, ...) and initialized with EVP_PKEY_derive_init before use.
mode must be one of: EVP_PKEY_HKDEF_MODE_EXTRACT_AND_EXPAND, EVP_PKEY_HKDEF_MODE_EXTRACT_ONLY, or EVP_PKEY_HKDEF_MODE_EXPAND_ONLY.
Callers must check the return value: 1 indicates success, 0 indicates error.
When using EXTRACT_AND_EXPAND or EXPAND_ONLY, the HKDF output length is variable and is determined by the size of the output buffer passed to EVP_PKEY_derive.
Do not pass inputs intended for HKDF-Extract to HKDF-Expand or vice versa; they are distinct operations with distinct keying material.

functions.name: EVP_PKEY_CTX_set_hkdf_md
functions.description: Sets the message-digest algorithm to use with HKDF in the EVP_PKEY context. Returns 1 on success and 0 on error. Typically called after initializing the HKDF context and before derive.
requirements: ctx must be a valid EVP_PKEY_CTX created with EVP_PKEY_CTX_new_id(EVP_PKEY_HKDF, ...) and initialized with EVP_PKEY_derive_init.
md must be a valid pointer to an EVP_MD describing the desired hash (e.g., EVP_sha256()).
Callers must check the return value: 1 indicates success, 0 indicates error.

functions.name: EVP_PKEY_CTX_set1_hkdf_key
functions.signature: int EVP_PKEY_CTX_set1_hkdf_key(EVP_PKEY_CTX *ctx, const uint8_t *key, size_t key_len);
functions.description: Configures the HKDF keying material. In EXTRACT_AND_EXPAND or EXTRACT_ONLY mode, key is the input keying material (IKM) for HKDF-Extract. In EXPAND_ONLY mode, key is the pseudorandom key (PRK) for HKDF-Expand. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: ctx must be a valid EVP_PKEY_CTX created with EVP_PKEY_CTX_new_id(EVP_PKEY_HKDF, ...) and initialized with EVP_PKEY_derive_init.
key must point to a buffer of at least key_len bytes; key_len specifies the number of bytes to use.
key must correspond to the selected mode: IKM for EXTRACT[_AND_EXPAND], PRK for EXPAND_ONLY.
Callers must check the return value: 1 indicates success, 0 indicates error.

functions.name: EVP_PKEY_CTX_set1_hkdf_salt
functions.signature: int EVP_PKEY_CTX_set1_hkdf_salt(EVP_PKEY_CTX *ctx, const uint8_t *salt, size_t salt_len);
functions.description: Sets the salt parameter used by HKDF-Extract to salt_len bytes from salt. Ignored in EXPAND_ONLY mode. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: ctx must be a valid EVP_PKEY_CTX created with EVP_PKEY_CTX_new_id(EVP_PKEY_HKDF, ...) and initialized with EVP_PKEY_derive_init.
salt must point to a buffer of at least salt_len bytes; salt_len specifies the number of bytes to use. (This parameter is ignored in EXPAND_ONLY mode.)
Callers must check the return value: 1 indicates success, 0 indicates error.

functions.name: EVP_PKEY_CTX_add1_hkdf_info
functions.signature: int EVP_PKEY_CTX_add1_hkdf_info(EVP_PKEY_CTX *ctx, const uint8_t *info, size_t info_len);
functions.description: Appends info_len bytes from info to the HKDF-Expand info parameter. Ignored in EXTRACT_ONLY mode. Can be called multiple times to build the complete info value. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: ctx must be a valid EVP_PKEY_CTX created with EVP_PKEY_CTX_new_id(EVP_PKEY_HKDF, ...) and initialized with EVP_PKEY_derive_init.
info must point to a buffer of at least info_len bytes; info_len specifies the number of bytes to append. (This parameter is ignored in EXTRACT_ONLY mode.)
May be called multiple times; each call appends to the existing info parameter used for HKDF-Expand.
Callers must check the return value: 1 indicates success, 0 indicates error.

functions.name: MD4_Init
functions.description: Initializes an MD4 hashing context for incremental hashing. Call this before any MD4_Update calls and once more if you wish to reuse the same context for a new hash. Returns a nonzero value on success.
requirements: md4 must be a valid, writable pointer to an MD4_CTX object.
Must be called before MD4_Update or MD4_Final on the same context.

functions.description: Feeds a chunk of the message into the pre-hashing state initialized by MLDSA44_prehash_init. May be called multiple times before finalize.
requirements: inout_state must have been successfully initialized by MLDSA44_prehash_init and not yet finalized.
If msg_len > 0, msg must be non-NULL; msg may be NULL if msg_len == 0.
Must be called between MLDSA44_prehash_init and MLDSA44_prehash_finalize.

functions.name: MLDSA44_prehash_finalize
functions.description: Finalizes the pre-hashing process and outputs a pre-hashed message representative (mu) to out_msg_rep. The resulting representative should be signed with MLDSA44_sign_message_representative.
requirements: out_msg_rep must reference writable storage of exactly MLDSA_MU_BYTES bytes.
inout_state must have been initialized with MLDSA44_prehash_init and updated with zero or more MLDSA44_prehash_update calls, and not already finalized.

functions.name: MLDSA44_sign_message_representative
functions.signature: int MLDSA44_sign_message_representative(uint8_t out_encoded_signature[MLDSA44_SIGNATURE_BYTES], const struct MLDSA44_private_key *private_key, const uint8_t msg_rep[MLDSA_MU_BYTES]);
functions.description: Signs a pre-hashed message representative (mu) using the ML-DSA-44 private key and writes the encoded signature to out_encoded_signature. The representative must be computed via the prehash APIs using the public key from the same key pair; otherwise verification will fail. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: out_encoded_signature must reference writable storage of at least MLDSA44_SIGNATURE_BYTES bytes.
private_key must be a valid MLDSA44_private_key.
msg_rep must point to a buffer of exactly MLDSA_MU_BYTES bytes that was produced by MLDSA44_prehash_init/update/finalize with the corresponding public key and same context.
Callers must check the return value (1 success, 0 failure).

functions.name: MLDSA44_verify_message_representative
functions.signature: int MLDSA44_verify_message_representative(const struct MLDSA44_public_key *public_key, const uint8_t *signature, size_t signature_len, const uint8_t msg_rep[MLDSA_MU_BYTES]);
functions.description: Verifies an encoded ML-DSA-44 signature against a pre-hashed message representative (mu) using the given public key. The representative must have been computed via the prehash APIs using the same public key and the same context as used for signing. Returns 1 if valid, 0 on error/invalid.
requirements: public_key must be a valid MLDSA44_public_key.
signature must point to the encoded signature; signature_len must equal MLDSA44_SIGNATURE_BYTES.
msg_rep must point to a buffer of exactly MLDSA_MU_BYTES bytes that was produced by MLDSA44_prehash_init/update/finalize with this public key and matching context.
Callers must check the return value (1 valid, 0 invalid/error).

functions.name: MLDSA44_marshal_public_key
functions.description: Serializes an ML-DSA-44 public key into the standard encoding and appends it to the CBB out. Returns 1 on success or 0 on allocation error.
requirements: out must be a valid, initialized CBB ready for writing.
public_key must be a valid MLDSA44_public_key.
Callers must check the return value (1 success, 0 failure).

functions.name: MLDSA44_parse_public_key
functions.description: Parses an ML-DSA-44 public key from CBS in, expecting the format produced by MLDSA44_marshal_public_key, and writes the result to public_key. Fails if parsing fails or if trailing bytes remain in in. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: public_key must be a valid, writable MLDSA44_public_key pointer.
in must be a valid CBS positioned at the start of a correctly-encoded ML-DSA-44 public key.
The input must contain no trailing bytes; the parse consumes exactly the encoded key.
Callers must check the return value (1 success, 0 failure).

functions.name: MLKEM768_generate_key
functions.signature: void MLKEM768_generate_key(uint8_t out_encoded_public_key[MLKEM768_PUBLIC_KEY_BYTES], uint8_t optional_out_seed[MLKEM_SEED_BYTES], struct MLKEM768_private_key *out_private_key)
functions.description: Generates a new ML-KEM-768 keypair. Writes the encoded public key to out_encoded_public_key, and the opaque private key to out_private_key. If optional_out_seed is non-NULL, the 64-byte seed used to derive the private key is written there. Use this before encapsulation/decapsulation to create keys; the seed can be stored to deterministically re-derive the private key later.
requirements: out_encoded_public_key must point to a writable buffer of size MLKEM768_PUBLIC_KEY_BYTES (1184 bytes).
If optional_out_seed is not NULL, it must point to a writable buffer of size MLKEM_SEED_BYTES (64 bytes).
out_private_key must be a valid, writable pointer to an MLKEM768_private_key struct.
Callers must treat the MLKEM768_private_key contents as opaque and not serialize them directly.

functions.name: MLKEM768_private_key_from_seed
functions.signature: int MLKEM768_private_key_from_seed(struct MLKEM768_private_key *out_private_key, const uint8_t *seed, size_t seed_len)
functions.description: Derives an ML-KEM-768 private key from a seed previously produced by MLKEM768_generate_key. Returns 1 on success and 0 if the seed length is incorrect.
requirements: out_private_key must be a valid, writable pointer to an MLKEM768_private_key struct.
seed must point to the seed bytes produced by MLKEM768_generate_key.
seed_len must equal MLKEM_SEED_BYTES (64).
Return value must be checked: 1 indicates success, 0 indicates failure (incorrect seed length).

functions.name: MLKEM768_public_from_private
functions.signature: void MLKEM768_public_from_private(struct MLKEM768_public_key *out_public_key, const struct MLKEM768_private_key *private_key)
functions.description: Computes the ML-KEM-768 public key corresponding to the given private_key and writes it to out_public_key. Useful when you already have a private key and need the public key without parsing an encoded form.
requirements: out_public_key must be a valid, writable pointer to an MLKEM768_public_key struct.
private_key must be a valid MLKEM768_private_key previously generated or derived (initialized).
Callers must treat both key structs as opaque; do not serialize their contents directly.

functions.name: MLKEM768_encap
functions.signature: void MLKEM768_encap(uint8_t out_ciphertext[MLKEM768_CIPHERTEXT_BYTES], uint8_t out_shared_secret[MLKEM_SHARED_SECRET_BYTES], const struct MLKEM768_public_key *public_key)
functions.description: Encapsulates a freshly generated random shared secret to the recipient's ML-KEM-768 public_key. Writes the KEM ciphertext to out_ciphertext and the shared secret to out_shared_secret.
requirements: out_ciphertext must point to a writable buffer of size MLKEM768_CIPHERTEXT_BYTES (1088 bytes).
out_shared_secret must point to a writable buffer of size MLKEM_SHARED_SECRET_BYTES (32 bytes).
public_key must be a valid, initialized MLKEM768_public_key.

functions.name: MLKEM768_decap
functions.signature: int MLKEM768_decap(uint8_t out_shared_secret[MLKEM_SHARED_SECRET_BYTES], const uint8_t *ciphertext, size_t ciphertext_len, const struct MLKEM768_private_key *private_key)
functions.description: Decapsulates an ML-KEM-768 ciphertext using private_key and writes the resulting shared secret to out_shared_secret. Returns 0 if ciphertext_len is incorrect; otherwise returns 1. If the ciphertext is invalid but length-correct, a substitute secret is produced in constant time, deterministically from the inputs, and must be used only with authenticated encryption to detect failure.
requirements: out_shared_secret must point to a writable buffer of size MLKEM_SHARED_SECRET_BYTES (32 bytes).
ciphertext must point to the received ciphertext bytes.
ciphertext_len must equal MLKEM768_CIPHERTEXT_BYTES (1088); otherwise the function returns 0.
private_key must be a valid, initialized MLKEM768_private_key.
Callers must check the return value: 1 indicates length-correct input; 0 indicates incorrect length.

If using the resulting shared secret for symmetric encryption, callers must use an authenticated encryption scheme to detect decapsulation failure when an invalid ciphertext of correct length was provided.

functions.name: MLKEM768_marshal_public_key
functions.description: Serializes an ML-KEM-768 public key into the standard encoding and appends it to the CBB out. Returns 1 on success or 0 on allocation error.
requirements: out must be a valid, initialized CBB ready to receive appended data.
public_key must be a valid, initialized MLKEM768_public_key.
Callers must check the return value: 1 indicates success; 0 indicates allocation failure.

functions.name: MLKEM768_parse_public_key
functions.description: Parses an ML-KEM-768 public key from CBS in, expecting the standard encoding produced by MLKEM768_marshal_public_key. Writes the parsed key to out_public_key. Returns 1 on success or 0 on parse error or if trailing bytes remain in in.
requirements: out_public_key must be a valid, writable pointer to an MLKEM768_public_key struct.
in must be a valid, initialized CBS referencing the encoded key bytes.
The CBS input must contain exactly one encoded ML-KEM-768 public key with no trailing bytes; otherwise the function returns 0.
Callers must check the return value: 1 indicates success; 0 indicates parse error or trailing data.

functions.name: MLKEM1024_generate_key
functions.signature: void MLKEM1024_generate_key(uint8_t out_encoded_public_key[MLKEM1024_PUBLIC_KEY_BYTES], uint8_t optional_out_seed[MLKEM_SEED_BYTES], struct MLKEM1024_private_key *out_private_key)
functions.description: Generates a new ML-KEM-1024 keypair. Writes the encoded public key to out_encoded_public_key and the opaque private key to out_private_key. If optional_out_seed is non-NULL, the 64-byte seed used to derive the private key is written there. ML-KEM-768 is generally preferred, but this provides the 1024-parameter set.
requirements: out_encoded_public_key must point to a writable buffer of size MLKEM1024_PUBLIC_KEY_BYTES (1568 bytes).
If optional_out_seed is not NULL, it must point to a writable buffer of size MLKEM_SEED_BYTES (64 bytes).
out_private_key must be a valid, writable pointer to an MLKEM1024_private_key struct.
Callers must treat the MLKEM1024_private_key contents as opaque and not serialize them directly.

functions.name: MLKEM1024_private_key_from_seed
functions.signature: int MLKEM1024_private_key_from_seed(struct MLKEM1024_private_key *out_private_key, const uint8_t *seed, size_t seed_len)
functions.description: Derives an ML-KEM-1024 private key from a seed previously produced by MLKEM1024_generate_key. Returns 1 on success and 0 if the seed length is incorrect.
requirements: out_private_key must be a valid, writable pointer to an MLKEM1024_private_key struct.
seed must point to the seed bytes produced by MLKEM1024_generate_key.
seed_len must equal MLKEM_SEED_BYTES (64).
Callers must check the return value: 1 indicates success; 0 indicates failure (incorrect seed length).

functions.name: MLKEM1024_public_from_private
functions.signature: void MLKEM1024_public_from_private(struct MLKEM1024_public_key *out_public_key, const struct MLKEM1024_private_key *private_key)
functions.description: Computes the ML-KEM-1024 public key corresponding to the given private_key and writes it to out_public_key. Useful when you already have a private key and need the public key without parsing an encoded form.
requirements: out_public_key must be a valid, writable pointer to an MLKEM1024_public_key struct.
private_key must be a valid MLKEM1024_private_key previously generated or derived (initialized).
Callers must treat both key structs as opaque; do not serialize their contents directly.

functions.name: MLKEM1024_encap
functions.signature: void MLKEM1024_encap(uint8_t out_ciphertext[MLKEM1024_CIPHERTEXT_BYTES], uint8_t out_shared_secret[MLKEM_SHARED_SECRET_BYTES], const struct MLKEM1024_public_key *public_key)
functions.description: Encapsulates a freshly generated random shared secret to the recipient's ML-KEM-1024 public_key. Writes the KEM ciphertext to out_ciphertext and the shared secret to out_shared_secret.
requirements: out_ciphertext must point to a writable buffer of size MLKEM1024_CIPHERTEXT_BYTES (1568 bytes).
out_shared_secret must point to a writable buffer of size MLKEM_SHARED_SECRET_BYTES (32 bytes).
public_key must be a valid, initialized MLKEM1024_public_key.

functions.name: MLKEM1024_decap
functions.signature: int MLKEM1024_decap(uint8_t out_shared_secret[MLKEM_SHARED_SECRET_BYTES], const uint8_t *ciphertext, size_t ciphertext_len, const struct MLKEM1024_private_key *private_key)
functions.description: Decapsulates an ML-KEM-1024 ciphertext using private_key and writes the resulting shared secret to out_shared_secret. Returns 0 if ciphertext_len is incorrect; otherwise returns 1. If the ciphertext is invalid but length-correct, a substitute secret is produced in constant time, deterministically from the inputs, and must be used only with authenticated encryption to detect failure.
requirements: out_shared_secret must point to a writable buffer of size MLKEM_SHARED_SECRET_BYTES (32 bytes).
ciphertext must point to the received ciphertext bytes.
ciphertext_len must equal MLKEM1024_CIPHERTEXT_BYTES (1568); otherwise the function returns 0.
private_key must be a valid, initialized MLKEM1024_private_key.
Callers must check the return value: 1 indicates length-correct input; 0 indicates incorrect length.

If using the resulting shared secret for symmetric encryption, callers must use an authenticated encryption scheme to detect decapsulation failure when an invalid ciphertext of correct length was provided.

functions.name: MLKEM1024_marshal_public_key
functions.description: Serializes an ML-KEM-1024 public key into the standard encoding and appends it to the CBB out. Returns 1 on success or 0 on allocation error.
requirements: out must be a valid, initialized CBB ready to receive appended data.
public_key must be a valid, initialized MLKEM1024_public_key.
Callers must check the return value: 1 indicates success; 0 indicates allocation failure.

functions.name: MLKEM1024_parse_public_key
functions.description: Parses an ML-KEM-1024 public key from CBS in, expecting the standard encoding produced by MLKEM1024_marshal_public_key. Writes the parsed key to out_public_key. Returns 1 on success or 0 on parse error or if trailing bytes remain in in.
requirements: out_public_key must be a valid, writable pointer to an MLKEM1024_public_key struct.
in must be a valid, initialized CBS referencing the encoded key bytes.
The CBS input must contain exactly one encoded ML-KEM-1024 public key with no trailing bytes; otherwise the function returns 0.
Callers must check the return value: 1 indicates success; 0 indicates parse error or trailing data.

functions.name: OBJ_dup
functions.description: Returns a newly allocated duplicate of the ASN1 object identifier obj. On allocation failure, returns NULL. Caller owns the returned ASN1_OBJECT and must free it with ASN1_OBJECT_free.
requirements: obj must point to a valid ASN1_OBJECT
On success, the caller must release the returned object with ASN1_OBJECT_free
If the return value is NULL, no object was allocated and no freeing is required

functions.name: OBJ_cmp
functions.description: Compares two ASN1 object identifiers a and b. Returns < 0, 0, or > 0 if a is less than, equal to, or greater than b, respectively. Useful for ordering or equality checks on OIDs.
requirements: a must point to a valid ASN1_OBJECT
b must point to a valid ASN1_OBJECT

functions.name: OBJ_get0_data
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the DER payload bytes of obj (the OBJECT IDENTIFIER contents excluding tag and length). If obj has no associated OID (nid-only), returns a pointer to an empty string (length is zero). The returned pointer is owned by obj and remains valid as long as obj remains valid.
requirements: obj must point to a valid ASN1_OBJECT
Caller must not free or modify the returned pointer
Caller should use OBJ_length to determine the byte length

functions.name: OBJ_length
functions.description: Returns the length in bytes of the DER payload of obj (OBJECT IDENTIFIER contents excluding tag and length). If obj is nid-only, the length is zero.
requirements: obj must point to a valid ASN1_OBJECT

functions.name: OBJ_obj2nid
functions.description: Returns the nid that corresponds to obj, or NID_undef if the object is unknown.
requirements: obj must point to a valid ASN1_OBJECT

functions.name: OBJ_cbs2nid
functions.description: Returns the nid corresponding to the DER-encoded OBJECT IDENTIFIER contained in cbs, or NID_undef if unknown.
requirements: cbs must point to a valid, initialized CBS
cbs must contain a valid DER encoding of an OBJECT IDENTIFIER

functions.name: OBJ_sn2nid
functions.description: Looks up the nid for the given short name string. Returns the nid, or NID_undef if no such short name is known.
requirements: short_name must be a valid NUL-terminated C string

functions.name: OBJ_ln2nid
functions.description: Looks up the nid for the given long name string. Returns the nid, or NID_undef if no such long name is known.
requirements: long_name must be a valid NUL-terminated C string

functions.name: OBJ_txt2nid
functions.description: Parses s as either a short name, long name, or dotted-decimal OID string and returns the corresponding nid. Returns NID_undef if the text does not map to a known nid.
requirements: s must be a valid NUL-terminated C string containing either a known short/long name or a dotted sequence of numbers

functions.name: OBJ_nid2obj
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the ASN1_OBJECT corresponding to nid, or NULL if nid is unknown. The returned object is static and immutable; do not free it. It is safe to pass this pointer to APIs that may free ASN1_OBJECTs because ASN1_OBJECT_free is a no-op for static objects.
requirements: nid must be an integer; if nid is unknown, NULL is returned
Caller must not modify the returned object
Caller must not free the returned object (it is static)

functions.name: OBJ_get_undef
functions.description: Returns the canonical ASN1_OBJECT instance representing NID_undef. Prefer this over OBJ_nid2obj(NID_undef) to avoid pulling in the full OID table.
requirements: Caller must not free or modify the returned static object

functions.name: OBJ_nid2sn
functions.description: Returns the short name string for nid, or NULL if nid is unknown. Returned pointer refers to static storage.
requirements: nid must be an integer; if nid is unknown, NULL is returned
Caller must not modify or free the returned string

functions.name: OBJ_nid2ln
functions.description: Returns the long name string for nid, or NULL if nid is unknown. Returned pointer refers to static storage.
requirements: nid must be an integer; if nid is unknown, NULL is returned
Caller must not modify or free the returned string

functions.name: OBJ_nid2cbb
functions.description: Appends the ASN.1 OBJECT IDENTIFIER for nid to the CBB out. Returns 1 on success or 0 on failure.
requirements: out must point to a valid, initialized CBB ready for writing
nid must identify a known OID; if unknown, the function fails
Caller must check the return value for success (1) or failure (0)
On failure, the CBB state may be unchanged or in an error state (handle per CBB API)

functions.name: OBJ_txt2obj
functions.description: Parses the textual representation in s and returns a freshly allocated ASN1_OBJECT. If dont_search_names is 0, s is matched against known long/short names; otherwise, s must be a dotted-decimal OID string. Returns NULL on error.
requirements: s must be a valid NUL-terminated C string
If dont_search_names is nonzero, s must be a dotted sequence of numbers (ASCII)
On success, caller owns the returned ASN1_OBJECT and must free it with ASN1_OBJECT_free
Caller must handle NULL return on parse/allocation failure

functions.name: OBJ_obj2txt
functions.signature: int OBJ_obj2txt(char *out, int out_len, const ASN1_OBJECT *obj, int always_return_oid)
functions.description: Converts obj to a textual representation. If always_return_oid is 0 and the OID is known, returns its long (preferred) or short name; otherwise returns dotted-decimal form. If out is not NULL, writes at most out_len bytes and always NUL-terminates if out_len >= 1. Returns the number of characters that would have been written (excluding NUL), or -1 on error.
requirements: obj must point to a valid ASN1_OBJECT
If out is not NULL and out_len > 0, out must point to a writable buffer of at least out_len bytes
Caller must check for return -1 to detect error
Caller should allocate out_len >= returned length + 1 to capture full string on a subsequent call

functions.name: OBJ_create
functions.signature: int OBJ_create(const char *oid, const char *short_name, const char *long_name)
functions.description: Registers a new known OID with the given dotted-decimal oid, short name, and long name, and returns the assigned NID. Returns NID_undef on error. This modifies process-global state and rejects duplicates (OID, short name, or long name). Prefer processing unknown OIDs directly instead of registering them at runtime.
requirements: oid must be a valid NUL-terminated dotted-decimal OID string
short_name must be a valid NUL-terminated C string
long_name must be a valid NUL-terminated C string
No duplicate OID, short name, or long name may already exist in the global table; otherwise registration fails
Caller must handle NID_undef on error
Callers should avoid concurrent conflicting registrations within the same address space

functions.name: OBJ_find_sigid_algs
functions.description: Given a signature algorithm NID sign_nid, looks up the corresponding digest and public key NIDs. On success sets *out_digest_nid and/or *out_pkey_nid (if non-NULL) and returns 1. Returns 0 if the mapping is unknown. For algorithms where the digest is unspecified, the digest NID may be NID_undef.
requirements: If out_digest_nid is non-NULL, it must point to an int for output
If out_pkey_nid is non-NULL, it must point to an int for output
Caller must check the return value for success (1) or failure (0)

functions.name: OBJ_find_sigid_by_algs
functions.signature: int OBJ_find_sigid_by_algs(int *out_sign_nid, int digest_nid, int pkey_nid)
functions.description: Finds the combined signature algorithm NID for the given digest_nid and pkey_nid. On success sets *out_sign_nid (if non-NULL) and returns 1. Returns 0 if no valid combination exists.
requirements: If out_sign_nid is non-NULL, it must point to an int for output
Caller must check the return value for success (1) or failure (0)

functions.name: OBJ_NAME_do_all_sorted
functions.signature: void OBJ_NAME_do_all_sorted(int type, void (*callback)(const OBJ_NAME *, void *arg), void *arg)
functions.description: Deprecated. Iterates over registered primitives of the given type and invokes callback once per entry, in a sorted order. type is OBJ_NAME_TYPE_MD_METH for hash functions or OBJ_NAME_TYPE_CIPHER_METH for ciphers/modes. Ill-specified and should not be used.
requirements: type must be one of the supported OBJ_NAME_TYPE_* constants
callback must be a valid function pointer accepting (const OBJ_NAME*, void*)
callback must tolerate being called zero or more times
arg is passed through to callback and may be NULL

functions.name: OBJ_NAME_do_all
functions.signature: void OBJ_NAME_do_all(int type, void (*callback)(const OBJ_NAME *, void *arg), void *arg)
functions.description: Deprecated. Equivalent to OBJ_NAME_do_all_sorted; iterates over registered primitives of the given type and invokes callback. Ill-specified and should not be used.
requirements: type must be one of the supported OBJ_NAME_TYPE_* constants
callback must be a valid function pointer accepting (const OBJ_NAME*, void*)
callback must tolerate being called zero or more times
arg is passed through to callback and may be NULL

functions.name: OBJ_cleanup
functions.description: Deprecated/No-op. Does nothing.

functions.name: PEM_read_bio
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int PEM_read_bio(BIO *bp, char **name, char **header, unsigned char **data, long *len);
functions.description: Reads the next PEM block from the BIO bp. On success, returns 1 and sets *name (PEM type, NUL-terminated), *header (header block, NUL-terminated), and *data (decoded DER bytes) with *len bytes. Caller must free *name, *header, and *data with OPENSSL_free. Returns 0 on error (PEM_R_NO_START_LINE if no block; other errors for decode issues).
requirements: bp must be a valid, readable BIO positioned at or before a PEM block.
name, header, data, and len must be non-NULL pointers to receive outputs.
On success, caller must release *name, *header, and *data with OPENSSL_free.
Function returns 0 on error; callers should consult the error queue for details.

functions.name: PEM_write_bio
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int PEM_write_bio(BIO *bp, const char *name, const char *hdr, const unsigned char *data, long len);
functions.description: Writes a PEM block to BIO bp with type string name, header hdr, and len bytes from data as the body. Returns 0 on error and the number of bytes written on success.
requirements: bp must be a valid, writable BIO.
name and hdr must be NUL-terminated strings (hdr may be empty or NULL by convention; header value is passed as provided).
data must point to len bytes to be encoded.
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates error; positive value is bytes written.

functions.name: PEM_bytes_read_bio
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int PEM_bytes_read_bio(unsigned char **pdata, long *plen, char **pnm, const char *name, BIO *bp, pem_password_cb *cb, void *u);
functions.description: Reads a PEM block of a specific type from BIO bp, potentially handling decryption via password callback. On success, outputs the decoded DER bytes (*pdata with *plen) and optionally the PEM type in *pnm, returning 1. Returns 0 on error. Details beyond signature are not documented here.
requirements: bp must be a valid, readable BIO.
pdata, plen must be non-NULL to receive decoded bytes and length; caller must free *pdata with OPENSSL_free on success.
If pnm is non-NULL, it receives an allocated NUL-terminated string of the PEM type; caller must free with OPENSSL_free.
If name is non-NULL, it likely filters/expects that PEM type (exact behavior not fully documented here).
If the PEM is encrypted, cb/u may be used to obtain a password; cb follows pem_password_cb semantics.
Caller must check return value (1 success, 0 error).

functions.name: PEM_ASN1_read_bio
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT void *PEM_ASN1_read_bio(d2i_of_void *d2i, const char *name, BIO *bp, void **x, pem_password_cb *cb, void *u);
functions.description: Generic helper to read a named PEM block from BIO bp and decode it using the supplied ASN.1 d2i decoder. Returns a pointer to the decoded object on success, or NULL on error. Used by type-specific PEM_read_bio_* wrappers.
requirements: d2i must be a valid ASN.1 decoder function for the expected object.
name must be the expected PEM type string for the object.
bp must be a readable BIO positioned at the PEM block.
x is an optional destination handle (may be NULL); ownership semantics of reusing *x are not specified here.
If the PEM block is encrypted, cb/u may be used to obtain a password.
Caller must free the returned object with the appropriate type-specific free function.

functions.name: PEM_ASN1_write_bio
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int PEM_ASN1_write_bio(i2d_of_void *i2d, const char *name, BIO *bp, void *x, const EVP_CIPHER *enc, const unsigned char *pass, int pass_len, pem_password_cb *cb, void *u);
functions.description: Generic helper to encode object x using i2d and write it as a PEM block named name to BIO bp, optionally encrypting with enc and a supplied password or callback. Returns nonzero on success and 0 on error.
requirements: i2d must be a valid ASN.1 encoder function for x.
name must be a NUL-terminated PEM type string.
bp must be a writable BIO.
x must point to a valid object compatible with i2d.
If enc is non-NULL, a password must be provided either via pass/pass_len or cb/u per pem_password_cb semantics.
Caller must check return value (0 indicates error).

functions.name: PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio

Returns a STACK_OF(X509_INFO) on success or NULL on error. If sk is NULL, a new stack is allocated; otherwise results are appended to sk. Encrypted certificates may be decrypted via cb; encrypted private keys are not decrypted and are represented as placeholder X509_INFO entries with empty x_pkey.
requirements: bp must be a readable BIO containing PEM blocks.
If sk is NULL, a new stack is allocated and must be freed with sk_X509_INFO_pop_free and X509_INFO_free; if sk is non-NULL, caller retains ownership regardless of success.
cb/u may be used to decrypt encrypted certificates; encrypted private keys are not decrypted by this function.

requirements: fp must be an open, readable FILE* positioned at the PEM data.
sk, cb, u semantics as in PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio.

functions.name: PEM_read

functions.description: FILE* variant of PEM_read_bio. Reads the next PEM block from fp, returning 1 on success and 0 on error. On success, outputs allocated *name (PEM type), *header (headers), and *data with *len bytes; caller must free with OPENSSL_free.
requirements: fp must be an open, readable FILE*.
name, header, data, and len must be non-NULL.
Caller must free *name, *header, and *data with OPENSSL_free on success.
Return value 0 indicates error; consult error queue.

functions.name: PEM_write
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int PEM_write(FILE *fp, const char *name, const char *hdr, const unsigned char *data, long len);
functions.description: FILE* variant of PEM_write_bio. Writes a PEM block to fp with given type, header, and data of length len. Returns 0 on error and number of bytes written on success.
requirements: fp must be an open, writable FILE*.
name and hdr must be NUL-terminated strings; hdr may be empty or NULL by convention.
data must point to len bytes to encode.
Caller must check return value.

functions.description: FILE* variant of PEM_ASN1_read_bio. Reads a named PEM block from fp and decodes it using d2i. Returns a pointer to the decoded object on success, or NULL on error.

functions.name: PKCS7_sign
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT PKCS7 *PKCS7_sign(X509 *sign_cert, EVP_PKEY *pkey, STACK_OF(X509) *certs, BIO *data, int flags);
functions.description: Constructs a PKCS#7 SignedData ContentInfo in one of two specific modes for compatibility: (1) Bundle-only mode: aggregates certs into a SignedData with external data and no signatures; (2) Detached-signature mode: generates a detached RSA-SHA256 signature over data using pkey and produces a SignedData containing it. Returns a newly-allocated PKCS7 on success or NULL on error. Only a subset of OpenSSL’s PKCS7_sign is implemented.
requirements: Mode 1 (bundle-only): sign_cert must be NULL. pkey must be NULL. data is ignored. flags must be exactly PKCS7_DETACHED. certs is the set to include; order will not be preserved.

Mode 2 (detached-signature): certs must be NULL. flags must be exactly (PKCS7_NOATTR | PKCS7_BINARY | PKCS7_NOCERTS | PKCS7_DETACHED). pkey must be a valid private key usable for RSA SHA-256. data must be a readable BIO containing the data to be signed.

The following flags cause PKCS7_sign to fail: PKCS7_TEXT, PKCS7_NOCERTS, PKCS7_NOSIGS, PKCS7_NOCHAIN, PKCS7_NOINTERN, PKCS7_NOVERIFY, PKCS7_BINARY, PKCS7_NOATTR, PKCS7_NOSMIMECAP, PKCS7_STREAM, PKCS7_PARTIAL (per header defines).
Certificates in SignedData are unordered; callers must not depend on input order being preserved.
On success, the caller must free the returned PKCS7 with PKCS7_free.
This function provides backwards compatibility only and implements a subset of OpenSSL’s behavior; any use outside the specified modes is unsupported and may fail.

functions.name: PKCS8_encrypt
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT X509_SIG *PKCS8_encrypt(int pbe_nid, const EVP_CIPHER *cipher, const char *pass, int pass_len, const uint8_t *salt, size_t salt_len, int iterations, PKCS8_PRIV_KEY_INFO *p8inf);
functions.description: Serializes and encrypts a PKCS8_PRIV_KEY_INFO into an EncryptedPrivateKeyInfo (X509_SIG) using PBES1 or PBES2 per PKCS#5. PBES2 is selected by providing a cipher and setting pbe_nid to -1; otherwise PBES1 is used and cipher is ignored. Supported PBES1 suites are pbeWithSHAAnd128BitRC4, pbeWithSHAAnd3-KeyTripleDES-CBC, and pbeWithSHA1And40BitRC2 (from PKCS#12). If pass is NULL it is encoded as the empty string (PKCS#12 semantics); for PBES1 (PKCS#12) the password is converted to a raw byte string per PKCS#12 B.1. If salt is NULL, a random salt of salt_len bytes is generated; if salt_len is zero, a default salt length is used. Returns a newly-allocated X509_SIG on success which the caller must free.
requirements: pbe_nid determines scheme: set to -1 to use PBES2 with the provided cipher; otherwise PBES1 is used.
When PBES1 is used, only the following suites are supported: pbeWithSHAAnd128BitRC4, pbeWithSHAAnd3-KeyTripleDES-CBC, pbeWithSHA1And40BitRC2.
When PBES1 is used, the cipher parameter is ignored.
When PBES2 is used, cipher must name a supported cipher (unknown exact set).
pass may be NULL and will be treated/encoded as the empty byte string; for PBES1 (PKCS#12), pass is converted per PKCS#12 B.1.
salt may be NULL to auto-generate a random salt; if salt_len is zero, a default salt length is used.
Caller must free the returned X509_SIG.
p8inf must reference a valid, initialized PKCS8_PRIV_KEY_INFO to be encrypted.
iterations is used for KDF/derivation; exact valid range is not specified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: PKCS8_marshal_encrypted_private_key
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int PKCS8_marshal_encrypted_private_key(CBB *out, int pbe_nid, const EVP_CIPHER *cipher, const char *pass, size_t pass_len, const uint8_t *salt, size_t salt_len, int iterations, const EVP_PKEY *pkey);
functions.description: Encrypts an EVP_PKEY into an EncryptedPrivateKeyInfo and appends the DER encoding to the provided CBB. PBES2 is selected by setting pbe_nid to -1 and providing cipher; otherwise PBES1 is used (cipher ignored). Supported PBES1 suites match PKCS8_encrypt. If pass is NULL it is encoded as the empty string (PKCS#12 semantics); for PBES1 (PKCS#12) the password is converted per PKCS#12 B.1. If salt is NULL a random salt of salt_len bytes is generated; if salt_len is zero, a default salt length is used. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: out must be an initialized CBB ready for writing DER output.
pbe_nid determines scheme: -1 selects PBES2 (uses cipher); otherwise PBES1 is used and cipher is ignored.
PBES1 support is limited to: pbeWithSHAAnd128BitRC4, pbeWithSHAAnd3-KeyTripleDES-CBC, pbeWithSHA1And40BitRC2.
pass may be NULL and is treated as empty; for PBES1 it is converted per PKCS#12 B.1.
salt may be NULL to auto-generate; if salt_len is zero, a default is used.
pkey must point to a valid EVP_PKEY to be serialized.
iterations is used for KDF/derivation; exact valid range is not specified in this header (unknown).
On success, DER is written to out; check the return value and handle 0 as error.

For PBES1 (PKCS#12), the password is converted per PKCS#12 B.1; if pass is NULL it is encoded as the empty string. Returns a newly-allocated PKCS8_PRIV_KEY_INFO on success which the caller must free.
requirements: pkcs8 must point to a valid EncryptedPrivateKeyInfo encoded with a supported PBES1 suite (as listed) or PBES2.
pass may be NULL and is treated/encoded as the empty string; for PBES1, conversion follows PKCS#12 B.1.

For PBES1 (PKCS#12), the password is converted per PKCS#12 B.1; if pass is NULL it is encoded as the empty string. Returns a newly-allocated EVP_PKEY on success or NULL on error.
requirements: cbs must point to a CBS containing a DER-encoded EncryptedPrivateKeyInfo and will be advanced on success.
pass may be NULL and is treated as the empty string; for PBES1, conversion follows PKCS#12 B.1.
Only PBES1 suites pbeWithSHAAnd128BitRC4, pbeWithSHAAnd3-KeyTripleDES-CBC, pbeWithSHA1And40BitRC2 and PBES2 are supported.

functions.name: PKCS12_get_key_and_certs

functions.description: Parses a PKCS#12 structure from the input CBS, authenticates and decrypts it with password, outputs the included private key via out_key and appends included certificates to out_certs. FriendlyName attributes (RFC 2985) are returned on the X509 objects as aliases. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error. The caller takes ownership of all outputs.
requirements: out_key must be a non-NULL pointer to receive a newly-allocated EVP_PKEY on success (may be set to NULL if the PKCS#12 has no private key).
out_certs must be an existing STACK_OF(X509) to which certificates will be appended; the caller assumes ownership of appended X509 objects.

password is used for decryption and MAC; exact length handling rules are not specified here (unknown).
Caller is responsible for freeing the returned EVP_PKEY (if any) and any X509 objects appended to out_certs.
