functions.description: No-op compatibility function retained for OpenSSL API compatibility. It performs no action.
requirements: No requirements; calling this function has no effect.

functions.name: d2i_PKCS12
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT PKCS12 *d2i_PKCS12(PKCS12 **out_p12, const uint8_t **ber_bytes, size_t ber_len);
functions.description: Dummy decoder that copies the bytes from *ber_bytes into a PKCS12 structure. On success, advances *ber_bytes by exactly ber_len bytes and returns a newly-allocated PKCS12. If out_p12 is not NULL, then on success any existing *out_p12 is freed and replaced. Unlike typical d2i functions, this function always consumes ber_len bytes.
requirements: ber_bytes must be non-NULL and point to a buffer of at least ber_len bytes; on exit it is advanced by ber_len regardless of success.
out_p12 should be NULL for new code; if non-NULL and the call succeeds, *out_p12 will be freed (if not NULL) and replaced.
Returns a newly-allocated PKCS12 or NULL on error; caller must free the result with PKCS12_free.
ber_len may be any size_t; semantics beyond full consumption are as documented.

functions.name: d2i_PKCS12_bio
functions.description: Acts like d2i_PKCS12 but reads the input bytes from a BIO. Returns a newly-allocated PKCS12 on success or NULL on error; if out_p12 is not NULL and the call succeeds, *out_p12 is freed (if not NULL) and replaced.
requirements: bio must be a readable BIO positioned at the start of the PKCS#12 bytes.
out_p12 may be NULL; if non-NULL and the call succeeds, *out_p12 is freed (if not NULL) and replaced.
Caller must free the returned PKCS12 with PKCS12_free.

functions.name: d2i_PKCS12_fp
functions.description: Acts like d2i_PKCS12 but reads the input bytes from a FILE*. Returns a newly-allocated PKCS12 on success or NULL on error; if out_p12 is not NULL and the call succeeds, *out_p12 is freed (if not NULL) and replaced.
requirements: fp must be a readable FILE* positioned at the start of the PKCS#12 bytes.
out_p12 may be NULL; if non-NULL and the call succeeds, *out_p12 is freed (if not NULL) and replaced.
Caller must free the returned PKCS12 with PKCS12_free.

functions.name: i2d_PKCS12
functions.description: Dummy encoder that copies the contents of p12 to DER. If out is not NULL, writes the result to *out and advances *out just past the written bytes. Returns the number of bytes in the result (written or not), or a negative value on error.
requirements: p12 must point to a valid PKCS12 object.
If out is not NULL, *out must point to a buffer with sufficient space; on success it will be advanced past the written data.
Caller must check the return value: negative indicates error.

functions.name: i2d_PKCS12_bio
functions.description: Writes the DER-encoded contents of p12 to bio. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: bio must be a writable BIO.
p12 must be a valid PKCS12 object.
Caller must check the return value and handle 0 as error.

functions.name: i2d_PKCS12_fp
functions.description: Writes the DER-encoded contents of p12 to a FILE*. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: fp must be a writable FILE*.
p12 must be a valid PKCS12 object.
Caller must check the return value and handle 0 as error.

functions.name: PKCS12_parse
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int PKCS12_parse(const PKCS12 *p12, const char *password, EVP_PKEY **out_pkey, X509 **out_cert, STACK_OF(X509) **out_ca_certs);
functions.description: Parses the ASN.1 data in p12, authenticates and decrypts it using password, and extracts the private key and matching certificate into out_pkey and out_cert, respectively. Extra certificates are appended or returned via out_ca_certs. If p12 contains no private key, both *out_pkey and *out_cert are set to NULL and all certificates are returned via *out_ca_certs. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error. Note: extra certificates are returned in file order (differs from OpenSSL 1.1.1). Prefer PKCS12_get_key_and_certs in new code.
requirements: out_pkey and out_cert must not be NULL pointers.
out_ca_certs may be NULL; if not NULL and *out_ca_certs is NULL, it will be set to a newly-allocated stack containing the extra certs; otherwise extra certs are appended to *out_ca_certs.
Caller takes ownership of the outputs and must free them appropriately.
Behavior with password lengths beyond NUL-terminated strings is not specified here (unknown).
Function may set *out_pkey and *out_cert to NULL if no private key is present; callers must handle this case.

functions.name: PKCS12_verify_mac
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int PKCS12_verify_mac(const PKCS12 *p12, const char *password, int password_len);
functions.description: Returns 1 if password verifies the MAC on p12, 0 otherwise. For compatibility with PKCS12_parse, password handling has specific constraints: password/password_len may be (NULL,0), or password_len may be -1 (treat password as NUL-terminated), or else password[password_len] must be zero and no other NULs may appear. If these checks fail, returns 0 immediately.
requirements: password may be NULL only if password_len is zero.
Alternatively, password_len may be -1 to indicate NUL-terminated password.
Otherwise, password[password_len] must be '\0' and there must be no other NUL bytes in password.
Caller must check the return value: 1 means valid MAC, 0 means invalid or argument check failed.

functions.name: PKCS12_create
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT PKCS12 *PKCS12_create(const char *password, const char *name, const EVP_PKEY *pkey, X509 *cert, const STACK_OF(X509) *chain, int key_nid, int cert_nid, int iterations, int mac_iterations, int key_type);
functions.description: Creates a new PKCS12 object containing pkey, cert, and chain, encrypted with the specified password and algorithms. name, if not NULL, is stored as a friendly name. key_nid/cert_nid/iterations/mac_iterations may be zero to use defaults (AES-256-CBC for both, PKCS12_DEFAULT_ITER for both iteration counts). If key_nid or cert_nid is a PBES2-capable cipher NID, PBES2 with a default KDF (currently PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256) is used; if a PBES1 suite NID is given, that suite is used; if -1, encryption for the key or certificate is disabled (not recommended; MAC still uses the password). Returns a newly-allocated PKCS12 on success or NULL on error. FriendlyName attributes from cert/chain aliases are included; specifying both an alias on cert and a non-NULL name is an error. key_type must be zero.
requirements: password is required for MAC; even if key/cert encryption is disabled with -1, a password is still needed for the MAC.
name may be NULL; if not NULL and cert already has an alias, providing name is an error.
pkey and cert may be NULL to omit them.
key_nid, cert_nid, iterations, mac_iterations may be zero to select defaults (NID_aes_256_cbc for both ciphers; PKCS12_DEFAULT_ITER for both iteration counts).
If key_nid or cert_nid is -1, encryption for that component is disabled; this is supported only for compatibility and may not be widely supported by other implementations.
key_type must be zero.
Caller must free the returned PKCS12 with PKCS12_free.

functions.name: PKCS12_free
functions.description: Frees a PKCS12 object and its contents.
requirements: p12 may be NULL; freeing a NULL pointer is a no-op (standard OpenSSL/BoringSSL free semantics; exact behavior is not stated here but typical).

functions.name: bssl::MakeDeleter<PKCS12>::operator()
functions.description: Call operator for the bssl::MakeDeleter<PKCS12> functor. It deletes/frees a PKCS12 object by invoking PKCS12_free on the provided pointer. Intended to be used as the deleter with smart pointers (e.g., std::unique_ptr) so PKCS12 objects are automatically freed. Details are inferred from BORINGSSL_MAKE_DELETER(PKCS12, PKCS12_free) in this header; the macro specializes the deleter for PKCS12.
requirements: ptr must be either NULL or a valid pointer to a PKCS12 object obtained from BoringSSL (e.g., PKCS12_create, d2i_PKCS12, d2i_PKCS12_bio, d2i_PKCS12_fp).
Do not call this deleter on the same PKCS12 object more than once (no double-free).
After this function is called, ptr and any aliases to the same PKCS12 object must not be used.
Thread-safety requirements are the same as PKCS12_free (not specified here).

functions.name: bssl::MakeDeleter<PKCS8_PRIV_KEY_INFO>::operator()
functions.description: Call operator for the bssl::MakeDeleter<PKCS8_PRIV_KEY_INFO> functor. It deletes/frees a PKCS8_PRIV_KEY_INFO object by invoking PKCS8_PRIV_KEY_INFO_free on the provided pointer. Intended for use as the deleter with smart pointers so PKCS8_PRIV_KEY_INFO objects are automatically freed. Details are inferred from BORINGSSL_MAKE_DELETER(PKCS8_PRIV_KEY_INFO, PKCS8_PRIV_KEY_INFO_free) in this header; the macro specializes the deleter for PKCS8_PRIV_KEY_INFO.
requirements: ptr must be either NULL or a valid pointer to a PKCS8_PRIV_KEY_INFO object produced by BoringSSL APIs (e.g., PKCS8_decrypt, parsing/ASN.1 APIs).
Do not call this deleter on the same PKCS8_PRIV_KEY_INFO object more than once (no double-free).
After this function is called, ptr and any aliases to the same object must not be used.
Thread-safety requirements are the same as PKCS8_PRIV_KEY_INFO_free (not specified here).

functions.name: CRYPTO_poly1305_init
functions.description: Initializes a Poly1305 authenticator state with a one-time 32-byte key. Call this before any CRYPTO_poly1305_update calls to begin computing an authentication tag for a message. There is no reset function; a given key must not be reused for multiple messages. Typical usage: initialize with a fresh key, stream message bytes via CRYPTO_poly1305_update, then finalize with CRYPTO_poly1305_finish to obtain the 16-byte tag.
requirements: state must be a valid, writable poly1305_state storage location.
key must point to a readable 32-byte buffer (one-time key).
The key is one-time: do not reuse the same key to authenticate multiple messages.
Call this before any CRYPTO_poly1305_update or CRYPTO_poly1305_finish on the state.

functions.name: CRYPTO_poly1305_update
functions.signature: void CRYPTO_poly1305_update(poly1305_state *state, const uint8_t *in, size_t in_len);
functions.description: Feeds message bytes into an ongoing Poly1305 computation. May be called zero or more times after CRYPTO_poly1305_init to process the message in chunks. The accumulated input is authenticated when CRYPTO_poly1305_finish is called.
requirements: state must have been initialized by a prior CRYPTO_poly1305_init call.
in must point to at least in_len readable bytes; if in_len is zero, it may be called zero times after init (no data).
May be called zero or more times after CRYPTO_poly1305_init and before CRYPTO_poly1305_finish.

functions.name: CRYPTO_poly1305_finish
functions.description: Finalizes the Poly1305 computation and writes the 16-byte authentication tag to mac. Call after all CRYPTO_poly1305_update calls for the current message.
requirements: state must have been initialized by CRYPTO_poly1305_init and reflect all intended CRYPTO_poly1305_update calls for the message.
mac must point to a writable buffer of at least 16 bytes.
Should be called once per message to obtain the tag, after processing all input bytes.

functions.name: CRYPTO_BUFFER_POOL_new
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new CRYPTO_BUFFER_POOL used to intern (deduplicate) CRYPTO_BUFFER instances. Returns NULL on allocation failure. Typical usage: create a pool, create buffers with it, then free the pool when it is empty.
requirements: The returned pool must later be freed with CRYPTO_BUFFER_POOL_free when it is empty.
Callers must check for a NULL return and handle allocation failures.

functions.name: CRYPTO_BUFFER_POOL_free
functions.description: Frees a CRYPTO_BUFFER_POOL. The pool must be empty (no pooled CRYPTO_BUFFER still referenced only by the pool).
requirements: pool must be an empty CRYPTO_BUFFER_POOL created by CRYPTO_BUFFER_POOL_new.
Do not call unless all CRYPTO_BUFFER objects associated with the pool are released such that the pool holds no remaining entries.
pool should be non-NULL (behavior on NULL is not documented).

functions.name: CRYPTO_BUFFER_new
functions.description: Creates a CRYPTO_BUFFER containing a copy of the provided data and returns it, or NULL on error. If a non-NULL pool is supplied, the returned buffer may be an interned reference to an existing identical buffer in that pool (deduplication). If pool is NULL, the buffer is unpooled.
requirements: data must reference at least len bytes of readable memory at the time of the call.
pool may be NULL or a valid CRYPTO_BUFFER_POOL; when non-NULL, deduplication may occur.
Callers must check for a NULL return and handle allocation failures.
The returned CRYPTO_BUFFER is immutable after creation (do not modify its contents).

functions.name: CRYPTO_BUFFER_alloc
functions.description: Allocates an unpooled CRYPTO_BUFFER of size len and returns it, writing a pointer to the underlying storage to *out_data. Returns NULL on error. After allocation, the caller must initialize exactly len bytes at *out_data before using the CRYPTO_BUFFER with any other BoringSSL API. Once initialized, the buffer must be treated as immutable.
requirements: out_data must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the writable data pointer.
The caller must write exactly len bytes to *out_data before passing the returned CRYPTO_BUFFER to any other BoringSSL function.
The contents must be treated as immutable after initialization.
Callers must check for a NULL return and handle allocation failures.

functions.name: CRYPTO_BUFFER_new_from_CBS
functions.description: Creates a CRYPTO_BUFFER from the contents of the given CBS, behaving like CRYPTO_BUFFER_new. Returns NULL on error. If pool is non-NULL, the buffer may be interned/deduplicated within that pool.
requirements: cbs must be a valid, initialized CBS whose referenced bytes are accessible.
pool may be NULL or a valid CRYPTO_BUFFER_POOL.
Callers must check for a NULL return and handle allocation failures.
The resulting CRYPTO_BUFFER is immutable after creation.

functions.name: CRYPTO_BUFFER_new_from_static_data_unsafe
functions.description: Creates a CRYPTO_BUFFER that references the provided data without copying it. This is unsafe because the function assumes the input data is immutable and will remain valid for the lifetime of the process. Returns NULL on error. If a pool is provided, the buffer may be deduplicated within that pool.
requirements: data must point to at least len bytes that are immutable.
data must remain valid for the lifetime of the address space (process).
pool may be NULL or a valid CRYPTO_BUFFER_POOL.
Callers must check for a NULL return and handle allocation failures.
The resulting CRYPTO_BUFFER must be treated as immutable.

functions.name: CRYPTO_BUFFER_free
functions.description: Decrements the reference count of buf and frees it if no references remain (or if the only remaining reference is from a pool).
requirements: buf must be a valid CRYPTO_BUFFER (non-NULL recommended; behavior on NULL is not documented).
After the reference count reaches zero, buf must not be used.

functions.name: CRYPTO_BUFFER_up_ref
functions.description: Increments the reference count of buf and returns one.
requirements: buf must be a valid CRYPTO_BUFFER (non-NULL).
Callers should not assume any return value other than 1 as documented (“returns one”).

functions.name: CRYPTO_BUFFER_data
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the immutable data contained in buf.
requirements: buf must be a valid CRYPTO_BUFFER (non-NULL).
The returned pointer remains valid as long as at least one reference to buf is held.

functions.name: CRYPTO_BUFFER_len
functions.description: Returns the length, in bytes, of the data contained in buf.
requirements: buf must be a valid CRYPTO_BUFFER (non-NULL).

functions.name: CRYPTO_BUFFER_init_CBS
functions.description: Initializes the CBS out to point at the data contained in buf, without copying. Useful for parsing buffer contents with CBS utilities.
requirements: buf must be a valid CRYPTO_BUFFER (non-NULL).
out must be a non-NULL pointer to a CBS to initialize.
The CBS will reference the buffer’s internal memory; do not modify or free through the CBS, and ensure buf remains alive while the CBS is in use.

functions.name: RAND_bytes
functions.description: Fills buf with len bytes of cryptographically strong random data and returns 1. If sufficient randomness cannot be obtained, the process aborts. Use as the primary API for random bytes in BoringSSL.
requirements: buf must point to a writable buffer of at least len bytes.
len may be any size_t; on failure the function aborts rather than returning an error.
Do not rely on a 0 return for error handling—insufficient entropy results in process abort.

functions.name: RAND_enable_fork_unsafe_buffering
functions.description: Globally disables BoringSSL’s expensive fork-safety measures under the assumption that clones of the current address space (e.g., via fork) will never call into BoringSSL. Intended only to improve performance when the application guarantees no BoringSSL use after fork. Calling this and then using BoringSSL across fork can leak secret keys. Obsolete naming retained for compatibility.
requirements: Only available/declared on non-Windows platforms (when OPENSSL_WINDOWS is not defined).
fd must be -1 (any other value is invalid per documentation).
Must not be called by library code; only application code with global knowledge of how BoringSSL is used may call this.
Do not use BoringSSL in child processes created via fork (or similar) after calling this function; otherwise secret keys may be leaked.
Intended only when a measured performance issue exists; otherwise do not call.

functions.name: RAND_disable_fork_unsafe_buffering
functions.description: Restores BoringSSL’s default fork-safety protections after a prior call to RAND_enable_fork_unsafe_buffering.
requirements: Only available/declared on non-Windows platforms (when OPENSSL_WINDOWS is not defined).
Call in the same process where RAND_enable_fork_unsafe_buffering may have been used to restore defaults.

functions.name: RAND_reset_for_fuzzing
functions.description: Resets the fuzzer-only deterministic RNG. Available only in the fuzzer-only build configuration (FUZZING_BUILD_MODE_UNSAFE_FOR_PRODUCTION).
requirements: Only available when compiled with FUZZING_BUILD_MODE_UNSAFE_FOR_PRODUCTION defined; not present otherwise.
Intended for fuzzing; not for production use.

functions.name: RAND_get_system_entropy_for_custom_prng
functions.description: Obtains len bytes of random data directly from a system entropy source and writes them to buf. Intended for seeding custom PRNGs or when malloc must not be called from BoringSSL. Prefer RAND_bytes for general use. Not FIPS compliant. Requests over 256 bytes or entropy retrieval failure cause process abort.
requirements: buf must point to a writable buffer of at least len bytes.
len must be <= 256; requesting more causes the process to abort.
Use only for seed material or when malloc must not be called from BoringSSL; prefer RAND_bytes otherwise.
Not FIPS compliant—do not use in FIPS-required contexts.
Do not rely on error returns; failures result in process abort.

functions.name: RAND_pseudo_bytes
functions.description: Deprecated. Wrapper around RAND_bytes that fills buf with len random bytes and returns 1; error conditions abort the process as with RAND_bytes.
requirements: buf must point to a writable buffer of at least len bytes.
Deprecated—new code should use RAND_bytes.
Do not rely on a 0 return for error handling; failures abort.

functions.name: RAND_seed
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT void RAND_seed(const void *buf, int num);
functions.description: Deprecated. Reads a single byte of random data to ensure any internal file descriptors are opened. Supplied parameters are not used for seeding in BoringSSL.
requirements: No specific requirements on buf or num; they are effectively ignored per documentation.
Do not rely on this to add entropy; it does not seed in BoringSSL.

functions.name: RAND_load_file
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int RAND_load_file(const char *path, long num);
functions.description: Deprecated compatibility stub. Returns a nonnegative number. Specific behavior (e.g., reading from path/num) is not implemented in BoringSSL.
requirements: Behavior and use of path and num are unspecified in BoringSSL; callers must not rely on data being loaded.
Only the nonnegative return is guaranteed; all other effects are unknown.

functions.name: RAND_file_name
functions.description: Deprecated compatibility stub. Always returns NULL. Does not produce a filename.
requirements: Return value is always NULL; buf and num have no effect.
Callers must handle NULL unconditionally.

functions.name: RAND_add
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT void RAND_add(const void *buf, int num, double entropy);
functions.description: Deprecated no-op. Accepts input parameters but does nothing in BoringSSL.
requirements: No effect regardless of inputs; do not rely on this to add entropy.

functions.name: RAND_egd
functions.description: Deprecated compatibility stub. Always returns 255.
requirements: Callers must expect a constant return value of 255.
Argument is ignored.

functions.name: RAND_poll
functions.description: Deprecated compatibility stub. Always returns 1.
requirements: No arguments; callers should not expect any side effects beyond the constant return value.

functions.name: RAND_status
functions.description: Deprecated compatibility stub. Always returns 1.
requirements: No arguments; callers should not expect this to reflect real RNG status in BoringSSL.

functions.name: RAND_cleanup
functions.description: Deprecated no-op. Performs no cleanup in BoringSSL.
requirements: No effect; safe to call but unnecessary.

functions.name: RAND_SSLeay
functions.description: Returns a pointer to a dummy RAND_METHOD. Provided only for compatibility; the returned method is not used by BoringSSL’s RNG.
requirements: Returned pointer refers to a dummy method; callers must not rely on it for real RNG operations.
Lifespan/ownership semantics are unspecified; treat as non-owning and do not attempt to modify or free.

functions.name: RAND_OpenSSL
functions.description: Returns a pointer to a dummy RAND_METHOD. Provided only for compatibility; the returned method is not used by BoringSSL’s RNG.
requirements: Returned pointer refers to a dummy method; callers must not rely on it for real RNG operations.
Lifespan/ownership semantics are unspecified; treat as non-owning and do not attempt to modify or free.

functions.name: RAND_get_rand_method
functions.description: Returns RAND_SSLeay(), i.e., a pointer to a dummy RAND_METHOD for compatibility.
requirements: Return value is a dummy method; do not rely on it for RNG behavior.
Treat returned pointer as non-owning; do not modify or free.

functions.name: RAND_set_rand_method
functions.description: Compatibility stub that returns 1. Accepts a RAND_METHOD pointer but does not change RNG behavior in BoringSSL.
requirements: Argument is accepted but effect is unspecified/no-op; callers must not rely on it to change RNG.
Expect a constant success return of 1.

functions.name: RC4_set_key
functions.signature: void RC4_set_key(RC4_KEY *rc4key, unsigned len, const uint8_t *key);
functions.description: Initializes an RC4 key schedule in rc4key using len bytes of key material from key. Call this once before using RC4() with the resulting key state. Note: RC4 is considered cryptographically insecure and should not be used for new designs.
requirements: rc4key must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to writable storage for an RC4_KEY state.
key must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to at least len bytes of key material.
len specifies the number of bytes read from key; it must accurately reflect the length of the provided key material.
The resulting rc4key must be used only with RC4() and should be (re)initialized again with RC4_set_key() before reusing with a different key.
Thread-safety: callers must ensure rc4key is not concurrently modified or used from multiple threads without external synchronization.
Behavior or valid range of len beyond “bytes of key material” is not specified here; typical RC4 key length constraints are unknown from this header.

functions.name: RC4
functions.signature: void RC4(RC4_KEY *key, size_t len, const uint8_t *in, uint8_t *out);
functions.description: Encrypts/decrypts len bytes from in to out using the RC4 stream cipher and the given key state. RC4 is symmetric; the same function is used for encryption and decryption. The key must be initialized with RC4_set_key() beforehand. Note: RC4 is deprecated/insecure for modern cryptographic use.
requirements: key must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an initialized RC4_KEY state produced by a prior successful call to RC4_set_key().
in must point to at least len readable bytes; out must point to at least len writable bytes.
The behavior for overlapping in and out buffers is not specified; callers should not assume in-place operation unless documented elsewhere.
len may be zero; for non-zero values, buffers must be sized accordingly.
key must not be concurrently accessed (read/write) from multiple threads while calling RC4() without external synchronization, as the keystream state is updated during use.

functions.name: RC4_options
functions.description: Returns a constant string describing RC4 implementation options; per the header comment it returns the literal "rc4(ptr,int)". Marked as deprecated. Useful only for legacy compatibility or diagnostics.
requirements: No arguments; may be called at any time.
The returned pointer refers to a constant, immutable, null-terminated string; it must not be modified or freed.
Thread-safety of the returned static data is implied but not explicitly documented.

functions.name: RIPEMD160_Init
functions.description: Initializes a RIPEMD-160 hashing context so it can accept data via RIPEMD160_Update and produce a digest with RIPEMD160_Final. Returns 1 on success. Typical usage: call once before any Update/Final calls.
requirements: ctx must be non-NULL and point to writable memory for a RIPEMD160_CTX object.
Must be called before any RIPEMD160_Update or RIPEMD160_Final on the same context.
Caller should check the return value (1 indicates success).

functions.name: RIPEMD160_Update
functions.signature: int RIPEMD160_Update(RIPEMD160_CTX *ctx, const void *data, size_t len);
functions.description: Feeds len bytes of data into an initialized RIPEMD-160 hashing context. Can be called multiple times to process streaming input. Returns 1 on success.
requirements: ctx must be a valid RIPEMD160_CTX previously initialized with RIPEMD160_Init.
data must point to at least len bytes of readable memory; if len is 0, data may be NULL (inferred from common OpenSSL conventions).
May be called repeatedly until RIPEMD160_Final is invoked on the same context.
Caller should check the return value (1 indicates success).

functions.name: RIPEMD160_Final
functions.description: Finalizes the RIPEMD-160 calculation by adding padding and writing the 20-byte digest to out. Returns 1 on success.
requirements: out must point to a buffer with at least RIPEMD160_DIGEST_LENGTH (20) bytes of writable space.
ctx must be a valid RIPEMD160_CTX initialized by RIPEMD160_Init (and optionally updated via RIPEMD160_Update).
After finalization, do not call RIPEMD160_Update on the same ctx unless it is reinitialized (inferred from standard hash API usage).
Caller should check the return value (1 indicates success).

functions.name: RIPEMD160
functions.signature: uint8_t *RIPEMD160(const uint8_t *data, size_t len, uint8_t out[RIPEMD160_DIGEST_LENGTH]);
functions.description: One-shot convenience function that computes the RIPEMD-160 digest of data[0..len-1] and writes the 20-byte result to out. Returns out.
requirements: out must point to a buffer with at least RIPEMD160_DIGEST_LENGTH (20) bytes of writable space.
data must point to at least len bytes of readable memory; if len is 0, data may be NULL (inferred from common OpenSSL conventions).
The returned pointer equals out; callers should not assume any other allocation or ownership semantics.

functions.name: RIPEMD160_Transform
functions.description: Performs one low-level RIPEMD-160 compression function on a single 64-byte block, updating the internal state in ctx. Intended for advanced or internal use when processing data in full blocks and handling padding externally.
requirements: ctx must be a valid RIPEMD160_CTX with an initialized internal state (typically via RIPEMD160_Init).
block must point to at least RIPEMD160_CBLOCK (64) bytes of readable data.

Caller is responsible for correct message padding and length handling when using this low-level interface; do not mix arbitrary Transform calls with Update/Final unless you fully understand the state machine (inferred from low-level nature).

functions.name: RSA_new_public_key
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new RSA object initialized with the given public modulus n and public exponent e. Returns NULL on error or invalid input. Prefer this over constructing a key field-by-field.
requirements: n must be a valid BIGNUM modulus.
e must be a valid BIGNUM public exponent.
Returns NULL on error or invalid input; caller must check for NULL and handle errors.
The returned RSA* must be released with RSA_free.

functions.name: RSA_new_private_key
functions.signature: RSA *RSA_new_private_key(const BIGNUM *n, const BIGNUM *e, const BIGNUM *d, const BIGNUM *p, const BIGNUM *q, const BIGNUM *dmp1, const BIGNUM *dmq1, const BIGNUM *iqmp);
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new RSA object initialized with a full private key (including CRT parameters). Returns NULL on error or invalid input.
requirements: All parameters n, e, d, p, q, dmp1, dmq1, iqmp are mandatory and may not be NULL.
Creates standard RSA private keys with CRT parameters.
Returns NULL on error; caller must check and handle.
The returned RSA* must be released with RSA_free.

functions.name: RSA_new
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new, empty RSA object. Prefer RSA_new_public_key or RSA_new_private_key to import keys.
requirements: Returns NULL on error; caller must check and handle.
The returned RSA* must be released with RSA_free.
Subsequent setters may defer some initialization; invalid inputs may be caught at first use.

functions.name: RSA_new_method
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new RSA object using the specified ENGINE, otherwise like RSA_new.
requirements: engine specifies the ENGINE backing; may be NULL depending on build/availability (not stated).
Returns NULL on error; caller must check and handle.
Release the result with RSA_free.

functions.name: RSA_free
functions.description: Decrements the reference count of rsa and frees it when it reaches zero.
requirements: rsa may be NULL (behavior not specified; typical BoringSSL allows NULL no-op, but not explicitly stated).
Do not use rsa after this call if reference count reaches zero.
Thread-safety: only call mutating functions when no other threads are concurrently mutating.

functions.name: RSA_up_ref
functions.description: Increments the reference count of rsa for shared ownership. Returns 1.
requirements: May be used concurrently; it does not mutate rsa’s contents for thread-safety.
Returns 1; caller may treat non-1 as error if ever returned (doc says returns one).
rsa must be a valid RSA pointer.

functions.name: RSA_bits
functions.description: Returns the modulus size of rsa in bits.
requirements: rsa must point to a valid RSA object with a modulus set (implicit).

functions.name: RSA_get0_n
functions.description: Returns rsa’s public modulus n.
requirements: rsa must be valid.
May return NULL if modulus is not set.

functions.name: RSA_get0_e
functions.description: Returns rsa’s public exponent e.
requirements: rsa must be valid.
May return NULL if exponent is not set.

functions.name: RSA_get0_d
functions.description: Returns rsa’s private exponent d, or NULL if rsa is a public key.
requirements: rsa must be valid.
Public keys return NULL.

functions.name: RSA_get0_p
functions.description: Returns rsa’s first private prime factor p, or NULL if absent or key is public.
requirements: rsa must be valid.

functions.name: RSA_get0_q
functions.description: Returns rsa’s second private prime factor q, or NULL if absent or key is public.
requirements: rsa must be valid.

functions.name: RSA_get0_dmp1
functions.description: Returns d mod (p-1) for rsa, or NULL if absent or key is public.
requirements: rsa must be valid.

functions.name: RSA_get0_dmq1
functions.description: Returns d mod (q-1) for rsa, or NULL if absent or key is public.
requirements: rsa must be valid.

functions.name: RSA_get0_iqmp
functions.description: Returns q^-1 mod p for rsa, or NULL if absent or key is public.
requirements: rsa must be valid.

functions.name: RSA_get0_key
functions.signature: void RSA_get0_key(const RSA *rsa, const BIGNUM **out_n, const BIGNUM **out_e, const BIGNUM **out_d);
functions.description: Outputs rsa’s modulus, public exponent, and private exponent (if present) to provided output pointers.
requirements: Each of out_n, out_e, out_d may be NULL to skip.
If rsa is a public key, *out_d will be set to NULL.
Output pointers must be valid writable pointers when non-NULL.

functions.name: RSA_get0_factors
functions.signature: void RSA_get0_factors(const RSA *rsa, const BIGNUM **out_p, const BIGNUM **out_q);
functions.description: Outputs rsa’s prime factors p and q (if present) to provided output pointers.
requirements: Each of out_p and out_q may be NULL to skip.
If rsa is a public key, outputs will be set to NULL.

functions.name: RSA_get0_crt_params
functions.signature: void RSA_get0_crt_params(const RSA *rsa, const BIGNUM **out_dmp1, const BIGNUM **out_dmq1, const BIGNUM **out_iqmp);
functions.description: Outputs rsa’s CRT parameters dmp1, dmq1, iqmp (if present) to provided output pointers.
requirements: Each of out_dmp1, out_dmq1, out_iqmp may be NULL to skip.
If rsa is a public key, outputs will be set to NULL.

functions.name: RSA_set0_key
functions.description: Sets rsa’s modulus, public exponent, and private exponent to the provided values (if non-NULL). Takes ownership on success. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: d may be NULL.
n and e must either be non-NULL or already configured on rsa.
Do not call after rsa has been used for a cryptographic operation; construct a new RSA instead.
On success, ownership of provided BIGNUMs transfers to rsa; caller must not free them afterward.
Returns 0 on error; caller must check and handle.

functions.name: RSA_set0_factors
functions.description: Sets rsa’s prime factors p and q (if non-NULL). Takes ownership on success. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: Each argument must either be non-NULL or already configured on rsa.
Do not call after rsa has been used for a cryptographic operation; construct a new RSA instead.
On success, ownership of p and q transfers to rsa.

functions.name: RSA_set0_crt_params
functions.description: Sets rsa’s CRT parameters (dmp1, dmq1, iqmp) (if non-NULL). Takes ownership on success. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: Each argument must either be non-NULL or already configured on rsa.
Do not call after rsa has been used for a cryptographic operation; construct a new RSA instead.
On success, ownership of the parameters transfers to rsa.

functions.name: RSA_generate_key_ex
functions.signature: int RSA_generate_key_ex(RSA *rsa, int bits, const BIGNUM *e, BN_GENCB *cb);
functions.description: Generates a new RSA key into rsa with a modulus of size bits and public exponent e. Optionally reports progress via cb. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: bits specifies modulus length in bits.
e must be a valid public exponent; RSA_F4 is recommended if unsure.
If cb is not NULL, it will be called with specific events as documented (including event=2 on rejected primes and event=3 on suitable p found).
Caller must pass a valid, allocated RSA object.
Returns 0 on error; caller must check and handle.

functions.name: RSA_generate_key_fips
functions.description: Generates a new RSA key into rsa with FIPS-compliant checks. Public exponent is fixed to 65537. bits must be 2048 or 3072. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: bits must be either 2048 or 3072.
Public exponent is always 65537; caller must not supply a different e (parameter is not present).
cb, if not NULL, may receive progress callbacks (as in RSA_generate_key_ex).
Returns 0 on error; caller must check and handle.

functions.name: RSA_encrypt
functions.signature: int RSA_encrypt(RSA *rsa, size_t *out_len, uint8_t *out, size_t max_out, const uint8_t *in, size_t in_len, int padding);
functions.description: Encrypts in_len bytes from in using the public key in rsa, writing at most max_out bytes to out and the actual length to *out_len. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error. Prefer this over legacy RSA_public_encrypt.
requirements: max_out must be at least RSA_size(rsa) to ensure success.
padding must be one of RSA_*_PADDING values.
For RSA_PKCS1_OAEP_PADDING, the OAEP and MGF1 digest are fixed to SHA-1 in this API.
When unsure, use RSA_PKCS1_OAEP_PADDING for new protocols.
Returns 0 on error; caller must check and handle.

functions.name: RSA_decrypt
functions.signature: int RSA_decrypt(RSA *rsa, size_t *out_len, uint8_t *out, size_t max_out, const uint8_t *in, size_t in_len, int padding);
functions.description: Decrypts in_len bytes from in with the private key in rsa, writing at most max_out bytes to out and the actual length to *out_len. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error. Prefer this over legacy RSA_private_decrypt.
requirements: max_out must be at least RSA_size(rsa) to ensure success.
padding must be one of RSA_*_PADDING values.
For RSA_PKCS1_OAEP_PADDING, the OAEP and MGF1 digest are fixed to SHA-1 in this API.
Using RSA_PKCS1_PADDING is deprecated and insecure; for mitigations use RSA_NO_PADDING with custom logic if required (e.g., TLS RSA KEX).
Returns 0 on error; caller must check and handle.

functions.name: RSA_public_encrypt
functions.signature: int RSA_public_encrypt(size_t flen, const uint8_t *from, uint8_t *to, RSA *rsa, int padding);
functions.description: Legacy encrypt API. Encrypts flen bytes from from to the public key in rsa and writes to to. Returns number of bytes written, or -1 on error. Prefer RSA_encrypt.
requirements: to must have at least RSA_size(rsa) bytes of space.
padding must be one of RSA_*_PADDING values.
For RSA_PKCS1_OAEP_PADDING, OAEP/MGF1 digest is fixed to SHA-1 in this API.
Caller must check for -1 on error.

functions.name: RSA_private_decrypt
functions.signature: int RSA_private_decrypt(size_t flen, const uint8_t *from, uint8_t *to, RSA *rsa, int padding);
functions.description: Legacy decrypt API. Decrypts flen bytes from from with the private key in rsa and writes plaintext to to. Returns number of bytes written, or -1 on error. Prefer RSA_decrypt.
requirements: to must have at least RSA_size(rsa) bytes of space.
padding must be one of RSA_*_PADDING values.
For RSA_PKCS1_OAEP_PADDING, OAEP/MGF1 digest is fixed to SHA-1 in this API.
Using RSA_PKCS1_PADDING is deprecated and insecure (see RSA_decrypt warning).
Caller must check for -1 on error.

functions.name: RSA_sign
functions.signature: int RSA_sign(int hash_nid, const uint8_t *digest, size_t digest_len, uint8_t *out, unsigned *out_len, RSA *rsa);
functions.description: Computes an RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 signature over a digest. Writes up to RSA_size(rsa) bytes to out and the actual length to *out_len. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: digest must be the hash output corresponding to hash_nid (e.g., NID_sha256).
Caller must ensure out has at least RSA_size(rsa) bytes available.
Caller must check return value and handle 0 as error.

functions.name: RSA_sign_pss_mgf1
functions.signature: int RSA_sign_pss_mgf1(RSA *rsa, size_t *out_len, uint8_t *out, size_t max_out, const uint8_t *digest, size_t digest_len, const EVP_MD *md, const EVP_MD *mgf1_md, int salt_len);
functions.description: Computes an RSASSA-PSS signature using MGF1. Writes at most max_out bytes to out and the actual length to *out_len. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: max_out must be at least RSA_size(rsa).
digest must be the hash of the message using md.
mgf1_md may be NULL to use md.
salt_len may be RSA_PSS_SALTLEN_DIGEST, RSA_PSS_SALTLEN_AUTO, or a non-negative byte length; when unsure, use RSA_PSS_SALTLEN_DIGEST.
Caller must check return value.

functions.name: RSA_sign_raw
functions.signature: int RSA_sign_raw(RSA *rsa, size_t *out_len, uint8_t *out, size_t max_out, const uint8_t *in, size_t in_len, int padding);
functions.description: Performs the raw private-key operation for building signature schemes. With RSA_PKCS1_PADDING, wraps in with PKCS#1 v1.5 signature padding; with RSA_NO_PADDING, performs a raw modular exponentiation. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: max_out must be at least RSA_size(rsa).
If padding is RSA_PKCS1_PADDING, caller must pre-encode input as DigestInfo of a hash.
If padding is RSA_NO_PADDING, in is interpreted as an integer modulo n; caller must supply correctly encoded input for their scheme.
This is a low-level building block; callers must implement full scheme checks externally.
Caller must check return value.

functions.name: RSA_verify
functions.signature: int RSA_verify(int hash_nid, const uint8_t *digest, size_t digest_len, const uint8_t *sig, size_t sig_len, RSA *rsa);
functions.description: Verifies an RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 signature sig over digest using rsa. Returns 1 if valid, 0 otherwise.
requirements: digest must be the hash output corresponding to hash_nid.
Caller must supply the signature buffer and length correctly.
Return value is 1 on valid, 0 otherwise (no -1 error code in this variant).

functions.name: RSA_verify_pss_mgf1
functions.signature: int RSA_verify_pss_mgf1(RSA *rsa, const uint8_t *digest, size_t digest_len, const EVP_MD *md, const EVP_MD *mgf1_md, int salt_len, const uint8_t *sig, size_t sig_len);
functions.description: Verifies an RSASSA-PSS signature using MGF1. Returns 1 if valid, 0 otherwise.
requirements: digest must be the hash of the message using md.
mgf1_md may be NULL to use md.
salt_len may be RSA_PSS_SALTLEN_DIGEST, RSA_PSS_SALTLEN_AUTO, or a non-negative byte length.
Caller must provide full signature bytes and length.

functions.name: RSA_verify_raw
functions.signature: int RSA_verify_raw(RSA *rsa, size_t *out_len, uint8_t *out, size_t max_out, const uint8_t *in, size_t in_len, int padding);
functions.description: Performs the raw public-key operation for signature verification. With RSA_PKCS1_PADDING, checks PKCS#1 v1.5 padding and outputs the remainder of the encoded digest; with RSA_NO_PADDING, performs the raw modular operation. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure/invalid input.
requirements: max_out must be at least RSA_size(rsa).
If padding is RSA_PKCS1_PADDING, caller must validate the resulting DigestInfo against the expected digest.
If padding is RSA_NO_PADDING, caller must validate the output according to their signature scheme.
This is a low-level building block; callers must implement full scheme checks externally.
Caller must check return value.

functions.name: RSA_private_encrypt
functions.signature: int RSA_private_encrypt(size_t flen, const uint8_t *from, uint8_t *to, RSA *rsa, int padding);
functions.description: Legacy signing building block. Performs the private-key operation for signature computation and writes to to. Returns number of bytes written, or -1 on error. Prefer RSA_sign_raw.
requirements: to must have at least RSA_size(rsa) bytes of space.
For padding semantics, see RSA_sign_raw.
Caller must check for -1 on error.

functions.name: RSA_public_decrypt
functions.signature: int RSA_public_decrypt(size_t flen, const uint8_t *from, uint8_t *to, RSA *rsa, int padding);
functions.description: Legacy verification building block. Performs the public-key operation for signature verification and writes to to. Returns number of bytes written, or -1 on error. Prefer RSA_verify_raw.
requirements: to must have at least RSA_size(rsa) bytes of space.
For padding semantics, see RSA_verify_raw.
Caller must check for -1 on error.

functions.name: RSA_size
functions.description: Returns the modulus size in bytes, which is also the size of a signature or ciphertext for rsa.
requirements: rsa must be valid and have a modulus set (implicit).

functions.name: RSA_is_opaque
functions.description: Returns 1 if rsa is opaque (key material not exposed), 0 otherwise.
requirements: rsa must be valid.

functions.name: RSAPublicKey_dup
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new RSA containing a copy of the public key from rsa. Returns NULL on error.
requirements: rsa must be valid.
Caller must free the returned RSA with RSA_free.
Caller must check for NULL on error.

functions.name: RSAPrivateKey_dup
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new RSA containing a copy of the private key from rsa. Returns NULL on error.
requirements: rsa must be valid and contain private key material.
Caller must free the returned RSA with RSA_free.
Caller must check for NULL on error.

functions.name: RSA_check_key
functions.description: Performs basic private-key validity tests on rsa. Returns 1 if they pass, 0 otherwise. Opaque keys and public keys always pass.
requirements: rsa must be valid.
On return 0, more detailed error is available on the error queue.

functions.name: RSA_check_fips
functions.description: Performs public key validity tests on key for FIPS compliance. Returns 1 if they pass, 0 otherwise. Opaque keys always fail. Non-mutating for thread-safety.
requirements: key must be valid.
Caller must check return value; opaque keys will fail.

functions.name: RSA_verify_PKCS1_PSS_mgf1
functions.signature: int RSA_verify_PKCS1_PSS_mgf1(const RSA *rsa, const uint8_t *mHash, const EVP_MD *Hash, const EVP_MD *mgf1Hash, const uint8_t *EM, int sLen);
functions.description: Low-level check that EM is a correct PSS encoding of mHash using Hash and MGF1 (mgf1Hash or Hash if NULL). Returns 1 on success, 0 on error. Prefer RSA_verify_pss_mgf1.
requirements: EM must point to exactly RSA_size(rsa) bytes.
mHash must be the output of Hash.
mgf1Hash may be NULL to use Hash.
sLen may be -1 (salt length equals hash length) or -2 (recover and accept all values), or a non-negative length.
Caller must check return value.

functions.name: RSA_padding_add_PKCS1_PSS_mgf1
functions.signature: int RSA_padding_add_PKCS1_PSS_mgf1(const RSA *rsa, uint8_t *EM, const uint8_t *mHash, const EVP_MD *Hash, const EVP_MD *mgf1Hash, int sLen);
functions.description: Low-level operation that writes a PSS encoding of mHash into EM, producing exactly RSA_size(rsa) bytes, using Hash and MGF1 (mgf1Hash or Hash if NULL). Returns 1 on success, 0 on error. Prefer RSA_sign_pss_mgf1.
requirements: EM must have space for exactly RSA_size(rsa) bytes (written unconditionally).
mHash must be the output of Hash.
mgf1Hash may be NULL to use Hash.
sLen may be -1 (salt length equals hash length) or -2 (maximal salt given EM size), or a non-negative length.
Caller must check return value.

functions.name: RSA_padding_add_PKCS1_OAEP_mgf1
functions.signature: int RSA_padding_add_PKCS1_OAEP_mgf1(uint8_t *to, size_t to_len, const uint8_t *from, size_t from_len, const uint8_t *param, size_t param_len, const EVP_MD *md, const EVP_MD *mgf1md);
functions.description: Applies OAEP encoding of from into to using the specified hash functions and optional label (param). Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: If md is NULL, SHA-1 is used.
If mgf1md is NULL, md is used (which may be SHA-1 if md is NULL).
to must have sufficient space (to_len) for the OAEP-encoded output appropriate to the RSA modulus size (exact constraints not stated here).
Caller must check return value.

functions.name: RSA_add_pkcs1_prefix
functions.signature: int RSA_add_pkcs1_prefix(uint8_t **out_msg, size_t *out_msg_len, int *is_alloced, int hash_nid, const uint8_t *digest, size_t digest_len);
functions.description: Builds a DigestInfo-wrapped version of digest for the given hash_nid and sets out_msg to point to it. If *is_alloced is set to 1 on success, the caller must free *out_msg with OPENSSL_free. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: out_msg and out_msg_len must be valid pointers.
is_alloced must be a valid pointer; if set to 1 on success, caller must free *out_msg with OPENSSL_free.
digest must match the hash_nid’s digest length (not enforced here; implied by context).
Caller must check return value.

functions.name: RSA_parse_public_key
functions.description: Parses a DER-encoded RSAPublicKey from cbs, advancing it. Returns a newly allocated RSA on success or NULL on error.
requirements: cbs must point to a CBS positioned at a DER RSAPublicKey structure.
On success, caller owns the returned RSA and must free it with RSA_free.
Caller must check for NULL on error.

functions.name: RSA_public_key_from_bytes
functions.description: Parses a DER-encoded RSAPublicKey from a byte buffer. Returns a newly allocated RSA on success or NULL on error.
requirements: in must point to DER bytes of length in_len representing RSAPublicKey.
On success, caller must free the RSA with RSA_free.
Caller must check for NULL on error.

functions.name: RSA_marshal_public_key
functions.description: Appends a DER-encoded RSAPublicKey for rsa to cbb. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: cbb must be a valid, initialized CBB.
rsa must contain a public key.
Caller must check return value.

functions.name: RSA_public_key_to_bytes
functions.description: Marshals rsa as DER-encoded RSAPublicKey into a newly allocated buffer and returns it via out_bytes and length via out_len. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: out_bytes and out_len must be valid pointers.
On success, *out_bytes must be freed with OPENSSL_free by the caller.
rsa must contain a public key.
Caller must check return value.

functions.name: RSA_parse_private_key
functions.description: Parses a DER-encoded RSAPrivateKey from cbs, advancing it. Returns a newly allocated RSA on success or NULL on error.
requirements: cbs must point to a CBS positioned at a DER RSAPrivateKey structure.
On success, caller owns the returned RSA and must free with RSA_free.
Caller must check for NULL on error.

functions.name: RSA_private_key_from_bytes
functions.description: Parses a DER-encoded RSAPrivateKey from a byte buffer. Returns a newly allocated RSA on success or NULL on error.
requirements: in must point to DER bytes of length in_len representing RSAPrivateKey.
On success, caller must free the RSA with RSA_free.
Caller must check for NULL on error.

functions.name: RSA_marshal_private_key
functions.description: Appends a DER-encoded RSAPrivateKey for rsa to cbb. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: cbb must be a valid, initialized CBB.
rsa must contain a private key.
Caller must check return value.

functions.name: RSA_private_key_to_bytes
functions.description: Marshals rsa as DER-encoded RSAPrivateKey into a newly allocated buffer and returns it via out_bytes and length via out_len. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: out_bytes and out_len must be valid pointers.
On success, *out_bytes must be freed with OPENSSL_free by the caller.
rsa must contain a private key.
Caller must check return value.

functions.name: RSA_new_private_key_no_crt
functions.signature: RSA *RSA_new_private_key_no_crt(const BIGNUM *n, const BIGNUM *e, const BIGNUM *d);
functions.description: Allocates a new RSA private key without CRT coefficients, given n, e, d. Less performant and cannot be serialized. Returns NULL on error.
requirements: n, e, d must be non-NULL valid BIGNUMs.
Keys created cannot be serialized and are less performant.
Caller must free the RSA with RSA_free and check for NULL on error.

functions.name: RSA_new_private_key_no_e
functions.description: Allocates a new RSA private key without CRT parameters or public exponent (no e). Less performant, cannot be serialized, and lacks hardening measures. Returns NULL on error.
requirements: n and d must be non-NULL valid BIGNUMs.
Keys are less performant, cannot be serialized, and lack side-channel/fault hardening.
Caller must free the RSA with RSA_free and check for NULL on error.

functions.name: RSA_new_public_key_large_e
functions.description: Allocates a new RSA public key allowing any e up to n (large public exponent). May perform worse than RSA_new_public_key. Returns NULL on error.
requirements: n and e must be valid BIGNUMs; e may be large up to n.
May perform worse due to disabled exponent bounding.
Caller must free the RSA with RSA_free and check for NULL on error.

functions.name: RSA_new_private_key_large_e
functions.signature: RSA *RSA_new_private_key_large_e(const BIGNUM *n, const BIGNUM *e, const BIGNUM *d, const BIGNUM *p, const BIGNUM *q, const BIGNUM *dmp1, const BIGNUM *dmq1, const BIGNUM *iqmp);
functions.description: Allocates a new RSA private key (with CRT parameters) allowing any e up to n. May perform worse than RSA_new_private_key. Returns NULL on error.
requirements: All parameters must be non-NULL valid BIGNUMs.
e may be large up to n.
Caller must free with RSA_free and check for NULL on error.

functions.name: RSA_get_ex_new_index
functions.signature: int RSA_get_ex_new_index(long argl, void *argp, CRYPTO_EX_unused *unused, CRYPTO_EX_dup *dup_unused, CRYPTO_EX_free *free_func);
functions.description: Registers a new ex_data index for RSA objects. See ex_data.h for details. Returns an index or negative on error (exact semantics in ex_data.h).
requirements: Usage and callbacks are defined in ex_data.h (not detailed here).
Caller must check return value for failure per ex_data.h.

functions.name: RSA_set_ex_data
functions.description: Associates application-specific extra data with rsa at index idx. See ex_data.h.
requirements: rsa must be valid.
idx must be an index obtained via RSA_get_ex_new_index (or appropriate).
Caller must check return value.

functions.name: RSA_get_ex_data
functions.description: Retrieves previously set ex_data from rsa at index idx. See ex_data.h.
requirements: rsa must be valid.
idx must be a valid ex_data index for RSA.

functions.name: RSA_flags
functions.description: Returns the bitwise OR of RSA_FLAG_* constants for rsa.
requirements: rsa must be valid.

functions.name: RSA_test_flags
functions.description: Returns the subset of flags in flags which are set in rsa.
requirements: rsa must be valid.
flags is a bitmask of RSA_FLAG_* constants.

functions.name: RSA_blinding_on
functions.description: Deprecated no-op behavior documented as returning one. Historically enabled blinding; now returns 1.
requirements: rsa must be valid.
Caller may ignore ctx (unused).
Caller should not rely on side effects; documented to return 1.

functions.name: RSA_blinding_off
functions.description: Deprecated function which does nothing.
requirements: rsa must be valid (no other requirements stated).

functions.name: RSA_generate_key
functions.signature: RSA *RSA_generate_key(int bits, uint64_t e, void *callback, void *cb_arg);
functions.description: Deprecated generator behaving like RSA_generate_key_ex. Returns a newly-allocated RSA on success or NULL on error. For compatibility only.
requirements: callback and cb_arg must be NULL.
bits specifies modulus length; e specifies public exponent.
Caller must free returned RSA with RSA_free and check for NULL on error.

functions.name: d2i_RSAPublicKey
functions.description: Parses a DER-encoded RSAPublicKey from *inp (len bytes) as in d2i_SAMPLE. Use RSA_parse_public_key instead. Returns RSA* or NULL on error.
requirements: inp must point to a buffer of length len containing a DER RSAPublicKey.
If out is non-NULL, behavior follows d2i semantics (not fully detailed here).
Caller should prefer RSA_parse_public_key.
Caller must check for NULL on error and free RSA with RSA_free if allocated.

functions.name: i2d_RSAPublicKey
functions.description: Marshals in to DER RSAPublicKey as in i2d_SAMPLE. Use RSA_marshal_public_key instead. Returns number of bytes written or a negative value on error (per i2d semantics).
requirements: in must contain a public key.
outp follows i2d semantics (may allocate if *outp==NULL).
Caller should prefer RSA_marshal_public_key.
Caller must check return value for error.

functions.name: d2i_RSAPrivateKey
functions.description: Parses a DER-encoded RSAPrivateKey from *inp (len bytes) as in d2i_SAMPLE. Use RSA_parse_private_key instead. Returns RSA* or NULL on error.
requirements: inp must point to a buffer of length len containing a DER RSAPrivateKey.

functions.name: SHA1_Init

Must be called before SHA1_Update and SHA1_Final on the same context.

functions.name: SHA1_Update

functions.description: Feeds |len| bytes from |data| into the ongoing SHA-1 hash state referenced by |sha|. May be called multiple times after SHA1_Init and before SHA1_Final. Returns 1 on success.
requirements: sha must be a non-null pointer to an initialized SHA_CTX (initialized via SHA1_Init).

Do not call after SHA1_Final has been called on the context unless the context is re-initialized with SHA1_Init.
The same SHA_CTX must not be used concurrently from multiple threads without external synchronization.
Callers should check the return value and treat 0 as failure.

functions.name: SHA1_Final
functions.description: Finalizes the SHA-1 computation for the context |sha|, writes the 20-byte digest to |out|, and returns 1 on success. After this call, the context is finished and must be re-initialized before reuse.
requirements: out must be a non-null pointer to a buffer with at least SHA_DIGEST_LENGTH (20) writable bytes.
sha must be a non-null pointer to a SHA_CTX previously initialized by SHA1_Init (and optionally updated via SHA1_Update).
Do not call SHA1_Update on the context after finalization unless re-initialized with SHA1_Init.
Callers should check the return value and treat 0 as failure.

functions.description: Computes the SHA-1 digest of the |len| bytes at |data| in a single call and writes the 20-byte result to |out|, returning |out|. Convenience, equivalent to Init/Update/Final sequence. SHA-1 is weak and not recommended for new designs.
requirements: If len > 0, data must be a non-null pointer to at least len bytes of readable memory.

functions.name: SHA1_Transform

functions.description: Performs a single low-level SHA-1 compression on one 64-byte block using the current state in |sha|. This is an internal/advanced API and bypasses padding and length processing; intended for specialized uses that manage block processing manually.
requirements: sha must be a non-null pointer to a valid SHA_CTX whose internal state will be updated in place.

functions.name: CRYPTO_fips_186_2_prf
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT void CRYPTO_fips_186_2_prf(uint8_t *out, size_t out_len, const uint8_t xkey[SHA_DIGEST_LENGTH]);
functions.description: Derives out_len bytes into |out| from the 160-bit |xkey| using the FIPS 186-2 Appendix 3.1 PRF (with change notice 1). The PRF emits a sequence of 320-bit (40-byte) big-endian blocks concatenated and truncated to out_len. Provided for compatibility with legacy EAP methods; SHA-1 based and not recommended for new protocols.

functions.description: Creates a SLH-DSA-SHA2-128s signature over a prehashed message using private_key. context may be NULL only if context_len is 0; otherwise must point to context_len readable bytes.
context_len must be <= 255; function returns 0 if larger.
Callers must check the return value (1 success, 0 failure).
Pointers must be valid and properly aligned for access.

functions.name: SLHDSA_SHA2_128S_prehash_verify
functions.signature: int SLHDSA_SHA2_128S_prehash_verify(const uint8_t *signature, size_t signature_len, const uint8_t public_key[SLHDSA_SHA2_128S_PUBLIC_KEY_BYTES], const uint8_t *hashed_msg, size_t hashed_msg_len, int hash_nid, const uint8_t *context, size_t context_len);
functions.description: Verifies a SLH-DSA-SHA2-128s signature over a prehashed message using the specified hash function (hash_nid). Returns 1 if the signature is valid; returns 0 if invalid, if the hash function is unsupported, or if hashed_msg_len is incorrect for hash_nid.
requirements: signature must point to signature_len bytes of readable data; typical usage provides exactly SLHDSA_SHA2_128S_SIGNATURE_BYTES bytes.
public_key must point to a readable buffer of exactly SLHDSA_SHA2_128S_PUBLIC_KEY_BYTES bytes.
hashed_msg must point to hashed_msg_len bytes of readable data and must be the exact length required by hash_nid.
hash_nid must denote a hash function listed in FIPS 205; unsupported values cause failure.
context must equal the value supplied to signing; may be NULL only if context_len is 0.
Callers must check the return value (1 valid, 0 invalid).
Pointers must be valid and properly aligned for access.

functions.name: SLHDSA_SHA2_128S_prehash_warning_nonstandard_sign
functions.signature: int SLHDSA_SHA2_128S_prehash_warning_nonstandard_sign(uint8_t out_signature[SLHDSA_SHA2_128S_SIGNATURE_BYTES], const uint8_t private_key[SLHDSA_SHA2_128S_PRIVATE_KEY_BYTES], const uint8_t *hashed_msg, size_t hashed_msg_len, int hash_nid, const uint8_t *context, size_t context_len);
functions.description: Creates a SLH-DSA-SHA2-128s signature over a prehashed message where the hash function is explicitly non-standard and not compliant with FIPS 205. Intended only for compatibility with external systems. Returns 1 on success; returns 0 if context_len > 255, the hash algorithm is unsupported, or hashed_msg_len is incorrect.
requirements: out_signature must point to a writable buffer of at least SLHDSA_SHA2_128S_SIGNATURE_BYTES bytes.
private_key must point to a readable buffer of exactly SLHDSA_SHA2_128S_PRIVATE_KEY_BYTES bytes.
hashed_msg must point to hashed_msg_len bytes of readable data and must be the exact length required by the specified non-standard hash.
hash_nid must denote a non-standard hash function (not compliant with FIPS 205); unsupported values cause failure.
context may be NULL only if context_len is 0; otherwise must point to context_len readable bytes.
context_len must be <= 255; function returns 0 if larger.
Callers must check the return value (1 success, 0 failure).
Pointers must be valid and properly aligned for access.

functions.name: SLHDSA_SHA2_128S_prehash_warning_nonstandard_verify
functions.signature: int SLHDSA_SHA2_128S_prehash_warning_nonstandard_verify(const uint8_t *signature, size_t signature_len, const uint8_t public_key[SLHDSA_SHA2_128S_PUBLIC_KEY_BYTES], const uint8_t *hashed_msg, size_t hashed_msg_len, int hash_nid, const uint8_t *context, size_t context_len);
functions.description: Verifies a SLH-DSA-SHA2-128s signature over a prehashed message where the hash function is explicitly non-standard (not FIPS 205 compliant). Returns 1 if the signature is valid; returns 0 if invalid, if the hash function is unsupported, or if hashed_msg_len is incorrect.
requirements: signature must point to signature_len bytes of readable data; typical usage provides exactly SLHDSA_SHA2_128S_SIGNATURE_BYTES bytes.
public_key must point to a readable buffer of exactly SLHDSA_SHA2_128S_PUBLIC_KEY_BYTES bytes.
hashed_msg must point to hashed_msg_len bytes of readable data and must be the exact length required by the specified non-standard hash.
hash_nid must denote a non-standard hash function (not compliant with FIPS 205); unsupported values cause failure.
context must equal the value supplied to signing; may be NULL only if context_len is 0.
Callers must check the return value (1 valid, 0 invalid).
Pointers must be valid and properly aligned for access.

functions.name: TLS_method
functions.description: Returns the SSL_METHOD used to create TLS (stream) connections. Use it with SSL_CTX_new to create a context for TLS. Typically used by clients and servers for TLS 1.0–1.3 depending on min/max settings.
requirements: Must be passed to SSL_CTX_new to create an SSL_CTX for TLS connections.
No arguments; returns NULL on internal error only via SSL_CTX_new.

functions.name: DTLS_method
functions.description: Returns the SSL_METHOD used to create DTLS (datagram) connections. Use with SSL_CTX_new to create a context for DTLS.
requirements: Must be passed to SSL_CTX_new to create an SSL_CTX for DTLS connections.

functions.name: TLS_with_buffers_method
functions.description: Returns an SSL_METHOD for TLS that avoids all use of crypto/x509. Client connections using this method will fail unless a certificate verifier is installed via SSL_set_custom_verify or SSL_CTX_set_custom_verify.
requirements: For client use, a certificate verifier must be installed; otherwise handshakes will fail.
Use with SSL_CTX_new to create an SSL_CTX.

functions.name: DTLS_with_buffers_method
functions.description: Returns an SSL_METHOD for DTLS that avoids all use of crypto/x509.
requirements: Use with SSL_CTX_new to create an SSL_CTX for DTLS without X.509.
Caller must handle verification via custom mechanisms if needed.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_new
functions.description: Allocates a new SSL_CTX configured by the given SSL_METHOD (TLS or DTLS). Returns a newly-allocated context with default settings or NULL on error.
requirements: method must be a valid SSL_METHOD pointer (e.g., from TLS_method or DTLS_method).
Caller must free the returned SSL_CTX with SSL_CTX_free.
Thread safety: once shared across threads, do not call configuration functions that mutate the context.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_up_ref
functions.description: Increments the reference count of the SSL_CTX. Returns one.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX pointer.
Balances a future SSL_CTX_free call elsewhere.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_free
functions.description: Decrements the reference count of ctx and frees it when it reaches zero.
requirements: ctx may be NULL (no effect) or a valid SSL_CTX.
All SSL objects created from ctx must be freed before ctx is freed or still referenced elsewhere.

functions.name: SSL_new
functions.description: Allocates a new SSL connection object using settings from ctx at creation time. By default, it is neither client nor server until SSL_set_connect_state or SSL_set_accept_state is called.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX.
Caller must free the returned SSL with SSL_free.
After creation, configure as client or server before handshake using SSL_set_connect_state or SSL_set_accept_state.

functions.name: SSL_free
functions.description: Frees an SSL connection object and any associated resources.
requirements: ssl may be NULL (no effect) or a valid SSL pointer.
Must not be called concurrently with other operations on ssl.

functions.name: SSL_get_SSL_CTX
functions.description: Returns the SSL_CTX associated with ssl. If SSL_set_SSL_CTX was called, returns the new SSL_CTX.
requirements: ssl must be a valid SSL pointer.
Returned pointer is non-owning; do not free it unless you hold a ref.

functions.name: SSL_set_connect_state
functions.description: Configures ssl to act as a client.
requirements: ssl must be a valid SSL pointer.
Call before the handshake begins.

functions.name: SSL_set_accept_state
functions.description: Configures ssl to act as a server.
requirements: ssl must be a valid SSL pointer.
Call before the handshake begins.

functions.name: SSL_is_server
functions.description: Returns one if ssl is configured as a server and zero otherwise.
requirements: ssl must be a valid SSL pointer.

functions.name: SSL_is_dtls
functions.description: Returns one if ssl is a DTLS connection and zero otherwise.
requirements: ssl must be a valid SSL pointer.

functions.name: SSL_is_quic
functions.description: Returns one if ssl is a QUIC connection and zero otherwise.
requirements: ssl must be a valid SSL pointer.

functions.name: SSL_set_bio
functions.description: Configures ssl to read from rbio and write to wbio. Takes ownership of the BIOs (one ref if same). Historical behavior is complex; calling this when BIOs are already configured is deprecated. Prefer SSL_set0_rbio and SSL_set0_wbio.
requirements: ssl must be a valid SSL.
rbio must implement BIO_read; wbio must implement BIO_write, and for wbio, BIO_flush via BIO_meth_set_ctrl with BIO_CTRL_FLUSH.
In DTLS, rbio must be non-blocking to handle timeouts/retransmits.
If reusing an already-configured BIO, see notes about asymmetry; prefer set0 functions.

functions.name: SSL_set0_rbio
functions.description: Sets the read BIO for ssl and takes ownership of rbio. For custom BIOs, must implement BIO_read. In DTLS, rbio must be non-blocking. Each set0_rbio/set0_wbio call takes a ref if sharing the same BIO.
requirements: ssl must be valid.
rbio may be NULL to clear the read BIO; if non-NULL, must implement BIO_read.
In DTLS, rbio should be non-blocking for correct behavior.

functions.name: SSL_set0_wbio
functions.description: Sets the write BIO for ssl and takes ownership of wbio. Custom BIOs must implement BIO_write and BIO_flush (via ctrl/FLUSH). Each set0 call takes a reference if sharing BIOs.
requirements: ssl must be valid.
wbio may be NULL to clear write BIO; if non-NULL, must implement BIO_write and BIO_flush returning one (no-op allowed).

functions.name: SSL_get_rbio
functions.description: Returns the BIO that ssl reads from, or NULL if not configured.
requirements: ssl must be valid.
Returned BIO is non-owning.

functions.name: SSL_get_wbio
functions.description: Returns the BIO that ssl writes to, or NULL if not configured.
requirements: ssl must be valid.
Returned BIO is non-owning.

functions.name: SSL_get_fd
functions.description: Returns the file descriptor that ssl is configured to read from (calls SSL_get_rfd). On Windows, may be a SOCKET cast to int. Returns -1 if not configured or not a fd BIO.
requirements: ssl must be valid.

functions.name: SSL_get_rfd
functions.description: Returns the read-side file descriptor from the read BIO if present and wrapping a file descriptor, otherwise -1. On Windows, may be SOCKET cast to int.
requirements: ssl must be valid.

functions.name: SSL_get_wfd
functions.description: Returns the write-side file descriptor from the write BIO if present and wrapping a file descriptor, otherwise -1. On Windows, may be SOCKET cast to int.
requirements: ssl must be valid.

functions.name: SSL_set_fd
functions.description: Configures ssl to read from and write to the given file descriptor. Caller retains ownership of fd. Returns one on success and zero on allocation error. On Windows, fd is cast to SOCKET and used with Winsock APIs.
requirements: Available only when !OPENSSL_NO_SOCK.
ssl must be valid; fd must be a valid file descriptor (or SOCKET on Windows).

functions.name: SSL_set_rfd
functions.description: Configures ssl to read from the given file descriptor. Caller retains ownership. Returns one on success and zero on allocation error. On Windows, fd is cast to SOCKET.
requirements: Available only when !OPENSSL_NO_SOCK.
ssl must be valid; fd must be valid.

functions.name: SSL_set_wfd
functions.description: Configures ssl to write to the given file descriptor. Caller retains ownership. Returns one on success and zero on allocation error. On Windows, fd is cast to SOCKET.
requirements: Available only when !OPENSSL_NO_SOCK.
ssl must be valid; fd must be valid.

functions.name: SSL_do_handshake
functions.description: Continues or runs the current handshake. Returns 1 if there is no handshake in progress or it completes (or False Start), otherwise <= 0. Pass the result to SSL_get_error. In DTLS, the caller must drive retransmissions/timeouts via DTLSv1_get_timeout and DTLSv1_handle_timeout and remain ready to receive post-handshake messages.
requirements: ssl must be configured as client or server before calling.
For DTLS: after calling, query DTLSv1_get_timeout and call DTLSv1_handle_timeout on expiry; must be ready to process SSL_read for remaining retransmissions and post-handshake processing.
On failure, always use SSL_get_error to decide next action.

functions.name: SSL_connect
functions.description: Configures ssl as a client if not already and performs SSL_do_handshake.
requirements: ssl must be valid and have BIOs/FDs configured.
On non-success, use SSL_get_error to interpret return value.

functions.name: SSL_accept
functions.description: Configures ssl as a server if not already and performs SSL_do_handshake.
requirements: ssl must be valid and have BIOs/FDs configured.
On non-success, use SSL_get_error to interpret return value.

functions.name: SSL_read
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int SSL_read(SSL *ssl, void *buf, int num);
functions.description: Reads up to num bytes into buf, implicitly running pending handshakes and renegotiations when enabled. Returns number of bytes read on success, otherwise <= 0. Use SSL_get_error to determine action. In DTLS 1.3, caller must drive timeouts for final flight and post-handshake messages via DTLSv1_get_timeout/DTLSv1_handle_timeout.
requirements: ssl must be a configured connection with I/O set.
buf must point to valid writable memory of at least num bytes.
On failure or zero, pass return to SSL_get_error. 0 may indicate transport EOF (see TODO in docs).
In DTLS 1.3, after call, manage timers via DTLSv1_get_timeout/DTLSv1_handle_timeout.

functions.name: SSL_peek
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int SSL_peek(SSL *ssl, void *buf, int num);
functions.description: Like SSL_read but does not consume the returned bytes.
requirements: Same as SSL_read; buf must be writable for num bytes.

functions.name: SSL_pending
functions.description: Returns the number of buffered, decrypted bytes available to read in ssl without reading from the transport. In DTLS, may be zero while undecrypted transport data is buffered (see SSL_has_pending).
requirements: ssl must be valid.

functions.name: SSL_has_pending
functions.description: Returns one if ssl has buffered decrypted bytes available or buffered undecrypted transport data; zero otherwise. In DTLS, may be one while SSL_pending is zero.
requirements: ssl must be valid.
Even if one, next SSL_read may still fail or need transport I/O.

functions.name: SSL_write
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int SSL_write(SSL *ssl, const void *buf, int num);
functions.description: Writes up to num bytes from buf, implicitly running pending handshakes. Returns number of bytes written on success, otherwise <= 0. Use SSL_get_error. TLS non-blocking semantics: failed SSL_write commits to data; retries must reuse the same buffer (or prefix), unless SSL_MODE_ACCEPT_MOVING_WRITE_BUFFER is set (contents must remain unchanged). TLS writes are all-or-nothing unless SSL_MODE_ENABLE_PARTIAL_WRITE. In DTLS, these modes do nothing; a single call writes a single record and num must be <= SSL3_RT_MAX_PLAIN_LENGTH.
requirements: ssl must be connected with I/O set.
buf must point to readable memory of at least num bytes.
For TLS non-blocking retries, reuse same buffer (or prefix) unless ACCEPT_MOVING_WRITE_BUFFER mode is set; contents must be unchanged.
In TLS, partial writes only if SSL_MODE_ENABLE_PARTIAL_WRITE is enabled.
In DTLS, num must be <= SSL3_RT_MAX_PLAIN_LENGTH.
On failure or zero, pass to SSL_get_error.

functions.name: SSL_key_update
functions.description: Queues a TLS 1.3 KeyUpdate message to be sent if not already queued. request_type must be SSL_KEY_UPDATE_REQUESTED or SSL_KEY_UPDATE_NOT_REQUESTED. ssl must have completed a TLS >= 1.3 handshake. Returns one on success, zero on error. The message is sent on the next SSL_write; a zero-length write can flush it.
requirements: ssl must have completed a TLS 1.3 (or later) handshake.
request_type must be one of SSL_KEY_UPDATE_REQUESTED or SSL_KEY_UPDATE_NOT_REQUESTED.
Caller must drive a subsequent SSL_write (possibly zero-length) to send the message.

functions.name: SSL_shutdown
functions.description: Shuts down the TLS/DTLS connection. Stage 1: sends close_notify and returns 0 or 1 on success (-1 on failure). 0 means close_notify sent but not received; 1 means peer’s close_notify already received. Stage 2: call again to wait for peer’s close_notify; returns 1 on success, -1 on failure. For errors, use SSL_get_error. DTLS is unordered; second stage is a no-op. Most callers stop after stage 1.
requirements: ssl must be valid and have I/O configured.
On failure, pass return to SSL_get_error.
If quiet shutdown is enabled, SSL_shutdown returns 1 synchronously without sending/receiving close_notify.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_set_quiet_shutdown
functions.description: Enables or disables quiet shutdown on ctx. If enabled, SSL_shutdown will not send or wait for close_notify and returns 1 synchronously.
requirements: ctx must be valid.
Set before calling SSL_shutdown on connections created from ctx for consistent behavior.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_get_quiet_shutdown
functions.description: Returns whether quiet shutdown is enabled for ctx.
requirements: ctx must be valid.

functions.name: SSL_set_quiet_shutdown
functions.description: Enables or disables quiet shutdown on a single ssl. If enabled, SSL_shutdown will not send or wait for close_notify and returns 1 synchronously.
requirements: ssl must be valid.
Overrides context-level setting for this connection.

functions.name: SSL_get_quiet_shutdown
functions.description: Returns whether quiet shutdown is enabled for ssl.
requirements: ssl must be valid.

functions.name: SSL_get_error
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int SSL_get_error(const SSL *ssl, int ret_code);
functions.description: Translates the most recent operation’s return value into an SSL_ERROR_* code, indicating whether the error is fatal or when to retry.
requirements: Call immediately after a failed SSL_* operation with its return value.
ssl must be valid.

functions.name: SSL_error_description
functions.description: Returns a human-readable string description for an SSL_ERROR_* value, or NULL if unrecognized.
requirements: err should be one of the SSL_ERROR_* constants returned by SSL_get_error.

functions.name: SSL_set_mtu
functions.description: Sets the DTLS MTU on ssl to mtu. Returns one on success and zero on failure.
requirements: ssl must be a DTLS connection (SSL_is_dtls(ssl) == 1) for the value to take effect.
mtu must be a positive integer; values too small may be rejected.

functions.name: DTLSv1_set_initial_timeout_duration
functions.description: Sets the initial DTLS handshake timeout duration (default 400ms as per RFC 9147 for real-time protocols).
requirements: ssl must be a DTLS connection.
Call before driving DTLS handshake timers.

functions.name: DTLSv1_get_timeout
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int DTLSv1_get_timeout(const SSL *ssl, struct timeval *out);
functions.description: Queries DTLS timers. If a timer is in progress, sets *out to the time remaining until the first timer expires and returns 1. Otherwise returns 0. Must be re-queried whenever the state machine changes, including after DTLSv1_handle_timeout.
requirements: ssl must be DTLS.
out must be a valid pointer when return is 1.

functions.name: DTLSv1_handle_timeout
functions.description: Handles an expired DTLS timeout. Returns 0 if no timeout had expired, 1 on success, or -1 on error. May write to the transport (retransmits) or update internal state/timers. On -1, SSL_get_error == SSL_ERROR_WANT_WRITE may indicate a non-fatal write BIO error; retry the original operation when writable.
requirements: ssl must be DTLS.
Caller should maintain an external timer compatible with ssl’s internal timers.
