On return -1, check SSL_get_error; on WANT_WRITE, retry original SSL_do_handshake or SSL_read when write BIO is writable.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_set_min_proto_version
functions.description: Sets the minimum allowed TLS/DTLS protocol version on the SSL_CTX. Pass zero to use library default. Returns 1 on success and 0 if version is invalid. Use to restrict protocol versions for all connections created from ctx.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, initialized SSL_CTX.
version may be zero to select the default, otherwise must be a valid protocol version constant (e.g., TLS1_2_VERSION, TLS1_3_VERSION, DTLS1_2_VERSION, etc.).
Call before creating or handshaking SSL connections derived from ctx to ensure consistent behavior.
Return value must be checked; 0 indicates invalid version.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_set_max_proto_version
functions.description: Sets the maximum allowed TLS/DTLS protocol version on the SSL_CTX. Pass zero to use library default. Returns 1 on success and 0 if version is invalid.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX.
version may be zero to select the default, otherwise must be a valid protocol version constant.
Check return value; 0 indicates invalid version.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_get_min_proto_version
functions.description: Returns the current minimum protocol version configured on ctx.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_get_max_proto_version
functions.description: Returns the current maximum protocol version configured on ctx.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX.

functions.name: SSL_set_min_proto_version
functions.description: Sets the minimum allowed protocol version on an individual SSL. Zero selects the default. Returns 1 on success, 0 if version is invalid.
requirements: ssl must be a valid SSL object.
Call before or during configuration and prior to handshake for effect.
version may be zero or a valid protocol version constant.
Check return value for errors.

functions.name: SSL_set_max_proto_version
functions.description: Sets the maximum allowed protocol version on an individual SSL. Zero selects the default. Returns 1 on success, 0 if version is invalid.
requirements: ssl must be a valid SSL object.
Call before handshake to ensure enforcement.
version may be zero or a valid protocol version constant.
Check return value for errors.

functions.name: SSL_get_min_proto_version
functions.description: Returns the minimum protocol version configured on ssl, or 0 if the connection's configuration has been shed.
requirements: ssl must be a valid SSL.
Be aware this can return 0 if configuration shedding was enabled.

functions.name: SSL_get_max_proto_version
functions.description: Returns the maximum protocol version configured on ssl, or 0 if the connection's configuration has been shed.
requirements: ssl must be a valid SSL.
May return 0 after configuration shedding.

functions.name: SSL_version
functions.description: Returns the negotiated TLS or DTLS protocol version in |*_VERSION| form (e.g., TLS1_3_VERSION). Result is undefined before version negotiation completes.
requirements: ssl must be a valid SSL.
Only meaningful after protocol version negotiation.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_set_options
functions.description: Enables the SSL_OP_* options bitmask in ctx. Returns the resulting enabled options bitmask.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX.
options must be a bitwise OR of SSL_OP_* constants.
Callers should use return value to read final bitmask.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_clear_options
functions.description: Disables the given SSL_OP_* options in ctx. Returns the resulting enabled options bitmask.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX.
options must be a bitwise OR of SSL_OP_* constants.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_get_options
functions.description: Returns the bitmask of SSL_OP_* options enabled on ctx.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX.

functions.name: SSL_set_options
functions.description: Enables the SSL_OP_* options on an SSL. Returns the resulting enabled options bitmask.
requirements: ssl must be a valid SSL.
options must be a bitwise OR of SSL_OP_* constants.

functions.name: SSL_clear_options
functions.description: Disables the given SSL_OP_* options on ssl. Returns the resulting enabled options bitmask.
requirements: ssl must be a valid SSL.
options must be a bitwise OR of SSL_OP_* constants.

functions.name: SSL_get_options
functions.description: Returns the bitmask of SSL_OP_* options enabled on ssl.
requirements: ssl must be a valid SSL.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_set_mode
functions.description: Enables the SSL_MODE_* behavior flags (API behavior modes) on ctx. Returns resulting enabled modes.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX.
mode must be a bitwise OR of SSL_MODE_* constants.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_clear_mode
functions.description: Disables the given SSL_MODE_* flags on ctx. Returns resulting enabled modes.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX.
mode must be a bitwise OR of SSL_MODE_* constants.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_get_mode
functions.description: Returns the bitmask of SSL_MODE_* flags enabled on ctx.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX.

functions.name: SSL_set_mode
functions.description: Enables the SSL_MODE_* behavior flags on ssl. Returns resulting enabled modes.
requirements: ssl must be a valid SSL.
mode must be a bitwise OR of SSL_MODE_* constants.

functions.name: SSL_clear_mode
functions.description: Disables the given SSL_MODE_* flags on ssl. Returns resulting enabled modes.
requirements: ssl must be a valid SSL.
mode must be a bitwise OR of SSL_MODE_* constants.

functions.name: SSL_get_mode
functions.description: Returns the bitmask of SSL_MODE_* flags enabled on ssl.
requirements: ssl must be a valid SSL.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_set0_buffer_pool
functions.description: Associates a CRYPTO_BUFFER_POOL with ctx for certificate storage/sharing; the SSL_CTX does not take ownership. Used to share cert buffers across objects to save memory.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX.
pool must outlive ctx and all objects referencing it (SSL, X509, SSL_SESSION, etc.). Do not free pool while in use.
Caller retains ownership; no up-ref is taken.

functions.name: SSL_CREDENTIAL_new_x509
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new empty X.509 SSL_CREDENTIAL, or NULL on error. Configure chain/key/etc. on it, then add to an SSL_CTX/SSL via add1_credential.
requirements: Caller must free the credential with SSL_CREDENTIAL_free when done unless ownership is transferred.
After adding a credential to SSL/SSL_CTX, do not modify it.

functions.name: SSL_CREDENTIAL_up_ref
functions.description: Increments the reference count of cred.
requirements: cred must be non-NULL and valid.
Use with corresponding SSL_CREDENTIAL_free calls to balance references.

functions.name: SSL_CREDENTIAL_free
functions.description: Decrements the reference count of cred and frees it (and its data) when it reaches zero.
requirements: cred may be NULL-safe in practice is not stated; pass valid pointers.
Do not use cred after it has been freed.

functions.name: SSL_CREDENTIAL_set1_private_key
functions.description: Sets cred's private key to key. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: cred must be a valid SSL_CREDENTIAL.
key must be a valid EVP_PKEY matching the credential’s certificate/key type.
Must be called before adding the credential to SSL/SSL_CTX.

functions.name: SSL_CREDENTIAL_set1_signing_algorithm_prefs
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int SSL_CREDENTIAL_set1_signing_algorithm_prefs(SSL_CREDENTIAL *cred, const uint16_t *prefs, size_t num_prefs);
functions.description: Configures the signing algorithm preference list for cred. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error. Not allowed for delegated credentials.
requirements: cred must be valid and not a delegated credential.
prefs points to num_prefs TLS signature algorithm codepoints and must not include SSL_SIGN_RSA_PKCS1_MD5_SHA1.
Call before using the credential.
Return value must be checked.

functions.name: SSL_CREDENTIAL_set1_cert_chain
functions.description: Sets cred's certificate chain (leaf-first) from certs. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: cred must be valid.
certs must point to a list of CRYPTO_BUFFERs (DER-encoded certs) with num_certs >= 0; leaf is first element.
Call before adding the credential to a context/connection.

functions.name: SSL_CREDENTIAL_set1_ocsp_response
functions.description: Sets the stapled OCSP response for cred. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: cred must be valid.
ocsp must be a DER-encoded OCSPResponse carried in a CRYPTO_BUFFER.

functions.name: SSL_CREDENTIAL_set1_certificate_properties
functions.description: Parses a CertificatePropertyList and applies recognized properties (e.g., trust_anchor_identifier) to cred. Returns 1 on success, 0 on parse/apply error.
requirements: cred must be valid.
cert_property_list must be a well-formed CertificatePropertyList per draft-ietf-tls-trust-anchor-ids-00.
Only recognized properties are applied; unrecognized are ignored or cause failure as documented.

functions.name: SSL_CREDENTIAL_set1_signed_cert_timestamp_list
functions.description: Sets the SignedCertificateTimestampList (RFC 6962) for cred. sct_list is the serialized list (u16 length-prefixed list of u16-length-prefixed SCTs). Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: cred must be valid.
sct_list must contain a correctly formatted SignedCertificateTimestampList with one or more SCTs.

functions.name: SSL_CREDENTIAL_set_must_match_issuer
functions.description: Configures whether cred should only be used if the peer requested a matching issuer (certificate_authorities or, with trust anchor ID, trust_anchors). Non-zero enables matching; zero disables (default).
requirements: cred must be valid.
If enabled, the certificate chain must be a correctly ordered certification path and (optionally) have a trust anchor ID configured.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_add1_credential
functions.description: Appends cred to ctx's credential list (earlier entries have higher preference). Returns 1 on success, 0 on error. After adding, modifying cred is an error and may cause inconsistent behavior.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX.
cred must be a fully configured SSL_CREDENTIAL; reference count will be incremented as needed by API semantics.
Do not modify cred after it is added.

functions.name: SSL_add1_credential
functions.description: Appends cred to ssl's credential list (earlier entries preferred). Returns 1 on success, 0 on error. After adding, modifying cred is an error.
requirements: ssl must be a valid SSL.
cred must be fully configured and must not be modified after adding.

functions.name: SSL_certs_clear
functions.description: Removes all credentials configured on ssl and clears the legacy certificate and private key from the connection.
requirements: ssl must be a valid SSL.
Call before handshake to reconfigure certificates safely.

functions.name: SSL_get0_selected_credential
functions.description: Returns the credential selected for the current handshake on ssl, or NULL if no current handshake or not yet at selection point. Intended for use in handshake callbacks to access credential-specific ex_data.
requirements: ssl must be valid.
May be called from handshake-related callbacks (e.g., private key methods).
When using legacy APIs (SSL_use_certificate, etc.), may return an internal credential without ex_data.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_use_certificate
functions.description: Sets the legacy leaf certificate on ctx to x509. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure. If an inconsistent private key is already configured, it is silently dropped.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX.
x509 must be a valid X509.
Prefer to set certificate before private key to avoid silent key drop.

functions.name: SSL_use_certificate
functions.description: Sets the legacy leaf certificate on ssl to x509. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure. If an inconsistent private key is already configured, it is silently dropped.
requirements: ssl must be a valid SSL.
x509 must be a valid X509.
Set certificate before private key for predictable behavior.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_use_PrivateKey
functions.description: Sets the legacy private key on ctx to pkey, replacing any existing key or private key method. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX.
pkey must be a valid EVP_PKEY.
Prefer to set certificate first; otherwise an inconsistent private key may be dropped when certificate is set later.

functions.name: SSL_use_PrivateKey
functions.description: Sets the legacy private key on ssl to pkey, replacing any existing key or private key method. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: ssl must be a valid SSL.
pkey must be a valid EVP_PKEY.
Prefer to set certificate first to avoid silent drop of inconsistent key afterwards.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_set0_chain
functions.description: Sets ctx’s certificate chain (excluding the leaf) to chain. Takes ownership of chain on success and returns 1; returns 0 on failure.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX.
chain must contain intermediates only (no leaf).
Caller must not free chain on success; ownership transfers.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_set1_chain
functions.description: Sets ctx’s certificate chain (excluding the leaf) to chain. Caller retains ownership. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX.
chain must contain intermediates only (no leaf).

functions.name: SSL_set0_chain
functions.description: Sets ssl’s certificate chain (excluding the leaf) to chain. Takes ownership on success and returns 1, otherwise 0.
requirements: ssl must be a valid SSL.
chain must contain intermediates only.

functions.name: SSL_set1_chain
functions.description: Sets ssl’s certificate chain (excluding the leaf) to chain. Caller retains ownership. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: ssl must be a valid SSL.
chain must contain intermediates only.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_add0_chain_cert
functions.description: Appends x509 to ctx’s certificate chain. Takes ownership on success and returns 1; returns 0 on failure.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX.
x509 must be a valid X509; caller must not free it on success.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_add1_chain_cert
functions.description: Appends x509 to ctx’s certificate chain. Caller retains ownership. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX.
x509 must be valid.

functions.name: SSL_add0_chain_cert
functions.description: Appends x509 to ssl’s certificate chain. Takes ownership on success. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: ssl must be a valid SSL.
x509 must be valid; do not free it after success.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_add_extra_chain_cert
functions.description: Alias for SSL_CTX_add0_chain_cert: appends x509 to the chain and takes ownership. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: ctx must be valid.
x509 must be valid; caller transfers ownership on success.

functions.name: SSL_add1_chain_cert
functions.description: Appends x509 to ssl’s certificate chain; caller retains ownership. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: ssl must be valid.
x509 must be valid.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_clear_chain_certs
functions.description: Clears ctx’s configured certificate chain. Returns 1.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_clear_extra_chain_certs
functions.description: Alias for SSL_CTX_clear_chain_certs. Returns 1.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX.

functions.name: SSL_clear_chain_certs
functions.description: Clears ssl’s configured certificate chain. Returns 1.
requirements: ssl must be a valid SSL.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_set_cert_cb
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT void SSL_CTX_set_cert_cb(SSL_CTX *ctx, int (*cb)(SSL *ssl, void *arg), void *arg);
functions.description: Sets a certificate selection callback for all SSLs created from ctx. Callback returns 1 on success, 0 on internal error, negative to pause (SSL_ERROR_WANT_X509_LOOKUP). On client, callback may query server’s request via SSL_get0_certificate_types/SSL_get_client_CA_list. On server, runs after extensions are processed but before resumption decision.
requirements: cb must follow return semantics: 1 success, 0 internal error, <0 pause/failure.
If pausing, caller must later retry the handshake and call SSL_get_error to drive state.
Callback must not use stale SSL_CLIENT_HELLO beyond its lifetime.

functions.name: SSL_set_cert_cb
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT void SSL_set_cert_cb(SSL *ssl, int (*cb)(SSL *ssl, void *arg), void *arg);
functions.description: Sets a certificate selection callback on a single SSL. Semantics as SSL_CTX_set_cert_cb.
requirements: Same as SSL_CTX_set_cert_cb, but per-connection.

functions.name: SSL_get0_certificate_types
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT size_t SSL_get0_certificate_types(const SSL *ssl, const uint8_t **out_types);
functions.description: For a client in the certificate callback or paused handshake, returns the server’s requested client certificate types array and length. Always empty in TLS 1.3.
requirements: Only defined during the cert selection/client-cert callbacks or when handshake is paused due to them.
ssl must be a client in the appropriate state.

functions.name: SSL_get0_peer_verify_algorithms
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT size_t SSL_get0_peer_verify_algorithms(const SSL *ssl, const uint16_t **out_sigalgs);
functions.description: Returns the signature algorithms the peer can verify, as an array and length. Only sent starting TLS 1.2; may be empty if not sent.
requirements: Only defined during certificate selection/client cert callbacks or when handshake is paused due to them.

functions.name: SSL_get0_peer_delegation_algorithms
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT size_t SSL_get0_peer_delegation_algorithms(const SSL *ssl, const uint16_t **out_sigalgs);
functions.description: Returns signature algorithms the peer is willing to use with delegated credentials; empty if not sent.
requirements: Only defined during the above-mentioned callbacks or paused state.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_get0_certificate
functions.description: Returns the legacy leaf certificate on ctx (non-owning).
requirements: ctx must be valid.
Returned pointer is owned by ctx; do not free.

functions.name: SSL_get_certificate
functions.description: Returns the legacy leaf certificate on ssl (non-owning).
requirements: ssl must be valid.
Returned pointer is owned by ssl; do not free.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_get0_privatekey
functions.description: Returns the legacy private key configured on ctx (non-owning).
requirements: ctx must be valid.
Do not free the returned pointer.

functions.name: SSL_get_privatekey
functions.description: Returns the legacy private key configured on ssl (non-owning).
requirements: ssl must be valid.
Do not free the returned pointer.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_get0_chain_certs
functions.description: Sets *out_chain to ctx’s certificate chain (non-owning) and returns 1.
requirements: ctx must be valid.
out_chain must be non-NULL.
Returned stack and contents are owned by ctx; do not free.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_get_extra_chain_certs
functions.description: Alias of SSL_CTX_get0_chain_certs: sets *out_chain to ctx’s chain and returns 1.
requirements: ctx must be valid.
out_chain must be non-NULL.

functions.name: SSL_get0_chain_certs
functions.description: Sets *out_chain to ssl’s certificate chain (non-owning) and returns 1.
requirements: ssl must be valid.
out_chain must be non-NULL.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_set_signed_cert_timestamp_list
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int SSL_CTX_set_signed_cert_timestamp_list(SSL_CTX *ctx, const uint8_t *list, size_t list_len);
functions.description: Configures the SCT list (SignedCertificateTimestampList as per RFC 6962) to send to clients that request it on all SSLs from ctx. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error. Caller retains ownership.
requirements: ctx must be valid.
list must be correctly formatted SCT list; caller retains ownership.

functions.name: SSL_set_signed_cert_timestamp_list
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int SSL_set_signed_cert_timestamp_list(SSL *ctx, const uint8_t *list, size_t list_len);
functions.description: Configures the SCT list to send for a single SSL. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error. Caller retains ownership.
requirements: ssl must be valid.
list must be a correctly formatted SCT list.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_set_ocsp_response
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int SSL_CTX_set_ocsp_response(SSL_CTX *ctx, const uint8_t *response, size_t response_len);
functions.description: Sets the stapled OCSP response to send to clients that request it for all SSLs from ctx. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error. Caller retains ownership.
requirements: ctx must be valid.
response must be a DER-encoded OCSPResponse.
Caller retains ownership.

functions.name: SSL_set_ocsp_response
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int SSL_set_ocsp_response(SSL *ssl, const uint8_t *response, size_t response_len);
functions.description: Sets the stapled OCSP response for a single SSL. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error. Caller retains ownership.
requirements: ssl must be valid.
response must be DER-encoded OCSPResponse.

functions.name: SSL_get_signature_algorithm_name
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT const char *SSL_get_signature_algorithm_name(uint16_t sigalg, int include_curve);
functions.description: Returns a human-readable name for a TLS signature algorithm codepoint, or NULL if unknown. include_curve includes the curve for ECDSA (TLS 1.3 style) when non-zero.
requirements: sigalg must be a TLS signature algorithm codepoint.

functions.name: SSL_get_all_signature_algorithm_names
functions.description: Writes up to max_out possible signature algorithm name strings to out and returns the total number of possible names. Intended for initializing tables; order and membership are not a support statement.
requirements: out may be NULL when max_out is zero to size the output.
Caller must provide storage for at least max_out pointers.

functions.name: SSL_get_signature_algorithm_key_type
functions.description: Returns the EVP_PKEY_* key type for the signature algorithm, or EVP_PKEY_NONE if unknown.
requirements: sigalg is a TLS signature algorithm codepoint.

functions.name: SSL_get_signature_algorithm_digest
functions.description: Returns the digest function used by the signature algorithm, or NULL if the sigalg has no prehash (e.g., Ed25519) or is unknown.
requirements: sigalg is a TLS signature algorithm codepoint.
Returned EVP_MD is owned by the library; do not free.

functions.name: SSL_is_signature_algorithm_rsa_pss
functions.description: Returns 1 if sigalg is an RSA-PSS signature algorithm, 0 otherwise.
requirements: sigalg is a TLS signature algorithm codepoint.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_set_signing_algorithm_prefs
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int SSL_CTX_set_signing_algorithm_prefs(SSL_CTX *ctx, const uint16_t *prefs, size_t num_prefs);
functions.description: Sets TLS 1.2+ signing algorithm preference list (for the local private key) on ctx. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error. Not used in TLS 1.0/1.1. prefs must not include SSL_SIGN_RSA_PKCS1_MD5_SHA1.
requirements: ctx must be valid.
prefs must be an array of TLS signature algorithm codepoints; must not contain SSL_SIGN_RSA_PKCS1_MD5_SHA1.
Callers should set min version to TLS 1.2 or higher to disable legacy hash usage, if desired.

functions.name: SSL_set_signing_algorithm_prefs
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int SSL_set_signing_algorithm_prefs(SSL *ssl, const uint16_t *prefs, size_t num_prefs);
functions.description: Sets TLS 1.2+ signing algorithm preference list (for the local private key) on a single SSL. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error. Not used in TLS 1.0/1.1. Do not include SSL_SIGN_RSA_PKCS1_MD5_SHA1.
requirements: ssl must be valid.
prefs as above; must not include SSL_SIGN_RSA_PKCS1_MD5_SHA1.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_set_chain_and_key
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int SSL_CTX_set_chain_and_key(SSL_CTX *ctx, CRYPTO_BUFFER *const *certs, size_t num_certs, EVP_PKEY *privkey, const SSL_PRIVATE_KEY_METHOD *privkey_method);
functions.description: Convenience to set the certificate chain (CRYPTO_BUFFERs, leaf-first) and private key or custom private key method on ctx. Exactly one of privkey or privkey_method must be non-NULL. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: ctx must be valid.
certs must be an array of CRYPTO_BUFFERs (DER certs) with num_certs>=1 (leaf included).
Exactly one of privkey and privkey_method must be non-NULL.
References are added as needed; caller retains ownership.

functions.name: SSL_set_chain_and_key
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int SSL_set_chain_and_key(SSL *ssl, CRYPTO_BUFFER *const *certs, size_t num_certs, EVP_PKEY *privkey, const SSL_PRIVATE_KEY_METHOD *privkey_method);
functions.description: Like SSL_CTX_set_chain_and_key, but applies to a single SSL. Exactly one of privkey or privkey_method must be non-NULL. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: ssl must be valid.
Exactly one of privkey and privkey_method must be non-NULL.
certs list must be leaf-first CRYPTO_BUFFERs.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_get0_chain
functions.description: Returns the CRYPTO_BUFFER chain set by SSL_CTX_set_chain_and_key (non-owning), or NULL if none set or chain was configured by non-CRYPTO_BUFFER APIs.
requirements: ctx must be valid.
Do not mix CRYPTO_BUFFER-based and non-CRYPTO_BUFFER-based chain configuration with this query.

functions.name: SSL_get0_chain
functions.description: Returns the CRYPTO_BUFFER chain for ssl set by SSL_set_chain_and_key, unless discarded (e.g., after handshake). May return NULL if none set or configuration has been cleared after completion.
requirements: ssl must be valid.
Do not mix CRYPTO_BUFFER and non-CRYPTO_BUFFER chain APIs when using this query.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_use_RSAPrivateKey
functions.description: Sets ctx’s legacy private key from an RSA*; returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: ctx must be valid.
rsa must be a valid RSA key compatible with configured certificate if already set.

functions.name: SSL_use_RSAPrivateKey
functions.description: Sets ssl’s legacy private key from an RSA*; returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: ssl must be valid.
rsa must be valid and compatible with configured certificate if already set.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_use_certificate_ASN1
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int SSL_CTX_use_certificate_ASN1(SSL_CTX *ctx, size_t der_len, const uint8_t *der);
functions.description: Load a DER-encoded X.509 leaf certificate into an SSL context. On success, ctx's legacy leaf certificate becomes the provided certificate. If a previously configured private key is inconsistent with the new certificate, it will be silently dropped. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, initialized SSL_CTX* for TLS/DTLS.
der must point to a DER-encoded certificate of length der_len.
Caller retains ownership of der buffer; it is not freed by the library.
If a private key was configured before the certificate and is inconsistent, it will be dropped without error.

functions.name: SSL_use_certificate_ASN1
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int SSL_use_certificate_ASN1(SSL *ssl, const uint8_t *der, size_t der_len);
functions.description: Load a DER-encoded X.509 leaf certificate into a single SSL connection. On success, ssl's legacy leaf certificate becomes the provided certificate. If a previously configured private key is inconsistent with the new certificate, it will be silently dropped. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: ssl must be a valid SSL* created from an SSL_CTX.
der must point to a DER-encoded certificate of length der_len.
Caller retains ownership of der buffer.
If a private key was configured before the certificate and is inconsistent, it will be dropped without error.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_use_PrivateKey_ASN1
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int SSL_CTX_use_PrivateKey_ASN1(int pk, SSL_CTX *ctx, const uint8_t *der, size_t der_len);
functions.description: Load a DER-encoded private key into an SSL context’s legacy credential. Replaces any previously configured private key or custom private key method. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure. The pk integer is an OpenSSL-legacy type selector (kept for compatibility).
requirements: pk is a legacy type identifier; value is not interpreted by BoringSSL beyond compatibility.
ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX*.
der must contain a DER-encoded private key of length der_len supported by the library (e.g., RSA, EC).
Caller retains ownership of der.
Any previously configured private key or SSL_PRIVATE_KEY_METHOD on ctx is replaced.

functions.name: SSL_use_PrivateKey_ASN1
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int SSL_use_PrivateKey_ASN1(int type, SSL *ssl, const uint8_t *der, size_t der_len);
functions.description: Load a DER-encoded private key into a single SSL connection’s legacy credential. Replaces any previously configured private key or custom private key method. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure. The type integer is a legacy selector for compatibility.
requirements: ssl must be a valid SSL*.
der must contain a DER-encoded private key of length der_len supported by the library.
Caller retains ownership of der.
Any previously configured private key or SSL_PRIVATE_KEY_METHOD on ssl is replaced.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_use_RSAPrivateKey_ASN1
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int SSL_CTX_use_RSAPrivateKey_ASN1(SSL_CTX *ctx, const uint8_t *der, size_t der_len);
functions.description: Load a DER-encoded RSA private key into an SSL context’s legacy credential. Replaces any previously configured private key or custom private key method. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: ctx must be a valid SSL_CTX*.
der must contain a DER-encoded RSA private key of length der_len.
Caller retains ownership of der.
Any previously configured private key or SSL_PRIVATE_KEY_METHOD on ctx is replaced.

functions.name: SSL_use_RSAPrivateKey_ASN1
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int SSL_use_RSAPrivateKey_ASN1(SSL *ssl, const uint8_t *der, size_t der_len);
functions.description: Load a DER-encoded RSA private key into a single SSL connection’s legacy credential. Replaces any previously configured private key or custom private key method. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: ssl must be a valid SSL*.
der must contain a DER-encoded RSA private key of length der_len.
Caller retains ownership of der.
Any previously configured private key or SSL_PRIVATE_KEY_METHOD on ssl is replaced.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_use_RSAPrivateKey_file
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int SSL_CTX_use_RSAPrivateKey_file(SSL_CTX *ctx, const char *file, int type);
functions.description: Read an RSA private key from a file and configure it on an SSL context’s legacy credential. The file is interpreted as PEM if type is SSL_FILETYPE_PEM or DER if SSL_FILETYPE_ASN1. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: ctx must be valid.
file must be a path to an accessible file containing an RSA private key.
type must be SSL_FILETYPE_PEM or SSL_FILETYPE_ASN1.
Any previously configured private key or SSL_PRIVATE_KEY_METHOD on ctx is replaced.
If PEM is encrypted, ctx’s default password callback/userdata may be used (see SSL_CTX_set_default_passwd_cb).

functions.name: SSL_use_RSAPrivateKey_file
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int SSL_use_RSAPrivateKey_file(SSL *ssl, const char *file, int type);
functions.description: Read an RSA private key from a file and configure it on a single SSL connection’s legacy credential. The file is PEM if type is SSL_FILETYPE_PEM, DER if SSL_FILETYPE_ASN1. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: ssl must be valid.
file must point to an accessible file containing an RSA private key.
type must be SSL_FILETYPE_PEM or SSL_FILETYPE_ASN1.
Any previously configured private key or SSL_PRIVATE_KEY_METHOD on ssl is replaced.
If PEM is encrypted, the parent SSL_CTX password callback may be used.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_use_certificate_file
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int SSL_CTX_use_certificate_file(SSL_CTX *ctx, const char *file, int type);
functions.description: Load a leaf certificate from file into an SSL context’s legacy credential. The file is PEM if type is SSL_FILETYPE_PEM or DER if SSL_FILETYPE_ASN1. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure. If an existing private key is inconsistent with the certificate, it is silently dropped.
requirements: ctx must be valid.
file must be accessible and contain exactly one certificate (leaf).
type must be SSL_FILETYPE_PEM or SSL_FILETYPE_ASN1.
If a private key inconsistent with the new certificate was configured, it will be dropped without error.

functions.name: SSL_use_certificate_file
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int SSL_use_certificate_file(SSL *ssl, const char *file, int type);
functions.description: Load a leaf certificate from file into a single SSL connection’s legacy credential. The file is PEM if type is SSL_FILETYPE_PEM or DER if SSL_FILETYPE_ASN1. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure. Inconsistent configured private keys are silently dropped.
requirements: ssl must be valid.
file must be accessible and contain exactly one certificate (leaf).
type must be SSL_FILETYPE_PEM or SSL_FILETYPE_ASN1.
If a private key inconsistent with the new certificate was configured, it will be dropped.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_use_PrivateKey_file
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int SSL_CTX_use_PrivateKey_file(SSL_CTX *ctx, const char *file, int type);
functions.description: Load a private key from file (PEM or DER) into an SSL context’s legacy credential. Replaces any previously configured private key or custom private key method. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: ctx must be valid.
file must be accessible and contain a supported private key.
type must be SSL_FILETYPE_PEM or SSL_FILETYPE_ASN1.
If PEM is encrypted, ctx’s default password callback may be used.
Any previously configured private key or SSL_PRIVATE_KEY_METHOD on ctx is replaced.

functions.name: SSL_use_PrivateKey_file
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int SSL_use_PrivateKey_file(SSL *ssl, const char *file, int type);
functions.description: Load a private key from file (PEM or DER) into a single SSL connection’s legacy credential. Replaces any previously configured private key or custom private key method. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: ssl must be valid.
file must be accessible and contain a supported private key.
type must be SSL_FILETYPE_PEM or SSL_FILETYPE_ASN1.
If PEM is encrypted, the parent SSL_CTX password callback may be used.
Any previously configured private key or SSL_PRIVATE_KEY_METHOD on ssl is replaced.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_use_certificate_chain_file
functions.description: Load a PEM-encoded leaf certificate, optionally followed by its chain, into an SSL context’s legacy credential, and configure the chain to be sent to peers. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure. WARNING: if the input contains TRUSTED CERTIFICATE PEM blocks, auxiliary properties are parsed and can be attacker-influenced if untrusted input is used.
requirements: ctx must be valid.
file must be accessible and contain a PEM leaf certificate optionally followed by intermediates.
Caller retains ownership of file path string.
Do not pass untrusted input containing TRUSTED CERTIFICATE blocks due to auxiliary properties parsing (see d2i_X509_AUX).

functions.name: SSL_CTX_set_default_passwd_cb
functions.description: Set the default password callback on an SSL_CTX for PEM-based convenience functions like SSL_CTX_use_*_file. Used when reading encrypted PEM keys. No return value.
requirements: ctx must be valid.
cb may be NULL to clear the callback.
Callback must conform to pem_password_cb semantics (write password into supplied buffer).

functions.name: SSL_CTX_get_default_passwd_cb
functions.description: Get the default password callback currently configured on the SSL_CTX. Returns the function pointer or NULL if none.
requirements: ctx must be valid.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_set_default_passwd_cb_userdata
functions.description: Set the userdata pointer that will be passed to the default PEM password callback for this SSL_CTX.
requirements: ctx must be valid.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_get_default_passwd_cb_userdata
functions.description: Get the userdata pointer configured for the default PEM password callback on this SSL_CTX. Returns the pointer (possibly NULL).
requirements: ctx must be valid.

functions.name: SSL_set_private_key_method
functions.description: Install a custom private key method on a single SSL object so that signing/decrypt operations are offloaded to user-defined callbacks (possibly asynchronous). key_method must remain valid for the lifetime of ssl.
requirements: ssl must be valid.
key_method must point to a valid, long-lived SSL_PRIVATE_KEY_METHOD vtable with non-NULL function pointers as needed.
If using RSA or ECDSA keys, configure signing algorithm preferences with SSL_set_signing_algorithm_prefs to avoid selecting unsupported algorithms.
Do not free key_method while ssl might use it.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_set_private_key_method
functions.description: Install a custom private key method on an SSL_CTX so all connections inherit user-defined private key hooks. key_method must remain valid for the lifetime of ctx.
requirements: ctx must be valid.
key_method must remain valid for lifetime of ctx and any derived SSLs.
If using RSA or ECDSA keys, configure algorithm preferences with SSL_CTX_set_signing_algorithm_prefs.

functions.name: SSL_CREDENTIAL_set_private_key_method
functions.description: Install a custom private key method on a specific SSL_CREDENTIAL. Returns 1 on success, 0 if cred does not use private keys. key_method must remain valid for the lifetime of cred. Use SSL_get0_selected_credential inside callbacks to find the active credential and any ex_data.
requirements: cred must be a valid SSL_CREDENTIAL* that supports private keys (X.509 or delegated cred as applicable).
key_method must remain valid for cred’s lifetime.
If using RSA or ECDSA keys, configure preferences via SSL_CREDENTIAL_set1_signing_algorithm_prefs. Not required for delegated credentials because they already constrain the algorithm.
Functions in key_method receive SSL*, not cred. Use SSL_get0_selected_credential + SSL_CREDENTIAL_get_ex_data to lookup per-credential state.

functions.name: SSL_can_release_private_key
functions.description: Return 1 if ssl will no longer call into the configured private key (e.g., after handshake), allowing the application to release private key-related state. Returns 0 otherwise. Note this assumes the application will not reuse the SSL via SSL_clear.
requirements: ssl must be valid.
Only safe if the application does not reuse the SSL via SSL_clear; otherwise the library may still need the private key later.

functions.name: OPENSSL_sk_new
functions.description: Creates a new, empty, type-erased stack (array of void*). If comp is non-NULL, it is the comparison function used for sorting and searching; it uses the type-erased qsort-style adapter signature documented here. Returns a new OPENSSL_STACK or NULL on allocation failure. Purpose: low-level implementation for typed sk_FOO_new. Usage: usually invoked via the typed wrapper; direct callers must pass a comparator matching the element type through the type-erased signature.
requirements: comp may be NULL (inferred from typed wrapper docs)
If provided, comp must be a function compatible with OPENSSL_sk_cmp_func: int (*)(const void *const *a, const void *const *b), and must compare pointers to elements of the actual stored type
On allocation failure, the function returns NULL and no stack is created (caller must check for NULL)

functions.name: OPENSSL_sk_new_null
functions.description: Creates a new, empty, type-erased stack without a comparison function. Returns a new OPENSSL_STACK or NULL on allocation failure. Purpose: low-level implementation for typed sk_FOO_new_null.
requirements: Returns NULL on allocation failure; caller must check the return value before use

functions.name: OPENSSL_sk_num
functions.description: Returns the number of elements in sk. Purpose: query size. Usage: safe on empty stacks. In the typed wrappers, a NULL stack is treated as empty and returns 0; behavior here matches the wrappers (inferred from typed documentation).
requirements: sk may be NULL; it is treated as an empty list and 0 is returned (inferred from typed wrapper docs)
The return value fits in int for typed APIs, but this function returns size_t

functions.name: OPENSSL_sk_zero
functions.description: Resets sk to the empty state without freeing individual elements (shallow clear). Purpose: clear container while keeping external ownership of elements (if any).
requirements: sk must be a valid stack pointer (non-NULL)
Elements are not freed; caller must manage element lifetimes if the stack owned them

functions.name: OPENSSL_sk_value
functions.description: Returns the i-th element pointer from sk, or NULL if i is out of range. In typed wrappers, a NULL stack is treated as empty and returns NULL; behavior here matches (inferred).
requirements: If sk is NULL, it is treated as empty and NULL is returned (inferred from typed wrapper docs)
i must be less than the current number of elements to obtain a non-NULL result

functions.name: OPENSSL_sk_set
functions.description: Replaces the element at index i in sk with p and returns p. Returns NULL if i is out of range. Purpose: overwrite an existing entry without changing size.
requirements: sk must be non-NULL and point to a valid stack
i must be in range [0, OPENSSL_sk_num(sk)-1] to succeed; otherwise NULL is returned
p is stored as-is (void*); caller must ensure it points to the correct element type for subsequent use

functions.name: OPENSSL_sk_free
functions.description: Frees the stack structure sk but does not free any elements stored within it. Purpose: deallocate container only. Use OPENSSL_sk_pop_free_ex to also free elements.
requirements: Safe to pass a stack that has been emptied with OPENSSL_sk_zero; elements remain the caller’s responsibility
Do not use sk after calling this function
Does not free element pointers; callers must free elements separately if needed

functions.name: OPENSSL_sk_pop_free_ex
functions.signature: void OPENSSL_sk_pop_free_ex(OPENSSL_STACK *sk, OPENSSL_sk_call_free_func call_free_func, OPENSSL_sk_free_func free_func);
functions.description: Calls free_func (via the adapter call_free_func) on each element in sk, then frees the stack itself. Purpose: deallocate both elements and container when using the type-erased API. Usage: the typed wrappers supply a matching adapter; raw callers must pass the correct adapter for their element type.
requirements: sk may be NULL; in that case no elements are freed and no crash should occur (typical container-free semantics; inferred from usage)
call_free_func must be the adapter that invokes free_func with the correct element type; passing a mismatched adapter leads to undefined behavior
free_func must accept the true element pointer type (i.e., void (*)(T*)) corresponding to the actual elements stored
Elements’ destructors must tolerate being called exactly once; do not reuse freed elements
After return, sk must not be used

functions.name: OPENSSL_sk_insert
functions.description: Inserts element pointer p at index where, shifting existing elements as needed. Returns the new length of the stack on success, or 0 on error (e.g., allocation failure or invalid index). Purpose: positional insertion.
requirements: sk must be a valid, non-NULL stack
where should be in [0, OPENSSL_sk_num(sk)] (inferred from typed wrapper docs); out-of-range may cause failure
On allocation failure or invalid arguments, returns 0; caller must check the return value
p is stored as-is; caller must ensure it matches the expected element type

functions.name: OPENSSL_sk_delete
functions.description: Removes and returns the element at index where, shifting remaining elements down. Returns NULL if where is out of range. Purpose: remove by index without freeing the element.
requirements: sk must be a valid, non-NULL stack
where must be in [0, OPENSSL_sk_num(sk)-1] to succeed; otherwise NULL is returned
The returned pointer is not freed; caller assumes ownership or must manage it

functions.name: OPENSSL_sk_delete_ptr
functions.description: Removes, at most, one instance of p from sk based on pointer equality. Returns p if found and removed, otherwise returns NULL. Purpose: remove by pointer identity without using a comparator.
requirements: sk must be a valid, non-NULL stack
Comparison is by pointer equality, not by comparator
If found, ownership of the removed element is transferred to the caller

functions.name: OPENSSL_sk_delete_if
functions.signature: void OPENSSL_sk_delete_if(OPENSSL_STACK *sk, OPENSSL_sk_call_delete_if_func call_func, OPENSSL_sk_delete_if_func func, void *data);
functions.description: Iterates over sk and calls func (via adapter call_func) for each element; removes elements for which func returns 1 (non-zero). Removed pointers are not freed by this function. Purpose: conditional removal with a predicate.
requirements: sk must be a valid, non-NULL stack
call_func must adapt func to the actual element type; mismatched adapters cause undefined behavior
func must have signature compatible with OPENSSL_sk_delete_if_func: int (*)(void *obj, void *data); it should return 1 to remove, 0 to keep
Removed elements are not freed; if the stack owns its contents, func should free the element before returning 1 (as noted in typed docs; inferred)

functions.name: OPENSSL_sk_find
functions.signature: int OPENSSL_sk_find(const OPENSSL_STACK *sk, size_t *out_index, const void *p, OPENSSL_sk_call_cmp_func call_cmp_func);
functions.description: Searches for an element equal to p in sk. If sk has a comparison function set, equality is determined by that comparator; otherwise pointer equality is used. If the stack is marked sorted, a binary search is used; otherwise linear search. On success, writes the index to out_index (if non-NULL) and returns 1; returns 0 if not found or if sk is NULL. Purpose: locate element and optionally obtain index. Notes: follows the typed wrappers’ documented behavior; does not implicitly sort (inferred).
requirements: sk may be NULL; treated as empty and returns 0 (inferred from typed wrapper docs)
call_cmp_func must adapt the comparator to the element type used in sk; mismatched adapters cause undefined behavior
If a comparator is not set on sk, comparison falls back to pointer equality (inferred)
If out_index is non-NULL and an element is found, the index is written

functions.name: OPENSSL_sk_shift
functions.description: Removes and returns the first element in sk, or NULL if sk is empty. Purpose: queue-like pop-front.
requirements: sk must be a valid, non-NULL stack
The returned pointer is not freed; caller assumes ownership or must manage it

functions.name: OPENSSL_sk_push
functions.description: Appends element pointer p to the end of sk. Returns the new length on success, or 0 on allocation failure. Purpose: push-back.
requirements: sk must be a valid, non-NULL stack
On allocation failure, returns 0; caller must check the return value
p is stored as-is; caller must ensure correct element type

functions.name: OPENSSL_sk_pop
functions.description: Removes and returns the last element in sk, or NULL if sk is empty. Purpose: stack-like pop-back.
requirements: sk must be a valid, non-NULL stack
The returned pointer is not freed; caller assumes ownership or must manage it

functions.name: OPENSSL_sk_dup
functions.description: Creates and returns a shallow copy of sk (duplicates the container and copies element pointers). Returns NULL on error. Purpose: duplicate without cloning elements; use OPENSSL_sk_deep_copy to copy elements too.
requirements: sk may be NULL; behavior is to duplicate an empty stack or return a valid empty duplicate (typical semantics; inferred)
On allocation failure, returns NULL; caller must check for NULL
Elements are not copied; both stacks will point to the same element pointers; caller must manage ownership accordingly to avoid double-free

functions.name: OPENSSL_sk_sort
functions.description: Sorts the elements of sk into ascending order using the comparator set on the stack, invoked via call_cmp_func. Sorting an already sorted stack is a no-op (tracked by a sorted flag). Purpose: in-place sort and mark as sorted.
requirements: sk must be a valid, non-NULL stack
A comparator must be set (typically via OPENSSL_sk_set_cmp_func) and call_cmp_func must correctly adapt it to the element type; passing a mismatched adapter leads to undefined behavior
If no comparator is set, behavior is implementation-defined; do not call sort without a comparator (inferred caution)

functions.name: OPENSSL_sk_is_sorted
functions.description: Returns 1 if sk is known to be sorted, 0 otherwise. Purpose: query the internal sorted flag; does not verify ordering.
requirements: sk must be a valid pointer (may be NULL only if the implementation treats NULL as empty; behavior not explicitly stated)

functions.name: OPENSSL_sk_set_cmp_func
functions.description: Sets the comparison function used by sk and returns the previous comparator. Purpose: configure comparator for sorting and searching.
requirements: sk must be a valid, non-NULL stack
comp may be NULL to clear the comparator (inferred from typed wrapper docs)
The comparator must have signature OPENSSL_sk_cmp_func and compare pointers to the actual element type stored

functions.name: OPENSSL_sk_deep_copy
functions.signature: OPENSSL_STACK *OPENSSL_sk_deep_copy(const OPENSSL_STACK *sk, OPENSSL_sk_call_copy_func call_copy_func, OPENSSL_sk_copy_func copy_func, OPENSSL_sk_call_free_func call_free_func, OPENSSL_sk_free_func free_func);
functions.description: Creates a deep copy of sk: duplicates the container and, for each non-NULL element, calls copy_func via call_copy_func to copy the element. On any error during copying, calls free_func via call_free_func on any copies already made, frees the new container, and returns NULL. Purpose: clone both the stack and its elements using type-erased callbacks.
requirements: sk may be NULL; behavior is to return an empty deep copy (inferred) or NULL on allocation failure
call_copy_func must adapt copy_func to the actual element type; mismatched adapters lead to undefined behavior
copy_func must have signature compatible with OPENSSL_sk_copy_func: void *(*)(const void *); it should return a newly allocated copy or NULL on error
call_free_func must adapt free_func to the actual element type
free_func must properly free elements produced by copy_func; it may be called on partial results if an error occurs
On success, returns a new stack owning copies of elements; caller must free it appropriately

functions.name: sk_new_null
functions.description: Deprecated alias of OPENSSL_sk_new_null. Creates a new empty stack, or returns NULL on allocation failure.
requirements: Deprecated: prefer OPENSSL_sk_new_null
Caller must check for NULL on allocation failure

functions.name: sk_num
functions.description: Deprecated alias of OPENSSL_sk_num. Returns the number of elements in sk. In typed wrappers, NULL is treated as empty and returns 0 (inferred).
requirements: Deprecated: prefer OPENSSL_sk_num
sk may be NULL and is treated as empty (inferred from typed docs)

functions.name: sk_value
functions.description: Deprecated alias of OPENSSL_sk_value. Returns the element at index i, or NULL if out of range (or if sk is NULL; inferred).
requirements: Deprecated: prefer OPENSSL_sk_value
i must be less than the number of elements to get a non-NULL result

functions.name: sk_free
functions.description: Deprecated alias of OPENSSL_sk_free. Frees only the stack container, not the elements.
requirements: Deprecated: prefer OPENSSL_sk_free
Do not use sk after calling this function
Elements are not freed; caller must manage element lifetimes

functions.name: sk_push
functions.description: Deprecated alias of OPENSSL_sk_push. Appends element p; returns new length on success or 0 on allocation failure.
requirements: Deprecated: prefer OPENSSL_sk_push
Caller must check for return value 0 indicating failure

functions.name: sk_pop
functions.description: Deprecated alias of OPENSSL_sk_pop. Removes and returns the last element, or NULL if empty.
requirements: Deprecated: prefer OPENSSL_sk_pop

functions.name: sk_pop_free_ex
functions.signature: OPENSSL_DEPRECATED void sk_pop_free_ex(OPENSSL_STACK *sk, OPENSSL_sk_call_free_func call_free_func, OPENSSL_sk_free_func free_func);
functions.description: Deprecated alias of OPENSSL_sk_pop_free_ex. Frees each element via free_func (through call_free_func) and then frees the stack.
requirements: Deprecated: prefer OPENSSL_sk_pop_free_ex
call_free_func must correctly adapt free_func to the element type
free_func must free the actual element type
After return, sk must not be used

functions.name: sk_pop_free
functions.description: Deprecated. Behaves like OPENSSL_sk_pop_free_ex but performs an invalid function pointer cast internally; exists for compatibility with legacy callers. Prefer bssl::UniquePtr or OPENSSL_sk_pop_free_ex.
requirements: Deprecated: do not introduce new uses
free_func must free the actual element type T* stored in the stack
Because of the internal invalid cast noted in comments, using mismatched free_func types can cause undefined behavior; ensure free_func matches the true element type

functions.name: TRUST_TOKEN_experiment_v1
functions.description: Returns a TRUST_TOKEN_METHOD describing the experimental Trust Tokens protocol using PMBTokens and P-384. Use the returned method when creating clients/issuers and generating keys for this protocol variant.
requirements: None beyond standard pointer validity for the returned value.
Use the returned method consistently with key generation and client/issuer contexts targeting this protocol.

functions.name: TRUST_TOKEN_experiment_v2_voprf
functions.description: Returns a TRUST_TOKEN_METHOD for the experimental Trust Tokens protocol using VOPRFs and P-384 with up to 6 keys, without RR verification.
requirements: None beyond standard pointer validity for the returned value.
Use the returned method consistently with key generation and client/issuer contexts targeting this protocol.

functions.name: TRUST_TOKEN_experiment_v2_pmb
functions.description: Returns a TRUST_TOKEN_METHOD for the experimental Trust Tokens protocol using PMBTokens and P-384 with up to 3 keys, without RR verification.
requirements: None beyond standard pointer validity for the returned value.
Use the returned method consistently with key generation and client/issuer contexts targeting this protocol.

functions.name: TRUST_TOKEN_pst_v1_voprf
functions.description: Returns a TRUST_TOKEN_METHOD for PST v1 Trust Tokens using VOPRFs and P-384 with up to 6 keys, without RR verification.
requirements: None beyond standard pointer validity for the returned value.
Use the returned method consistently with key generation and client/issuer contexts targeting this protocol.

functions.name: TRUST_TOKEN_pst_v1_pmb
functions.description: Returns a TRUST_TOKEN_METHOD for PST v1 Trust Tokens using PMBTokens and P-384 with up to 3 keys, without RR verification.
requirements: None beyond standard pointer validity for the returned value.
Use the returned method consistently with key generation and client/issuer contexts targeting this protocol.

functions.name: TRUST_TOKEN_new
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new TRUST_TOKEN containing the provided token bytes (issuer: token itself; client: token plus signature). Returns NULL on allocation failure.
requirements: data may be NULL only if len is zero (inferred typical C convention; exact behavior for NULL data not otherwise specified).
Caller takes ownership of the returned TRUST_TOKEN* and must free it with TRUST_TOKEN_free.

functions.name: TRUST_TOKEN_free
functions.description: Frees a TRUST_TOKEN allocated by TRUST_TOKEN_new. Safe to call with NULL.
requirements: token must either be NULL or a pointer returned by TRUST_TOKEN_new.

functions.name: TRUST_TOKEN_generate_key
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int TRUST_TOKEN_generate_key(const TRUST_TOKEN_METHOD *method, uint8_t *out_priv_key, size_t *out_priv_key_len, size_t max_priv_key_len, uint8_t *out_pub_key, size_t *out_pub_key_len, size_t max_pub_key_len, uint32_t id);
functions.description: Generates a new Trust Token keypair labeled with id for the specified protocol method, serializing the private and public keys into caller-provided buffers. Writes lengths to out_priv_key_len and out_pub_key_len. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: method must be a valid TRUST_TOKEN_METHOD (e.g., from TRUST_TOKEN_* method getters).
out_priv_key and out_pub_key must point to writable buffers of size at least max_priv_key_len and max_pub_key_len, respectively.
max_priv_key_len and max_pub_key_len should be >= TRUST_TOKEN_MAX_PRIVATE_KEY_SIZE and TRUST_TOKEN_MAX_PUBLIC_KEY_SIZE, respectively, to ensure success.
out_priv_key_len and out_pub_key_len must be non-NULL.
id is an application-chosen key label; must be within 32-bit range (uint32_t).
On success, caller must use the resulting key encodings with the corresponding protocol (same method).

functions.name: TRUST_TOKEN_derive_key_from_secret
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int TRUST_TOKEN_derive_key_from_secret(const TRUST_TOKEN_METHOD *method, uint8_t *out_priv_key, size_t *out_priv_key_len, size_t max_priv_key_len, uint8_t *out_pub_key, size_t *out_pub_key_len, size_t max_pub_key_len, uint32_t id, const uint8_t *secret, size_t secret_len);
functions.description: Deterministically derives a Trust Token keypair labeled with id from the provided secret for the specified method, serializing private and public keys into caller-provided buffers. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: method must be a valid TRUST_TOKEN_METHOD compatible with the intended use.
secret must point to a buffer of length secret_len; content drives deterministic derivation (length requirements are not specified).

out_priv_key and out_pub_key must point to writable buffers sized at least max_priv_key_len and max_pub_key_len, respectively; to ensure success, sizes should be >= TRUST_TOKEN_MAX_PRIVATE_KEY_SIZE and TRUST_TOKEN_MAX_PUBLIC_KEY_SIZE.
out_priv_key_len and out_pub_key_len must be non-NULL.
id is an application-chosen key label within uint32_t.

functions.name: TRUST_TOKEN_CLIENT_new
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new TRUST_TOKEN_CLIENT for the given method and maximum issuance batch size. Returns NULL on error. Issuance requests must be smaller than max_batchsize; too-large values may be rejected.
requirements: method must be a valid TRUST_TOKEN_METHOD for the protocol you intend to use.
max_batchsize must be within limits supported by the Trust Tokens method; requests must specify counts < max_batchsize.
Caller owns the returned pointer and must free it with TRUST_TOKEN_CLIENT_free.

functions.name: TRUST_TOKEN_CLIENT_free
functions.description: Frees a TRUST_TOKEN_CLIENT allocated by TRUST_TOKEN_CLIENT_new. Safe to call with NULL.
requirements: ctx must either be NULL or a pointer returned by TRUST_TOKEN_CLIENT_new.

functions.name: TRUST_TOKEN_CLIENT_add_key
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int TRUST_TOKEN_CLIENT_add_key(TRUST_TOKEN_CLIENT *ctx, size_t *out_key_index, const uint8_t *key, size_t key_len);
functions.description: Configures the client to support the given public key encoding. On success sets out_key_index to the index assigned to this key. Returns 1 on success; 0 if the key cannot be parsed or too many keys have been configured.
requirements: ctx must be a valid TRUST_TOKEN_CLIENT instance.
key must point to a valid serialized public key compatible with ctx's method; key_len is its size.
out_key_index must be non-NULL to receive the assigned index.
May fail if the key encoding is invalid or the client has reached its key limit.

functions.name: TRUST_TOKEN_CLIENT_set_srr_key
functions.description: Sets the public key used by the client to verify the SRR (Signed Redemption Record). Returns 1 on success and 0 on error.
requirements: ctx must be a valid TRUST_TOKEN_CLIENT.
key must be a valid EVP_PKEY containing the issuer’s SRR verification public key compatible with the protocol version requiring SRR verification (e.g., v1).
For protocol variants that verify SRR (e.g., TRUST_TOKEN_experiment_v1), this must be set before calling TRUST_TOKEN_CLIENT_finish_redemption.

functions.name: TRUST_TOKEN_CLIENT_begin_issuance
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int TRUST_TOKEN_CLIENT_begin_issuance(TRUST_TOKEN_CLIENT *ctx, uint8_t **out, size_t *out_len, size_t count);
functions.description: Creates a request to obtain count trust tokens. Serializes the request into a newly allocated buffer returned via out/out_len. Caller must OPENSSL_free the buffer. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: ctx must be a valid TRUST_TOKEN_CLIENT.
count must be less than the max_batchsize configured at client construction.
out and out_len must be non-NULL; on success, *out must be freed with OPENSSL_free.

functions.name: TRUST_TOKEN_CLIENT_begin_issuance_over_message
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int TRUST_TOKEN_CLIENT_begin_issuance_over_message(TRUST_TOKEN_CLIENT *ctx, uint8_t **out, size_t *out_len, size_t count, const uint8_t *msg, size_t msg_len);
functions.description: Creates a request to obtain trust tokens derived over the provided message msg. Serializes the request into a newly allocated buffer returned via out/out_len. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: ctx must be a valid TRUST_TOKEN_CLIENT.
count must be less than the max_batchsize configured at client construction.
msg must point to msg_len bytes (may be empty if msg_len==0).
out and out_len must be non-NULL; on success, *out must be freed with OPENSSL_free.

functions.name: TRUST_TOKEN_CLIENT_finish_issuance
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT STACK_OF(TRUST_TOKEN) *TRUST_TOKEN_CLIENT_finish_issuance(TRUST_TOKEN_CLIENT *ctx, size_t *out_key_index, const uint8_t *response, size_t response_len);
functions.description: Consumes the issuer’s issuance response, extracts the issued tokens, and returns them as a STACK_OF(TRUST_TOKEN). Sets out_key_index to the index of the key used to sign the tokens. Ownership of the returned list passes to the caller. The list is empty if issuance fails.
requirements: ctx must be a valid TRUST_TOKEN_CLIENT configured with the issuer’s public keys (via TRUST_TOKEN_CLIENT_add_key).
response must point to response_len bytes received from the issuer.
out_key_index must be non-NULL to receive the key index.
Caller must free the returned stack with sk_TRUST_TOKEN_pop_free(..., TRUST_TOKEN_free).

functions.name: TRUST_TOKEN_CLIENT_begin_redemption
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int TRUST_TOKEN_CLIENT_begin_redemption(TRUST_TOKEN_CLIENT *ctx, uint8_t **out, size_t *out_len, const TRUST_TOKEN *token, const uint8_t *data, size_t data_len, uint64_t time);
functions.description: Creates a redemption request for the given token and associated data. time is seconds since the UNIX epoch and is used to verify issuer responses in TrustTokenV1 (ignored in other versions). Serializes the request into a newly allocated buffer returned via out/out_len. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: ctx must be a valid TRUST_TOKEN_CLIENT.
token must point to a valid TRUST_TOKEN to be redeemed.
data must point to data_len bytes (may be empty if data_len==0).
out and out_len must be non-NULL; on success, *out must be freed with OPENSSL_free.
time must be a UNIX timestamp in seconds when using TrustTokenV1.

functions.name: TRUST_TOKEN_CLIENT_finish_redemption
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int TRUST_TOKEN_CLIENT_finish_redemption(TRUST_TOKEN_CLIENT *ctx, uint8_t **out_rr, size_t *out_rr_len, uint8_t **out_sig, size_t *out_sig_len, const uint8_t *response, size_t response_len);
functions.description: Consumes the issuer’s redemption response. In TRUST_TOKEN_experiment_v1, verifies the SRR and, if valid, outputs newly allocated buffers containing the SRR (out_rr/out_rr_len) and its signature (out_sig/out_sig_len). In other versions, returns response as out_rr without validation. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: ctx must be a valid TRUST_TOKEN_CLIENT.
response must point to response_len bytes from the issuer.
out_rr and out_rr_len must be non-NULL; on success, *out_rr must be freed with OPENSSL_free.
For v1, out_sig and out_sig_len must be non-NULL to receive the signature; for other versions they may be ignored.
For protocol variants that verify SRR (e.g., v1), the SRR verification public key must have been set via TRUST_TOKEN_CLIENT_set_srr_key before calling.

functions.name: TRUST_TOKEN_ISSUER_new
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new TRUST_TOKEN_ISSUER for the given method and maximum issuance batch size. Returns NULL on error. Issuance requests must be smaller than max_batchsize; too-large values may be rejected.
requirements: method must be a valid TRUST_TOKEN_METHOD for the intended protocol.
max_batchsize must be within limits supported by the method; issuance requests must have batch size < max_batchsize.
Caller owns the returned pointer and must free it with TRUST_TOKEN_ISSUER_free.

functions.name: TRUST_TOKEN_ISSUER_free
functions.description: Frees a TRUST_TOKEN_ISSUER allocated by TRUST_TOKEN_ISSUER_new. Safe to call with NULL.
requirements: ctx must either be NULL or a pointer returned by TRUST_TOKEN_ISSUER_new.

functions.name: TRUST_TOKEN_ISSUER_add_key
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int TRUST_TOKEN_ISSUER_add_key(TRUST_TOKEN_ISSUER *ctx, const uint8_t *key, size_t key_len);
functions.description: Configures the issuer to support the given private key encoding. The key must be a private key returned by TRUST_TOKEN_generate_key. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error (e.g., if the key cannot be parsed or too many keys have been configured).
requirements: ctx must be a valid TRUST_TOKEN_ISSUER.
key must be a serialized private key as produced by TRUST_TOKEN_generate_key for the same method; key_len is its size.
May fail if key encoding is invalid or issuer has already configured the maximum number of keys.

functions.name: TRUST_TOKEN_ISSUER_set_srr_key
functions.description: Sets the private key used by the issuer to sign the SRR. Returns 1 on success and 0 on error.
requirements: ctx must be a valid TRUST_TOKEN_ISSUER.
key must be a valid EVP_PKEY containing the SRR signing private key appropriate for the protocol.

functions.name: TRUST_TOKEN_ISSUER_set_metadata_key
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int TRUST_TOKEN_ISSUER_set_metadata_key(TRUST_TOKEN_ISSUER *ctx, const uint8_t *key, size_t len);
functions.description: Sets the key used to encrypt private metadata (used to encode the private metadata bit in the SRR). The key is a randomly generated bytestring of at least 32 bytes. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: ctx must be a valid TRUST_TOKEN_ISSUER.
key must point to a randomly generated bytestring.
len must be at least 32 bytes.

functions.name: TRUST_TOKEN_ISSUER_issue
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int TRUST_TOKEN_ISSUER_issue(const TRUST_TOKEN_ISSUER *ctx, uint8_t **out, size_t *out_len, size_t *out_tokens_issued, const uint8_t *request, size_t request_len, uint32_t public_metadata, uint8_t private_metadata, size_t max_issuance);
functions.description: Processes a client issuance request and issues up to max_issuance tokens. Produces a response in a newly allocated buffer (out/out_len) and reports the number of tokens issued via out_tokens_issued. Tokens are issued with public_metadata (must match a configured key ID) and private_metadata (0 or 1). Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: ctx must be a valid (configured) TRUST_TOKEN_ISSUER with at least one key added via TRUST_TOKEN_ISSUER_add_key.
request must point to request_len bytes from the client.
public_metadata must be one of the previously configured key IDs.
private_metadata must be 0 or 1.
max_issuance is an upper bound on tokens to issue; the actual number is returned in out_tokens_issued.
out, out_len, and out_tokens_issued must be non-NULL; on success, *out must be freed with OPENSSL_free.
Incoming requests must have batch size smaller than the issuer’s max_batchsize set at construction.

functions.name: TRUST_TOKEN_ISSUER_redeem
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int TRUST_TOKEN_ISSUER_redeem(const TRUST_TOKEN_ISSUER *ctx, uint32_t *out_public, uint8_t *out_private, TRUST_TOKEN **out_token, uint8_t **out_client_data, size_t *out_client_data_len, const uint8_t *request, size_t request_len);
functions.description: Verifies a redemption request and extracts metadata, the redeemed token, and client-provided data. Writes public metadata to out_public, private metadata (if any) to out_private, the token to a newly allocated TRUST_TOKEN* (out_token), and the client data to a newly allocated buffer (out_client_data/out_client_data_len). Caller owns allocated outputs. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error. Caller must globally track tokens to detect replays before responding to clients.
requirements: ctx must be a valid (configured) TRUST_TOKEN_ISSUER.
request must point to request_len bytes from the client.
out_public, out_private, out_token, out_client_data, and out_client_data_len must be non-NULL.
On success, *out_token must be freed with TRUST_TOKEN_free; *out_client_data must be freed with OPENSSL_free.
The caller must maintain a global set of previously seen token values and reject redemptions that replay a token (to prevent double-spending).

functions.name: TRUST_TOKEN_ISSUER_redeem_over_message
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int TRUST_TOKEN_ISSUER_redeem_over_message(const TRUST_TOKEN_ISSUER *ctx, uint32_t *out_public, uint8_t *out_private, TRUST_TOKEN **out_token, uint8_t **out_client_data, size_t *out_client_data_len, const uint8_t *request, size_t request_len, const uint8_t *msg, size_t msg_len);
functions.description: Verifies a redemption request and that the token is derived from the provided message msg. Extracts public and private metadata, the token, and client data, allocating buffers for outputs similarly to TRUST_TOKEN_ISSUER_redeem. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error. Caller must track tokens to prevent replays.
requirements: ctx must be a valid (configured) TRUST_TOKEN_ISSUER.
request must point to request_len bytes; msg must point to msg_len bytes (may be empty if msg_len==0).
out_public, out_private, out_token, out_client_data, and out_client_data_len must be non-NULL.
On success, *out_token must be freed with TRUST_TOKEN_free; *out_client_data must be freed with OPENSSL_free.
Caller must globally track previously seen token values and reject replays.

functions.name: TRUST_TOKEN_decode_private_metadata
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int TRUST_TOKEN_decode_private_metadata(const TRUST_TOKEN_METHOD *method, uint8_t *out_value, const uint8_t *key, size_t key_len, const uint8_t *nonce, size_t nonce_len, uint8_t encrypted_bit);
functions.description: Decodes the encrypted private metadata bit using the specified method, a metadata key, and a nonce. In TRUST_TOKEN_experiment_v1, the nonce is the SRR’s token-hash field. Sets out_value to 0 or 1. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: method must be a valid TRUST_TOKEN_METHOD matching how the metadata was encoded.
key must point to the metadata key bytes (random key used by issuer); key_len is its length.
nonce must point to nonce_len bytes; for v1, this is the SRR token-hash.
out_value must be non-NULL to receive the decoded bit.
encrypted_bit is the encoded metadata bit to be decoded.

functions.name: X509_up_ref
functions.description: Increments the reference count of the given X509 certificate object and returns 1. Use when sharing an X509 across components to avoid premature free.
requirements: x509 must be a valid, initialized X509 pointer.
Caller must later balance with X509_free to decrement the reference count.

functions.name: X509_chain_up_ref
functions.description: Returns a newly-allocated stack with the same X509 elements as chain and increments each element's reference count. Returns NULL on allocation or other failure.
requirements: chain may be NULL only if caller tolerates a NULL return (interpreted as error).
Each X509 in chain must be valid; the function increments their refcounts.
Caller must free the returned stack with sk_X509_pop_free and X509_free for each element.

functions.name: X509_dup
functions.description: Creates a newly-allocated deep copy of x509 by serializing and parsing it. Auxiliary properties are not preserved. May fail if x509 is incomplete.
requirements: x509 must point to a decodable certificate; incomplete/inconsistent objects may cause failure.
Caller owns the returned object and must free with X509_free.
Auxiliary properties (i2d_X509_AUX extras) are not duplicated.

functions.name: X509_free
functions.description: Decrements the reference count of x509 and frees it when the count reaches zero.
requirements: x509 may be NULL (no action), or a valid X509 pointer.
Must not be used after free; ensure refcounting is balanced with X509_up_ref or ownership transfers.

functions.name: d2i_X509
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT X509 *d2i_X509(X509 **out, const uint8_t **inp, long len);
functions.description: Parses a DER-encoded X.509 Certificate from the input buffer (advances *inp) and returns a new X509 on success; follows the standard d2i_ semantics.
requirements: inp must point to a buffer of at least len bytes containing a full DER-encoded certificate.
If out is non-NULL and *out is non-NULL, semantics follow d2i reuse rules; typically pass *out == NULL unless reusing.
On success, caller must free the returned X509 with X509_free.

functions.name: X509_parse_with_algorithms
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT X509 *X509_parse_with_algorithms(CRYPTO_BUFFER *buf, const EVP_PKEY_ALG *const *algs, size_t num_algs);
functions.description: Parses an X509 from a CRYPTO_BUFFER without trailing data and retains a reference to buf. Only public key algorithms in algs are considered decodable; otherwise X509_get0_pubkey will return NULL.
requirements: buf must contain exactly one DER-encoded certificate with no trailing bytes.
buf must outlive the returned X509; the returned X509 increments buf's refcount.
algs may be NULL only if num_algs is zero; provide supported algorithms list to enable pubkey decoding.
Caller must free returned X509 with X509_free.

functions.name: X509_parse_from_buffer
functions.description: Parses an X509 from a CRYPTO_BUFFER using the default algorithm list; retains a reference to buf. Fails on parse error or trailing data.
requirements: buf must contain exactly one DER-encoded certificate with no trailing bytes.
buf must outlive the returned X509; the returned X509 increments buf's refcount.
Caller must free returned X509 with X509_free.

functions.name: i2d_X509
functions.description: Serializes x509 to DER as described by i2d_ semantics. Writes to *outp if non-NULL and advances it, or returns length if outp is NULL.
requirements: x509 must be a valid certificate; incomplete objects may cause failure.
If outp is non-NULL and *outp is NULL, function allocates; caller must OPENSSL_free the allocated buffer.
If outp is non-NULL and *outp is non-NULL, caller must ensure sufficient space and manage pointer advancement.

functions.name: X509_get_version
functions.description: Returns the numeric version field of the certificate: 0=v1, 1=v2, 2=v3.
requirements: x509 must be a valid parsed certificate.

functions.name: X509_get0_serialNumber
functions.description: Returns a non-owning pointer to the certificate's serial number.
requirements: Do not modify the returned ASN1_INTEGER.
x509 must be valid for the lifetime of the pointer.

functions.name: X509_get0_notBefore
functions.description: Returns a non-owning pointer to the certificate's notBefore time.
requirements: Do not modify the returned ASN1_TIME.
x509 must remain valid while using the pointer.

functions.name: X509_get0_notAfter
functions.description: Returns a non-owning pointer to the certificate's notAfter time.
requirements: Do not modify the returned ASN1_TIME.
x509 must remain valid while using the pointer.

functions.name: X509_get_issuer_name
functions.description: Returns the issuer X509_NAME. Non-const for compatibility; caller must not modify.
requirements: x509 must be valid.
Caller must not free or mutate the returned X509_NAME.

functions.name: X509_get_subject_name
functions.description: Returns the subject X509_NAME. Non-const for compatibility; caller must not modify.
requirements: x509 must be valid.
Caller must not free or mutate the returned X509_NAME.

functions.name: X509_get_X509_PUBKEY
functions.description: Returns the SubjectPublicKeyInfo (X509_PUBKEY). Non-const for OpenSSL compatibility; do not modify.
requirements: x509 must be valid.
Do not modify or free the returned pointer; it is owned by x509.

functions.name: X509_get0_pubkey
functions.description: Returns the certificate's public key as a cached EVP_PKEY, or NULL if unsupported/un-decodable. Caller must not mutate or free the returned EVP_PKEY.
requirements: x509 must be valid.
Returned EVP_PKEY is non-owning and cached; do not modify or free.

functions.name: X509_get_pubkey
functions.description: Like X509_get0_pubkey but increments the EVP_PKEY refcount. Caller must free with EVP_PKEY_free.
requirements: x509 must be valid.
Caller must call EVP_PKEY_free on the returned key.
Returned key is cached in x509; do not mutate its internal state.

functions.name: X509_get0_pubkey_bitstr
functions.description: Returns the BIT STRING of the SubjectPublicKey (without AlgorithmIdentifier). Non-const for compatibility; caller must not modify.
requirements: x509 must be valid.
Do not modify or free the returned ASN1_BIT_STRING.

functions.name: X509_check_private_key
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT int X509_check_private_key(const X509 *x509, const EVP_PKEY *pkey);
functions.description: Checks if pkey's private key matches x509's public key. Returns 1 on match, 0 otherwise.
requirements: x509 and pkey must be valid and initialized keys of compatible types.

functions.name: X509_get0_uids
functions.signature: OPENSSL_EXPORT void X509_get0_uids(const X509 *x509, const ASN1_BIT_STRING **out_issuer_uid, const ASN1_BIT_STRING **out_subject_uid);
functions.description: Outputs non-owning pointers to issuerUID and subjectUID fields if present; sets them to NULL if absent.
requirements: Any of out_issuer_uid or out_subject_uid may be NULL to ignore.
Returned pointers must not be modified or freed.
x509 must remain valid while using returned pointers.

functions.name: X509_get_extension_flags
functions.description: Decodes relevant extensions and returns a bitmask of EXFLAG_* reflecting properties (e.g., CA, critical, invalid). Includes EXFLAG_INVALID on decoding error.
requirements: x509 must be valid. Function may compute and cache flags inside x509; avoid concurrent mutation of x509.

functions.name: X509_get_pathlen
functions.description: Returns path length constraint from basic constraints, or -1 if not present or if some extension in x509 was invalid.
requirements: To distinguish invalid-extension cases, call X509_get_extension_flags and check EXFLAG_INVALID.
x509 must be valid.

functions.name: X509_get_key_usage
